generated_text: Oh, did I ever tell you about that night out Grace had with the girls? It was hilarious! She was clearly the life of the party, insisting everyone order the most unreal food on the menu. Oh, yes, I remember hearing about that. Why didn't you just bring up the subject earlier? I could have totally used another good story to make the day seem less endless. Well I had to wait till now when it’s just us and the baby keeps changing our flow. Hey, little sweetheart, okay to be left for a minute with Auntie Hilary? Of course, just let her know you have to take a call. Yeah, yes, that's what I’ll tell you. So anyway, as if Ron didn’t order enough food, she then proceeded to convince everyone that they needed to try all the local drinks. You should have seen the waitress’s face when she brought a tray heaped with ten different pints and glasses. I can just imagine. That’s just so like her, always the adventurous one. Isn’t it though? And you know, she convinced the others to order some ridiculous dessert too - a chocolate fondue bar for the table! A whole bar of chocolate, melted and served with different fruits and biscuits. They were all laughing so hard by the end of the evening, but that’s what keeps our family together I suppose - doesn’t matter what we do as long as we do it together. And then on the other hand, we have people like the baby over here who only need enough food for a tiny sandwich. Speaking of food, have you checked on what we have for lunch later? We can probably get something simple in and it’s always easier to grab a bite when the baby takes a nap soon. Good idea. Have you thought about what we're doing when the baby is a bit older? Like, how often we’ll see the family, maybe plans to travel? Well, we've discussed just being relaxed about it. I mean, with work and everything we’ll see how it works out. But we definitely want to make trips up to see your family and mine, especially when the baby starts to ask questions about grandparents. I know that will be a special time. We can always make the effort when it matters.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we drove from Spain to France and lost our GPS? Whole day was a mess! You're right, that was quite a fiasco. Especially now, the border checks are a doddle compared to back then! But even with the increased checks, I feel like the whole EU travel thing has become a lot less of a hassle, don't you think? Definitely! I've heard loads of stories about difficulties when the UK was in the EU but I've noticed it's been relatively effortless for me as a student passing through. Yeah, from a research standpoint, the open borders made my job much easier, especially when I had to conduct research across various countries. It was almost like we were all part of this big travel hub of ideas and knowledge. I can imagine. We've had our fair share of conference and study visits across the continent since the Brexit referendum. But now there are a few more headaches, like visas for longer stays. That's true. I'm currently doing some research on the impact of Brexit on academic exchange programs. It's fascinating but also pretty depressing at times. In what way depressing? Well, the funding and the ease of collaboration has taken a hit for British students and researchers. The whole point of being in the EU, especially for academics, was the seamless flow of people, ideas, grants... Now it's more complicated, and a lot of good stuff is harder to come by. I see. But it's not just about the academics though, right? The whole freedom of movement has also affected regular people, if I'm not mistaken? Absolutely! The whole idea of passport-free travel was so... natural to us. I used to travel regularly to Ireland, France, or Germany without even thinking about it. Now, it's just a different story. From queues to visas, it's changing the whole dynamic of how we travel and interact across borders. True. I spent a few months last year in Austria for my PhD research. It was wonderful but, as you said, getting there and back was a bit of a process. The paperwork felt like a project in itself! I had to fill out forms for hours just for a short trip to Belgium for a conference recently. It felt like bureaucracy had got in the way of my freedom.

Alright, I don't think we've ever had such a varied spread of desserts before, have we? We've got everything from fruit salad to key lime pie. What are we going to do? Choose one at a time? I want key lime pie, Mummy! I think I'll go for the strawberry mousse! Okay, fair enough. We can start with your key lime pie, Emma. And Leah, how about we have strawberry mousse as our second dessert? Yeah! Can we play Monopoly after, Mummy? Not tonight, sweetie. We're not going to play Monopoly every night. But we always have time for Monopoly! It's true, we do seem to play a lot of Monopoly lately. It's not every night, though. Alright... It's not a bad thing to have a bit of variety, though, right? We need other things to talk about and do as a family. Exactly. So, let's talk about something else for a while. Do either of you like my new recipe for chocolate chip cookies? Chocolate chip cookies? For real? I like them! But it's not just any chocolate chip cookie. It's a special recipe from my university days. I thought we could make them together during the weekend. That sounds like fun. I like the idea of making cookies together. Oh, can we play Monopoly while we bake cookies? Please, please? We could sit together and play while the cookies bake, I suppose. That way we get to talk and make cookies at the same time. Hooray! And we'll use the sweet treats as our money! Alright, deal. But real money will still be involved in the game tonight, though. Well, I can't wait. I've been needing to figure out if I'm better at banking or hotels this season. We'll see about that. I already know my strategy. Me too! I always get the Boardwalk! Of course you do. You're very lucky with Boardwalk, aren't you? Yes, very lucky. I helped you win last time. No, it's because I'm the best! Of course, Emma. Of course. Well, let's not spoil the surprise tonight. True. Let the games begin. Alright, dessert first, then? And when we're done, we'll set up the board. Yes! Can we have dessert now? You're eager, aren't you? She sure is. Let's get the key lime pie out, and we'll all try a bit together.

Yo, mate, did you seen any of that latest document from Simmons? I was expecting today's delivery but it ain't arrived yet. Yeah, talked to our admin person, and she said she's been working through some delays in the processing. Still waiting on some documents to finalize the clauses for the contract questions. Oh, right, I see. She's the one working out of Sunderland, isn't she? I've heard she can be a bit of a stickler for details, but she's good for us. But even so, it's been a bit touch-and-go with these deadlines. Absolutely, and considering her background with the graduate qualifications from Newcastle, she knows her stuff. The trouble is sometimes our paperwork just gets held up down there. But she was fairly confident it'll be in hand soon. Fair point. What's been keeping you up to date? You're out of the office a lot with your engineering consultancy work, right? Yeah, got a big job in central London at the moment. It's been hectic, but it should be peaking soon. Then I can catch a breather. But while I'm out this often, it means I see less of you and all. I know. It feels like ages since we last properly caught up. You've been in and out of Harpenden so much lately, even weekends are packed. Though at least you're making good coin with it, I'm happy to hear you're doing well. Well, it isn't all bad, but I do miss you guys when I'm away so much. The lifestyle isn't the only benefit of my job, though - doesn't come close to beating the thrill of seeing the progress we make with our projects. I get that. We've done alright for ourselves, considerin' where we come from, hasn't we? I just wish, sometimes, the routine would be a little less... routine. I know what you mean. There's a comfort to routine, but sometimes changing the scenery keeps life interesting. Definitely, though a bit more balance would be nice. You know, for me, I've been plodding along in my job so long, I thought I might want to see if there's a postgrad option available to me too. The industry's changed a bit since I graduated almost 5 years ago.

Ah, mates, remember when we used to play cricket in those spare fields near the old brick factory? Whole afternoons slumped out there, just talked about our dreams and worried about the world. Indeed I do! You were always the one with the fancy swings on your bat. I'd have had me eye on that ball but never could hit it quite like you, Tom! But why didn't you two never pursue cricket professionally? All that talent and passion. It could've changed everything for you two, at least financially. Hah! Dreamed of it for sure, but life had other plans I suppose. Couple of lazy London years, a bit too much to drink, missed my chances. "Couple of lazy London years", Tom? That's a polite way of putting it! But I didn’t have the hunger, the fire in the belly. And now we spend our days watching the grandkids or whatever TV series they watch at the moment, eh? We could have it worse, Pat. I've plenty of stories about that brick factory to tell the youngsters. Where did you all grow up? Was it pleasant in Costessey? It was fine, but like Norwich, it's changed beyond recognition. New families, new faces. The old pub where I'd go for darts still stands though. Oh really? Costessey's not too far from me, but I don’t know the area well. I've always thought it's a bit too quiet for me. Harrow had its own charm, you know? Busy, bustling, but it had the heart of London close by. Ah, the city life. I used to love that whenever I'd visit. But now, this quiet life is more my speed. No confrontations with trains running late or forgetting where you parked your bike. Speaking of which, I was late on the train for the last time in 1983 and never missed it again! Sounds familiar! I once missed my bus by 5 minutes and had to walk the whole way. That's almost 6 miles, just for fun! Ah, the humble joys of public transport! We've had our share of adventure. And all that education we got for free...mostly reduced to discussing the weather and recalling old times over a cuppa nowadays. True. Sometimes I wonder what our lives would be like if we hadn’t become long-term unemployed.

So, how's Honest Skincare coming along, Sarah? I have to say, the fact that you've branched out into selling online is quite impressive. Oh, thanks, Anna! It's been a whirlwind really. I never thought it would get this big, but the response has been fantastic. We've had sales from all over the country and even a few from abroad. But of course, with the good comes the challenges. I'm still struggling with marketing and getting the word out. Really? That's interesting. You know, I've actually been reading up on marketing strategies for small businesses, particularly those using social media. It might be worth considering. What marketing methods have you been using so far? We've just been using a bit of Instagram and word of mouth, honestly. We've tried some boosted posts but they haven't really taken off. Ah, okay. Boosted posts can be hit or miss, especially if you're just starting out. But have you thought about influencer collaborations? Or running a giveaway campaign? It might help raise your brand visibility. That's a great idea! We've thought about it, but it's a bit daunting to contact influencers when we're just a small business. Well, don't be discouraged. Even medium-sized influencers might be interested, not just the big names. And there are platforms now that can connect you with micro-influencers who might be more open to collaborations. True, true. I really need to look into that. Alright, I'll take that on board and see what I can do. But it's not just about the reach. Think about the content you're creating too. Authentic customer reviews and user-generated content can do wonders for a brand. Yeah, I've tried to get some testimonials. We'll need to work on getting more of those. Absolutely. And what about the product line? Have you considered any new products or updates to what you have? We've got a few ideas – more products for sensitive skin, maybe some natural formulations. But I'm a bit nervous about pushing out something new so quickly. That's natural! It's always a risk, but if it aligns with what you're known for and what your customers want, it could pay off. You could do a soft launch and see if it goes well before fully committing to a bigger production run.

Ah, I hear that your weekend was quite eventful, wasn’t it? I hope you didn’t have too much trouble with the council about your extension plans again? Oh, you had heard? Well, yes, it was eventful to say the least. The council wasn’t very cooperative, but we managed to work things out eventually. It seems they’ve finally granted us permission, but it’s been a long and arduous process. I can imagine! I hope I had such luck when I applied for my own extensions when I was living in Scotland. Anyway, how are you finding things at work these days? I suppose, after all these years, you’ve come to expect such hurdles, but I can’t help but feel a bit of sympathy for you trying to make your house more comfortable for the kids. Yes, it’s become a bit of an expected pain. As a teacher, you’d think certain processes would be streamlined by now, but it seems bureaucracy is the same everywhere. But we’re managing, and the kids are excited about the new playroom we’re going to have. That’s wonderful! Children really do need their own space to grow and develop. You and Pat certainly provided a lovely environment for your kids growing up. Thank you, I think so too. Though, to be honest, the recent news about the public education budget cuts really worries me. It’s a bit like déjà vu, hearing about all the underfunding and overcrowding that I faced in my early days teaching. Pat isn’t in education any more, but she often expresses her concerns about the state of the system. And with me working in it, it feels like we’re facing similar challenges that you and I went through. The budget cuts and overcrowding? Yes, it’s hard to believe it’s gone full circle. When did I last hear, they’re talking about a return to the class sizes we used to have? Exactly! It seems we’re forgetting some of the lessons of the past. There’s a generation of kids out there who benefit so much from having more attention in class, not less. I couldn’t agree more. I remember when class sizes were often so large in my early days, it was so difficult to give each student the attention they needed. And the students who were struggling the most, they were always the ones who needed the most individual attention...

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we had our heating break down during Christmas? Well, no, but sounds like chaos. What happened? Was it the heater or the boiler? Both actually! But it was so bad because it was freezing out and Christmas day, of course, so the timing was just terrible. But why didn't you fix it before Christmas? Oh, we tried, but the companies had such long waiting lists. That's a nightmare. I know, right? So we had to rely on electric heaters and blankets, and trust me, it was chilly. So, was it a good excuse to have an indoor picnic then? Almost, but between the cold and the lack of proper heating, it was more like a festival of shivering. I can't imagine. We just got our new heaters last year, and they've been faultless so far. Well, at least you have some good technology to rely on. Aye, definitely, but still, it wasn't a festive experience as I'd imagined. So, maybe you should have asked for tools for Christmas instead of that mulberry tree you wanted. Oh, dear, I don't think so. The mulberry tree was a great idea. The kids loved it. But maybe a few tools wouldn't have been a bad idea either. If you think about it, tools can be like insurance. Always handy to have around and it's always good to learn a new skill. Absolutely, especially if you're into DIY or gardening like me. I've been meaning to learn how to take care of the garden properly. Speaking of skills, I've been trying out those new cooking recipes this month. Oh, and what did you make? Well, I tried a new mulberry tart recipe. I know it's not exactly traditional for Christmas, but I like to experiment. Mulberry tart? That's a bit specific. Oh, it was actually amazing. The mulberries are quite sweet, and the tart itself came out really good. So, did everyone enjoy it? Well, it was quite divisive, but I think everyone liked it once they tried it. That's actually interesting because I've noticed Swindon has a lot of mulberry trees. They're quite hard to use though. Really? I've never heard of using mulberries like that. It's quite hard to find recipes with mulberries because they are very...sensitive, I suppose.

Oh, Dad, remember when you used to tell us these crazy stories about how your mum would never tolerate improper use of cutlery at the table? That always cracked me up. Yeah, I remember. She was quite particular wasn’t she? Oh, definitely. I still make sure to use the correct fork and knife even now, just in case mum’s watching from up there. All very well for you lot to remember that, coming from families where it was always done properly. You kids just don’t know, do you? Oh, Dad, we were just as well trained as anyone else. Though, to be fair, even I mess up sometimes when I’m in a hurry. I suppose you’re all still trying to live up to your mum’s standards, aren’t you? It’s not just about living up to her standards; it’s about respect and tradition, isn't it? I mean, even though we might not use the same cutlery set every day, it’s about showing respect for the meal and for each other. Exactly. And don’t even get me started on the proper way to set the table. Ah, the proper way. I remember, we always laid the table before mum even got in from work. She’d come in, and the table would be set, and she’d smile and say, “Well done, doesn’t look half bad today.” Oh, dear, I don’t think I was as particular as the rest of you. I just measured the festivities by whether there was enough food. That's true, we were all about the food before anything else, weren’t we? But still, you always found a way to make sure everyone was included and comfortable. That was one of mum’s greatest traits - making sure everyone felt included and at ease. She always said it was more important than the food or the cutlery. Again and again, she'd say, "The most important thing at any meal is the company and the conversation." She had a point. Though, I don’t think she’d ever trade our lively discussions for silent meals. You're right, there’s something special about sharing food and stories with loved ones. Whether it’s at a well-set table or not, it’s the company that makes the time meaningful. Speaking of which, have we talked about dinner plans for tomorrow?

Oh, did I ever tell you about my day at work? No, what happened? Well, I had this horrendous meeting with our new client and I thought for sure we'd lose the project. But then this idea just popped into my head and it was like a lightbulb moment. We ended up winning them over and now they're our biggest clients of the year! Really?! That's fantastic! So how is that going to affect us here? Oh, it's going to be good news for everyone. More projects, more work, and I'm expecting a nice bonus in my paycheck soon. That's great! Well, good for you! Thanks. It's nice to finally have a bit of good news at work after all the stress we've been through. Did we decide on the skiing trip yet? Oh! Now that? I've been thinking about it and I think we should definitely go. It'll be a nice break from everything. Yeah, I was thinking the same. We haven’t had a holiday together since last year, and the kids have been excited about it too. Right. And I've found a lovely place, really good reviews. It's in the French Alps and they have fantastic ski schools for the kids. The French Alps? That sounds lovely, but won't it be a bit far? It's true, it's a bit of a journey, but I've researched it and I think we can handle it. Plus, it'll be worth it. There's so much to do for all of us and it's supposed to be beautiful. It might be a good idea to start packing soon. I know the kids are excited, but I have to make sure they remember their goggles, gloves, and all that. You're absolutely right! And don't even get me started on what I need to pack. Probably half of the house. I know! But it'll be fun. And don't worry, we can discuss our lists together, so we don't forget anything. That's a great idea. And maybe we can prepare some of the things we need in advance, like booking the lessons for the kids. Good thinking. We should sit down and make a list this weekend, so we're ready come December. Definitely. I'll start with that, and also sort out the travel arrangements.

Yo, so I'm losing my mind with maths homework. We've got these gods-awful word problems that my teacher just assumes we intuitively understand. Oh, maths! I'm with you there, honestly! I spent like, hours trying to do the quadratic equations last night. Exactly! You remember that one where we had to work out the area of a field using Pythagoras and then calculate the cost to fence it? I still don't get how to get the answer. Yeah, that one. I managed to get most of it, but I'm still not 100% sure. I have to check with someone else today. Same here! I almost gave up and just made up a number. No, no, we can't do that! Our teacher would just mark it wrong. Exactly! So, did you hear that Ms. Patel decided we're doing a creative writing project in English too? What a joy. Ugh, I was dreading that. I'm really not good at coming up with stories. Oh, come on, it’s not that bad! It’s different from writing essays. We can make fun stories! Maybe. But don't tell me you're happy about the food tech project we also have to do? It’s so much to manage. True, but at least we get to eat some of what we make. And you know what, we should actually really plan out that project together, maybe even swap tips on what we're cooking and working on? Yeah, good idea! But it's tough because we both have such different styles. I’m finding it hard to make my pastry not turn out like a brick. Don't worry, we can practice together. Plus, I saw a recipe online for a really easy quiche. We can do that? Sounds like a plan! Maybe we can also do it in your house, so we don't make a mess in my mum’s kitchen. Definitely! We can make that quiche for our parents. Maybe for dinner or something. That would be so much fun! And they might even give us a break on the food tech homework. Plus, could you imagine our Spanish teacher almost fainting when we tell them we made a quiche in Spanish? Haha, no way! That would be hilarious. Maybe we should prep a little cheesy Spanish speech while we’re at it.

Right, so I was going over some of the latest reviews and I've been thinking we should pick a film to watch together. There are a few new ones that look good, but I'm not entirely sure which one to choose. That sounds like a plan! Which ones did you have in mind? I'm open to anything, but I do have a soft spot for sci-fi. Ah, I saw 'The Lost City of Alchemy' got quite impressive reviews, and 'The Long Night' is also up for consideration. 'The Lost City of Alchemy' sounds interesting, but 'The Long Night' – that's more my style. I've heard it's very well made and has some fantastic visuals. So, shall we make that our pick for tonight? I've actually never seen either of those, but hearing you say that makes me even more curious. Definitely! It'll be fun to discover a new film together. While we're deciding, maybe we should also consider food choices. You're in charge of cooking, so should I help with anything or just stick to preparing dessert? We could have a night in with some homemade pasta and garlic bread if you're busy or want to stay relaxed. The rest of the family should be home soon. That sounds lovely! Do we also need to pick a time for it? Ah, let's aim for 7:30. That gives us time to wind down a bit and maybe even get the little one off to bed by 9 if all goes well. Perfect! I can finish up a few things at work and be home around 7. That works for me, then. I just need to make the pasta and get into the mood for a film together. I'll come help with setting up the living room and getting everything ready. You know me by now; movies are one of my favorite rituals and it's always more enjoyable when it's a shared experience. I can tell you do love it, which makes it even better for me. Let's not forget to put the kettle on. We always have a soothing tea later at night while we unwind. Right, tea will be ready and waiting. Excellent. Now, just in case the film picks don't work out or we want a little break, have you got any other ideas for fun films we could watch if we need a back-up plan?

Oh, Mum, I haven't seen you in ages! It's so lovely to finally have some proper catch-up time. How's life been treating you? You know, it's been alright dear. Just the usual court cases and drama, but I love it really. Can't imagine doing anything else now. What about you, how have the teaching gigs been going? Oh, I'd love to say everything is perfect, but this semester has been a bit of a nightmare with all the new curriculum changes... I just hope we manage to settle into the new system soon. Well, change is never easy, but just like in court, you'll get the hang of it. You're a good teacher, you'll adjust. And the summer's nearly here, so you'll have a bit of a rest soon. Yeah, I'm looking forward to that. Actually, have you guys thought about where we're going on holiday this year? We were thinking maybe the coast again... this time it might be somewhere in Devon, or maybe Cornwall. Oh, that sounds great! We haven't been to Cornwall in ages. Yeah, and the sea air is always good for everyone's health too. Speaking of health, how is old Blackberry doing? I remember last time he was having a bit of an arthritis problem. He doesn't seem much better, it's tough seeing him in pain that way. The vet suggested we could try some supplements, but I'm not sure yet. Oh, that must be difficult. I've always loved Blackberry. Do you think we could look at some home-made remedies too? There are some herbal options that might help. Perhaps, but I've always preferred to follow the vet’s advice. Of course. Maybe we could also talk to a specialist, see what they recommend. Yeah, that's a good idea. So, how is work at the court going? We don't catch up as often as we used to. It's been busy. Always a lot of cases, late nights sometimes. But it’s what I know best, I suppose. And don’t forget to take care of yourself, Mum. Late nights and endless paperwork can take a toll. I know, I know. Though sometimes I feel like I've been doing it so long, I've forgotten how to do anything else! You could always try retirement...

I've decided I need a new wardrobe. I just can't see myself wearing the same old conference t-shirts and jeans anymore. I don't blame you, love. You deserve to feel amazing every now and then. You've been doing so well with your students this semester. Going over the moon and back for them, and you still have the time to lecture! Thanks, I do enjoy it, but it's still very tiring sometimes. But that's keeps me going. Anyway, about shopping... Do you have any recommendations for places here in China? I've been lazy about it since we moved here, just sticking to what's closest or online. Absolutely, there are plenty of places, especially in Beijing. But let me think for a second... Shengxian Lu is well-known for its fashion scene and has a lot of high-end boutiques, but if you're looking for something more affordable and also creative, you might want to check out the shops around Wudaokou. It's a bit of a trek, but the area is known for its independent or boutique stores. They have some cute designs and really unique pieces. Oh, that sounds great! I want something quirky but still professional, while also being relatively affordable. Definitely, Wudaokou could be perfect. There's a place called Hangzhou Road 1950, or just call it '1950' for short. It's a bit pricey, but really good quality and funky designs. And, I'm pretty sure they sell 'informal chic' types of items - doesn't sound ideal for academia but hell, it's the weekend now, so why not! Right, just the weekend. That's very thoughtful of me. More like reckless, but I appreciate the suggestion. Hell, let's be honest, we all need some recklessness from time to time. There's also another place called 'Nobody Music Bar' on Xingfu Road. You'd never guess it from the name, but they have a store section with some amazing pieces. The owner used to be a designer in Hong Kong before moving here. It's like mixing vintage trends with a modern twist. Ooh, that sounds intriguing and sounds right up my alley. I love browsing in places that feel unique and authentic. Good. I’ll text you the exact locations. And don’t worry about time. We’ve both finished teaching for the semester. Might as well treat yourselves to a day of shopping and brunch.

Alright, girls! Let's move on from books for now. Who'd like to talk about our weekend plans and how the babysitting went? Oh, it was so fun! The new babysitter, Lily, was super kind and played with me all day. She even let me help her bake cookies! Yeah! And we even made a big mess, but it was fun! I think I want to learn to bake cookies with you, mom! Well, that's lovely to hear, but I think next time you'll have to help clean up the mess, huh? Yeah, maybe we can make a deal! If we help with the cleaning up, we get to learn to bake too? That sounds like a fair deal to me! Sounds like we have a deal then! We can make it a fun day tomorrow. Now, how about dinner tonight? I was thinking we could make some fun comfort food. Any ideas? Maybe mac and cheese? Yes, mac and cheese! Alright, mac and cheese it is then. I'll add some roast chicken to go with it. That sounds yummy! Can we also plan when we'll see friends? Sofia is coming over next week and I can't wait to show her my new bike. Of course! But the first thing we have to do is get your hair cut, I just booked the salon for Thursday afternoon. You two can decide what you want to do while I take you to get your haircut. I want to play outside while mom takes us to the haircut. Yeah! I want to play outside too. Can we make a deal that we get to play outside as soon as we get back? Alright, deal! But only if you don't run around and get too dirty just before the haircut. No promises! Well, let's get this mac and cheese started while we chat. Maybe there's time to squeeze in another chapter from this really cool book Speaker_3 was reading earlier today? Yeah! Can we? I want to hear what happens next! Yeah, please! Though, can Speaker_1 read it? She's way better at reading aloud and making it fun. Sure, happy to. Here, sit back down and let's continue where we left off. Who could that be? Not expecting anyone right now. Maybe it's Sofia or Alex! I think it's Sofia! She said she was coming over later!

Oh, did I tell you about the banging lecture I attended today? The lecture on microeconomics was less exciting than watching paint dry! Are you kidding me? I had to leave halfway because it just wasn't cutting it. I kind of regret going to university this morning haha. But then, the tutorial afterwards was a game-changer! The tutor makes complex stuff so accessible and understandable. Yeah? That’s good to hear. I wish I'd stuck around. Anyway, how was the canteen food? Eh, not bad. They always seem to have pasta with questionable sauce and soggy salad. But the café in the library near Penrhys is actually pretty decent. Right, but it costs a fortune! I'm making do with this free lunch. Hence why I'm here with you instead of going there. Fair point. Anyway, shall we actually grab lunch somewhere else today? Maybe somewhere not so far and less expensive? Absolutely! But where? I’m really up for trying that new noodle place near the river. I’m game. Where exactly is it? It’s just in the St. Margarets area, not far from the university. It’s apparently super popular. Ah, OK. I’d been wanting to try some authentic noodle dishes. It'd be a nice change from the canteen chaos. Agreed. What do you say we head there after this break? We can finish our lunch here, and then... ...we can have a proper lunch. Sounds like the plan. Shall we just grab this tray together and go? Yep. On that note, did you see Lady Bird or A Star Is Born before they were taken off Netflix? Oh, Lady Bird, yeah! It was brilliant. As for A Star Is Born, I haven’t seen it yet, but I’ve heard it's also really good. Right. I loved how Lady Bird showed such an honest, relatable depiction of teenage life. The ending got me right in the feels. Agreed. And I heard A Star Is Born has such real depth. Bradley Cooper was amazing in it. Yeah. It's amazing how films like that really can capture raw emotion and tell real stories. Definitely. Sure beats some of these lectures this morning. Exactly, if only our lectures could be as engaging as A Star Is Born. Maybe one day, though, let’s not hold our breath. Oh, let’s at least hope for that.

Yo, lads! How've you both been? We're good, thanks for asking. How about you, Sarah? Still buried under mounds of paperwork at work? As usual, isn't it? But, hey, it's a fair trade for the questions I get asked. "What's the policy on this form?" and "Can I have access to that report, please?", all day, every day... But actually, I've been thinking, we should plan a road trip for this summer! Maybe to Scotland or maybe get out of the country altogether. Oh, that sounds like a plan! I've heard about a few spots in Cornwall, they say it's really pretty this time of year. Yeah, or we could head to Germany. My dad is always going on about the Black Forest and how well it does in the summer. Hmm, either sounds doable. But before we splurge on travel, have you both watched the new Stranger Things? I'm on season three now and it's keeping me up all night. Yeah! I finished it last week. Such a mixed bag, really. Some episodes were brilliant but others were a bit rushed. Totally agree. But the music and the nods to the 80s were spot on. Spot on! Well, technology-wise, I'm really looking to upgrade my TV soon. I’m thinking, maybe a 4K model? That could be a good idea, but they are pricey. You working that into your budget? It's part of the backlog of the post-lockdown retail therapy phase, I suppose! That's understandable. Seems like the whole world went together buying new TVs and gadgets. Speaking of which, have you guys tried this new chippy around the corner from yours, Sarah? There's a queue every time I walk past. You mean Midland’s Fish and Chips? Oh, yes, that place is a goldmine! The portions are generous, and the fish is always crispy. I suggest we stop by there on our road trip if we head to the south. Again, agreed. Or perhaps we can go to Nandos if we're in the mood for something different. As a Londoner, I miss my peri-peri chicken. Deeelish! Peri-peri chicken is underrated. You two know me well! I could live off a diet of Nando’s and fish and chips. Just as long as they bring that garlic peri-peri too, yeah?

Right, I hear that city's a whirlwind these days. Been anywhere interesting recently? You know, aside from what's going on at home? Well, we did consider a trip to London. It's been a while since we've all gone together, but with all the doings and chaos in the city now... Ah, did you hear that they're considering a big horse parade actually? Now that would be noteworthy! You two get on with your horsey tales. Speaking of, those new houses you spoke of in Cornwall, did you have a look around? I've heard that's been a hot market too. Might just be the next thing to catch. Ah, yes - oh we did. It's such a beautiful area, but prices these days are sky-high! It's a bit beyond our budget, especially if we also need to think about upgrading the cars. And these days, it seems like the money's disappearing between all these little things! Money's always a common topic, isn't it? I’ve found myself browsing eBay more lately. Bought myself a nice set of old DVDs of classic TV shows. Makes the evenings more enjoyable at least. Any other interesting sales, you two noticed? Ah, eBay, you'd think I'd have given up all things 'new', but I still dip in occasionally. Once got a decent deal on a used, but good-condition Omega watch. Smashing thing! But I don't think buying and selling would be my idea of a proper "trip" though. We've just had to let the car go. Seems like the young ones reckon they’re doing just fine on their bicycles and public transport. But it feels a right odd, not having one. There’s also been talk about moving a boarding house for the election campaign. We could sit on our little spot here and watch it all unfold – make that worthwhile for once! Well, election, my dear, is like a spectator sport for the like of us! Can't do much about it, but we can still enjoy the mudslinging and all. Though, speaking of being spectators, I've had a thought about those trips. If we pooled some resources, maybe we could still manage a small trip somewhere. Nothing fancy, perhaps just a week in a Youth hostel in Cornwall. That's not... a bad idea! Just the thought of some fresh sea air.

So, how's everything going with the little one? Oh, you know. It's been quite an adventure. The early days were chaotic, but now she's getting more settled and we're adjusting to this new routine. I've heard, the early days can be quite overwhelming! Is she sleeping through the night now? Sleeping through the night? Not quite yet. But she has settled into a slightly better routine, and I'm trying to get as much rest as possible when she does sleep. That's good to hear! I suppose breastfeeding is going okay? Yes, thankfully, that's been going well. She's a good feeder. Though, let me tell you, it can be quite tiring. Sometimes I feel like a human dairy cow! I can imagine. I never realized how much work it takes to feed a baby until I saw you and [Mother's name] with little [Child's name] and [Sibling's name]. You're doing great though. Thanks. I hope so. But it's nice to talk to someone who knows what I'm going through, you being newly graduated and all. You’re right, though, while the research job can be intense, it’s not the same kind of exhausting as looking after a baby 24/7. Ah, but studies and jobs aren't awake at 3am demanding to be fed! True! Tell me about some of the funny moments. There have been a few… The other day, she rolled over and the first thing she grasped was this tiny toy tractor that [Child's name] had left lying around. And then the next day she rolled again and got hold of his mobile phone. Oh my, she's already showing early signs of following in her brother's footsteps! Indeed! While [Child's name] is usually very protective, there was this one time when she was crying, and out of nowhere, he just started singing to her. It was so sweet and it just stopped her crying in seconds. That's lovely! The bond siblings can have is quite remarkable. Absolutely. And it's almost as if she recognizes his voice. Maybe she's just getting used to hearing his singing all the time around the house. It's amazing. [Child's name] has been so patient with her too. He enjoys playing with her and is actually taking his responsibility quite well.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my shift last night? We had a patient who was super stubborn and refused to take his medications. You're right though, Alison, it's always nice to have these kind of days, keeps us on our toes. It's good to hear, though, that you've got them sorted now. I wish I could have seen you dealing with the patient, you’re such a natural. Thanks! It's keeps me busy, but it’s a job I love. I just hope we can get those new policies through at work soon – it’s frustrating waiting for bureaucracy. Might just highlight the reasons why you’re thinking about taking that management role in the long term, isn’t it? Exactly. Hence why I'm planning to take the course soon. It'll be a challenge but I've got my eye on the bigger picture. Plus, there's barely any nurses taking up those leadership roles from the clinical side. It's about time we had more representation! That's true. I'm a bit of a stickler for details myself, which might be why I’ve enjoyed running the department. There's a certain sense of achievement from seeing everything running smoothly. Speaking of running smoothly, I’ve been meaning to ask, do you lot have any plans for the garden this weekend? There's so much to do since the rain stopped, and it's perfect weather for it. Ah, yes! I'd been thinking the same. Maybe we can finally deal with the overgrown part by the shed? Or do you want to start redesigning the vegetable patch first? The vegetable patch sounds like a great idea! I might even have the time to join in – just got this one big project off my schedule yesterday, so I'm a bit freer. If you're free, we could do Saturday? It's usually less chaotic after morning shift. Plus, we should use the chance to get the lawn mowed. It was looking a little shabby last week. Sounds like a plan. Just for the record, I'll just need to check my schedule. But I'm pretty sure I'm free if anyone else is. That’ll work. I'll start clearing those leaves and weeds by the shed this afternoon, just in case the weather changes. Perfect, I can help with that.

Yo, I can't believe we have another maths test on Monday. I'm so worried. I don't understand anything about algebra! Oh, talked about that! I'm really down about that too. Especially sine curves! They're so confusing. Exactly! And on top of that, we have to learn about calculus next term! Yep, and it says they're going to give us more marks for showing our working out. That's so annoying! I'm much better at getting the right answer right away. Haha, tell me about it, dude. Like, I barely have time to finish all the questions, let alone show my working out. I know, right? So what about the art project? You finished it for next week? Yeah, it's going on pretty well. I made a collection of stamps from various countries. Stamps? That's an interesting choice. What countries? Uhm, mostly from Europe and some from the US. I thought it would be cool to show how different countries express their histories and culture on stamps. Oh, that's a great idea! I picked plants for my project. I'm studying about plant biology. Cool! I might learn something interesting there, can't believe I used to think biology was boring. It's not that bad once you start looking at it from different angles. Like, how plants really are so important for life, you know? Yeah, I get it. Plus, doesn't Ed Sheeran have a song about plants too? Oh, that's right! I forgot! "The A Team". But the plants song is actually "Castle on the Hill". Right right. I love how he talks about nature in his songs. It's so relatable. So, what's the plan for Christmas break? We should hang out. Definitely! I was thinking of visiting a garden center somewhere. Cool idea! I like visiting those. Plus, my uncle has a huge garden at his house, we could help him with some gardening. That could be fun. And we could even collect some new plant species for my art project. Perfect! Do you want to go on the 26th or 27th? I think 27th works for me. 26th is when we go to... Oh right, family dinner? Yep! That's what my parents said. How about you? What's your family doing? Same here. So 27th it is. We can meet after lunch at the garden center, how's that?

I seen a great rat puppet last year's Norfolk Show. Got me thinkin' of when us youngsters would make such things out of our mum's old gloves. You mean glove puppets, don't you? I used to make those with the kids at the nursery back in the days. We had so much fun with them! Ah, I remember watching a show with those glove puppets when I was a lad. But now, it's all computer animation and digital keepsakes for kids. Think about it, in our time, it was all about imagination, using what you had. Exactly, and I used to love watchin' them on TV, just like you said. So simple, but so effective. But back to my point, this particular show - "Ratty the Rat" - gave a lesson about recycling and being kind to animals. It did me good, made me think about pollution and all. That's a great topic, you know? Did the kids ever bring up their own versions of puppet shows in the nursery? Perhaps we could even do something like that now? Maybe a group of retired folks and make some homemade shows for the community center or somethin'. That's an excellent idea! I've always thought we could use more community activities that bring people together, especially for the elderly. It's good for mental health and keepin' the community engaged. You're right! There's not a lot in our area for folk like us to get involved in without it costing a fortune. And with the bus fares these days, traveling to community centers… it's not easy. So, keep the activity local, make it accessible. Absolutely, and if we're planning something like that, we should also consider the elderly's mobility and seeing issues. Some won't feel comfortable travelin' on the bus if it's far or uncomfortable. Yes, that's a great point. There must be ways to address transportation or even changing the locations where we gather. Perhaps we could also involve younger volunteers to help with transportation or event setup. Right. I often struggle seein' when I'm out on the bus. I thought I might get my eyes tested soon, just to make sure. That's a good idea! Mobility and healthcare support are just as important as any community activity. As someone who used to care for children, I came across many situations where older people struggled with sight.

I've been meaning to ask you, have you ever had those vegan donuts from that new café in town? They're apparently all the rage now. Oh yes! I tried them once. They were surprisingly good considering, but I suppose that’s the questions when you're looking for donuts that are actually good for you, eh? Exactly! I'm thinking of grabbing one before we head out to explore Venice today. They recommend it as one of the best places for coffee alongside a nice view over the canal. That sounds like a plan. Remember when Venice used to be so quiet? It's changed so much in the past few years. I read that in the past decade, over a million tourists have been visiting each year. And you know, even though it's become quite touristy, the town still has its charm. True, but it's hard not to wish for the old days. I remember growing up here and the canals were always so peaceful, or as peaceful as Bolton could get, I suppose. I can only imagine. I've noticed they've started renovating the old buildings along the canal. It’s really making a difference. I found a picture the other day on a local blog, and the before and afters are quite amazing. Yeah, it’s good to see the town trying to keep up its historical look whilst also being modern and tourist-friendly. We have to love that it's still bringing in money and work for the local community. For sure. Speaking of which, you planning on anything special today? I just had a call with the local botanists club, they want to do a guided walk through the fields just outside the town. It's supposed to be quite informative but also fun. That sounds great! I could use a bit of learning today. After all the partying of last night – I'm not old but I sure feel like it. Don't worry, you're young for a good few years yet! You want to join the walk? I think it’d be a lovely way to spend the morning. As tempting as that sounds, if I joined you, I doubt I’d make it through without sleeping. . Don't worry about it then. Enjoy the day exploring this lovely city with your... ...strength. Thanks! Yeah, maybe I'll make up for it by doing some shopping later; there's some lovely local shops around here I've never had the chance to explore properly.

So, I hear you've seen some of the latest workouts at the gym these days. You know, I've been meaning to try out that new Pilates class, talked about it for ages but never had the time. Oh, yeah! Actually, the new Pilates class is great! It's really challenging but it’s so good for flexibility and core strength. I tried it this week and I'm totally hooked. Have you ever thought about trying it out? Actually, yeah! I've seen some of the videos online and it looks like it could really benefit my routine. I just haven't had the guts to join in. Honestly, I used to be just as lazy. But then, just like you, I started saying I’ll do it tomorrow, next week, whenever... Then I finally just signed up. And it was definitely a good call. It's funny you say that because that was my exact thought process too! Maybe we could go together next time? I could use the motivation That sounds amazing! Perfect, I'll send you the details. What's your schedule? Maybe we can fix it on a day that works for both of us. I'm pretty flexible this weekend except maybe Saturday afternoon. We could do Friday evening? It sets up the weekend right? Perfect, I'm free on Friday. Let's meet at 6 pm at the gym. Sounds good, 6 pm it is. I'll book the class for us both then. Great! That's settled then. How about your holiday plans? [Laughs] Just got back from a weekend trip to Brighton with some friends. It was so much fun, we just relaxed on the beach, went for walks along the pier, and tried out a lot of good food. Ah, I've always wanted to visit Brighton but never got around to it. That sounds like a perfect weekend! Yeah, it’s a gorgeous place. Definitely recommend it. I'm sure you're right. I should start planning something soon. Anywhere in particular you want to visit this year? Me? I want to go to Ibiza, and this time I don’t want it to be a quick few days. I’m thinking maybe a whole week or more. There’s a little retreat I found where you can do yoga, meditation, and swim. Totally healthy vibes. That sounds incredible!

Ah, I hear you've seen some of the latest developments regarding bollards in our area. I've been meaning to take a closer look. Have they finalized the plan to add more around the main road? Yes, they did. Apparently the local council has decided to install a number of additional bollards along the highway. It's part of a new safety initiative to reduce the speed of traffic and make the road safer for pedestrians. I'm not sure if I agree with the aesthetics of it, mind you. I think it could be a good idea in theory, but it'll crowd the already narrow footpath. Plus, there's already a speed limit enforced in that area, so I wonder if this really addresses the root of the problem. Indeed. I noticed the same concern when I attended a recent public meeting about it. They presented diagrams and all that, but I still feel it's a superficial fix. True. Maybe they should focus on creative speed reduction measures like speed ramps instead? That might be more effective. And it would save the visual appeal of the street. So true. But it's the bureaucrats for you. Schemes and measures that sound good on paper, but may not have enough practical sense. Exactly. Reminds me of the French system; they often over-engineer solutions. I met some French people last year at a conference in France and they explained similar issues over there with their bureaucratic processes. Oh, really? I've always been curious about the bureaucratic chaos in France compared to the British system. We have our own share of red tape, of course, but it doesn't come close to what I've heard about France. No, it's a different beast altogether. During my time in Paris, I dealt with a lot less paperwork to set up my business than I would here, but the process of getting anything done took so much longer due to endless layers of bureaucratic approvals. It was bizarre but intriguing. Fascinating! I'd love to hear more. You've always been good with making connections anywhere you go. Well, let me tell you, the French people I met were often quite frank about it. They'd complain about the red tape, but they also seemed to have a way of finding ways around it. That's interesting. I suppose it's similar to how we deal with the new landlord around here who seems to be stalling on any form of dialogue.

Yo, lads, check out this dumpling! It's so juicy and delicious. You guys have tried it before? Yeah, talked about it before. Got some garlic chili sauce on it, right? Yeah, that’s the way to do it. Makes it even better. But have you tried the beef noodles here? They’re legit too. Oh, I've never had them. But now I’m definitely intrigued! True. You should try. You'll probably be hooked! I heard about a new superhero comic just came out today. It's supposedly really good. Which one? Is it about the Avengers or something else? No, it’s a new series. They’re called the "London Legends." It's about four kids from different parts of London who get powers after touching an ancient artifact. That actually sounds cool! Did you grab it from the comic book shop on High Street? No, I saw it online. I'm thinking about ordering it on my tablet. Anyone else interested? Honestly, I missed the last chapter of the Spider-Man series. I need to catch up before this new one comes out. Same here. Though I’ve heard the first issue was pretty good reviews already. Yeah, I’m expecting good things from it. But isn’t it weird how all superhero series seem to be following a similar plot lately? Shows about normal kids becoming superheroes? Yeah, I think that's a popular concept because it's easy to relate to. Everyone wants to think they could be a hero, right? That's true. Seems like the writers are tapping into that collective fantasy. For sure. Speaking of fantasies, anyone remember when we tried to make our own superhero cartoons back in primary school? Ha! I actually still have the drawings somewhere. We were making this series called "The Slough Guardians." I remember! Our heroes used to fight off menacing rhubarb attacks, or something ridiculous like that. It was so much fun. We thought we were the real deal. Now we're just students worrying about exams and real-world stuff. Clearly, those were simpler times. True. Though exams aren’t that bad. Especially if you're thinking about something outside of school during them. True that. But I’m more worried about the diet thing... I’ve been trying to eat better for some reason. Like what? Going vegetarian or something? No, just trying to eat less junk and actually cook sometimes.

Well, haven't talked about this for ages, but I've been meaning to clear out some of these old things. It feels like I’ve been hoarding a lifetime of trinkets and memories. Absolutely, cleaning out isn’t just about getting rid of old stuff, it’s about sorting out what’s really valuable to us, right? I swear, every time I help a student organize their study space, it's such a revelation. It's amazing how much you forget you have when your space is cluttered. Speaking of valuable, I didn’t know you used to be so into computers, Grandma . That old laptop is still working? For a time, this was cutting-edge tech, certainly. Now it's just a relic. But the sentiment, oh the fun I had with that thing! You know, teaching myself to program and all. It was a real journey. Fascinating. Shows how technology evolves and how we can't help but hold onto pieces of our past, don't we? Just like the way we associate different items with memories and moments. Yes, and it's so relevant to what we’re doing here today, right? Clearing out a house isn't just physical, it’s emotional as well. You're making space for new experiences and memories. Speaking of which, have you all thought about what to do with everything you’re getting rid of? Well, I thought some for charity, some for family. But I know it’s not just what, but also how we do it. I've heard about these new retail schemes where they’ll even come to your house and deal with the clearing out. Must be something almost too convenient, ha? Yeah, and they’ll even deal with the branding! We've learned all about branding at school, you know, making everything look special when it’s new again for resale. But I suppose it’s not just about selling... True, it’s the thought, the intention behind it. It’s like a form of storytelling, isn’t it? Storytelling is at the heart of all this, isn't it? The old, successful brands still do it best, like Burberry or John Lewis. We can learn something from how they handle legacy and branding amidst changes. I wish I could've seen a time when technology was advancing so fast! In my day, you'd buy something new and it would last.

Yo, so I'm really stressed about choosing my GCSE options. I have no idea what to pick and GCSEs seem so daunting. Have you decided what you're doing yet? I still can't decide either! But I heard that now, the system’s changed a bit – do you have any preferred subjects or jobs you want to consider later? I like history and English, but I’m not sure about science right now. And job-wise I'd love to be a journalist or a teacher. But even if I want to be a journalist, would history and English be enough? Do we need to pick more 'practical' subjects? Honestly, I’ve been questioning that too. I was thinking of just trying out a bit of everything, but then I read that some subjects can be useful in particular careers - like science for med school or maths for engineering. Exactly! It feels like whatever I choose could affect paths I might want to take in the future. But it’s hard to know what I want to do in the future. Sometimes I feel like I might want to be a youtuber! But that seems so... uncertain. A youtuber is definitely a different kind of job, but if that’s what you enjoy, there's no reason not to try. It’s more about finding something you love to do, isn’t it? They can do whatever they want on their channel. Like, my favorite youtuber, Vlogbrothers, isn't in school any more really - they're making life vlogs about science and all sorts. And there’s so many famous youtubers who started young… Yeah, and now they're doing huge things! It's kind of inspiring. But, if I’m honest, I’ve also seen less fortunate side of that, where some people feel a lot of pressure. That’s true, but it's like another job - it's all about being good at it and making it work. There must be technical skills too, right? Definitely. You'd have to be good at video editing, understanding of marketing, and some are also musicians or play an instrument like you and your clarinet. Oh, speaking of which, practicing the clarinet has been a great escape for me. It's something I enjoy and could even maybe use in the future, like if I wanted to join the school band or music lessons later.

Ah, so many topics we've got to cover. Wildlife, history, software, cars. Should we start with what's most immediate to our area, perhaps? Right, wildlife seems to be the most pressing, given the recent sightings of ospreys and peregrine falcons around here. That's right, I saw the big bird catching a fish right outside my window the other day. Just awesome. And it's not uncommon here now due to all the conservation efforts in the area. I heard about the wildlife park near here, too. I used to take the grandkids there. It must be quite a bit different now. Ah, yes, the Wildlife Trust did well to develop that park. It's wonderful for educational purposes, too. Speaking of education... how about switching gears? What are your thoughts on recent history? I've been following this new book on the history of the English Industrial Revolution. It's fascinating. Oh, certainly. I'm no expert but that period has always piqued my interest. The photographs alone in the book are beyond compare. I also used to walk through Norwich's streets and see some of the old mills – remnants of the industrial past. Fascinating to think about how much things have changed. And now it's all about silicon and all that, isn't it? Technology is a big topic for us doesn't it? Oh, absolutely. I've been following some of the latest design trends in software development. The future of coding is changing so fast, it's hard to keep up! Speaking of which, I tried to help my son with his coding project but... I struggled. I remember when it was all about changing the color of text on screen. Oh, yes, that seems like ancient history now. But software has changed so much, just like when I used to work as a civil engineer. I couldn't even imagine the tools available now. Did you use to use MS-DOS back in the day? Oh, I did. And I came a long way with things like AutoCAD before I retired. Still, thinking back, it's amazing just how far we've come. I know what this feels like. I used to do all the bookkeeping for my childcare business manually. Now, everything is just a tap away. By the way, how's your son finding the new coding environment? Is he enjoying it, or is there a steep learning curve?

Ah, did I ever tell you about when I was at school? It was a right ruckus every time we had the holidays coming up. You wouldn’t believe the escape plans we’d cook up. Oh, yes, I remember when holidays were something to look forward to. Going over to the sea house for the summer and hearing the waves while I was tucked up in bed. And the school trips... I had a few trips to the countryside for my school when I was younger. Learning loads and it was always something to look forward to. You know, I thought I heard about a tractor at St Mary's, but I never really believed it until I actually saw it out with the students in the garden. They had a lovely little vegetable garden there, from what I remember. I suppose times were different then. Nowadays everything is so strict and safe, I suppose that’s a good thing though. Absolutely, it’s all health and safety these days. I recall this one time when I was teaching, we had a kid climbing the wrong tree in the playground. Had to call in the health and safety officer! Still, I reckon fun should be factored in. You need some of that to make learning more enjoyable. Speaking of fun... have you noticed how the TV’s been full of programs about people cleaning up their homes lately? I find it rather bizarre. Like a new kind of binge-watching – binge cleaning. That's right, "Tidying up with Marie Kondo"… it's like it's the new Netflix for some people. Yes, I saw it. But the problem is, no one shares their wardrobe like that. I tried, mind. Cleaned mine out once. Grabbed a bin bag and started throwing in all the old things. Found out I had too much of what I didn’t need but nothing I wanted to wear. Reminds me of a joke I heard. What's the problem with people’s wardrobes and government today? Too much structure, too little style! All three laugh. Speaking of little, have either of you had those new deliverymen? They pop up at your door with all the care in the world and say "Hello. I'm here for your delivery." Oh, yes! “In order to keep your safety, please sign here.” It’s like they’re dealing with nuclear waste...

I've never seen Cambridge so white! We've got enough snow today to make a decent snowman. It's the first proper snow we've had in ages here. I was thinking we could build a snowman in the garden. How about that? Oh, definitely! It would make a lovely photo opportunity. But let's not forget our gardening chores, as soon as this snow melts. Our garden is looking a bit neglected during these winters. Totally agreed. We'll need to do some spring preparations. I was thinking we could have a 'gardening day' soon, and I can invite our friends from grad school. That would be fun! I read that the best time for pruning is during the dormant season. We could tackle that. And have you seen those beautiful flower bulbs they have at The Garden Centre on Hills Road? I have. They have such pretty choices. And it would be a perfect excuse to get out of the house and do something productive. We could make it a fun day! Perhaps we can have a little party after gardening - with friends. You know, a mini Come Dine With Me. You're ambitious, aren't you? But I love it. We could all bring a course and have a nice little evening in. A bit like those dinners on TV. Exactly! And it's a great way to get all our friends together. Plus, maybe we could plan a bigger holiday in the spring or summer. Oh, that reminds me. Have you and our friends planned any big trips yet? We should start planning soon. More or less. We were thinking about the Greek Isles. The weather is usually so lovely in May and June, and it's still not too crowded. Of course, that's if budget permits. We could always make it an eco-friendly trip and try camping. I’ve heard great things about Corfu – it’s stunning and eco-friendly. That’s an interesting idea, but camping... I mean, I’m not sure if that’s for me! You used to love camping when you were younger. Oh, we camped extensively when I was a uni. I liked it until our tent leaked and it rained every night. I suppose we could compromise. How about... a holiday home? Somewhere we can relax, garden together if we want, and still have access to the beach or the countryside?

Ah, this homemade roast beef's as tender as ever. You know, I was lucky enough to grow up in the countryside where our parents talked about proper cooking the whole time. Made me love traditional Norfolk dishes. That's lovely to hear, Uncle John. I've always been interested in the cultural and historical aspects of food and how it shapes identity and community. And, of course, regionally, there's nothing quite like a good old roast dinner to bring family and friends together. Right, let me just try my beef before we dive into those deep culinary discussions. Your mum's cooking is still top-notch, Beth. Indeed, she's the best. But seriously, John, your stories about home are always making me nostalgic. Even though your life has had its challenges, the simple joys are what you always seem to appreciate the most. Ah, well, bless you, love. It's funny, growing up, I never thought I'd end up never working a 'proper job'. Things just didn't pan out for me, you know? But being able to enjoy a good dinner like this, surrounded by people I care about, makes up for everything. It's interesting, John. I've been focusing on workforce development at university. It's fascinating how socio-economic status and education can determine life outcomes, perhaps even more so now than it used to. But isn't it remarkable how, really, everyone here is connected through the love of good food and company? Food is definitely a universal language. And the way we enjoy it says so much about us. I think that's part of what I find so stimulating about cultural studies— the way we shape and reflect the world through our preferences, rituals, and what we eat. Well, let me tell you, even with my own job history being less conventional, looking after kids, it was all about providing for them. You know, sure, there was the day-to-day routine, but it was a different kind of fulfillment. I suppose in its way, it’s like providing a meal—it's about nourishment, isn’t it? That’s it! You got it spot on, dear. It’s about the nourishment. And this roast beef is just the ticket. I couldn’t agree more. Speaking of which, what do you make of all these new diet trends and changes in food culture?

Oh, Dad, this dinner was just fantastic as always. Mum's cooking never disappoints. Yeah, talked about her chicken roasted just right. You two really need to share the recipe with us. It’s just perfect. You both are just so lucky to have a house where everyone comes together and enjoys food like this. It's not just about the food, though – it's about the company, and I'm grateful to be part of it. Absolutely, it’s always a treat. You know, it's funny, during studies for my post-grad, I had to learn all about the importance of having a fulfilling social life connected to your diet. It just makes me appreciate even more what we're doing tonight. Well, let’s hope that knowledge doesn’t go to waste when you’re living on your own, eh? Don’t worry, I won't be living on just salad for dinner. But seriously, it’s so wholesome to have everyone together like this. For me, it's the stories that make it all round out. Your grandad always has a fascinating story or two. You’re lucky to have him while he can still share them. Speaking of which, I heard stories about the old bakery where he used to work. Oh, really? I never knew about that. What was that like? Oh, it was hard work but rewarding. I saw the world through the bakeries, it was a different time. Actually, that kind of makes me want to explore more of these old traditions. We could look into doing some baking classes together. I'd love that! Maybe we can even do some family workshops here or at my house. As long as you'll make sure to add proper amounts of flour. Everyone laughs No danger there. I remember when you used to try to help Mum in the kitchen and always overdid the sugar. Oh, and don’t even get me started on the almost disaster of the Christmas puddings. Ah, that came out just right in the end, right? It was more adventure than disaster. Definitely a memorable moment. Speaking of adventures, any hobbies or interests you've taken up since retirement, Grandad? Well, I've always loved gardening, so that's how I keep myself busy. Though, mostly keep trying to advise Mrs. Robinson outside who never listens much. I do the same with my parents.

So, I've been going over some of the latest teaching strategies I've seen online and today's modern students are really into interactive education. They want to feel engaged, not talked at. Makes me wonder if we could create an app that virtually brings the classroom to life. A bit like those viral videos, but with educational value. Oh, that could work really well! But how would you ensure the quality and accuracy of the content? I mean, I'm all for using technology, but I've seen some really poor stuff out there. Right, authenticity and reliability are key. We could have a curated platform, monitored by educators. Sort of like a hybrid of YouTube and Khan Academy. The best part is, we could make it dynamic—students could create and share their own content, making it a collaborative learning experience. And the best of those could even get featured! And what about the tech side of things? I'm not a tech expert, but I understand this kind of platform could be quite complex to develop and maintain. Absolutely, there are potential technical hurdles. But for starters, we could leverage existing or open-source platforms. Or maybe we look into this new tech on the block—AI-powered learning tools. They're promising a lot in terms of personalization and engagement. Personalization is fascinating. It’s like the secret sauce for modern learning. I also really like the idea of students creating content. It could actually keep them accountable and invested in their own learning. Exactly! And it'd be a unique selling point—a really active, student-centered platform. Alright, but let’s not forget about the "viral" part. How do we make sure it gets noticed and used? Well, content quality is a must but so is marketing. We'd need to do some research on how these platforms go viral—is it through partnerships, social media campaigns, or events? We could look into getting professors or famous educators to endorse and personally contribute. It's a great credibility booster and it could generate buzz. Plus, if we make it free or low-cost for students, they’re more likely to use it. We could make the revenue model based on universities or schools for premium features like analytics or customization. I love how you think about the business side! The key would be finding the right balance between appealing to the students and institutions.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my Halloween party plans? I still can't believe you didn't attend! Honestly, I had a long shift at the hospital and had to miss it. I’m so sorry though! But tell me, how did it go? It was amazing, totally hit the theme of a "Pumpkin Patch" and we even had this wicked spooky DJ. That sounds fantastic! And how was work keeps coming up? You know how it is in healthcare, right? Oh, you have no idea – it’s been chaotic, just like always. I’ve been working on managing a project with a tight deadline and it’s been a nightmare. I feel you – project management can be a challenge. And what about your weekend? Any quiet plans? Not really, thought I might go check out some of those English counties we used to talk about? Maybe visit Kent or Sussex. You ever been? I’d love to, actually never gotten a chance. They say the castles are really something there. Totally, especially Hever Castle. I’ve been meaning to paint it, the way the pictures look. Speaking of plans, have you started thinking about your five-year plan? You know, beyond the project you're working on? A bit, but honestly, it's all so vague right now. I guess I want to keep advancing in my career, maybe get a PMP certification. You working on any goals? Yeah, well, it's tough in mental health nursing but I kind of see my next step as specializing in trauma counseling. We really need more people trained for that, you know? That’s a great ambition, and so much-needed. Do you think our job roles affect how we think about goals and future plans? Definitely, and honestly, it keeps me grounded. Every day, I see how my work impacts people’s lives, so I’m motivated to do more – make that real difference for people. That’s inspiring. Sometimes, my job seems so different – but I guess we all have our way of making an impact. True. Alright, enough about work and futures. What’s for dinner? Just thought I’d cook a bit of a traditional Sunday roast. How does that sound? Sounds perfect. You know how Sundays feel empty without a good roast. Exactly! And don’t you think we should also plan a DIY Halloween feast next year?

Right, so I was going over some of the old family photos the other day and found this one of your mum when she was younger. Ah, that must have been from when she was a student in Oxford. She really loved her time there. That's right! She used to talk about her time at university and how it was one of the best experiences of her life. And, funnily enough, she said you remind me very much of her at that age. Oh, that keeps coming up. She always tells me how much I'm like her. She says, "Not just you look like her, but you think like her too." Well, that's lovely. She's just trying to make you feel good. I guess she can't help making me blush, even from across the decades. It's just family love. Now, let's talk about something else. What have you been up to lately at work? Lots of deadlines. I've been trying to get the new production schedule in order before the upcoming festival. It's quite challenging but it's good experience. I'm sure it is. I assumed that while the pressure must be intense, the satisfaction of seeing the production come together must make it all worthwhile. It does. Well, most of the time at least. A few weeks ago, we had this major hiccup where one of the key venues backed out at the last minute. That must have been stressful. How did you handle that? We had to scramble for a last-minute replacement. Luckily, we managed to find an alternative, but it's just one of those things that keeps you on your toes. I can imagine, and I'm sure it’s not easy dealing with stress. You're lucky to be so young and able to handle it all. It isn't always easy but changing the venue ended up working out for the best. The new venue was actually better suited for the size of the audience we're expecting. That’s wonderful! A little bit of luck in bad times, indeed. And have you had some time to look into holiday plans this year? Ah, holiday plans... I was thinking of maybe spending some time in Scotland. The Highlands have been calling. I've always loved the idea of just driving and seeing everything by car.

Yo, how's studying going over here? Thought you'd be banging your head against a wall with these GCSEs. Oh, it's alright, not too bad. Mostly just been doing a bit of revising for my A-levels, but I have a drama exam coming up soon, so that's been stressing me out a bit. But besides that, it's quite chilled. You seem to be handling the French pretty well, right? Erm, yeah, it's alright. Starts to make more sense once you get used to it. But sometimes I just blurt out English, then realize I spoke in English while everyone here is waiting for the translation. Heh, that's been embarrassing a few times. Haha, that happens to me in English places when I mix in a bit of old Cambridge slang. They gave me some weird looks too. But speaking of Cambridge... how's your new flatmate? The girl you met last month? You told me her name started with an 'A', right? Yeah, it was Alice? I met this really interesting person and we had some great conversations but she's been kinda busy lately because of her extra-curricular activities. I haven't seen her much lately. Oh, that's a bit of a shame. I remember you were saying she was into theatre or something like that? Aye, she's part of this drama group and does her own musical stuff on the side. Talented too, always finds time to practice her singing and stuff. Wow, impressive! Does she do any gigs around the university? Actually, she has one coming up in a couple of weeks. I think the venue is near Place du Marché, if you're interested. Seriously? That's quite a central location. I think I will definitely try and make it. Great! It'll be a fun evening for sure. Definitely. So, what’s your situation with your coursework? Actually, it's alright. Just had to run through some scientific method revision because we've got a test on that next week. Again, it's one of those things that makes almost too much sense once you read over the notes a few times. Do you reckon there are any translation apps or tools that could help us with our French? I've been using one called "Duolingo" for practice. It's pretty helpful for... well, for any language study, I suppose.

Ah, I can't believe what happened yesterday at work! I almost had a heart attack. You know how I have this huge fear of spiders? Oh, yeah, I remember. You're quite the fainter around creepy crawlies! It isn't a joke! But, anyway, I was about to make a presentation to our biggest client and then, this...this monstrous spider just... I mean, it was huge and it suddenly appeared right behind me on the screen! I can't even begin to imagine. So, how did you react? Well, I first just froze. Then I did what any normal person would do - I screamed and panicked. Everyone in the room was shocked but started following me around trying to "help". LOL. They were all trying to find this spider but of course, it had already gone off into some dark corner. That must have been quite a sight! Did the client notice anything? Well, fortunately, they never even saw it. They were all so caught up in the presentation that they only noticed my weird behavior but didn't see why. Honestly, I just changed the slide and pretended nothing happened. Phew, that was lucky. I also really don't like spiders, by the way. One time, I was cleaning a nice old lady's house and I came across, like, a whole family of mice in her kitchen cupboards. She had no idea! No way! That sounds like a real ordeal. Oh, that was quite the ordeal. I had to call in extra help and pest control just to clean things up. I can imagine.
