I just tried to relax and focused on keeping a casual tone throughout the rest of the meeting. Yes, that's probably the best way to handle it. You know, it's interesting though - we often take certain things for granted. Like birds, for instance. I've always been fascinated by them but I've never paid much attention to them. Birds? What about them? Well, the other day, while I was out for a walk, I noticed this one bird just sitting on a fence and singing this beautiful song. It was complete freedom and joy, you know? It just got me thinking about the stress we all carry around. That's a beautiful way to describe it. Sometimes I get that too, while I'm cleaning. There's something so peaceful about the quietness and the outside-world sounds.

Ah, I can't believe we're finally getting to meet each other properly. I've heard so much about you from my sister, Rachel. It sounds like you two had talked quite a bit over tea and cake on many visits. Indeed we have! I remember those afternoons very fondly. Both of us sharing stories and catching up on each other's lives. She's always been quite the storyteller, isn't she? She certainly is! I think she's set quite high hopes for us rebuilding our family connection. She wanted me to let you know how much she truly admired seeing your passion for teaching even in retirement. Oh, thank you, that's very kind of your sister. It just felt right to share my knowledge with others, you know? And retirement gave me the chance to focus on my own family’s history. Ah, you have such a rich family history, I understand. Coming from Welsh roots, I can only imagine how fascinating the stories are. Oh, it's quite the journey. There’s so much to share, from the coal mining industry to the development of the railroads in Wales. One side of my family even has a connection to the famous Welsh poet, Dylan Thomas. That's incredible! I've always loved Dylan Thomas’s work. Especially "Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night." It's so powerful and moving. Yes, yes it is. His influence has had a lasting impact on the literary landscape of Wales, really. But I never thought we'd have such a personal connection. Absolutely. Speaking of connections… would you like a cup of tea before we dive deeper? I've got some lovely English breakfast tea and some coffee, if you prefer. Oh, that would be lovely, thank you. A cup of tea, please. Here you are. Mmm, it's very good. I'm so glad. So, how's your life in Stevenage? No plans for any more teaching or perhaps some local activities? Well, my days are quite peaceful now. I've been focusing on genealogy and community work. However, it's been great strengthening the family tree. I've discovered many fascinating ancestors, some of which were quite... adventurous! Fascinating! I enjoy that side of things too. I've been helping out with our family history, especially after my mother's passing. She left such a detailed book of our family history, but there were some gaps...

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we went hot air ballooning over Bristol? You told me, but that was years ago. Are you still as excited about it as you were back then? Absolutely! It was just so surreal, floating over the city and watching people down below going about their day like ants. And the dogs, don't forget about the dogs! Right, the dogs. That was our hot air balloon's mascot, wasn't it? Yeah, and I swear that dog looked like it had just as much fun as we did. Speaking of dogs, I've been thinking about getting one. You know how much I adore wildlife? I think it would be great to have a dog with me on my walks out here. Is that a good idea? Dogs can be a lot of responsibility and we're not really in a place that's conducive to having a dog. We're often out on the road, teaching, or at home. You're right, we do travel a lot. But don't worry, I was thinking more about a dog that's also suitable for the outdoors. A breed that's good for wildlife walks, camping, stuff like that. Ah, now I see where you're coming from. You're thinking about life in general here, not just about the immediate future. Exactly! Plus, it's not just about the dog. I kind of see it as our next adventure. We could take turns walking or camping together with the dog. I like the spirit of that idea. But let's think about the practicalities for a bit. Dogs can be quite expensive, especially if they get sick or need special care. Right, sure. I was thinking we could plan financially for that, though. We make a comfortable income for our higher professional occupations, so I don't see it as a real obstacle. True, we are well-off. Also, let's not forget, this countryside is just teeming with wildlife. The walks would be amazing. I was reading about the local wildlife. Did you know Norfolk has one of the highest concentrations of barn owl populations in the country? I didn't know that. That's...kind of cool. Yeah! And we're right in the middle of it here. I could take the dog out every day to see these things. It’s also worth considering that if we get a high-energy dog that we might need to be out here more often, or at least take turns walking if we both have a busy schedule.

Ah, I thought it was overcast today but then it cleared up. It's been a bit of a mixed bag, weather-wise, hasn't it? Definitely, down in Yorkshire we're still waiting for the cloud to clear. Still, now that the days are getting a bit longer, it's a welcome change. You'd think the longer days would bring more sunshine, but it seems the UK has a mind of its own when it comes to weather. It's always unpredictable! keeps it interesting, I suppose. Back to work, how's teaching English to non-native speakers been treating you? It must be challenging yet rewarding at the same time. It is! I've just finished a course with a group of students from various countries. Their motivation and efforts are always inspiring. It's wonderful to see the language barriers fading away bit by bit. That's great to hear. I've been trying to learn French, but it seems like a mountain to climb. I find it rewarding too, but it's often a battle. I completely understand! It's not easy. I think the key is finding interesting and engaging ways to learn. For example, using different media types like films, podcasts, or even books in the target language. I tried reading a French novel last week, but it was a grind. Maybe I just need to start with simpler texts. A good start would be finding books or materials you're interested in. For example, if you're into cooking, buy a French cookbook or if you're into history, try a historical analysis in French. True, I didn't think of tailoring the content to my interests. I've been reading more historical books lately, so maybe that's the way to go. Exactly, and of course, practice makes it perfect! Listen to French music, watch French movies, even try to have brief conversations with native speakers. That's a great idea. You know, my gym has a diverse clientele, and one of our advanced trainers is French. Maybe I can ask him for some tips. Perfect, take advantage of local resources. It always helps to have a native speaker to guide you or correct your pronunciation. Speaking of resources, my gym almost doubled in membership this year. We've had to hire a lot more staff and deal with increased expectations from members.

Alright, Dad, Grace, today we're discussing how to sort out the garden and perhaps the house a bit. It's been a bit of a downer since Mum passed away, you know. Ah, yes, it’s changed things around a bit, hasn’t it? But I suppose that's life. What’s your thoughts, Grace? Erm, well, it’s just that the garden looks a bit... untidy, and it seems like it could do with some weeding, and perhaps a bit of renovation in the house as well. Like, the windows need cleaning, and maybe some new curtains. Right, right, I’ve been meaning to do those things. I suppose it’s a project we could all pitch in on, isn’t it? Ooh, yes, it would be good to get the whole family involved. It’s not every day we all get together like this, or even have something to work on together. We could make it a bit of a day out. Yeah, and we could even have a little picnic afterwards. Like we used to do when the kids were young. That sounds like fun! Can we do that? Absolutely, we definitely can. But first, let's make a list of all the things we need and want to do. First, the garden doesn’t need much - just a bit of tidying and some weeding. Then, inside we could start with the windows and curtains, and maybe see if there’s any other bits that could do with some fresh paint or updating. Right, I remember when your mum used to do all this. She had a real eye for making things look nice and she always made sure it was a family effort. You know, it's good to keep her memory alive through small things like this. Yes, yes, I know what you mean. She always made our home feel like a home, indeed. Can I do the garden then? I’ll weed it and could even maybe paint the shed if we need that. Oh, we definitely need to paint the shed, Grace. It looks a bit worse for wear. But we might need some supplies, so let me just get all that sorted out and we'll get started soon. We could even make it a bit of a family competition. Who can tackle the most jobs by the end of the day?

Alright, John, we'll take the A68 then we've got about 2 miles before the roundabout down by the old mill. You got the voice guide sorted? Ah, the satnav says we'd save a minute going through the town centre, but I trust you’ve got a better idea of things, as always. Well, we avoid that keeps coming up due to all the roadworks in Malton. Plus it's a bit narrow. I've driven this route thousands of times to parents’ house, dear old Darlington. So what's the plan for the weekend, then? The ceilidh at the old hall? Yeah, I've got my band's set for 8pm. You planning on staying the night after, or should we call it a night after it's finished? A ceilidh sounds lovely! Though, I’ve got a busy weekend with the final edits on my novel. I might just have to leave around 9. But I’d love to watch the first set at least. Ah nice, you'd take a walk before bed, maybe? There's this new craft brewery near the venues. Their ginger ale is fantastic. Always up for a good brew. So, is the ceilidh subject to the weather then? The forecast looks a bit iffy. At this rate, they might need to cancel. The flood watch is still in place for parts of the North East. But usually they manage to keep it going. Last year it was bonkers with the rain but people still turned up in wellies. Wellies and wellies for the ceilidh, then. Funny how a bit of rain doesn’t stop folk from enjoying themselves. You know it. This region still has the heart of the old world in it. Even the rain won’t keep folks away from music and dancing. Speaking of joys, any sense of what's new with our nephew? The last I heard, he was eyeing up university for next year? Ah, yes! He's looking into Leeds and Durham for Theatre Studies. He’s really into the drama and performing arts. Maybe we can convince him to join our school play next year. Bringing out the thespian in the family? There’s no stopping him. His parents might be finding that a challenge though. How are they holding up? I've not seen them in a while. To be honest, with this housing market and the logistics of moving him to uni... I think they're holding up all right

I've decided I need a full English. Bacon, eggs, baked beans; the works. How about you, what are you having? Mmm, I need a hearty one too. I'll have the same as you, but with extra toast. Perfect. It's been one of those weeks. Site visits, clients, and design adjustments. I've been working non-stop. I know what you mean. Speaking of keeps me busy. I just finished a project brief for a university design project we're looking at. It was quite challenging, but I'm excited about the potential. Oh, that sounds interesting! What's the project about? It's a proposed village concept for a sustainable community. We need to reduce carbon footprints and build housing solutions that are energy efficient and low cost. That's a challenging brief, but very timely. How are you planning to approach that? We've decided on a modular design that uses recycled materials and relies heavily on renewable energy sources. The goal is to keep it affordable and scalable. That’s fascinating. I think most of our clients are now looking for the 'sustainability label' in their portfolio. It’s interesting to see how we, as architects, can actually make a positive impact on the environment. Absolutely. A friend of mine, Alex, is really struggling with a project at the moment because his client is stubbornly sticking to traditional, unsustainable methods. I know what you mean… Clients sometimes don't fully understand the long-term benefits that come with sustainable design. Exactly! I was planning to have a chat with him and advise him to emphasise those benefits more clearly to the client. That's a good approach. Sometimes, it's about explicitly linking the environmentally friendly features to cost savings or increased long-term value. Yep. It's not just about making buildings 'green', but also ensuring it makes financial sense. Right. On a different note, have you seen Natalie lately? She's been quite quiet lately. Not since the last architecture meet-up. Did she say anything about what's going on? Nothing much. I just thought it was odd. She's usually so vibrant and engaging. She mentioned things being tough at work. Oh, I'll definitely reach out to her and check in. You know, it can get really overwhelming with tight deadlines and demanding clients. Exactly. If anyone understands that, it's us.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I drove through London? The traffic was absolute madness. I was doing a presentation at a conference and was so worried I'd be late. Made me realize just how much you have to expect to arrive on time and plan the drive, even with traffic – do you have any preferred routes or tips for navigating around Cambridge? That sounds like a nightmare! I’ve learned a few things of my own as a civil servant. You know, presenting and getting to places on time is very important in that line of work. I actually try to use my bike most days, but yes, for longer trips, I have to drive too. These days, I use Waze or similar apps to navigate London traffic. It’s been surprisingly reliable even with city traffic. Waze is a life-saver. And biking’s always great if you can, less stress involved, I find. It also helps with pollution and all that. What’s it like, being a civil servant these days? Everything going alright? Yeah, it's all good here. Been quite busy, especially with the new initiatives coming through. But, it’s rewarding, see the impact your work has on the community. Speaking of which, I just got back from this amazing concert the other night. They played so many good songs, and the atmosphere was fantastic. I met some nice people too. Oh, nice! I'd love to hear more about it. Was it an old band or something new? It was an indie band, Soundflower. They were pretty new, but I saw them at a local venue in Cambridge. Ah, I haven’t heard of them. Did they have any notable songs or styles? They’ve got this one tune that blends electronic and folk, really catchy. The singer’s voice is unique, really carries through the venue. That’s great! I’m actually changing the radio to that station. Ah, I think I found them! Oh, you didn’t have to do that! I know, but this way, you can introduce the real thing. You know what, I think you need to make time for some more concerts. It’s not just about work, but also these things to keep your mind fresh. We could really go to a festival or something like that. Maybe there are some coming up in the area?

So, I've been going over my resume for this media producer job application. I want to make sure it sounds right and that I've included everything they're after. That's really smart of you, I need to work on mine as well. A friend just told me that this industry is all about networking, have you heard that too? Absolutely, and I've read about making sure your cover letter links specifically to the job description. But right now, I'm a bit stuck on how to structure it. Should it be formal or informal? Right, most media jobs do expect a certain level of professionalism. But you can still show personality without being too casual. You need to strike the right balance. I like that, balance is key. Exactly! And don't forget to highlight your transferable skills, even if you haven't worked in media before. Think about how your language teaching background has given you excellent communication skills and experience in creative work. That's a great point! Maybe I can structure it like a story. Start with a strong opening that catches their attention or a hook. Like how my love for storytelling led me to study and teach languages. Then use that as a bridge to media production. That's an excellent idea! You could then talk about the skills you think are most relevant for the job - writing, video production, interview techniques, whatever. Ah, and maybe use specific examples where I could have included media-related things in the classroom or through volunteer work. Absolutely, give concrete examples and focus on what you can do for them rather than what you want. Employers love that. Makes sense. So, kind of like 'Here's what I bring to the table and how it can help your team'? More or less. Also, a bit of modesty always helps. You want to show that you're eager to learn and grow in this new field. Good tip. I've always struggled to talk about myself in my CV. You know, not bragging but also not underselling. It’s a tough art but I think practice makes perfect. Just like rehearsing for an interview. Have you thought about that? Not yet, to be honest. Should I have a few standard questions ready about the job or company? Definitely worth asking. It shows interest in the role and if you're prepared, it can show that you're thinking ahead.

So, I've been thinking a lot about changing careers, and I've been looking into starting my own business. Have you ever thought about doing something similar? Actually, I have. As a teacher, I love my work with students, but I've always had this side passion for cooking and food – specifically, creating unique food products. I've been thinking about starting a small business creating and selling those products, but I'm not quite sure how to get started. That sounds like a fantastic idea. You've got a great combination of skills there, teaching and baking. You could really leverage your experience to build something truly unique. Exactly! However, the logistics of starting a business, especially here in Australia where you've got to deal with a whole new set of regulations and market, is daunting. What was your experience when you decided to transition into entrepreneurship? It was quite challenging, to be honest. My background is in finance, but I always had an interest in tech. So, I started a small tech consulting firm. The biggest hurdle for me was probably understanding the business side of things – the paperwork, accounting, and so on. But the most valuable advice I can give is to start small, see what works and what doesn't, and then scale up. That makes sense. What about the financial side? How did you manage the initial costs to get started? I used a combination of savings and a small loan from a bank. The initial costs were manageable as I started small. But the tricky part was in estimating the costs really. You have to account for so many things and it’s almost impossible to predict some of the expenses until you’re actually in it. True, and the loan part is something I'm really worried about. You also mentioned accounting, which I'm not very comfortable with. Well, there are a few options. You could, for instance, hire an accountant or use online tools. Services like Xero or Quickbooks can help you keep track of your finances, and they're pretty user-friendly. While you’re dealing with the business side, you can save on accounting costs initially. That does make things sound a bit more manageable. Have you also considered the marketing side? As a small business starting from scratch, it's hard to get noticed. Marketing is a challenge, for sure.

I've decided I need to lose some weight. I've been hearing so much about this paleo diet and Mediterranean diet. Have any of you tried them? You know, Emma, I think the best diet is the one you stick to, regardless of what it's called. Absolutely, and it's important to get into a healthy routine. I wish I had more time to focus on diet when I was working. All those publishing parties and book signings didn't exactly lend themselves to healthy eating. Yes, I can imagine! What do you think, little one? Are you going to grow up with a beard just like your Dad is trying to grow? No! I want to be a superhero! The joys of parenting! Speaking of parenting, I just saw an article on how it's becoming harder to find good schools in the area due to the housing shortage. It's not just the schools that are full, it's the whole city. I've noticed that too. It seems like everyone is looking to move to Cambridge. I've even seen entire families moving here just for the schools. It's really affecting the local community. Can we play video games instead of talking about this, Mummy? Not until you finish your dinner, sweetie. It's quite a concern, doesn't it? My sister had the same problem finding the right school for her kids. I've heard of one solution being to have the school run less like traditional schools and more like those in Poland. They seem to handle overcrowding much better. Really? That's interesting. Do you think that's something that could be implemented here? Perhaps. But the key issue in Cambridge seems to be the lack of housing for teachers and families. Without teachers, schools can't function, and without housing for those families, it's just a vicious cycle. Absolutely, we have a real dichotomy here. We're attracting so many immigrants and foreign workers, yet we can't accommodate everyone. The cultural impact is being felt, particularly in education and health services. Do they bring noodles to school? I hope so! Diversity in diets and culture is good for schools, but we do need to make sure there’s capacity for everyone. Exactly, it's a challenge we need to address. I've recently been volunteering at a literacy program, and many of the young mothers are worried about their children's future, given the state of the schools.

Oh, Brenda, I haven’t seen you in ages! How are the kids these days? How's Joe getting on with his Sixthform? He's doing well, thanks for asking. There have been some bumps, but it's all part of growing up, isn’t it? Especially with this new course he's taken on. It's something to do with computing, but I haven't quite figured it out yet. But I have no idea how I'd manage to deal with it myself. Are you still working at Sainsbury’s? I always find it fascinating, those new car park passes. I heard about the confusion earlier this year, did it affect you at all? It did, but thankfully, most customers were understanding. It was more of a headache for us staff than the shoppers. What about that referendum stuff? What do you think now? I remember we had the big discussion last time we met, was it two years ago now? Honestly, it's all still a bit of a mess, isn’t it? I still find myself wondering what could have been. We've seen it affect everything from business to local events here in Fradley. Even the little ones are affected because of the funding changes. That's the worst part, isn’t it? Politics seems to infiltrate every aspect of our lives now. Have you seen the new community centre? They've decided to redo the space for more events. Hopefully, it'll bring more activities and prevent it from falling into decline. I'm glad they're doing something about that. These small events are what keep us connected in the community. I went to the farmers’ market last week and it was lovely. Except, I couldn’t find the time to play the piano since the baby came. Seems like the whole world went together with her. You were always getting jittery about losing your piano practice before that! But babies are great, aren't they? They bring a new rhythm to life. You'll catch up soon enough. I hope so. I do find some moments to sit down these days. But I have to say, when I do manage to play, it's quite therapeutic. Reminds me of when we’d catch up over a show at the BWM. Did you go to the new display at the art gallery? Actually, yes!

Ah, I've been meaning to talk to you about social media's impact on my job. It's been quite a challenge balancing personal use and professional use. Do you find yourself using Twitter for professional purposes at all as Director of Studies? Aye, I do. It's a great tool for sharing questions students might have outside of class, or sometimes I use it to promote upcoming events at the university or share student successes. It's also where I get most of my professional news, you know? All the influential scholars and educators are active on Twitter. Absolutely. That's exactly how I use it too, although, I admit to sometimes getting lazy about keeping up with all the threads. But professionally, I've been using it a lot more to promote the PR campaigns my company is working on. Right, but do you feel like that affects your personal life? Definitely. Sometimes I find myself thinking about a promotional angle or buzzword for a project while I’m out with friends or family. It’s like the lines blur a bit, you know? Mhm. I can understand that. I find the opposite though. It helps me stay connected with this side of my life, see what people are saying, even if it’s not strictly professional. Plus, fun fact: Twitter’s also the best tool for seeing some of the most awkwardly humorous university student responses to things. Well, that’s certainly a bonus! Do you use Twitter as a way to engage with students, or rather to provide a platform for them? A bit of both. It’s a good way to give and receive quick feedback. I don’t tweet doesn’t come across as formal as email, so I think it’s easier for students to reach out or ask general questions without feeling too formal. That makes sense. Seems like the flexibility is part of its appeal. I also use it for networking with peers. Do you ever find yourself losing track of who you’re connecting with online and personally? It's quite strange, suddenly seeing someone you’ve followed online meet you in person for the first time. Definitely. It's happened to me a few times. But it's also opened up some new professional relationships. For instance, I’ve met several co-authors through Twitter. It’s one of the most efficient ways to network, if you ask me.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that awkward situation I had today at work? Not yet, but you must have something funny to share then, right? Oh yes, very funny. We had this meeting with some new clients and I was so nervous that I accidentally got them all the wrong proposals out of the drawer. Oh no, that's pretty awkward. How did they react? They were very understanding, thankfully. They laughed about it too and it actually ended up breaking the ice a bit. Well that's a relief then. Accidents happen to the best of us. Exactly. But seriously though, have you had a busy weekend? It's been quite hectic. Long shifts at the hospital, then having to deal with some very emotional patients. Oh, I can imagine. How was it for you? A bit draining. Some patients can really keep you on your toes, you know. I understand. I often feel the same way when I have to deal with difficult deadlines and clients. Maybe we can both use some pampering tonight? Some good food, perhaps a movie or something? That sounds perfect actually. I've been craving for some comfort food all day. What do you say to some homemade burgers and chips? Or would you like to try something else? That sounds like heaven. I'd love if you could make that for me. Deal. While we're at it, shall we make it a double date? Invite our other housemates over for dinner? Oh, that would be amazing! We haven't all hung out in ages. Yeah, it's a bit boring when it’s just us two in this big house. Plus, it’s always nice having company over. Definitely! I’ll text them and see if they’re free. Just be sure to tell them we're getting burgers. There's no way they'd say no. Oh, trust me. They will. You know what else we can use? A bit of laughter therapy after all that chaos today. Absolutely. I'll make sure to pick out the funniest movie we own. And I’ll get started on the burgers. You've been my favorite at cooking comfort food. Thanks! I appreciate the vote of confidence. We can make this a lovely evening, right? Absolutely. This is what I love about our relationship. We're able to have some fun despite the bad days.

Right, so I've been thinking. I don't think we should change the plans for today. ANON arrives tomorrow and we've got everything ready. I've also purchased his favourite biscuits, just like he likes them. Yes, that's lovely of you, but have we thought about what questions we need to ask his nurse about the visit? I mean, there's the whole thing about his medications and whether he should have someone watching over him at all times. Oh absolutely, that's a good point. We should get an itinerary from the nurse. Also, let's make sure everything is planned around his needs. His medical needs, I mean. Absolutely, that's been done. I've already spoken to the nurse and she's given us a whole list of things we need to do and watch out for. They even suggested we install that portable oxygen thingy in case he needs it. That's good thinking. But speaking of his needs, have we got the special diet covered? I know ANON has particular food requirements. Ah yes, ANON's diet. That's firmly in mind. We've prepared a gluten-free menu for the whole visit. And I’ve tried a few new recipes just to make sure they're all right. That's very good of you. And the meal today? I’ve made roast beef and Yorkshire puddings. Everyone loves them. Should we make sure his portion is without any... you know, no mashed potatoes or gravy or anything? Yeah, that's a good idea, and let’s see if we can make that his special treat. Maybe we can also sneak in that mint jelly he loves so much. Actually, that jogs my memory, we should make sure to bring his favourite book or DVD too. He loves his comedy videos. Right, we should. On that note, have we dealt with parking for ANON's visit? His car's quite large, I believe. I booked a spot for him down by the village centre. It’s a spot we've used before. Should be more than enough for his vehicle. Excellent, that's sorted then. Now, let’s run through the timetable again. Arrival tomorrow afternoon, 2 pm. We’ve arranged for me to be at the airport, and then we’ll bring him here for the afternoon. We can relax and have some dinner.

Ah, I hear you've been tackling Spanish recently, Alan. How have you found it so far? It's been a bit of a struggle, Sylvia. Honestly, I thought I'd pick it up quicker given my background in languages and all the free time I have now – but man, Spanish is a real humdinger! Well, my dear, that's the thing about language learning right? It never gets easier no matter how many languages you've learned. But I always say, keeps the old grey matter working. That's true, keeps me on my toes. I've been using Duolingo mostly, sticking to it day by day. But sometimes I just want to just throw the whole thing out of the window when I struggle with the conjugation! Oh, I know that feeling all too well. But have you thought about mixing your methods up a bit? Maybe some grammar books, podcasts, or even language exchange? I thought about language exchange. Someone to chat with would really help. But finding a good conversation partner is easier said than done. There're plenty of apps that could help with that. I used to recommend Duolingo, but for conversation practice, you might want to try something like Tandem or HelloTalk. Ah, good idea, thanks. Perhaps I'll try those. The grammar is perhaps where I’m struggling, especially with the subjunctive. Ah, yes, the subjunctive. That's a nightmare for many learners! But it's like anything else, practice makes perfect. Perhaps. It's just hard to get the head around when and how to use the subjunctive. I just wish there was a better way to learn it, some trick or tip. Well, remember when I was teaching EFL, we used this method called the “four questions method” to explain grammar concepts. Perhaps changing the scenario to something more relatable can help. Like, instead of saying, "When does one use the subjunctive?" Ask "Who, what, where, when, why" in a hypothetical situation. For example? For instance, “Why do you think you might need to use the subjunctive?” It’s like... if I say “I hope we don’t go to the store because it’s closed.” The part after “because” is something you wish or doubt, so you use subjunctive. I see. That makes it a bit clearer. So the subjunctive is like the “umbrella” verb when you're expressing uncertainty or wishful thinking?

Right, Dad, so I've got all these papers scattered around. We have flight tickets for the upcoming holiday, some documents that need to be scanned, and a bunch of banking stuff that needs sorting out. Right, right. Alright son, let's get this done. Which one do you want to tackle first? The documents I think. There's a form about access to my student loan, a bunch of stuff about Kelly Brook, actually, I don't know why, and then there are some for my computer course enrollment. Can we start with the loan document? Oh, right, that's important. Okay. Let me have a look. What's with the Kelly Brook documents, by the way? You're not planning a fan convention or something, are you? No, Dad! It's actually just an invitation to this corpus linguistics project. They're using her as an example because she's famously used archaic expressions. But yeah, creative... Ah, that makes sense now. You're not as strange as I thought for a moment. Maybe a bit. Anyway, about the loan. Do I just scan this and send it to the student finance website? Let me have a look. Usually, they ask you to print and sign and then scan to PDFs, right? And do you have a scanner or are we going to have to haul out the old one? There's a scanner here somewhere. I'll look for it. But can you remind me of the exact process? I know it's changed a few times over the years. Okay, it's usually just "Scan > Save as PDF > Upload to the website." But make sure you don't crop or resize it. They need it in original format. Also, you may need to use a specific type of PDF. The website usually specifies it. Ah, okay. Good to know. And for the computer course enrollment, I just need to print and sign? You usually just need to print and sign. No need for a scan, I think. Just store it someplace safe. Let's not get ahead of ourselves though. Let's just focus on this loan thing first. Right, right. The scanner's upstairs in the study, I think. I could go get it. Alright, go on. And I'll review this form while you're gone. You know, this is actually really useful work.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we drove past that petrol station and saw all those bikers lined up waiting for petrol? No, you didn't mention that. What happened? Was it a nice scene? Yeah, kind of! It was quite amusing. There must have been at least 20 of them, parked in a row, and they all looked so out of place next to those slick, sleek cars. Haha, that does sound odd. Are bikers particularly fond of that station? I don't know. But there seemed to be a few others waiting for petrol too, but I guess we only noticed the bikers. You know, like they stood out. It's actually really nice of you to notice such details. As a consultant engineer, I suppose you have to have a keen eye for observation, right? Well, I aspire to, at least. My job as a corpus administrator involves quite a bit of discerning details, between all the paperwork and meetings. But driving, especially with you, makes me feel like I have a bit more free time to observe. I understand the sentiment. Driving can be quite relaxing, while also giving you time to reflect. Have you noticed the different types of petrol stations around here, or are there any particular ones you prefer to use? Oh, definitely! Like, my favorite is the one near our hometown. It's a family-owned business, and they have the best cup of coffee and the most genuine staff. But sometimes, it's a bit of a trip from here doesn’t it? Indeed. I usually use the one near the office. It's convenient but not my favorite. We should actually explore more around the area and find better options. More local ones perhaps. You always make sense. I noticed a lot of foreigners using them, especially when they're on holiday. It’s interesting to see how they navigate different places. Yeah, and sometimes they seem lost on whether to use cash or cards… I remember my cousin was on holiday and he had to teach someone how to use a self-service pump just because it wasn’t as intuitive as back home. Right! Because some of these newer petrol stations are so automated, and unless you're used to it, they can be confusing. There's also the matter of prices. Did you see those new bicycles, or should I say motorbikes with those crazy gadgets?

Alright Timothy, are you enjoying your weekend so far? Morning, mum! Yeah, weekend is good so far. All good then? Yeah, good, how was school? School was okay. We had our history test today. How did that go, then? Not bad, just some usual struggles with dates. But I aced the essay on the importance of the Industrial Revolution in Britain though. That's great! Make sure you practice those dates, you can't wing them all the time. Now, how about your tennis lessons with Coach Howard last week? For me, it was good. He spent quite some time on my backhand volleys. I’ve been practicing, but still need to work on consistency. That's right. Remember, tennis is also about mental control and patience. It’s not just physical. And you know what, there’s a really good quote that I read from Roger Federer, and it might help. ' "The moment you doubt whether you can fly, you cease forever to be able to do it." Really? Roger Federer? That's cool. He’s one of the best for a reason. Speaking of which, your dad and I were talking last week about taking you to see one of the LTA tournaments in Birmingham next month. Oh, that would be amazing! It might be a chance to learn a few tricks too. And maybe catch an autograph if you’re lucky and timing right. Yeah, plus you could watch the real technique firsthand. Sometimes I think you’ve got to see it live to really understand the concept. That would be awesome! Funny thing... I remember when I used to play when you were a bit younger, I was actually a better volley player than me now. Seems like I should get back into it sometime. Speaking of which, I saw Andy Murray come to Birmingham last year for the tournament. I managed to get his autograph for one of your old tennis trophies. I should still have it somewhere if you want to see it. Really? That’s cool! Yeah, maybe it’s time for us to have a mixed doubles match sometime soon, just the three of us. You sure about that? Don’t forget my doubles strategy is quite... unorthodox. Oh, absolutely! And I'm equipped for it. Anyways, dinner’s ready. Let’s enjoy while it's hot. Thanks, can't wait! Enjoy your dinner, Tim.

Yo, anyone got any ideas what we could do while we watch Downton Abbey tonight? Maybe we can have a competition to see who can remember the most about the episode afterwards? You lot are always competing about something, aren't you? But I love it though, keeps things interesting. How about we do something more fun this time? Like guess who gave the worst gift in last Christmas's Secret Santa? Ah, now that’s a thought! But actually, I've always wondered, does anyone know why we never do turkey again after that weird one we had last year? It tasted like rubber. Thanksgiving's a bit of a different story, isn't it? But yeah, that's a very valid point. Maybe we should stick to just having chicken next year. No way, turkey's the classic. But maybe we can experiment with different recipes. And what about your famous stuffing? It's always so tasty. Ah, my stuffing? You mean the one with the secret ingredient? That's a family recipe. And it's actually not secret. It’s just a few extra herbs and love. For me, Christmas this year has been weird without having to study or worry about assignments. I’m actually looking forward to a relaxed dinner without too much stress. That's the good part of university over for now, hasn’t it? But can't help but think about how we spend Christmas. Should we stick to the traditional way or try something new? Like no visiting all the family? I for one would never miss visiting the relatives, but a little downtime is always nice. Plus, it gives us plenty of time for showing off all the new dance moves we learned in that dance class. Everyone laughs. Honestly though, seeing your mum bust the moves at that party was the highlight of my year. More music and dance, less talking next time, please! Well, let me tell you, there was laughter and maybe a few questionable elbow-digs and knees, but we all had a great time. You know, it's things like that which make these gatherings so memorable, isn’t it? Definitely. And another thing I noticed was the family friends gathering, it was so much fun. Did anyone else notice the meme of the napkins that looked like underpants? It was the biggest laugh of the year.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my culinary adventure last week? I tried making a traditional English roast and it was a bit of a disaster. Oh no, what happened? You can't mess up a roast – it's the epitome of comfort food. A bit of a disaster in the kitchen, eh? I've had my share of those, especially when you’re trying out new recipes. Yeah, I wanted to make it for my friends. It was supposed to be Thanksgiving style. But I underestimated the cooking time for the turkey, so it was still pink in the middle. And then I overcooked the vegetables. It was a comedy. That sounds like a whole episode of a cooking show. And what did your friends say? Well, they were very supportive. One of them said, "Don’t worry, it's the thought that counts." But another couldn’t help but mention it on social media - "Today, I had the rarer side of turkey!" So, it's now a bit of a joke between us. That's fun. I had a similar experience with trying to make a traditional Midland stew. My family thought it was so bad it ended up being the joke at the Christmas dinner. Yeah, I remember trying to make an old family recipe for my first serious date. It was supposed to impress him, but I somehow managed to burn the entire dish. We ended up laughing so hard, and I think that's when we knew we were the real deal. See, it's funny now, but at the time it was definitely stressful. Still, it was just me, so I could keep it a secret. What about you, Speaker_3? What’s been new at work? It's always something with exams and everything. It's been hectic. The exams are around the corner and it feels like everyone’s workload has doubled. I'm trying to keep things organized but it's just getting busier by the day. Exams can be stressful, especially leading up to them. Did you have to adjust anything this year? Actually, yes. We’ve had to adapt to some new online testing tools and procedures. It complicates things a bit but we’re managing. Still, thinking about it reminds me, have you all seen those new cookbooks I’ve been getting? They inspire me to try some new recipes over the weekends.

I've decided I need a new blender. Our old one is still working but it's super old and I've seen some great new models at Marks and Spencer recently. What do you think? Are you still using the old one from our wedding or have you updated? Oh, I'd like to say we upgraded but I think my blender is older than ours! Honestly, I wish I could get a better one but I never seem to find the time to look around. Plus, my work life has been keeps me busy. Did you hear about the new appraisals at work? I'm a bit nervous about how it will go. Oh dear, I can imagine. Appraisals are always a bit stressful, aren't they? So what's the vibe like in your department? I've heard that the admin team's been quite busy with the new project and that could add pressure to the whole appraisal process. Yeah, it's been a bit of a challenge. We've had to deal with a lot of changes and it seems like the higher-ups are expecting us to perform at a higher level or something. But on the bright side, our new manager seems quite supportive, so I'm hoping for a fair review. I’ve been diligently working on my presentation though, so I'm trying to stay positive. That's good to hear. It really does make a difference when your manager is on your side. I'm sure you'll be okay. Speaking of food, isn't it bizarre how Marks and Spencer has suddenly become a go-to for gourmet pizzas? I tried that new Italian pizza recipe from their Food department last week and it was fantastic! Yeah, I saw that on the TV ad. I might have to try one of those myself soon. More convenient than ordering in, I guess. But I always question the quality. Do you think it's better than Domino's or Pizza Express? Honestly, it's hard to beat a good old-fashioned pepperoni from Domino's, but Marks and Spencer’s one was surprisingly good. Alright, defender of traditional pizzas. But I must admit, Marks and Spencer has been stepping up their food game recently. Speaking of food, what’s for supper? It's going to be a casserole with roasted vegetables, potatoes, and maybe some of that new gourmet pizza for a side or after.

Yo, lads! I've decided I need a new wardrobe. I'm getting so bored of wearing the same old stuff all the time. Thoughts? Definitely! I've been feeling the same way. I really need to get some new heels, though. You know heels, they do elevate the whole outfit, innit? But, have you seen the pain after wearing them for hours?! I wish they could make them less of a nightmare. Erm, yeah, but for nights out, they're a must, can't they? You look fab and all. True that! They're not always comfy but they just add a certain something to your evening out. Comfort over style, that's my life motto but for big nights, I totally understand making the effort. Anyway, what about you three? What're you lovelies wearing today? Oh, I'm wearing a nice little dress I got last year and some pair of heels I barely ever wear. They're not that high, though. Aww, that sounds nice! I'm actually just wearing my usual jeans and a sweater today. Oh, I’ve got some pretty decent shoes on though—loads of support so hopefully they’ll last me the entire day. Yep, comfort is key. I’ve got my trusty corduroys and nice trainers. Honestly though, I could use some new ones for a night in, maybe something really comfy. That sounds dreamy. Guess that’s the life of a student—choosing between comfort or style. Talking of nights out, do any of you have any plans soon? More specifically, do any of you know good, less popular spots around town for a drink that won’t be heaving? There's this dive bar next to the park that's pretty chill but we should probably make sure it'll be open and not too crowded. It’s one of my favorites. Oh for sure! Let's say we do go out, though, can't we take turns so we don’t tire ourselves out trying to see too many places in one go? Makes sense. Plus, there's almost always this one café just over the river that stays open till late. Ooh, now that's a good tip! I've heard it's still thinking of turning it into a late bar. Might be interesting to check it out. We could even make it a theme night!

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I was convinced I was reincarnated from ancient Egypt? Ancient Egypt? No, you've never told me that one. Is that from your occasional delve into astrology or was it a specific meditation weekend retreat? It was definitely a combination of both, and a bit of curiosity after watching too many history documentaries. I spent a whole week feeling like I was born to build pyramids and deal with pharaohs. Right, let me guess, you started eating figs, chanting to the sun god, and insisting on wearing kaftans around the house? Not quite as dramatic, but close. You really have an adventurous soul though. And you do well with imagination. Hence your stellar recommendations when we want to throw up a fancy party. Thanks, love. I guess that's the creative part of my job as a PA. You couldn’t have a successful party without a good imagination, could you? Definitely not, especially with this side of yours. Now, imagine we were the hosts of a magical time-traveling party. What period would you choose? I've always been fascinated by the Roaring Twenties. Jazz, flapper dresses, and prohibition. It's like a whole world away from IT consulting. The flapper dress idea, I like that. I'd add a twist, though. We'd have a 'visitors through time’ theme. Each guest would come in costume, and we'd have props for them to use during the party. That sounds amazing! We could have a speakeasy corner, and have side conversations about the significance of being there. Plus, the blurred lines between time periods would add a fun element. Exactly! And by the end of the night, we'd all be friends, sworn to secrecy about who actually comes from which time. Like, I’d meet you somewhere in 1920s New York City, and we just happened to bump into each other at a speakeasy. And I’d be dressed as a flapper, completely by coincidence. Both laugh. Where would we hold this? Maybe use our backyard as the base and we could set up different time zones throughout? We've got a big garden. We could use different sections for different eras. But it would mean decorating and prep. A lot of prep. I see the look of horror in your eyes. Not exactly horror, though it does give me a flutter.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that online workshop I attended today? It was quite enlightening. The guy was clearly well-versed in the latest marketing techniques for selling small businesses. Made me think about what changes we might make to our company's online presence, you know, to attract more customers. Oh, that sounds fascinating! I've been looking for ways to help my brother improve his small bakery's online store right now. Now, you never cease to amaze me with how you're always up-to-date with these things. You're like a walking internet search engine. Well, I'm lucky I've got someone like you who can translate all this marketing mumbo-jumbo into something I can understand. Though I did just spend the entire day dealing with staffing issues. You know how it is. Sure, I do. It can be endless. But speaking of creative outlets, have you ever tried knitting? I just started recently and I find it so relaxing. Almost like meditation for me. Actually, that's so cool! I've been knitting for years, it's my go-to hobby whenever things get too hectic at work. Makes me feel like I'm creating something while unwinding. Ah, really? I've always wanted to learn but never really had the time. Though I do remember my grandmother knitted a lot in her spare time. Yes, it's amazing how knitting can be passed down through generations. I wish I could've learned from my mother the way that you might've learned from your grandmother, but unfortunately, she was more of a... career lady. Ah, that's a common story. But it's never too late to start. I’ve been following quite a few knitting channels on YouTube recently and it really makes me want to pick up my needles again. Speaking of which, have we talked about anything happening in Peterborough? I noticed there’s a new culture festival coming up next month. Oh, yes! I saw that. It'll be great to catch some of the performances and food markets. Plus, the cultural exchange can be fantastic... although sometimes cultural differences can lead to stereotypes... Not necessarily. People often misunderstand or simplify cultures they don't know much about, but that's usually because they haven't been exposed to enough. I think that festival is a great opportunity to learn and appreciate...

Yo, lads and lasses. I'm pretty knackered from that anthropology lecture today. The lectuer was talking about some theory about how the Bronze Age had more use of copper rather than bronze and I thought to myself 'why can't they just stick to the facts?' and then the bell rang. Oh, definitely. It's like those people couldn't have focused on what was actually important. I've never eaten Istrian pasta like this before. Look how full the sauce is! Agreed! The local flavors are quite different from what we're used to in England. Well, yes and no. Some areas like Manchester can be quite expensive, but there are still affordable places if you know where to look. Ah, mates, I haven't seen any place as beautiful as Cornwall. The sun, the sea, the cliffs – it was just idyllic, wouldn't you say, Susan? Yes, absolutely. And the grass was so lush, and the flowers were all in bloom. It was like stepping into a picture postcard, wasn't it, Peter? I've actually got some great shots I took there. Wanted to get out, meet new people, and do something useful. I remember, you were telling us about the group in the pub, really good bunch of people. Yes, they were. Despite coming from all different walks of life, we all had the same passion for the lighthouse maintenance and the environment. That's right. And the sunsets at the lighthouse, they were incredible. The cycle paths through the moors are stunning. That's a bit ambitious, isn't it, Peter? You're forgetting I haven't been on a bike in decades.

Oh, did I ever tell you lot about that stupid buffet today? The lentil soup was watery and the cucumber sandwiches were soggy. You're quite the food critic. But even if it is great, still, nothing beats having my mum make it. She's got that certain touch. Definitely. I used to have this mate in London who swore by her mum’s coronation chicken. I never understood the hype back then but when I tried it – wow! And what about your own experiences with foods? I remember when I did my stint in university, I decided to try making pasta from scratch once. It turned into a barely edible mess! But now I can cook decently. Sounds like something I’d try once! Well, at least you have some good stories to tell – like a couple of us from work had a pretty disastrous bonding dinner at a friend’s place. We tried making a BBQ but ended up having to order takeout because the grill didn’t work. Guess that’s the life of attempting the perfect meal. Speaking of living arrangements and housemates, I’ve just started looking for a new place since the lease is up. Can be quite stressful. Oh, completely. I moved out of my family home a couple of years ago and it was a roller coaster. Lots of wrong choices but you eventually find the right place. Have you two checked out the South of Bridge? There’s a good mix of flats and more affordable compared to the rest of the city. Plus, job opportunities are decent if you work in the factories or around that area. Oh, that’s a great tip. I'll definitely look into it. Oh, wow, Barcelona was amazing! We had such a fun time. The Gaudí Park was incredible, and the beaches were just perfect. I'm glad you enjoyed it! Was the food up to standard? Oh, absolutely. We had the best seafood paella and tapas. But, I have to say, it was a bit of a struggle to find a place that wasn't too touristy. Are you still on about that? I swear, you're going to love Paris. They have the best brasseries with delicious, authentic French food that's not overdone for tourists. Oh, really? That sounds amazing! I've never been to Paris, but I've heard so much about it. What's the most underrated spot you've found there? Well, it's not really underrated per se, but I'd say try the old market districts. They have some of the best, most authentic places that aren't marked in the guidebooks. That sounds promising! Speaking of fun plans, have we made any plans for the weekend? Not yet. I was thinking we could try out that new bakery that just opened up near us. Apparently, they have the best sourdough bread in town. Sounds good! And then maybe catch up on some tv shows? We've been meaning to watch "The Crown" together but never seem to find the time. Exactly! I was thinking the same thing. Let's set a time and make it happen. Yeah, that works for me. Okay, how about Saturday afternoon at 4? Sounds like a plan! And what about Sunday? Any changing plans for that? Not really. We can make that day up as we go. Maybe we could try out that park we keep talking about, take a picnic? Oooh, that sounds lovely! And we can even invite _______ and _______ if they're free. Yeah, definitely. They love hanging out with us. How's work been? Well, as usual, a bit crazy. But this week has been okay... except for the new patient who's been a bit of a handful. That sounds tiring. I bet though, it's rewarding too, right? Definitely. Though sometimes, it can get overwhelming. But it makes all the difference to see someone improve and trust you. That's true. I envy you sometimes, being able to make such a direct impact. That's sweet of you to say. But trust me, it's not all sunshine and rainbows.

Ah, I can't believe I'm finally getting some sun after all these weeks of rain. It's been quite dreary back in London and Manchester. I've been finding it so difficult to get out and enjoy some fresh air. Indeed, it's lovely here in North Cyprus, isn’t it? The weather catches up with you over time. I was getting frustrated with the day-to-day physical management and found that running a digital startup was more scalable and less geographically dependent. That makes sense. In my business, scale and consistency were my biggest challenges. But, unlike teaching, tech enables a lot more automation and virtual support for customers. It was quite a learning curve but it’s been rewarding to see some of our projects gain traction. It's great that you see the positives in that. As for me, finding the right balance between understanding and guiding each student can be tough. But the rewarding part is when one of them says they’ve finally grasped a difficult concept, or when former students come back to tell me how my teaching helped them in their careers. I’ve seen the business grow and help people on a wider scale, but the personal connections with my clients – it’s what keeps me motivated. I suppose it's all about finding what gives you purpose. After being a teacher for over a decade, I’d say it's the little successes, like when a student returns and thanks you for believing in them.

Alright, I don't think I've ever felt more comfortable with someone than I do with you. Well, I'm glad to hear that, I love that you feel that way too. We've had our share of tricky situations, but also, we've learned a lot from them. Like, in my case, I learned to communicate better when something's bothering me instead of just letting it boil over and then exploding. Well, I think the communication part is key. Maybe a two-bedroom flat would work. That could be perfect. And if we're in the city centre, I could walk to work and you wouldn't have to deal with a long commute to uni. Yeah, that would be ideal. And it could be a bit more expensive, but like you said, we might be able to do better with our own place than some of the housemates situations we've had.

Ah, marvellous weekend. I managed to get some buns and some cheap veg. The Co-op was having a sale, and I got a good bargain. Oh, that's right! You got out today, isn't it? I must say, it's a welcome change of scenery after being cooped up so long. Indeed, it is. The walk did me good too. Though I'm glad to be back, as the weather's taken a turn. All gloomy and damp. Yeah, nothing like a good English summer. Always blustering about, isn't it? Even when there's no storm to speak of. Can't say I've ever understood why we persist with it, but there we are. It's in our blood, I suppose. Hehe, you could say that. Speaking of which, want a cuppa? I made some tea before you arrived. That would be lovely, love. Black, if you don't mind. Right you are. So, how were the crowds in town today? As you'd expect, busy. Lots of the usual silly season tourists about. Makes me think of the '60s and '70s, when we'd spend our summer holidays down there every year. Oh, do tell me! Those must have been good times. I love listening to your stories from back then. Ah, yes. Young and carefree. We didn't have a care in the world. Just enjoying the simple things. Simple things can be the best, can't they? Though, to be honest, sometimes I worry about these days. With the way things are going... I know what you mean. The world moves faster than we ever thought possible. Sometimes it feels like we're just trying to keep up. Exactly! Especially with the tech and changing ways. It's not easy on my nerves. Don't worry about it. I'm sure we're not the only ones feeling a bit left behind. Us old folk, we like our routines, our familiar ways. You know, I found it took me some time to adjust when they started selling milk in plastic bottles. Seemed so... impersonal. I remember! Milkmen used to deliver everything fresh in glass. And the rounds. Always a highlight of the day. I know! Now, it seems so... convenient, but... I do miss the personal touch, I must say. Mhmm, that's the thing though, isn't it? Convenience over character. Takes away a bit of community, as far as I'm concerned.

Alright, Dad, Grace, today we're discussing how to sort out the garden and perhaps the house a bit. It's been a bit of a downer since Mum passed away, you know. Ah, yes, it’s changed things around a bit, hasn’t it? But I suppose that's life. What’s your thoughts, Grace? Erm, well, it’s just that the garden looks a bit... untidy, and it seems like it could do with some weeding, and perhaps a bit of renovation in the house as well. It’s a lot to manage, school and everything else at home, but you’re doing well, I’m sure. You are, you know. Keep it up, and all this will help you in the long run. As for the garden, perhaps we can do it together. It’ll be good for everyone, kind of a family activity. Except, we’ll have to wait for when Dad’s feeling up to it, of course. That’s so typical of you, Nan! Tea is on the way. Grace, would you pour the tea for us and bring the biscuits down? Sure, I’ll do that. --- Here’s the tea, Nan. And I brought some of the shortbread biscuits too. Lovely, thank you, Grace. Brings back memories, this does. --- You know, when I was your age, Grace, I used to help out in my sister's garden. It was during the war. Every bit of food we grew was precious. She had a whole section just for vegetables. That sounds quite different.

Yo, lads, what've you all been up to since we last caught up? You know, just the usual uni grind, trying to tackle that dissertation. Got you lot on my mind though. Aye, same here. Been busy with some assignments, but questions if anyone's interested in starting an online class together for something like, say, web development or digital marketing? That sounds useful, right? Might be able to learn something practical and get a certificate. Definitely get on it. Could actually apply it to my future job prospects, you know. Plus, it's always good to keep your skills sharp. Yeah, definitely. I've been looking into something like that too. Maybe we could work on our own projects in the process. As long as it doesn’t require excessive logging in and all that time-wasting stuff. But the idea of staying hydrated and measured, I'm in. Right, right. Hydration is key, especially when you're chasing deadlines all day. So, what's the best way to get one? Any recommendations online? Let’s check Amazon or maybe a specialized health store’s website. Plus, I saw in a fitness group on Facebook that a discount code can be available. That’s a good idea. Maybe we can also scroll through Reddit to see if anyone’s reviewed the latest models. Good idea. Reddit can be a goldmine for these sort of things, especially if you're looking for unbiased feedback. Totally. While we're at it, I just watched this one YouTube series about staying fit that was pretty informative. Endorsed some unique hacks and tips that even the pros might not know.

Right, so I think we need to make a shopping list for tomorrow. I'm going to the supermarket and I don't want to forget anything. You lot always need a reminder. What do you need? I think we need milk, bread, fruit, and some meat for dinner tonight. Good thinking, [Speaker_3]! And some vegetables too. I've got this recipe for a lovely vegetable stew that I'd like to try. Are you still on about your vegetables? Yes! They're good for you. What else? And don't forget sugar. We're out. And what about cleaning supplies? We need some more of that floor cleaner. Great point. And let’s get some insect spray too. We've had an issue with flies in the kitchen lately. Ugh, flies? That's gross. What if we get bit? But if it happens, you can use some antihistamine cream if it’s itchy or just plain old water and soap if we don’t have any other treatments. Speaking of which, I saw a [speaker_3] come home covered in bites last week! Yeah, I know. There were tons of wasps at the park. Shows you should listen to me about that insect spray! Or maybe we could get some natural remedies too. There are lots of ways to keep bugs away without using harsh chemicals. Good idea, [Speaker_4]! And we should talk to [Speaker_3] about keeping things sealed and cleaned up around the house to prevent them becoming a nuisance in the first place. Alright, alright, I'll keep my room tidy. Alright, let's include that on the list. And while we're discussing this, did you hear the news about Man United getting beaten by 5-0? No way! How can they lose so badly? I know it's frustrating but these things happen. They often bounce back. I know it’s a setback, but the season isn’t over. Plus, football is just a game. What can I say, a true Boltonian fan here! It's just so embarrassing, losing by five goals. I know the team will get back on track but it's hard to see them like this.

Yo, so I just heard that PE is gonna be first lesson on Monday. I'm dreading it already. Honestly, me too. It's not that I mind the activity but I need a break after a long weekend. Still, now I'll have to wear those dodgy shorts again. Oh, I know! And Mr. Wright always makes us run so much, it feels like we're training for a marathon. Exactly! But it’s okay. Maybe they just got that way by playing Sports Day activities. Speaking of which, did you hear about the new Instagram post by Chloe? No! What did she post? It was a story about our recent Science project. It’s creative and very well done. I wonder when she even found the time to do it on top of her regular studies. I hope Ms. Davis gives us some extra time for this project. It was quite challenging. I know right! I was just about to ask you, while on the subject. I wish we could do something like that for our project. That would be amazing! But I don’t know if Ms. Davis would let us. Maybe if we ask nicely? Just pointing out our idea to make our project more engaging. That could work. Seems like the right kind of initiative to show. Plus, I saw that the local Science club is experimenting with making their own solar oven. Oh wow, that’s great! If we can get Ms. Davis to agree to changing the format, that would be so much more fun. Definitely. Also, I’ve been thinking, have you noticed how Chloe uses social media differently? Blimey, I've been feeling so dreadful. This cold is really getting to me. Oh, mate, you do sound rough. What've you been taking for it? Ah, just the usual ginger and honey thing and some paracetamol. But it’s been going on for days now. Ginger and honey are good, but maybe you should also try some lemon water and keepself warm. You know how Lloyd Grossman does those medical shows? He’d be saying fluids and rest are key. I know, I know. I’ll have to try that lemon water then. He makes health stuff sound so simple, even if it is sometimes oversimplified. He does have a way of making complex health issues sound straightforward. Still, it's fun to watch him, even if you know he's not always spot on. Totally. I love his enthusiasm. It’s more entertaining than informative but adds to the drama, right? It's entertaining, but sometimes I wonder if it prompts people to self-diagnose rather than seeing a real doctor. Like, really, if you think you have the plague, don’t assume you do because you watched that episode of First Aid. True. Self-diagnosis might not always be the best idea, but I do find his documentaries inspiring in a way. He makes you want to learn more, try those things he talks about, like taking a probiotic for good gut health or regularly checking your body for unexplained lumps. Absolutely! Though his advice and TV knowledge might be great, I still value the actual medical professionals more. I do wish I could see a real doctor right now, but I don't want to go to the hospital if it’s just a cold. Wise decision! No need to overreact, but if it persists or worsens, definitely get it checked. Yeah, definitely. It’s the persistent thing that’s worrying me. Persistent symptoms, fever, or difficulty breathing? That’s when it’s time to head to the hospital. You know I’ve taken you often enough when this happened while we were students. We had that infamous incident with food poisoning at that dodgy little restaurant in Leeds. Oh yeah! I remember, we thought we were dying then.

I've used "FLUB" twice now. I'm winning today! I've been thinking, the word "scrabble" itself could be a powerful one if we had the right letters, but I haven’t seen many of those on the board today. Ah, marvellous weekend so far at the TME's working party, don't you think? All these people gathered to talk about Manchester and its history, and the little old town of Taunton isn't short on stories, you know. Quite, quite right, dear! I've always found questions about this kind of history so fascinating. The way inventions and industries have grown, companies have blossomed and faded, it's absolutely enthralling. Absolutely!
