But we try our best. As someone in a routine occupation, I know that better than most. Yes, we all juggle different schedules. But family is important. I know that well, too. I was talking to Sarah... ...

Alright, now let's talk about this. We were talking about slavery yesterday, right? Yes, Miss, you told us about the horrid lives of people back then. And how even children were treated as slaves, just like me and [Speaker_2's name]? Yes, that’s right. It is very important to understand that slavery was a terrible aspect of our history. People were taken from their families and homes and sold to work for others. It was a form of exploitation and did not value the rights or dignity of people. It also happened in many parts of the world, not just in America. But Miss, why would people do that? Well, there were a lot of reasons. It was often linked to wealth and power. The people who owned the slaves often acted under a belief that this was the way of the world. Others just genuinely thought they had a right over other people because of the color of their skin. It's an extremely complex and disturbing history, but one we must understand and never repeat. But it's not happening now, is it? No, we’re lucky that much of the world has moved away from that through a painful process of change, reform, and recognizing that it was fundamentally wrong. Many people fought for abolition and the rights of all people to be free and equal. We still have to be vigilant though, as inequality and prejudice can take many forms, and it’s our responsibility as individuals to keep advocating for justice. So, is that why we talk about it in school and learn about it? Exactly. It's important to understand where we've come from to know where we are today and to avoid making the same mistakes in the future. Just like when we talk about war. Have you ever wondered why there are wars? Because some countries don’t like each other, Miss? That can be part of it. Wars often start over disagreements or disagreements over resources, power, or beliefs. But if you think about it, no one really wants war. It's really damaging for everyone. It hurts innocent people, disrupts families, and often leads to a lot of pain and loss. But...we do have any wars now, Miss? There are conflicts around the world, but they are often not as widespread and tend to be more local.

Oh, did you see the last episode of "The Crown"? It nearly made me tear up. The way they depicted the late Queen Mother, it felt so... real, you know? Did any of you watch it? Oh, yes! I was so gripped! I couldn’t believe the last few scenes. But have you noticed how much history has changed now? Daisy, I bet you noticed the historical accuracy too. Absolutely, it’s fascinating how they mixed fact and fiction. Made me want to read more about the time period. I’m not sure I could watch anything historical any more, though. Gave me flashbacks of our history lesson in school! Well, you three are all about history now, aren’t you? I decided to watch a different kind of show. "The Great British Bake Off", it was relaxing. And it made me think of all those old recipes my mam used to make. Now that’s a show I don’t mind watching with you. Baking is therapeutic. Did you try anything new from the show? No, but it made me think of when we used to bake together as a family. What a lovely memory that is. Speaking of baking, has anyone heard from Emily recently? I haven’t seen her in ages. Actually, I saw her post about baking bread the other day. Shows are great but social media keeps us connected too! Well, social media can be a mixed bag. Just last week, I saw a post on the local town group about the new community garden. You know, the one near the library? Looks like a great initiative, maybe we could volunteer sometime. That’s a brilliant idea! It's about time we did something for the local community. While I’m self-employed now, it feels good to contribute. Absolutely, and it’s not like we’re sitting idle just because we’re retired or self-employed. It’s all about giving back and staying active in our community. Speaking of active, how’s Scruff doing? Oh, Scruff. He’s livelier than ever. Keeps running around the garden chasing birds. Always gives us a chuckle. But it’s interesting how pets change the dynamics of the household, don’t they? Oh, absolutely! I’ve always found that having a pet makes you more empathetic and responsible. Like last week, I was working on a copywriting project about animal therapy; it’s astonishing what a difference pets can make in people’s lives.

Alright, I need some help unloading this dishwasher. Who can reach the top shelf? Me! Me! I can do it. Me too, me too! Okay, let's see what we've got here. I always like to keeps things backwards. Mom says putting them this way makes it easier to grab one when you want one. Yeah, and then the plates and cutlery can go over there. Well done! You two are doing great. Auntie, can we talk about George Stephenson now? Yeah, we were reading about him in our history book today and I didn't really understand. Of course, I'm more than happy to explain. I love history, and George Stephenson is one of my favorites. Please do. Alright, so George Stephenson was an engineer from the 19th century. You know how trains exist today and we use them all the time? Yeah, we know trains. Well, George Stephenson helped invent the first usable steam locomotive in Britain. That's basically the first train that people could use together. But why is he so important? What was he like? Good questions! George Stephenson wasn't very rich or educated when he was young. You know how most people who became famous in history were? Like, they were usually from rich families? Right! But George Stephenson was self-taught. He taught himself to read and write. And he became an apprentice at a very young age and learned how to work with mechanics. That's amazing. So he really liked machines? He loved them! He was fascinated by finding ways to make machines work better and faster. And what was his most famous machine? His most famous is called the "Rocket". He made this train, which was the very first to win a competition because it was so powerful and could go really fast. Wow, so he helped make the trains we have today! That's right! He won the Rainhill trials in 1829 which was a big competition to see who could make the best steam locomotive. Can we read more about him? Maybe there's a picture book or something? Well, there are lots of books, but let's start with our encyclopedia at home. I think we can find some fun facts there. Yes, please! Alright, let's tidy this up and then we can have some more history fun. Speaker_2 and Yes! Now, did you two know that George Stephenson was not only a great engineer, but he also helped lay the tracks for many of the early railway lines?

Oh, did I ever tell you about my culinary adventure last weekend? I tried making a traditional English roast and it was a bit of a disaster. Oh no, what happened? Struggled to come back down, couldn’t figure out why it wasn’t as easy to climb back down as it was to go up. Grandad, you’ve got some pretty wild childhood stories! Yep, it's just through here on the right. We’re getting close. Oh, look! There's the sign for Mothercare! We can see it from here. Alright, let’s get out the parking lot. Do we need anything specific today? Oh, can we maybe find some new blankets for the baby room? She’s growing fast and I think changing the colors and patterns would be fun. I remember when you used to love these bright, colorful blankets when you were little. You could even pick some baby stuff for your younger cousins or friends if you like. We can put those into your own little stash for when they're born. That’s a great idea! I have three friends who are due soon. I could totally do that. And... We're also talking about DIY and renovations, right? That old guest room is crying out for a new coat of paint and some new furniture. Yes, and maybe some new wallpaper for the living room too. We’ve been talking about giving it a fresh look for ages, especially since the move is going smoothly. Have you both had a chance to think about colleges and all that? I mean, I’ve got GCSEs coming up. It's scary but also exciting. It does come around fast, doesn’t it? My own memories from university are quite vivid. I never thought about it that way back then but kids when I was at Bolton Uni... it wasn't easy but it was... ...

I've been playing this new game online and it's totally addictive. The graphics are so real and the characters are really well-developed. Oh, that sounds like fun! Are you still into gaming quite a bit? Yeah, games do consume a lot of my time now. You know, it's kind of a stress reliever. But sometimes I worry that it affects my mood, you know, if I spend too much time on it. Oh, I get that! I've heard loads about this whole 'gaming addiction' stuff. Do we know much about it? True, it's a form of escapism I suppose. I read somewhere that it affects your psychology, like it messes up your social skills or something. That could be true - I've noticed how I sometimes struggle to be present in real conversations after a long bout of gaming. The language and communication aren't the same in games, are they? And these games are designed to keep you hooked. They're all about engagement and reward mechanisms, or so I've read. That's interesting. So it's almost like psychological manipulation. Exactly. It's kind of like we're the 'lab rats', and they're studying how to make games more addictive. It's really unsettling when you think about it. Well, as long as you know about it, it's not as harmful. But it does make you wonder, doesn't it? Alright, I'm shifting gears here. How about that Christmas? Anyone planning anything exciting? I'm hoping to go to my cousin's in London. They always have a fantastic party. That sounds fun. My side of the family does a big dinner. We usually have a good time, but I worry a bit since my grandma's not as mobile as she used to be. Oh, and it's always so much effort to arrange for everyone. But it's worth it, isn't it? Definitely worth it. Although I'm sure we're all feeling a bit tired after the year. Anyone working over Christmas? Actually, I have a work project due around that time. But it's something I enjoy, so it's not too much of a drag. Good job. I wish I could work. I've been feeling a bit stuck. We've been wanting to travel more. Always plans, never execute. Maybe this is the year to actually plan something?

You know, kids, the world around us is made up of so many different things. Most of these things are made from either metals or fabrics. Let's think about some examples of metals and fabrics we use everyday. Like LEGO! That's a block right? But it's not metal, is it? Is it a fabric like my sweater, or is it something else? Good questions! You both are right. LEGO isn't made of metal or fabric, it's made from a type of plastic. But for example, coins are metal, and your clothes might be made of fabrics like cotton or polyester. And guess what? Even the buildings and machines we use are often made from both metals and fabrics. I know! Like, if we’re in Minecraft, the tools we use are made from different types of metals. Iron, gold, diamond... And fabric! Because we can craft armor to wear from materials like leather! Exactly, really good point! Now let's talk about something entirely different. What if we invent some new legends for Minecraft? Like, what if there was a legend about a diamond sword that could control time? Oh, that’s so cool! What would happen if you used the sword? Maybe it would be really strong and could cut through anything, but only if you use it at night! That’s a great idea! Perhaps changing the time could also affect the things around us. Like, certain monsters might only appear at certain times of day. Could it also take you back to different eras? Like, if we have a real world history project at school, the sword could help us go see the dinosaurs or go to ancient Egypt. As a teacher, I think if Minecraft were real, it would make learning so much more fun. But remember, our thinking about this is just pretend. In real life, we have to rely on science and historical records to learn about those things. Aww, no dinosaur rides with a Minecraft sword? What can I say, maybe we can make it part of a school project instead. Like, write a story about it, or even make a little movie using the Minecraft game. You boys could be the heroes finding this magical sword. That would be awesome! Oh, can we invent a legend about a treasure chest that gives you what you wish for? And wouldn’t it be cool if it was hidden somewhere, like under a school hidden room under the slide?

Yo, mate, did you hear about that strict new law they's bringing in to stop paedophiles from social media? It's about bloody time innit? Yeah, I did. It's been long overdue, really. Specially after that creep case near our area. Hope it actually works. Exactly! I mean, I knew some people who got caught up with that kind of thing at school. Heartbreaking, you know? I know, absolutely. All very serious stuff. And talking about serious, how's your guitar playing coming along? Oh, you know. Up and down. Been playing a bit of Stairway to Heaven recently, that's been a challenge. Though, any band that does a proper cover of that is hard to beat, in my opinion. Haha, yes, that's a tough one. One of my mates plays in a band, they did do a cover of that. But you know, they added some punk influences, it was quite something. Really? How'd it go? Did you go see their gig? Yeah, last Saturday actually. It was a mixed bag, to be honest. Some of their covers were great, but they lost me during that heavy metal section. Too much for my tastes. Fair enough, not everyone's into metal, right? Though I used to listen quite a bit. It's like a whole different language when you get into it. Definitely different vibes, that's for sure. Speaking of vibes, did you get a chance to listen to the new Greta Van Fleet album? Not yet, actually. I've been busy catching up on some uni work this week, but I do want to check it out. Last one was really good. Oh, same here. I tried to get through the readings for my English lit course, but it's like another language to me. Lol, been there. I always found it easier to read for fun than for academic purposes. Right? Like, reading Dickens on your own time for enjoyment is completely different from having to critically analyze it in an essay. Exactly! Can't see Dickens ever figuring into my 21st century hobbies unless I could go back in time and almost unintentionally haunt him. Maybe meet him at a pub or something and annoy him into including sci-fi elements in his novels? Haha, exactly. "Um, Mr. Dickens, I know you're brilliant and all, but a bit of steam punk wouldn't hurt, yeah...?"

Yo, lads and lasses. What d'you lot's been up to since school's been out? To be honest, just chilling out. Had a few escape plans down on my spreadsheet. Want to hear? Yeah, shoot, let’s hear it! Is it anything as exciting as your EPQ project? Nah, nothing that cool . I've been thinking of suggesting a food festival trip to Tamworth, there's gonna be loads of food stalls and weird keepsakes to get. Think about it, fry-ups, savory stuff, veg, and vegetarian options too. It’ll be fun! Cool idea, food festivals are always a blast. Though, let’s also consider a bit of preparation, shall we? Make sure we can sample from all over the place - South-East London, South-West London, you know how diverse our culinary backgrounds are? That's true! But, we should also check if there's anything around here that's doing good for poverty issues. I was reading about this charity thing in Slough, they’re doing a food recycling drive. Oh, that sounds quite cool. We're gonna balance between party and giving back, huh? Exactly! Suppose we can combine the fun with some good work. Speaking of which, I’ve also been meaning to look at some exhibitions. There’s an art exhibit in Wembley that’s been on my radar. Maybe we could hit that up after the food festival trip? Wembley? They’re famous for that arena, but never knew there were art exhibits there. I’m in unless doesn’t clash with anything. Yep, I'm down for anything artsy, including art exhibitions. It’s time off from all that sixth form madness, after all. I just wish the project work wasn't so overwhelming. The EPQ is such a stress. Oh, I know! I've been trying to decide on a topic. I considered changing the world through humanitarian work, but my tutor said it’s too broad. Yeah, I'm in a similar boat. I thought about just exploring something around environmental issues because so much of it is relevant to everyday life now. For real! That's something I might’ve mentioned as well. I considered almost going vegetarian just because of it. But real talk, getting the balance right with school and personal beliefs is tough. Honestly, I can't decide. But I’ve been reading up on sustainable living and it’s got me wondering if that could be part of this project.

Oh, did I ever tell you lot about my stupid landlord today? He's trying to charge me £50 for the noise from our flat talked about at the student forum last month. You two remember that, right? The one time I spilled pasta and the whole floor was covered? Oh yes! We all thought it was hilarious. Like, of course, you weren’t deliberately making a mess, but still... But why the extra charge? I thought we had agreed on £10 for minor incidents like that? Well, tell him to stick that in his pipe and smoke it! We're not paying an extra quid for someone's whims. You've already had so many issues with that landlord, Emma. I bet he’s just trying to make a little extra money off of us. Yeah, and the room is so tiny, I feel like I’m living in a cupboard. Our uni accommodation seems to get smaller each term. Totally, and the common areas are always a mess or occupied. But £50? That’s more than I pay for my phone bill some months! You’re right about that, but the bigger problem here is that they’re trying to make a substantial fee for something that’s, really, just part of the wear and tear of living in shared accommodation. But hey, maybe we can all take that to the student union, suggest they review the flat quality in general. An excellent idea! We should do that and also maybe highlight some of the other issues, like the kitchen being poorly equipped. Last week I had to use my own utensils for our communal dinner because there weren’t enough. Can we talk about something else? Our flats just seem to be a never-ending complaint session. Alright, alright, but we can't let them just get away with everything. Especially now when accommodation is changing so quickly. Speaking of which, have we updated our uni accommodation choices for next year yet? I heard there’s a new building in the city centre opening up. Yeah, I’ve looked into it. It seems like it might offer better facilities and a more modern layout. Plus, the location could be more convenient for some of us. Oh, we should definitely consider it then. The price might be a bit steep but if it resolves some of these current issues, maybe it’s worth it.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time during Christmas when my nephew nearly set off the fire alarm trying to roast chestnuts? You must be joking, Alison! No, you never did. That must have been quite a drama! Oh, it was! The house was full of people and the whole thing was very chaotic. Anyway, that's why I'm glad you suggested we meet here at the Seven Stars, where things are a bit more... calm. Yes, and it's always nice to catch up, isn't it? Especially in a place like Totnes, with its old-world charm. Exactly! It just feels right to sit here talking among the old stone walls, even if we do have a lot to catch up on. What's new with you? Quite a bit, actually. I've been working with a few new clients, and we've been discussing some training strategies over the past few weeks. Offsite training seems to be popular right now for whatever reason. That's interesting. I'm facing this trend a bit too, actually. My students seem to value the different learning experience the outdoors provides. We recently did a lesson in the Dartmoor national park. Seeing the joy on their faces when they successfully used English to describe the landscape was priceless. That's wonderful! It's nice to see you're still bringing some creativity into your teaching. It wasn't always in practice when we were doing our initial training courses, was it? I'm glad they're becoming more flexible and practical these days. Absolutely. It's about giving the students real-world opportunities to use the language. And it's also helped me, personally, appreciate just how varied English teaching really is. As it was for me, I'm sure. You never stop learning when you're teaching, do you? Of course not! Although sometimes I wish I could turn my brain off like you, and just enjoy the views like these. I'm sure you do have days like that, but just because we're working doesn't mean we can't also enjoy the moment, right? You're right, of course. It's about balance. Speaking of which, how was your Christmas? Very quiet, as you might expect. I spent most of it with my cat, but it was cozy. No travel, no particular plans. You enjoy your solitude sometimes, I know.

Yo, Dad, it's good to finally see you! It's been ages. It certainly has, haven't talked this much in person since you left for uni two years ago. What've you been up to? Loads – I graduated, started working as an English Language instructor, and moved to Brighton last summer. Brighton! I wish I could have gone with you. You know me and how much I love the sea! But coming here was a big change - not just geographically, but also in terms of the pace of life and such. Yeah, I heard Brighton's very fast-paced. It is, but I like the vibe there. Was thinking of following in your footsteps - customer service sounds interesting, but I've started seeing some of those new traffic cameras around here. Ah, yeah, speed cameras. Exactly! Is that going to affect your job at all? Are those cameras all over England now? Now that you mention it, they've been popping up all over Kent and into Sussex. The Government’s busy installing them pretty much everywhere. The debate is still on whether they’re effective. Speaking of effectiveness, do you hear stories from the workforce about the licenses people have or don’t have? Well, there’s always something about silly reasons why someone got fined, really. But you should see some of the conversations I have – they’re hilarious. But it's serious business too, isn't it? Too true. Let’s not forget about the serious stuff. How about your career? Seems like the English Language teaching gig’s treating you well? It is fun, but it's been tough. Just couple of months ago, I had this one student who really needed help but couldn't attend classes due to severe sickness. It got me thinking about our health system. Sad to hear that. The healthcare situation sure has people worried. Exactly. I was thinking of maybe moving back to help if things get real bad here. I know how you feel. It’s concerning. Anyway, tell me about life in Crayford. Everything changed much since I left? Well, pretty much the same. The new condos are finally complete but they’re affecting housing prices for sure. More traffic, too. Weird, feels like a different place when you're back, isn’t it? It does. Speaking of changes, planning a trip to Tanzania next year.

So, I was browsing on Amazon yesterday and found this amazing stationery set. Looked really professional; these are notebooks and pens that would be perfect for our lectures. Oh, that sounds interesting. Do you think we could use those for our new course next semester? Absolutely. It could make our presentations look really classy. Besides, students always appreciate when we bring materials that are not just functional but also aesthetically pleasing, right? Definitely. Engaging materials make a big difference in how they respond to the content. Speaking of which, have you started brainstorming ideas for your section of the lecture on public relations? I’ve been thinking about starting with a case study of a recent successful PR campaign, then linking it to our current topic on the evolution of communication strategies. That sounds perfect. I was thinking of doing a similar approach for my part but with more focus on the role of social media in shaping PR narratives. We could then compare and contrast these two approaches in the lecture. That will work well together. Maybe next week we could sit down and start drafting our notes so we can share it on our lecture plan before the semester starts. Exactly. And while we're on this topic, I’ve been meaning to ask, what do you think about our university’s public relations department? I’ve noticed a bit of a struggle with communicating their initiatives to the community and student body effectively. I agree, it feels like there’s a disconnect in their communication strategy. They need to ensure they’re speaking the language of their audience, but also being transparent and engaging. I saw that tweet they sent out last week about the new scholarships and the language used was quite... academic. Right, and it’s not even clear who it’s meant for or how to apply. It’s almost as if they’re speaking to the faculty rather than the students or parents who would benefit from it. Exactly. We should really offer our services to help them out. We could even make it an academic project for our PR course. Brilliant idea. We could build that into the course for next semester. It would give our students real-world experience and the university gets improved PR. And it would also look great on our own resumes and for the university. A win-win almost gone too well.

I've decided I need a new shower curtain. Our old one's so faded and worn. Well, haven't talked about that for ages, have we? You love your decorating projects, don’t you? Oh, very much! But do you have any suggestions on where to start? Hmm, I suppose the first thing would be to decide on a design. Do you want something of a specific color, or perhaps a theme? The bathroom is relatively small, so I’m leaning towards something simple and light. Colour-wise, maybe white or cream, but with a bit of texture – I’ve seen some lovely printed ones recently. Oh yes, I know what you mean. You could also consider patterns. A small, discreet pattern can add some interest without overwhelming the room. Exactly. And while we talk about décor, did you see that new knitting project I started? I'm making a bean bag. Ah, yes, I did see the knitting needles next to your couch! How’s it going? It’s coming along! I've finally figured out how to do a decent cast-off, so the fun part is starting now. That's great! You know, you're so good at these DIY projects. Maybe next time, you could create a matching set for the bathroom? Hmm, that's an interesting idea. Like, a cushion cover for the lounge chair in the bathroom, and a matching bean bag. That could look nice. Or perhaps you could make a set of soft washcloths? Just a thought. That’s actually brilliant. I can totally do that. Thanks for the idea! Of course! I love having matched sets in a bathroom. It feels so coordinated. Oh, by the way, are you making us something for supper? I was changing the recipe up a bit. I was thinking about making a sort of herby chicken dish – I have some fresh thyme and rosemary. Perfect, I adore the smell of those herbs! Can we have vegetables with it? Maybe some sweet potatoes and asparagus? Absolutely! I'll roast them in the oven. And you’ve started the cooking? The house already smells amazing! I’ve been working on it while we chat. I suppose while this is cooking, I should start looking for that shower curtain... Do you think we could also look at DIY storage solutions for the bathroom? Why not? We can discuss that over dinner.

You know, it's hard to believe we've been idle for so long now. Seems like it was just yesterday I was working at the local factory and you were running that nursery in Harrow. That's right, John. Time sure seems to fly when you're not keeping busy, doesn't it? Perhaps it's time we started keeping busy again, eh? All this sitting about is doing us no good. Absolutely, Richard. There was a time I wouldn't dream of sitting idle. But these days, with nothing to do from morning till night, the days just seem to wash over me. You're right, though. We never thought we'd end up like this. Both of you were always so busy, managing your respective roles, I didn't think it would end for either of us. But what holds us back from doing something now? We're all still capable, right? I mean, I used to run that convenience store of mine, it wasn't nothing to sneeze at! Where to start, I suppose. You see, Richard, the world moves on, and sometimes people like us get left behind. Not that we can't still do something, but technology, for one, keeps evolving. I'm not sure I'd even know how to apply for a job these days in this digital age. I feel that too, John. And maybe there's also a bit of stigma attached to our situation, being long-term unemployed and all. I don't buy that. Anyone can start something new at any age. Look at me - after being a childminder, I started that small shop. It wasn't easy but it ended up being my thing. Why couldn't either of you find something similar? Perhaps changing the world view that we're 'old' might be part of the challenge, though. I get it, but it's precisely what we're so often told by society that might make it hard for people to consider us anew. But let's not let that be the obstacle. What if we... what if we tried to start something here, right from where we are? Like what, for instance? I've always been interested in gardening. I know it takes work, but it's therapeutic too. Maybe we could start a community garden or something around here. We could involve our neighbors, teach them some of the old skills like John might know about his factory days, and share what I know about childcare.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to deal with a patient who was super-sensitive to penicillin and clearly hadn't mentioned it prior to being administered? No, that sounds quite challenging! Was it serious? Yeah, kind of. We had to move fast to administer the right med and manage her reaction. She was okay in the end, but it was quite a scramble. That reminds me of working with some of the weird and wonderful medications in copywriting. You'd think certain ads would tell you everything, but, you know, not always! As a trainee nurse, I'm learning about all sorts of things. Sometimes even the most routine medication can cause reactions. It really places an emphasis on thorough pre-consultation checks! Exactly. It's a good reminder why communication with patients and thorough prep work are so crucial. Now, shall we talk about something a bit more light? What are your Christmas plans for this year? Well, I've been thinking or a quieter one at home, maybe a small family gathering. The last few years have been a bit crazy with different plans falling through. I'm the same. I actually don't even like the commercial aspect of Christmas so much anymore. It's nice when it's simpler, you know? Ah, I agree. I'd rather enjoy some good food, maybe some good films, and quality time indoors. Less stress for everyone. We might actually do something like that over at my end too. Less doesn't always mean less, it means intentional and meaningful, which is lovely. Speaking of food, do you all fancy trying out that new Italian place in town? Seems to have got some decent reviews. Ooh, I've heard it's pretty good. But honestly, another trip to town seems a bit much for me right now. How about we order in? We can each bring a dish and make it feel like a proper feast at home? I love that idea! No muss, no fuss. Plus, we get to choose what we really want. I can bring over some of that amazing Keralan curry my mum makes. Excellent! That sounds almost as good as being at a local restaurant. We can all do that! Great. Let's solidify everything by Wednesday. How does that sound? Works for me. I’m free this week, so Wednesday is perfect.

Ah, I can't believe I'm finally getting a firsthand experience of northern Cyprus. I've always been fascinated by its rich history and unique cultural blend. Do you enjoy living here? Oh indeed, yes. It's got quite a different vibe compared to the rest of the UK. I kind of regret not coming here earlier, but now it seems like a lovely place to spend my retirement. Absolutely makes sense! It's peaceful, isn't it? I mean, compared to the hustle and bustle of London... So how is it socially? Do people here still keep strong ties to the UK or are there any cultural differences you've noticed? Well, there is definitely a mix of cultures here - a lot of Turkish influence, and surprisingly a bit of Greek among the older generation too. As for social ties, a lot of us expats do keep in touch with friends back home, but over here we've also formed a pretty close community of our own. That’s nice. I wonder, have you experienced any of the ongoing political issues here? As an outsider, I can't help but wonder what the local attitudes towards the division are? Sure, the political situation is still a topic of conversation among the locals. There's a kind of assumed tension but surprisingly, it's not overtly in your face all the time. People seem to have moved on with their lives. Of course, you notice it more when you're at the checkpoints or visiting specific historical sites. But in daily life, it's not really a central feature. I see, so it’s not all about conflict and politics then? What about everyday life here? Is it easy to adapt to, especially for a retired person? Very easy, actually. It's incredibly relaxed, and if you're retired, you've got all the time to settle in, try new things, and just enjoy the sun. The local communities are really friendly and warm. Plus, living costs are much lower than in the UK, which is a huge bonus. That sounds great! And the food? As a foodie, I've heard a lot about Turkish cuisine, but I'm curious what influence it has in this part of Cyprus. Oh, the food here is incredible! It's a fusion of Mediterranean and Turkish flavours. You get all the juicy meze, doner kebabs, and of course, the amazing seafood here.

I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen Grace's latest article on environmental policy? It's quite insightful. Yeah, I've read it. There's quite a bit to digest there. She's really diving deep into the kind of research on questions we've been discussing lately. You involved in anything similar in your research lately? I’ve been dabbling with sustainable cities and how they plan out their urban gardens. Our very own Norwich is doing quite well with it, given its size, but it's interesting to see how larger cities like London, where you are, deal with similar issues. Well, London's got its own set of problems. While we have more green spaces, our planning can be a bit of a mix. Some areas do a great job, but others leave a lot to be desired. Plus, with so much population density, even small improvements make a big difference. Absolutely, that's where good policy can make a real difference. You know, I've seen those tiny parks in some urban areas. They really seem to make a significant impact on local air quality and community morale. True. Where I lived in Shoreditch, there's a small community garden that’s the highlight of its street. Do you also think we can't underestimate individual effort in making a bigger impact? I do, but it's tricky isn't it? Individual efforts really need to be amplified through policy and larger, collective action to achieve anything meaningful and widespread. Like when I saw those community-based initiatives in parts of China where the government supports and the locals are enthusiastically involved – it’s quite inspiring. And yet the pollution levels here are staggering, despite all those efforts. I just saw the AQI today; it’s really poor. You were right to choose another city for this conference. Well, it was a deliberate choice to avoid the smog hiatus. We could sit here and complain all day, but it's a bit more complex than that. I read in one of the journals I follow that just because something is available doesn't mean people will use it or indeed want to see it as the default policy. Speaking of which, just look at this street here. We could put up more posters and bicycles, but if the local population doesn’t see the need or value or if it’s not connected to other urban planning efforts, it’s all just window dressing.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I made those shepherd's pies? It was a complete disaster! I clearly overestimated my potato mashing skills. I still remember! You really did try. Still, they tasted all right, even with lumps in the mash. I remember watching and couldn't help but shake my head. It was quite the comedy of errors. All in the name of trying to make dinner special... So, what shall we have for lunch today? We could continue my fine culinary tradition, or actually make something edible. Maybe today's a good day for a lazy Sunday. How about just having sandwiches or leftovers? We could save cooking for the usual dinner prep. Actually, that sounds perfect. I could use a quiet day. Speaking of which, I watched that new series on Netflix yesterday and it was quite good. What have you two been up to these past few days? How was everyone's week? A bit of the usual. We had a team meeting and it went on for hours but it was productive. I’ve been diligently working on some patient charts, while the kids have been practicing their exams. Yep, endless exams. Poor kids. And my week hasn't been much different. The new policy update has taken up a lot of time but it should really improve things in the long run. I'm glad you said that about working on patient charts though. That’s a very real part of your day. It’s easy to forget that sometimes when we only see the end result. Exactly. A lot less glamorous than people think. Still, it’s rewarding in its own way. The kids are really improving though, so it's nice to see them growing and learning. That's really great to hear! And what about you, what's new? Any interesting projects at work? Well, I’ve been brainstorming for a new campaign and I have a rough draft. I need some second opinions though. Can you guys be my sounding board? Of course! What’s the ad campaign about? It's for a new line of eco-friendly cleaning products. The challenge is to make it sound not too preachy and actually fun. That’s a tall order! How about something that connects to people's daily lives? Like, how it makes a small difference in their day-to-day that helps the planet?

Yo, mate, did you hear about that new bus route running through the city centre? Seems like it's meant to alleviate congestion in the morning rush hour. Yeah, I did. Thinking about using it. It's supposed to make it easier for students and staff to get to university. Though, personally, I’ll still need to catch one of the other buses to get home, but it might shave a few minutes off. That's a right good idea then, innit? Just hope they don't set it up so it goes past keeps changing backwards and forwards, like some of the other bus routes do. Exactly! Consistency is key when it comes to public transport. You're so right, just like the Cambridge University Press bookshop. Used to read there in uni but when I moved to the city for work, found they had this amazing selection of local authors and everything seemed so much more laid-back there. Oh, I know what you mean. Went there a couple of times during my postgrad. They’ve got a really good selection for all the English lit students and faculty. For sure! We should go there on our day off next weekend. Sounds like a plan. Speaking of uni, you saw that student protest? Wasn’t it something about the university’s research into certain technologies? Yeah, something about artificial intelligence or technology companies buying up too much influence. Cambridge is all about tech and innovation right, but it's got its drawbacks. Exactly. Young people are worried about the ethics and humanity losing sight of values through all this advancement. Plus doesn’t help that the chancellor is from those big tech companies now. You'd think with all the prestige and history, Cambridge would be ahead of the curve on the ethics, wouldn’t ya? Precisely. On that note, did you ever think about what it would’ve been like to attend Oxford instead of Cambridge? I often think about that. Accents are different there, aren't they? For sure. The influence of Oxonian is quite distinct. I know a few from there and they do sound so formal, almost posh at times. Lol! Yeah, definitely posher. I don’t think I’d fit in there at all. Clearly, Cambridge and its quieter, more laid-back vibe was more your cup of tea. Exactly, mate. I just felt more at ease here.

Ah, I can't believe we're finally getting out for brunch. It feels like ages since we've done something together. Yeah, it's been far too long. I've missed these lunches. What shall we order? You know we always have a hard time deciding between the salads and the full English breakfast, don't we? Absolutely! I've been thinking, maybe we can split the two? Sounds perfect. Did I tell you about this new recipe for Irish soda bread I found online? I never thought I'd ever bake again but it actually calls this 'easy and fun.' That sounds fascinating! My husband always talks about how traditional Irish baking is, but I’ve never had the chance to try it. I’d love to learn more. Maybe we can have a baking day sometime? Well, I can certainly discuss our dialect variations, but I'm no linguist. However, there's certainly been a shift in how young people use English now compared to when we were younger.

I keep reading that the Queen first took a ride on these riverboats nearly 50 years ago to celebrate the Olympics. I don't know, wouldn't it be better if we could just take a boat here instead of walking? That’s kind of you, but I preferred the exercise and the chance to walk alongside the river and talk. Plus, the River Thames has such a rich history, right? Definitely. It’s always fascinating how it is deeply intertwined with the history of London. You know, it's funny, though. They even had the invitation to see the concert with Eiffel 65, which was the big thing at the time. Yes, yes, that was big! We actually went there for a concert in the late 2000s. It's quite the landmark, isn't it? Absolutely. Despite all the initial controversies, it’s become a staple for big events. You know, it's still the biggest of its kind in the world in terms of dome-shaped structures. Speaking of big... have you noticed how difficult it is to equate British and American cup measurements? But personally, I find it less confronting traveling and not having to drive. I often think about the car culture in the US and sit back and think, do we really need all these cars on the road? And yet... we're just as guilty in the UK of having traffic and pollution. True. We need more investment in public transport or alternative travel options. For example, I heard about all these new initiatives for riverways and that they’re trying to encourage more boat travel along... True. But like the old Docklands Light Railway, it feels like they're moving forward slowly though.

Oh, did I ever tell you about's this stupid story? On the way here, I was caught in this absolute torrential downpour! I talked to someone who said it was down to that low pressure system that got stuck over here for days. That’ll be why it's been so bad. I was cleaning out my car and got soaked while I was doing it! He's just been obsessed with 'build a bear' since we went there a few weeks back. Yes, I saw it. And the look of pride on his face was just adorable. Though potty training is a different story. Still finding toys with... well, you know, wet surprises in them. Oh, yes. Toby's still getting the hang of it. I hope he's not the only one still using a potty. One side effect of being a full-time mum is that I’m running the risk of never leaving this kind of stuff behind. You’re right. I remember when I was potty training. It’s a bit like swimming in England; you never really know when to expect the next 'accident'. Speaking of, swimming lessons start soon isn't it? Yeah, Toby’s really looking forward to that. Just hope it’s not raining then… I do hope not. Swimming lessons on a sunny day would be nice for a change. And let the poor pool staff have one day off from mopping up after a swimming day, if you ask me. Yeah, and me with my phone! It's supposed to be water-resistant but I swear it's developing a new hobby of finding any droplet it can drown in. Ah, phones and water. Haven't we all been there? Either it slips out of your hand into the bath or you leave it on the kitchen counter when the kettle boils over. That's almost happened to me once. Luckily the kids caught it before anything serious. Speaking of the kitchen, I can't believe our fridge broke down last week. I've been so reliant on it for lunches and dinners. Oh... I know the feeling. Just don’t

I've been thinking a lot about our life plans. I mean, we've been quite comfortable and stable for a while, but I don't know, there's a part of me that still feels like we need to strive for more. You're right, there's always room for improvement isn't there? What kind of goals are you looking at? Career-wise, I'm thinking about looking into more mentoring roles. Teaching isn't very viable for me right now, but I've always been good with people and leadership. That makes sense. You've had quite a leadership role in our current house-sitting set-up, despite not being the 'official' leader of the group. You even organized those social gatherings when we first arrived in Australia! Yeah, those were fun. Though I have to say, being out of my comfort zone did take its toll at times. True. But it also showed us that we're good at these kinds of things. How about you though, any thoughts on yours? You've been teaching for a while now. Well, I'm at a bit of a crossroads myself. I've been teaching at the same school for the last five years. It's rewarding, but the work is repetitive and sometimes feels unfulfilling. Maybe I need to look into some extra certifications or consider moving into a different area within education perhaps? Sounds like a good plan to me. We’d have to do the content creation, marketing, and all that, but it could be lucrative and we might enjoy it. I like the sound of that. But I have to say, when it comes to side projects, I'm always wary about how sustainable it is. Understandable. Again, it's about balance. And there are many upsides too—a side income, the flexibility of working from home, etc. True. Speaking of balancing, how are you doing with our family plans? Sure, that's another area we need to work on...

I've been meaning to ask you lot about this. I discovered today that nearly every new person I've met this year is from out of town. It's kind of funny because all of you are from right here, you know? You mean because of our accents? Yeah, some folks outside this area say we sound a bit... rough, don't they? Or maybe they just can't quite place where we are! I get that all the time with my Yorkshire friend, keeps calling me "mate" at the most inopportune times. Like when you start talking about the MMU and he thinks you're saying 'mummy'! It just sounds like "mummy" to him! Exactly! But seriously, though. Have any of you ever faced any issues because of how we speak? I remember when I did my stint in London, a few people sometimes made comments about how we sound "rough" or "uncultured", but that's just silly isn't it? I’ve had that too. But you get used to it. I mean, it's just how we talk, right? As long as the message gets across. And it's all in the accent of it. There's something quite homely about a North-Western accent. Yeah, it’s comforting. Reminds me of home. But I wonder if that's why I sometimes feel like outsiders here... does everyone else feel like they have to keep adjusting when we’re the minority? No, I don’t think so. It's like Pokémon. Everyone plays and collects them now, but we were the ones who had to explain to everyone else what they were and how to play the first time. Now it's just normal. That’s a good point! You were right at the cusp of that phenomenon. But before Pokémon, weren't we all just playing and talking about gaming in general? I remember changing the world with pokéballs was the newest craze. I still don't understand why. But I know a lot of people who got into gaming because of Pokémon. It was one of the first times people my age were all into the same thing at the same time. Speaking of shared experiences, did you hear about the new tech they're trying to push? Yeah, the new apps for tracking habits or whatnot. I still thinking about getting a Fitbit just to see how much I walk but I'm not sure I like the idea of being that tracked...

Ah, did I ever tell you lot about the time I attended a football match at the Carrow Road? It was back in the 70s. You mean the one where Norwich almost won the league? Yep! Can't believe it was almost 50 years ago. The atmosphere was electric, even then! But Norwich didn't win, I believe, did they? No, they didn't. But it's always fun to reminisce. It's amazing how much you've seen. Sentimental value to those matches, even if they didn't win. Ah, absolutely! They say life’s all about the journey, isn’t it? Not the destination. True. Ron, you know how much Norwich FC means to the folks around here? Oh, it's more than just a club, it's the community, it's the identity, it's this... it's everything, really. Reminds me of when I used to take the kids to the local matches. They were all about ten, eleven then, really enthusiastic. They'd wear those Norwich kits and run around the park pretending to be the star players. Sounds like they picked up that enthusiasm from me, probably. Speaking of which, did you two catch the latest Norwich match? Not recently, no. Don't get around as much now. But I do keep up with the news, less so the actual games. It’s a shame though, Norwich is getting a new stadium now, should’ve had a bit more of a boost, really. Yep, hope that helps. New football clubs are often a good thing for local communities. Imagine having a full stadium again just like when we were young. Speaking of youth, did anyone watch the latest episode of The Crown? As a historian, I find those things fascinating. The Crown? Oh, I love that series. Always gives me something to talk about with company. I must admit though, I prefer this sort of sports talk... Don't worry, we'll get back to sports again. But really though, it's quite enlightening to see from a different perspective, isn’t it? Definitely. It helps put our little local games into context, the broader historical, social context. I've always liked how it's presented. Makes me feel more connected to history, you know? Me too. And having a lecturer right here really helps clarifying things. Ah, well, I guess that's one job from which you can't escape even in retirement.

Oh, Lena, remember when you kept insisting you'd never drop out? Now here we are, and I've actually considered it more than once! You're right though, Alison! University isn't all fun and games, is it? But I kind of regret not pursuing it full throttle just yet. You never know what opportunities could come from it, right? Absolutely! I guess we've both seen things change quite a bit since we came to Lancaster. Do you still think about home that much? You know, it's funny, now that I've been away for a bit, I miss the little stuff. Liverpool's pints, the accent in our local shops, just the general atmosphere. How about you, Falmouth? Was it really as idyllic as people say? It was wonderful, but you can't live in a postcard all the time, right? It also had its quirks. Like the beaches, though, those were pretty special. And it's funny because everyone here says "Falmouth" as "Fal-muth" but we actually say "Fal-mont". Oh, I can't imagine! That's fun. I assumed we pronounced everything 'properly' here in the North. Well, the Southwest can have some peculiarities. But speaking of dialects, have you ever been told that your name sounds 'posh'? I've had that before, being from Falmouth and everything. Oh yeah, I get that too! Lena doesn't sound 'Northern' to most people here. I've explained so many times that it's actually a Greek variant of Helena, but most people just assume it's the Lena from Limehouse or something. The stereotypes we deal with. Speaking of which, do you remember when we were kids and had those muddy shoes from playing in the Cornish countryside? My mum used to make us changing them before we came home. Oh, yes! Noonie’s had to deal with more dirty shoes than I care to remember. Remember when our little sister hid her shoes under the bed to avoid clean up? Oh, and the smell. It was like she’d walked through an entire bog just for fun. Did you know, though, that my mum still occasionally sends us care packages with those really fine handkerchiefs to keep our shoes clean during the muddy seasons? That's so sweet... I kind of miss our childhood, when life was simpler and less about exams and university troubles.

Oh, it's been ages! I almost didn't recognize you today. The last time we met was when we were both slumped over our laptops working on our thesis. Exactly! I was just about to say the same. How's life treating you after all this time? Quite well, thanks for asking. I took up a job as a project co-ordinator at a sustainable development agency after I graduated. It's been quite a challenge but also really rewarding. That sounds great! I've been stuck with marketing for Pearson, but I'm enjoying it. I have to keep up with all the new developments and products, it's quite interesting in its own way. Interesting, but probably not as varied as your project work. Tell me, how do you find balancing work and your own personal time? It's been one of the big challenges for me since I started. Honestly, it's a struggle. I've recently started trying to establish a routine where I leave the office by 5 and then dedicate the evenings to whatever. But that doesn't always work out, especially with the endless emails and work-related social media. Yeah, it's hard. I find myself often telling my team that I'm available to pick up work on weekends, but sometimes I just can't resist. It's like a habit to always be connected. It feels like an old habit we could've picked up from all those late night session we used to have at the library. And relationships and friendships can't help but suffer. How about you? Dating? Ha! If you'd like to know. I've had one or two people in the past year. But nothing lasting enough to worry about yet. I just tried to relax and focus on work for a while. You? Just dating casually. There's someone I've been seeing, but it's honestly complicated. They work in a very different industry so our schedules are always on opposite ends. I can imagine. Our lives have changed so much and it's hard when you're trying to fit relationships into busy schedules. Definitely! It's like we're leading parallel lives and only see each other in bits and pieces almost unintentionally. I love that we're still catching up like old times. Totally. We should get together outside of work more often.

Right, now I'm on to the next item. You know, online shopping these days. It's like a whole different world out there. Especially eBay and Amazon. You wouldn't believe the things you can find. Yeah, I agree. I've just ordered this new game from Amazon. It was on sale because it was being discounted. That's what I mean. Discounts can be great deals but you’ve got to be careful of false or knock-off goods. I've had dealings with it before with some of the GCSE papers I get. You'd be surprised how many people try to pass off fake GCSE certificates. That's crazy. But, on eBay, I’ve had a good experience. It just needs you to research and check reviews. Correct. Always check the seller's rating and read reviews. And be aware that even then, there can be some dodgy people. Yeah, I know. I always check the rating before I buy something. But, you can’t entirely trust them. Some buyers will leave fake reviews. That's true. So, it's a bit of a gamble. But when you’re buying from reputable sellers or with good seller ratings, it's usually fine. Exactly. I think the main thing is to make sure to buy from verified sellers or those with a lot of high ratings. Right you are. A good tip for you, always check the return policy. You never know when something might not be what you expected. That's a good point. I didn’t think of that. It's a bit like the real world. If you're buying from a shop, you've got all these rights as a consumer. But the internet? It’s a bit of a free market. More so with eBay. Do you think prices are better on eBay or Amazon? It's hit and miss really. There are some things that are cheaper on eBay because it’s like a large auction and items might go for less if there's less interest. But Amazon often has fixed prices and sometimes these can be lower than what you'd find in real life. That’s true, I see what you mean. It's all about the specific product and how many other sellers have it. Exactly. And sometimes Amazon can put stuff on sale and you’ve got to be quick because prices can change in minutes.

Ah, marvellous weekend so far, haven't we? The weather's been surprisingly kind; these May showers didn't come and spoil everything after all. Oh indeed, it's been lovely. I really enjoyed our little walk yesterday and the grass was still quite green despite the season. You took a lovely walk then? I was settling for the armchair and a good cup of coffee. You know me, always for a stroll even if it is just around the block. You should try it sometime. After a lifetime of factory work, dear, I think I've had my fill of walking. Might just stick to my armchair for now. Oh, oh, no need to be so dramatic! Dramatic? It's just being realistic. Alright, alright. Anyway, did you hear the news about the council plans to revamp the park in Mordern next year? No, I hadn't. That's interesting. Yeah, they're planning to make it more accessible for everyone and add some new facilities. Suppose it'll be good for the kids around there. Yes, it probably will. London's always expanding, isn't it? It's always something new, never still. Indeed. They're even talking about adding more green spaces and all that. And with the new tech jobs coming up, hopefully it doesn't become too overcrowded. Green spaces, jobs... sounds all nice and dandy but what about the rents? Seems to me, every time they make it a bit nicer, the prices just shoot up. That is a concern. But at least they're also planning to create affordable housing and community spaces to offset it. That's all well and good, but do you think it’ll really help? I mean, I've seen enough people forced out of their homes because of it. I agree, it's a tough one. They need to do more to protect long-standing residents and not just be a hub for more affluent newcomers. Exactly. As someone who's lived here all my life, it’s hard to see things changing so much. Sometimes I feel like I'm a stranger in my own city. Sure, but you know change is inevitable. The important thing is we keep any community spirit alive and work together to ensure that no one gets left behind. I suppose you're right. It’s just, sometimes it feels like youth and newer ideas are the only things being considered.

Yo, mate, got your Christmas plans sorted yet? Yeah, nearly. I've got to work on Christmas Eve and Boxing Day, but the rest of the time I'm free. Going to be involved in some local festivities and I'm opening the café part-time. But Boxing Day I'm free, I can definitely come over! Christmas Eve at work is a nightmare. But, do you have any ideas for Christmas food? I'm thinking of making a traditional roast this year. Definitely, roast or a big old gang of pies? I’m more of a dessert and pastry person though. But, nice to see Santa’s helpers always hustling, even if it is silly hours. True, it is quite the logistical nightmare. What do you guys make of the idea of having roadkill deer for dinner? [laughs] [laughs] Only if it’s part of a game and if it’s properly regulated and the animal isn't done out of cruelty, right? As for a fox, I've always wondered about that. Do people actually eat those? [laughs] No way, mate! We’re not that hard up for food! But, I’ve heard of people in some parts of the world doing odd things like that. Yeah, I've heard stories about foxes being part of certain culinary traditions, but I think we can leave those overseas! [laughs] [chuckles] Agreed. How about we stick to what we know and love for Christmas dinner. We can all bring something over and make it a potluck? That sounds like a great plan. I can bring some pies or pastries. Perfect! I'll bring this year’s special roast. We can all share the effort and the tastes.

Yo, mate, did you hear about that new car that's been making waves these days? It’s like an all-electric beast, and it’s apparently got silent mode which sounds pretty rad. What are your thoughts? Hi there! Yes, I've heard about the electric cars. I kind of like the idea because they're better for the environment. But I'm surprised how fast they've caught on, especially with the silent mode that makes them almost stealthy on the road! Yeah, truly fascinating how far electric cars have come! As someone who works in tech, it's amazing to see. But it's not just about the environmentally friendly aspect. I’ve been thinking about how such cars could influence urban soundscape. The absence of engine noise could change the way we perceive sound in cities. Have you ever thought about that? That’s a brilliant point! I never thought about it that way. The absence of traffic noise would definitely change the acoustics of city life. Maybe we could even get creative with how we use sound in urban planning? Exactly! It’s like, for example, in places like Cambridge here or even London. They could use that silence to bring back a bit more serenity to the city. But I’ve got a question for you both. You’re both quite educated, but I’ve noticed how different accents can change how you perceive a person. Any thoughts on that? Absolutely. Accents and dialects can often create stereotypes or preconceived judgments, perhaps unintentionally. Speaking for myself, coming from a higher professional background, I’ve often felt that having a strong regional accent, like a strong Birmingham accent, can sometimes lead to assumptions about education or socio-economic status. True that. I’ve experienced similar things. Just last week, I was in a meeting, and someone made a joke about my accent, assuming less serious side of things, which was a bit frustrating. I can totally relate. As an engineer, when I use terminology or technical jargon, people are more likely to take what I say seriously but as soon as I relax and use colloquialisms from Birmingham, my own city’s accent, suddenly I’m perceived as less capable. It’s weird, isn’t it? It’s unfair but true. I mean, having a distinctive accent should be a badge of identity, not a marker of intelligence or capability.

Yo, dudes, check out this new song by The 1975. I listened to it non-stop yesterday. It's like, the whole album is deep, you know? Oh, yeah! I really like that. It’s like, the way they mix those kind of electronic beats with some kind of grunge vibes... and yet it sounds so catchy. But have you heard them live? I heard they're coming to this big festival in the summer, hope I can catch them. Nah man, I'd rather watch them on YouTube. I mean, live stuff is cool but seeing them on screen with a good sound system – that's where it's at. Yeah, totally. Speaking of festivals, what about Glastonbury? You lot gonna be following it this year? Probably. Though I have exams soon, fingers crossed I can watch it without too much stress. True, studying for exams is no joke. But when it's over, Glastonbury would be great. It’s like, the whole vibe of it... I hope they have some cool acts this year. We should make it a group trip! That would be sick! We should plan ahead. Where should we go, while we're dreaming? Any particular acts in mind? For me, it's gotta be Arctic Monkeys. Have you seen their new music video? Ah, and maybe The Killers if they're playing. Oh, can’t wait for those. They're both UK bands, so probably, but you never know. Yeah, but doesn’t matter much if you weren’t born there. I mean, I kind of love how The 1975 do all these different concerts and stuff worldwide. More reason for us to watch a few online, maybe. Exactly. Speaking of acts, did either of you see The Smiths' documentary? I heard it's pretty good but also pretty emotional. Yeah, I watched that on Netflix. It was interesting to learn about Morrissey’s childhood and how that influenced their music. Right. I always take notes from how he managed to write such relatable lyrics even when the themes were so serious. True that. Also, let’s not forget pop culture. There's this movie I just watched, “Tenet”. Did you both catch that? Nope, but I’ve heard it’s a bit of a mind-bender. How was it? Sure was. I like how it plays with time and... stuff. I feel like my brain's already hurt from thinking about it, haha.

Ah, you two really seem to be enjoying that Balanceability stuff! You know, I've read something about how this kind of activity can help with a child's balance and coordination. Do you remember what we did in your class about it? Oh, yeah, we had a day when our teacher brought out all these weird bikes and we had to balance on them. It was actually quite fun, just like playing but we also learned. Yeah, and she said it's kind of like training for when we're older and do more sports. But man, it also made me realize how tricky it could be when you first start. But once I got it, it was cool. For me, learning this skill reminded me about succeeding at something for the first time. The feeling you get when you finally get the hang of something that was difficult. You must have felt that, right? It’s a great way to learn about perseverance and resilience, isn’t it? Like when you learnt to ride a bike, Mum? You were really proud and we all were really happy for you, even though we probably didn’t understand it fully. Yeah, and doesn’t it show that assessments weren’t just about getting the right answers, but about the process and trying hard, too? I don’t really like tests in school, but when we get into things like Balanceability or other projects, I actually enjoy the process of learning and improving. Exactly. It’s about the journey, not just the destination. That’s what assessments are often trying to test – not just if you know the answers, but can you think critically, work out problems, that sort of thing. Homeschooling for me wasn’t so different in that respect. Even though I was with you at home, I still had to learn to balance my own work and time. Homeschooling? What’s that like, Mum? Homeschooling is when we, or parents, teach you at home instead of going to a normal school. Some people prefer it because they think it gives more individual attention. But it’s not without its challenges – finding balanceability in learning while being at home can be hard. Yeah, I saw a school friend moving into a newly renovated house. It was huge and had a swimming pool and a manmade waterfall. Super cool! Oh, that sounds quite impressive, but also, what about safety, especially with the waterfall and pool?

Oh, did I ever tell you about my new gym routine? I signed up for this crazy crossfit class and let me tell you, it's been quite a challenge. No, you never did. That sounds intense! I need to get in shape for this conference that I'm organizing in a few months.
