Booked a yoga class for Saturday morning, then breakfast at that new café near my place. That sounds lovely, but not really my style. We’re thinking about going to the local park for a BBQ. I’ve been trying out some new recipes for a healthier lifestyle, so maybe I can take you two up on that BBQ but next time. Healthier lifestyle? What’s this? You working out? Not quite. More just trying to eat better. I’ve been trying out this new fitness app that tracks all your meals and stuff. Turns out, I was eating way more than I thought! To healthier choices then! Whatever gets you to the end of the week feeling good about yourself! Belated cheers! I actually think that’s brilliant. I’ve been feeling sluggish lately, maybe I should try out some healthier eating too. I can send you my notes if you like. It’s all about balance though, so don’t worry if you still want that extra slice of pizza now and then. Balance... right. I think that’s what I’ve been missing lately. Too much work, not enough fun. I agree. But talking of fun and balance, how are living arrangements going? Are you two still sharing... Yeah, still in our little house together. It’s chaotic at times, but it's home.

Alright, John, you were telling me about this eclipse thing we've been hearing talked about? Ah, the eclipse, yes! You know, I was quite fascinated by it when I was involved in some civil engineering projects, the precision required for such an event blows me away. Oh, I've got a keepsake from when I was at school, my science teacher gave us all eclipse glasses, and it was truly magical. Accusations aside, I do think we should be eating better, that’s what I’ve been reading these new health books. Ron, if you're going to start policing our eating habits, you might as well throw in complete freedom from work, social norms, and now healthy eating! I'm not so sure I agree about all that but fair point about eating well. I often think back to when we first started... Ah, no, no, let's not go that way. I was just saying maybe a bit less meat and a few more veggies; it won’t hurt. On that note, let's toast to functional successful retirement living! Speaker_1 & To functional, successful retirement living! Speaking of functional, our garden could use a tidy up.

Yo, mate, did you hear about that new restaurant that just opened up in Gracechurch Street? I went there for lunch last weekend and it was bloody brilliant! No, I haven't but I'm always up for trying new places. What was good? The food was top-notch! They had this amazing fish & chips that was seriously close to the best I've ever had. And the atmosphere was brilliant - really modern and cosy at the same time. Sounds good. Which bus would I take to get to Gracechurch Street if I wanted to check it out? There's plenty. The 8, 242, or the 35 bus would get you there. Or if you like, you could take the tube. Moorgate station’s the closest from your place, right? Yeah, Moorgate is right next to where I live so it’ll be a piece of cake. Great! Make sure you check it out, you won't be disappointed. Yeah, I’ll definitely look into it. For me, it really puts it on the map as one of my new favorite spots. Now talking of good food, have you noticed how often we still say 'chippy' instead of 'fish & chip shop'? Oh, definitely. It's like an informal term that just stuck, isn’t it? In Dorset, where my mum’s from, they actually say 'chippy' for a chip shop but we’re used to saying it for almost anything that’s "chippy-like" like a doesn’t-live-up-to-expectation situation. Oh, I've never heard that one! That's so quirky. Yeah, it’s just one of those funny dialect differences. I noticed a lot of those quirks when I visited my family last. For example, my cousin from Bournemouth always says 'bloody' so often, changing the tone and meaning dramatically. Yeah, it's like how I use 'brilliant' or 'cheeky' often and it just rolls off the tongue. Exactly! And if anyone uses 'standard' to mean 'okay’ in Bournemouth, be prepared. It’s like almost gone out of common use in the north. Ah, that's a reminder of how diverse our country is. Each region has its own little peculiarities. Spot on! I’ve realized this often while driving around. Driving down to Cornwall and hearing people say 'proper' at the end of sentences, like 'it's proper good' instead of just 'it's good'. How about you, ever notice place name pronunciation changes as you travel?

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I was trying to wake up and failed miserably? I set my alarm to let the dawn chorus help me out, thinking natural sounds would be more pleasant. Oh, yes, please share! Well, I was really committed to it. I set my alarm for about 4:30 AM, hoping the bird sounds would gradually wake me up as the dawn chorus began. And how did that turn out? Oh, hilariously. I ended up setting it to a recording of birds singing, thinking it's just as good. But then I discovered that the recording I chose included a robin, which was lovely, but also a blackbird that decided to imitate a car alarm. A blackbird sounding like a car alarm? Exactly! It got me out of bed faster than any alarm ever could, but not in the way I planned. I had to find a new recording or go back to the regular alarm. That sounds like something right out of a comedy sitcom. I thought the same! But then it made me realize how little I know about birdsong. Do you happen to know a lot about it? Well, I've always been interested in birds, especially their songs. I learned quite a bit about different species in my EFL teaching career. One time, we even used bird songs to teach pronunciation. Really? That doesn’t surprise me at all! I’ve always found the dawn chorus so beautiful and mysterious. Absolutely! I just wish I knew the different species. Sometimes I just hear them and think “ah, just lovely, another one I can’t identify.” Same here! But it’s quite fascinating, isn’t it? How something so simple as a bird can create such a complex song. It really is. And then there’s all these different dialects. I’ve had students teach me about the local birds' songs in their countries. I’ve always found that if you listen closely, you can hear subtle differences depending on where the bird lives. Yes, just like accents in people. Exactly! Just like how I came from Yorkshire and still have a bit of that in my accent. Indeed. You can never fully get rid of the Yorkshire in this accent, can you? True that! So, speaking of subtle differences, I recently started feeding birds in my garden. I used to have a friend who was an avid birdwatcher

Ah, it's been ages hasn't it? How was your job as a social worker today? I've heard it can be quite emotionally draining. It was the usual really. Mostly visits and meetings, some quite challenging cases to handle. But now, let's not focus on work – how about questions on IVF? Going through it gave me a new perspective on life and the whole thing about "success" and "failures". Now that you mention it, I was going to ask. It's always so interesting how it brings up such deep questions about when life begins, right? I suppose seeing your friends going through it makes you see parenting in a different light. Absolutely. And then of course, there is the added bitterness when people post their success stories on social media without realizing how much pain or disappointment someone else might be going through. Hence my recent decision to take a break from most social media platforms. I get you. I've started doing the same, it's just too much these days. I mean, people showing off their perfectly curated lives… Exactly! For me, it's not about what they post, it's how it makes me feel. I find the constant exposure has affected my self-confidence, while the 'like' culture has made me question my own life choices. It's like the highlight reel of someone else's life shouldn't make us feel bad about ours, but it does, right? It's funny how silly it can seem when you say it out loud but it's really quite profound when you think about it. I know. And then there are the constant debates about the benefits and the dangers of social media for young people and children, including mine. I don't want my daughter to grow up thinking she needs validation from strangers just to feel okay about herself. Totally hear you. I'm a teacher and it's even trickier in schools now. There's this pressure to be 'active' online and it creates another whole set of problems for kids. You know, it's especially tough for those who can't access it or don't feel comfortable sharing their lives online. Definitely. I’ve actually been thinking of starting a book project, perhaps on zeroing in on real conversations and experiences instead of curated posts. That sounds like an amazing project.

Ah, lovely to see you over for a cup of tea, Mr. Johnson. How are you finding these quiet moments after teaching all those students for years? You know, it's been a big change, really. I almost miss it now and then, but I also kind of do not. Those young folks kept me on my toes and made sure I never ran out of stories about grammar rules! I can imagine! I've actually been quite busy with my language school. We're expanding our online courses which has been interesting keeps changing ways students approach language learning. Oh, that's fascinating. Tell me, do you think the digital approach helps with the learning process? Absolutely. For some, online learning offers flexibility and makes education more accessible. However, in some places, access to the internet or proper tech can still be a barrier. Hence, we're also working on partnerships with local community centers to provide more resources for those who need it. That's admirable. It's always good to hear about people making it easier for others to learn. When I was teaching, I loved seeing the 'light bulb moment' when a student finally grasped a difficult concept. Definitely. Those moments are truly rewarding. You know, I sometimes worry about the pressure kids are under nowadays. The emphasis on exams and standardized testing can make it tough, right? Certainly. Well, technology can certainly help in equipping them for exams, perhaps even making some tasks easier, but it's tricky isn't it? Tests aren’t all that measure intelligence or understanding. That's a very valid point. Despite all the technology, doesn't change that we need to find a balance and ensure they still develop other valuable skills — critical thinking, creativity, understanding context, and so on. Right. Seems to me, there's a whole lot of focus on the end of the process — exams — rather than the joy of learning itself. Yes, that's a great point. There's a push to meet certain standards but not enough on ensuring learning is engaging and meaningful. It’s a big challenge. Education for education’s sake, not just for grades and tests. I completely agree, but I suppose that’s an age-old conundrum isn’t it? Indeed it is, and it’s one we can’t seem to solve once and for all. It’s like repeatedly asking what’s the best way to evaluate a student’s learning and potential.

Better to work out gradually and correctly. Still, they didn't take it very well. Hahaha, that's classic gym culture. Like they've been part of a montage from a 90s sports movie right? Although, it can be dangerous when people get too competitive at the gym, right? I've seen some pretty silly stuff before, too, but I guess exercise brings out the best... and worst, in people. Exactly, just like the weather recently, makes you want to stay in bed all day but when you feel the sun - oh, you dust off that gym gear! Absolutely! There's a golden hour sometimes, when the sun breaks through clouds, you feel invincible! Almost like you can grab it. We were planning on hiking this summer. Maybe we can find some weather on our side this time round. Oh, good idea! Where were you planning on going? We were thinking about the Lake District. It's always packed but breathtaking. Ah, the Lake District is gorgeous! A bit spiritual in there, feels like mother nature is all around you. Definitely. We might combine it with a music festival there. I saw that there was a fairly big one next month. It could be the perfect blend of nature and tunes! That sounds amazing! I might join you for that. But have you guys been to any other music festivals? We went to Glastonbury a couple of years ago, it was quite an experience. Oh, absolutely! The rain changing the whole dynamic of the day. You end up dancing in the mud, it's a bit more unforgettable for that. Glastonbury is truly legendary. And it's always fun to see the creativity people bring to their outfits. It's like a fashion display almost. Though, I laughed at the guy dressed as a cactus. A cactus? That's brilliant! Speaking of fun stuff for kids, have any of you heard about this summer camp that's... ... running DIY music workshops for kids? Yeah! Maybe Tom from Speakers 4 and some of his mates are planning to run some sessions, teaching kids to make their own instruments and all? That would be cool! I remember helping at a similar thing as a volunteer, the kids learned so fast and loved it.

Oh, did you see that last move by Sterling? I mean, what a goal that was! Absolutely! He's got unreal speed. You can't teach that. I really admire his pace on the field, even if he's not always reliable in front of the goal. Indeed, sometimes it feels like he's more of a sprinter than a finisher. But right now, he's on fire! So how about those Aston Villa this season? They've been performing surprisingly well, haven’t they? Definitely. I wasn't sure they'd do as well as they have, but Smith is doing a great job as manager. But let’s be real, it’s still the big teams that get all the attention. Hence why we're watching the EPL, not the Championship. True, but you have to admire the ethos of these smaller clubs. They’re always fighting against the odds. Yeah, it's really refreshing to see a team like West Bromwich or Leeds giving it their all, even if they're not the expected powerhouses. Reminds you that in football, anything can happen. Speaking of unexpected, let's spin over to the film side. What have you seen lately that's been good? Oh, I saw Tenet last year. I really enjoyed it, even though it was a bit confusing at first. Christopher Nolan is always working over our heads, isn’t he? Yes! But that's part of his allure, I think. And the visuals were just incredible. I just tried to watch the latest Star Wars. I liked it, but it's definitely another standalone film that seems to move away from the original trilogy for me. I'll probably be in the minority on that one. I really enjoyed the direction it took, but I do understand some people feel disconnected. Either way, it's good to see new stories being told in franchises we love. For sure! And speaking of stories, how about those Easter traditions back home in Birmingham? You know I love telling stories, don’t you? Well, in my family, we always did the Easter egg hunts and then we’d have a big family meal. Someone would always complain about the food being too much or this or that, but it’s all part of the fun. That’s exactly what happens here in Sunderland. My mum would spend too long boiling the eggs, and then watching as we scrambled to make sure we got the most eggs.

Ah, look at young Jack here, so little! He's all grown up now, just finished first year at university. Speaker_2 : You always talk about when I was young. Like this is so last year! But I want you to see where you came from, boyo. Speaker_3 : True, true. These memories need to be preserved, despite our little mate's grumbles here. Speaker_4 : And each of these little ones gave us so much joy when they were this age! What's in the next picture? Ah, here we are at the London Marathon! You remember that one, Forbsie? Sure, I've seen that before! The big city running races with silly costumes. Where did you all finish? We didn't actually run the marathon, but we were there to cheer on some friends. Though I must admit, it was an adventure for all of us, especially for you as a young lad at the time. And in another book, I have pictures of your first trip to Iceland, I think? That was a blast, wasn't it? Indeed it was. The geysers, the landscapes, and oh, the hot springs! More like your insistence on trying a cold bath, isn't it? Well, it was exhilarating! And what about the cinema trips? You used to love animated movies. Yeah, can we see those? Let me see. Ah, yes! Here we are at 'Finding Nemo'! That's funny! I remember the fish. And there's almost a picture of me falling asleep in the cinema... Boys and cinema, always an adventure! And don’t forget the fun fairs. The Ferris wheel, the candy floss... You were a bit of a daredevil when you were young. I was fearless! Maybe a bit too much sometimes. Remember the doughnut spinning? Oh, that was memorable! Groaning over, successful birthdays have been celebrated there too. Here’s your fifth birthday! Seems like forever ago! But what's changed is how much you've grown up, isn’t it? Indeed. Every picture here, every memory, it's a piece of our family story. So what do you want me to take away from all this? Well, cherish the moments as they come, because they won't last. And perhaps a bit of that fearlessness could still be useful at times. And maybe stop complaining about looking at old photos? Okay, okay. It's not so bad. Some of those look fun, actually.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we played 'Whisper Down the Lane' at Jeannie's birthday party when we were kids? That game was the most unreal! Oh, yes, I remember that! We were all so young then. It was hilarious and chaotic at the same time. "Pizza and jelly" turned into “a big, angry elephant wearing a hat and dancing in the garden”! That's exactly how it ended up. You two were always full of energy, making up the wildest nonsense while playing those games. It's amazing how much fun we could have with just a few words whispered into each other's ears. And how many times has this exact phrase "It's a small world" come up in our conversations over the years?! It's ridiculous, innit? But it's so true. You end up meeting people from all around, and suddenly you find out you have more in common than you expected. It’s especially delightful when it comes to food. The other day, while I was reading an e-book, I stumbled upon this recipe for a traditional English Sunday roast. Have you seen how many variations there are across different regions? It's like a small world in food, you know? Oh, for sure. I was just talking about that with a colleague from Yorkshire. 'Ey, you'd think we were talking about two different meals, weren’t we? Yes, and just the words themselves! A "bubble and squeak" for some, and a "stir-fry" for others. It's fun, but also a reminder of how diverse we are within our own country. True, but changing the subject to something more fun... You both might not know this, but I've taken up knitting again. Specifically, making little toy animals. Funny how a hobby from when we were children comes back as such a comfort. No way! You're like me with the baking. I've started almost exclusively baking British classics for friends and family. I swear, if I don't bake a classic Victoria sponge at least once a month, everything feels off. I remember when you two would spend hours playing with those toy animals we used to make with knitting needles and odd balls of yarn... Do you still have the old bear I made for you? Oh, that bear! I still have it, actually. It's very much well loved, although a bit worn out now.

Ah, so many sandwiches you've prepared, have you? Yeah, I thought we should indulge a bit, considering we don't have much else on today but just relaxing here at home. Quite right, quite right. I suppose we do get questions popping up in our heads sometimes, don't we? But never have the time to discuss them? Exactly! Like this morning, I was just thinking... I wonder how things would've been different for us if we had better opportunities coming up. You know, jobs, education... all that. Oh, absolutely. It's a question many of us from our generation often ponder. I have thought about that a lot too. It just seems like there was never enough. And sometimes, when I'm with the children I used to look after... They're all grown up now and doing so well, going to universities, working... It makes me feel a little envious, to be honest. Envious? But in a good way, I hope? You did well by those children, after all. So many parents were grateful. Oh, absolutely. I certainly enjoyed it and gave it my all. But when I compare... I just think, what if we had the means? Their futures would've been different; ours as well. Ah, come on, we mustn't dwell on 'what ifs'. We made do with what we had, learned to appreciate the little things. True, life is what it is and all that. And we've got each other. I don't mean to sound down in the dumps. It just is the nagging thought sometimes. You're not on your own with that. I've gone through days or weeks where I just feel, you know, that I lived in the wrong time. The world’s so different now, so fast-paced. Yes! It's hard to keep up and it feels like we got left a bit behind. You know, reading about all these technologies they use these days… I wouldn’t even know where to begin! I just shake my head when my grandkids try to 'teach' me about the latest app or gadget. I show them pictures on my phone and they go, "That's almost as old as you, grandpa!" Boys and their little gadgets! They're the future though. And we must make sure to keep up with them, if only so we can keep a bit of that connection.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to explain the difference between 'present' and 'gift' to my Year 4 class? They thought that if you give someone something, it's automatically a gift. No, little ones, a present is something you give on a special occasion! Haha, that’s a classic teaching moment! I remember when I had a class where they actually asked if fractals were a type of vegetable! Are you serious?! That would’ve been a funny lesson! I swear, the things kids come up with. I’ve always loved your teaching stories, Amy. It's amazing how much you've grown into this role. Thanks, Carol. It can be tough sometimes, but the kids make it so worthwhile. Anyway, what about you two? Any funny work stories lately? Well, not really work-related, but in a copywriting job, someone asked me to write a travel guide for Spain and ended up majorly confusing Spain with Portugal! Oh dear! That’s on the same level as 'fractal vegetable'! I’ve had some silly mistakes myself. The other day, while correcting assignments, I spelled ‘queue’ as 'cue' over and over again. It was embarrassing, but also oddly satisfying when I finally noticed it! A ‘queue’ of mistakes! Classic. Speaking of embarrassments, I recently realized I gave John, my neighbour, the wrong Christmas present. I mistakenly bought him a cat litter scoop because I was thinking of something else. Oh no! Did you explain to him? I hope he took it well. He was actually really good about it! He’s got a cat, so I told him it was a thoughtful gift for his pet. He even chuckled and said he could use it. But still, I felt pretty awkward. Accidents happen. I was on a similar spot once when I tried to give a colleague a self-help book thinking they were going through a tough time and it just turned out they were already reading so much self-help content they couldn’t handle any more. Again, timing is everything. How about holidays? Anyone gone anywhere interesting recently? I went to Devon over the summer with some friends. It was beautiful. The beaches, the countryside... it really is something else. I went to Cornwall last year for a bit of a work conference, but managed to squeeze in some beach time. The sea was so chilly, though!

You two are doing a great job at keeping this place so tidy, aren't you? Must say, I don’t remember the house being this spotless the last time we met at my brother's wedding. Aye, it’s a big house, takes time. You know how it is, when you've got a big family like mine, you learn to keep up. And now with Anthony at school all day, well, it gave us some extra time to get things sorted. That’s nice to hear. What about you, young man? You’re old enough to help around, aren’t you? Learned any tricks while watching us? Ah, I’m more into my phone than chores, but sure, I can help. It’s not like we’re at the library or anything. Fair enough! Can't blame you, perhaps you could help us set up for this afternoon’s Harry Potter marathon then? We’ve got all the books and we’re missing some good company. I'd be happy to help set that up! I've read the series like 5 times. That's dedication. Seems like the young man’s got his priorities straight! On that note, did any of you catch the recent news about ISIS? Scary stuff, innit? While I agree, changing the subject to something less scary might be wise. Like, how's your week been, Speaker 4? School's treating you well? School’s alright. Boring as ever. Harry Potter is quite the read. I've read them all with my kids when they were little. Do you remember how much the first book changed the literary world? Absolutely. The idea of a global phenomenon from children’s fantasy fiction... it was almost like magic itself. Magic's cool, sure, but literature-wise, have you guys seen the movie adaptations? I think the first one did the book justice really well. Well, Mrs. Robinson here was never much into magic and all that, but she enjoyed the stories for the children. True, but when you're a part of a fast-paced cleaning job like mine, you find joy in simpler things, like catching up on a good story. Speaking of simpler things and, well, joy... How's your health been managing with this job, Speaker 2? Teaching and being a house-keeper must be tiring. Oh, it's been up and down to be honest.

Ah, I hear that the Tour of Britain will be passing through our area soon. Did you learn that it arrives in Berkeley around the second week of September? It's been talked about at the local tea and cake social. Yes, I did. It’s just a few days after the Sports Day at the school, so some of the students and staff are already excited. But speaking of sports, have you heard about my daughter's progress training for the Iron Man race? She’s very diligent and I couldn't be prouder. That's wonderful to hear. She must be working quite hard. You know, it's fascinating, isn't it? Even at our age, many of us try to stay active and I’ve been training for a charity 10K just like my husband is doing preparation for the local swimming gala. It really keeps us motivated. Sports do indeed inspire. Speaking of keeping healthy, I’ve heard talk about the new school lunch menu being more inclusive with gluten-free and diet options. What’s it like in Berkeley? Do you guys have similar menus in your schools now? Yeah, we do. It's quite the challenge, but it's worth it. We've noticed it helps with the children’s focus and participation, especially if they have specific dietary needs. Plus, it gives them wider choices while still being healthy. It’s interesting, we’re seeing the same trend here. More attention to diet, allergies, and such. But did you know, I once had a pupil who was on a wartime rationing diet for a week for a history project? She gave us all a great insight, and it was fantastic for classroom discussion. That’s a brilliant idea for a project! I remember my mother saying how rationing during the war taught her so much about using leftovers, and stretching one’s ingredients. But the rationing was done out of necessity, of course. Our sausages won't be limited to a few a week. Right! Speaking of which, have you noticed how the Village Shop and the local Farm Shop now cater to all these new diets and dietary needs? I was there last weekend and they had such a wide variety of gluten-free products. I also stocked up for our trip to Nepal later in the year. Have you ever been?

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time during Grace's wedding? The caterers ran out of food! We ended up running around the nearby Tesco at 9 pm trying to find some backup. It was chaos! That’s hilariously chaotic, Laura! I had one of those situations at work where the whole production line halted due to a part malfunction. It was a bit like your catering disaster, actually. We had to call in an emergency CNC engineer from Germany at 2 am! Crazy stuff! You know, those kind of situations always make for good stories afterward. Yeah, I just dealt with a similar thing recently, but with a much smaller scale. We had a catering mix-up for the conference we organized. It was stressful, but we managed to sort everything out before the event started, thankfully. It reminded me of the importance of contingency planning... Absolutely. You couldn’t have planned it without it. I mean, those kinds of situations or even just the everyday work stress? I’m really glad I have my friends to vent to. True. Where would we be without the support of friends? Laura, what about your job as a conference and events co-ordinator? How do you deal with the stress? It’s always a balancing act, you know? A mix of managing expectations, dealing with last-minute changes and trying to keep everyone calm. Communication is key. For instance, when I was dealing with that catering issue, staying calm and having clear communication was crucial. True, and the skills that you learn from managing those situations end up being very transferable, don’t they? Definitely. I’ve had to deal with production delays a few times, and having to keep customers calm while explaining the situation is surprisingly similar to managing conference attendees who are worried about something going wrong. Absolutely! And it’s so important to learn from those experiences. Like, I was tasked to organize a conference for a charity event a few weeks ago. The speaker cancelled last minute, and we had to scramble to find a replacement. But because we had a list of backups, we managed to pull it off. Again, it’s about those contingency plans. Speaking of which, anyone know the exact date and time for the upcoming charity conference I’m helping with? It’s the 15th of next month, 9 am.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that online workshop I attended today? They were discussing brain training and memory techniques and how they can improve our work productivity. You mean the one about mnemonics? I heard about that, but I never thought of applying it at work. Exactly! But once they gave an example about using "P.O.O.R" to remember the steps for managing tasks - Prioritize, Organize, Oversee, and Review. It was so simple yet keeps coming back to me when I'm overworked. That makes sense. Prioritization is always the key, isn't it? But reviewing... that's often what we let slip by the wayside. Absolutely. And while we're on the topic of "slipping by," have you noticed the demolition plans for the Plumstead library? They're already announcing it on their website, as if it's a done deal. Did I miss it? How did it end up this far along without us knowing? Apparently, the council just started this process a few months ago, but no one thought it would be so swift. They're assuming most of us won't pay attention while the 'public consultations' are happening in August. That's really sneaky. And now they're saying it's about 'economy' and 'moving forward with the times.' Like we don't understand the need for budget cuts, but we’re talking about a library here! And what 'moving with the times' means is turning us into a digital-only society. It’s not the progress we need. Precisely. I don't understand why they can't find the funds or lessen their budget elsewhere, rather than erasing a community space. Right! Listen, I've been thinking we should start a petition. It’s about time we fight back. If we can gather enough signatures, maybe they’ll think twice. That’s a good idea. I was just on the Council’s website last night. They say there’s a meeting planned in September. We should take advantage of that. Yes! And maybe involve other community members. We need to make it personal. Share anecdotes, like how many of us learned to read here or meet friends. Perfect. Do you think we could also talk to the librarians or any local groups supporting our cause? I already texted Samantha and she’s on board. I know there’s a group that used to meet there for any community event...

Ah, mates, remember when we used to argue about religion? On the odd occasion that some Jehovah's Witness would knock on our door, I'd have a little fun with them. Made my day. Indeed I do! You were quite the debator, weren't you, John? But times have changed, haven't they? I'd almost forgotten those days. It's been a while since I've had such a lively discussion of belief and faith. It's always interesting how belief can shape our worldview. I've had my share of interactions too, although, as a childminder, I've always tried to keep such topics light, seeing kids are very impressionable. Light or not, it was our way of testing the waters of big ideas. But let's not bring the heat back. What about your marriage? How's things between you two? Well, we've made peace with the fact that we're just good pals now. It's worked well for us. We share the house, the bills, and the occasional hobby. It's a quiet coexistence. Sure beats the alternative! I've always thought long-term marriage was kind of assumed, but the reality isn't always so straightforward. Absolutely. It's a bit like our current lives, isn't it? A bit uncertain without the structure of work or family, but still comfortable in its own way. Speaking of comfort, anyone up for a bit of food and drink when we're done here? There's a new place in the village that's supposed to have a decent menu. Yes, please! I've been meaning to try that new pub just east of Norwich. They say their fish and chips are the best around. Only if they have a quiet corner for us old folks to sit. Last time I went to eat out, I ended up changing my mind because of the noise. Don't worry, Arthur. I'm sure we can find a spot. But before we leave, what do you think about voting? Ever thought of participating in the local elections? They're having one soon. Honestly, it feels quite disenfranchising when you're in our position. I get that. The system can feel disconnected. But even a little bit of participation can make a difference. Though, I must admit, I'm not too keen on the tax system either. It always feels like I'm paying for... well, not sure what most of the time.

Ah, marvellous to see you both again! It's been far too long. How was your trip to Tokyo? I've always wanted to go there, though talked about it less and less with each passing year. It was quite an adventure! The food – incredible, and the culture, just so rich! We had a logistical plan, but the best experiences were always the unexpected ones. Have you ever tried a proper Japanese log burner? Now that’s something noteworthy! Oh, I've got one at home, indeed. Though, it's mostly decorative, I think it warms the heart more than the room. And what's with this fudge from a London antique shop that just opened down the street? Your daughter said it's fantastic, but I'm always a little skeptical about new businesses making bold claims, isn't that so? She's quite right, I assure you. We've decided to splurge a bit and try out the new restaurant down by the river. But honestly, we're not sure about the financial side – between the fudge and the log burners, it's getting a bit costly. We certainly enjoyed some fine food in Tokyo, especially the traditional street food. But coming back to basics, we noticed the 'next door neighbors' are in a bit of a commotion about outsourcing to India; we can't help but chime in on their discussion about it – it's quite heated. Ah, outsourcing to India is tricky isn't it? Economically it seems to make sense for many businesses here, but it’s never simple. I always try to look at both sides: doesn’t India benefit from such global interest? On the other hand, I do feel for those finding jobs harder to find because of it. Indeed, it's about finding that balance, isn't it? Our old school tried outsourcing a few projects last year and while it saved money, the professors were not pleased about the loss of local connections. I hope no one outsources transcriptions to India; my nerves might not take it well. Ha! Well, I suppose there’s always something for everyone isn't there? And speaking of jobs, how is the school doing? The policy changes are quite the talk in the neighborhood. Yes, it's quite the challenge. The new policies are all about academies and freedom for schools, which inherently is a good thing.

Ah, mates, remember when first we's used to own our own homes; these new taxes and housing prices are a right mess, don't ya think? You got that right, John. It's just not the same, is it? We used to have a proper home back in Costessey and now it seems like a luxury. It's not right actually, all the young ones are struggling to get on the property ladder. And us... well, we're stuck in this limbo of never working and long-term unemployment, seeing all those new houses being built for commuters and not for locals! You're not just talking to the walls there, Emma. I've seen it too. And the places being built now, they're not even designed for families. They're all tiny and compact, just razmatazz for city workers. You're right there, John. And those tax changes last year, it seems like they never end, do they? One moment it's council tax, then it's stamp duty, then income tax... it just piles up! Exactly! And the prices of basics keep going up. You try going shopping and they're all about the 'organic this' and 'sustainable that'. It's all well and good, but at the end of the day, we're on a fixed income! And in my day, I built some of those roads we’re talking about. We didn’t need all these "sustainable" and "solar-powered" nonsense back then! You engineers always think you can design or build your way out of a problem. But let me tell you, those green roofs weren’t designed by civil engineers! Alright, alright, but seriously, what about our pensions and all? We've got so many of these new policies and schemes now, but making sense of them is like trying to drive through a fog on that new Sat Nav I got. That new Sat Nav, I thought it was going to be a real help! It's been more trouble than it's worth. Keeps trying to direct me to these back roads that haven’t existed for years. Ah, that's a reminder of my driving days. Used to navigate fine with a map and a bit of memory. Now I just rely on the voices in that little box. I know! And don’t get me started on TV. Why are all the shows so predictable?

Ah, I see you're trying to sort out this computer business. What seems to be the issue exactly? It won't turn on, talked to my Dad and he said maybe it's overheating or something. Is that possible? That could be it, oxidation and overheat are common computer problems. Any chance you updated the drivers recently or installed any new software? No, didn't do any of that. Even if there's a warranty, it's worth checking before we dive into it. Can't take your computer apart if we can simply return it. Agree on that but from what I've observed, warranties usually only cover hardware failures. If it's software-related, we might need to look into other options. How can we check if it's software or hardware? We'll start with the software side. I can help you look at what you have installed recently. But if it's a hardware issue, we might need to open it up and possibly replace the fan or anything else that's causing overheating. Wait a second, I think I know the right papers for the warranty. Shouldn't be a problem for most hardware failures, especially if it's under a year old. Oh really? That would be great, we could just get a replacement if it's under warranty. Alright, let's first try to diagnose the problem. Just to be sure, you haven't dropped the computer or spilled anything on it recently, have you? No, nothing like that. Good. Let's check the software then. Can you show me the computer? Sure, just let me turn it on again to see if I can get past the initial boot screen. It’s not booting past the initial screen? That doesn't sound good. It could be the motherboard or hard drive. Found it! There's a 1-year warranty from when you bought it from that electronics shop downtown. Great! So if it's covered, we can just take it back, right? Yes, if it's covered, we should be able to get it repaired or replaced. But first, let's try a bit more: if you have a safe way to clean the inside without voiding the warranty, maybe we can check if it's just dust buildup. But yeah, if cleaning it doesn’t help, and it's under warranty, I’d take it back to where you bought it, ideally with the receipt.

Alright, kids! As you know, Dad's made our favorite pizza for dinner tonight. How about we all promise to eat politely and not use our phones while eating, just like we learned in our dinner etiquette class at school? Really? We get questions on this kind of thing at school? Can we talk about handstands now? I'm pretty sure I can do one without landing on my head! Great! You two can discuss handstanding outside when you're done eating. But we should try to focus on eating and communicating tonight – it's important to talk with each other and listen to what everyone has to say. This way, we can hear about your day and what happened at school. Why do we need to do that, Mummy? Why can't we talk later? Well, it's fun for all of us, and we can actually learn something new about each other. Plus, good communication skills are useful in life. You will need them in school, at work, or even when you're playing games with friends. Yeah, like when we tried to make the fairy garden. We had to talk and plan. That's right! You had to decide where to put the plants and why, and that's a lot like solving problems at school or work. Like basic addition problems I teach in class. Can handstands be a problem we solve, too? Like if we're trying to balance? Actually, that's a great comparison! Balance is kind of like solving a problem, like subtracting to get to zero if one side is heavier than the other or less than the center point. Like the Loch Ness monster isn't real since we subtract all the evidence? Oh, I see where you're going! While the Loch Ness monster might not be real, discussing things and debating is a good practice of using our communication skills and critical thinking. Like, we can listen to each other’s views without just saying something isn’t true because we want it to be. So, can we have a debate after dinner about the Loch Ness monster? I think that's a brilliant idea! But remember, it's about listening to each other's viewpoints and sharing information, not just thinking you're right. And maybe finding out if this Loch Ness thing is... a kind of monster of the mind?

Oh, this weather is really nice isn't it? Quite a change from Bolton. I miss the rain but not today! Indeed it is! Makes a change from the rainy Manchester weather. You know, when I worked nights in the hospital, those clear nights were always the best – easy to see all the stars. And the stars here must be amazing. I've been reading about the project to build an observatory near here. Would be cool to check it out sometime! Yeah, that would be amazing. I've been meaning to get into photography. The Formentera beaches this morning were perfect for it – so clear. Speaking of photography, have you guys heard about the new technology they're introducing at school? They're talking about integrating A.I. in media studies to help kids learn different techniques in visual arts. Oh wow, that sounds really advanced. I mean, us getting a laptop for classes last year was a big deal. I kind of see how technology could help, but I do worry sometimes if it’s changing how things are done. Sorry, I’ve arrived late but just had to get through those immigration officers. Always seems to take forever. Don’t mention it. Travel’s always a hassle these days. Funny how it’s easier when you’re coming from somewhere as obscure as Istria! True. Though you know, the swimming pool at our accommodation here in Poreč is just fantastic. Been looking forward to a little relaxation after that flight. You just made it in time to enjoy the pool before dinner. I hope you weren’t too stressed with... ...the current situation? Everything okay? Yeah, just the usual. They are quite vigilant across the EU now, I suppose, with all that’s going on in the world. Oh, you mean like Ebola or something? We learned about that in history. Mm, similar. But between you, me, and the hidden cameras under the table, it seems more about regulation than health concerns. The world’s gotten a bit... complica... complicated. Well, as long as we’re all equipped for it. Speaking of complicated, have you considered your choices for next semester, lad? You know, new subjects and all? Honestly, still thinking. Maybe try some new things actually. Geometry seems interesting. It’s all about shapes and stuff, right? Shapes and more. It’s about understanding the world around you in a complex way.

Ah, mates, remember that first time I had to deal with that debt collector? It was like he thought I was made of money or something! You poor thing. You were quite the squeeze back then. That’ll be some kind of story. Do tell, John. But first, shall we have some lunch? Oh right, right. I always forget when we're having a good time. You two are too funny. By the way, did any of you watch that new TV show about the tractor drivers? Television wasn’t my thing when I was working. But I suppose it’s nice to relax in retirement, isn’t it? Indeed. After years of caring for other people’s children, sometimes I just want to watch a show that doesn’t involve creative bedtime stories or playing hide-and-seek. You two should catch up on those next time we have a gathering. But speaking of gatherings, are we still on for that party this weekend? Yes, we’re on for this Saturday. I’ve already sent out some reminders. It’s at 4, as agreed. Well, then! Should we make a playlist or something? Why not? We can even practice singing those songs for the Church competition next month. You and your singing, Bertha. Always aiming for the heights. Well, it’s good for the soul, isn’t it? Indeed it is. I’ve always enjoyed your music at the Church. Thanks, John. It does bring me joy. While you’re planning party arrangements, I’ve also been thinking about my driving test. It’s been a while since I’ve driven out of this village. Well, it’s never too late to start. If you need someone to practice with, just let us know. You’ll be driving like a pro in no time, John. Maybe even faster than when you were 20. Don’t make me regret my years on the road, Alice. You're right, we should practice while we still can. We don’t know when we might need to go somewhere impromptu. Like last week when I needed to pick up a batch of seeds for my garden. Oh, your garden is flourishing at the moment! Yes, I’ve been getting some good tips from the community garden club. That’s great, Em. I might take a leaf out of your book for my own garden.

Ah, I thought that case was interesting today. The first one's conclusion was fascinating. Oh, really? I wasn't able to follow it all, to be honest. Got distracted by various matters here. Yes, it was quite the case, wasn't it? It's questions like this that make me appreciate the complexity and nuance of the justice system. Absolutely. I've seen cases where right appears very clear, and others... well, it's very grey. Indeed. As a language teacher, I sometimes use case studies in my class, ethical dilemmas and such. It helps to keep things relevant for the students. Does work intrigue you sometimes? You're not just a teacher, but a bit of a social worker as well, given the nature of the court. Well, yes. You meet all sorts of interesting people here. On some days it's quite uplifting to see resolutions, on others, it can be very heavy. Absolutely. I imagine it must take a lot of emotional resilience. Yes, it does. For me, it's a way to contribute, see the system work. Not always perfect, as we know, but most days it seems to do what it's meant to. It must be challenging to balance work, given you're part-time now, isn't it? Yes, I'd say that's the hardest part. But it's manageable. I've got time for my grandkids when they’re here, and a bit of help with the garden and stuff. That sounds like a good balance. I'm in that stage of life myself; finding the right balance between work and all else can be tough. Yes, definitely. I do miss teaching a bit, though. Do you ever regret not pursuing further education? No, not really. My family didn’t encourage it much, but I was happy with my life. You know, working, getting married, kids. Plus, by the time I was of an age, it was also not as standard for women to go further in education, especially out in the Highlands. I see. Back then, social influences played a much bigger role, and education wasn't as accessible. That's almost unimaginable now. You're right. I'm just glad my girls made different choices. One's a doctor, the other's a teacher! That's wonderful! Education has opened so many doors for them, I suppose. Indeed. And it’s opened doors for me too, in a different way.

Alright, kids! Let's move on from happy poems and talk about something a bit more serious. What does it mean to you to be "rich"? To have lots and lots of money so that we can buy anything, like a treehouse in the back garden! And a trampoline! A very big one, with a safety net so we won't fall off! That sounds like a lot of fun! But money is not just about buying things, you know. It's also about feeling safe, having enough for food, a nice house, and even for fun stuff like going on holiday or visiting the museum in London. Do you have lots of money, Miss? Well, we have enough to live comfortably and enjoy some nice things, but I wouldn’t say we’re "rich" in the sense that we have millions in the bank. But we're very lucky and grateful for what we have. So, it's not just about having a lot of money, but also enjoying what we have? Exactly! Being "rich" doesn't always mean you have loads of money. It's about appreciating the things you do have, like our family time, our health, and being able to do things we love. Yeah, like being happy! We can be happy even if we don’t have all the things from your list. That's a very wise point! Happiness isn't just about things or money. But it's good to recognize the value of money as well, so we can use it wisely and be thankful if we do have more than the basics. So, if being rich is just about being happy, then are we already rich? We’re happy right now, playing with toys! Well, you kids are rich in happiness! But as you'll learn as you grow, there are also responsibilities that come with having resources, such as helping others or supporting causes you care about. That means if we are happy, we can make other people happy too? Absolutely! Again, very good thinking. Happiness can be almost like a droplet of water in the ocean—one droplet might not seem like much, but if you gather enough droplets, you can create a wave of happiness around you. And sometimes, thinking about others and helping them can bring us even more happiness. I like that. So, being rich... is kind of any of the things we already have that make us happy, like our family and playing together?

Yo, mate, did you hear about that Chinese tech company that's making waves these days? They've just filed for what's called a "patent" for a new type of solar panel. Yeah, I saw that. I think it’s just the next big thing. If they get it right, it could be a game changer for energy and could make them even richer than they already are. For real, China is just chomping at the bit for innovation and tech now. They've really become a powerhouse in tech and manufacturing alongside the US. Definitely, and it's not just tech. They're also really active in the global markets and investments, despite the trade wars. Exactly, but what about the rest of us? Should we be following in their footsteps or do we need to focus on our own thing? Well, the UK has its own strengths too, right? London is a hub for fintech, there's a lot of focus on green tech. And it seems like the world is moving towards sustainability, climate change and all that. For sure, and this is where we come in as the next generation. What do you think we can do with this? Should we be focusing on tech while the 'Rae is still hot in the UK, at least? Maybe, but we should also look at what we're actually good at or what we're passionate about. I mean, I love tech, but maybe we should also consider fields in science or engineering because they're key to all of these innovations, and they might lead to our own "Eureka" moment. True that, it's not just about the money though. If we're passionate and good at something, that could be our niche or even lead to an invention of our own. Maybe we can get our own patent one day! I'd like that, but first, we need to figure out what we can actually contribute. So you're saying we need a business idea, something unique that solves a problem and we can patent it? Exactly. What’s the one problem in everyday life that you always complain about or see that could be fixed? Hmm, for me it's waste. The amount of waste we generate as a society and how it could be reduced. Maybe something like a smart bin or a new material that breaks down plastic faster?

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we went skiing with the kids? It was absolute chaos! The kids kept falling over, and I was so worried someone would get hurt. I remember now, the mountain was so crowded that day! We had a hard time finding them at one point and ended up having to wait in line for about 15 minutes to get a lift back up. Absolutely, and then Sam got very upset about not getting his turn on the lift right away. You know how he can be... Oh, absolutely! He's such a character, but I love him for it. He's got a lot of energy, that one. Anyway, I've been thinking - do we want to try and go to a less crowded area today? Maybe the upper slopes? It seems to be more quiet up there. That seems like a great idea, actually. I've heard good things about it. Let me just check the weather forecast real quick... ...and it looks like there's a slight chance of snow showers this afternoon, but nothing too severe. That's good news then, I think? Suppose we can plan for the upper slopes later today. Yep, and while we're at it, shall we also consider skipping the apres-ski plans we had? I noticed the lineup for that bar is silly long and we could use the rest for a bit. I'm all for skipping that and just spending the evening relaxing at the hotel doesn't sound bad at all. Exactly. Just food and some serious relaxation time sounds perfect to me. Seems like the best plan for today. Shall we also, maybe, check with Sarah if she'd like to join us at the hotel tonight or does she have other plans? Good call, but let's wait a bit - she's usually in a good mood after she's done her skiing for the day. She does love that hot tub after a long day on the slopes. Ah yes, the hot tub! And maybe we can all get a nice dinner at the hotel restaurant? Sounds good. Let's let Sarah decide and we can just make the general plan and finalize later. Perfect! Are you okay with leaving it wide open for Sarah to decide or should we plan something more specific? I left the decision up to her, but if she doesn't make up her mind, we can always suggest the restaurant or a quiet evening watching a film.

Ah, I see you've seen the bill for the last badminton racket stringing. It nearly cost more than buying a new one! This business idea of ours sounds much more cost-effective. What are we going to do about all these broken strings? Yes, the cost of stringing is ridiculous! That's why this idea could work so well. We could use something durable and cheap, like cable ties, but of course, that's just one idea. Cable ties? That's an interesting idea. They're inexpensive and flexible... but how would that hold up with the tension required in badminton strings? Good question! I was thinking of that as well. Maybe we need to experiment with different materials. We've got to consider dimensions, positioning, the weight of the racket... ensuring it doesn't affect the gameplay. Exactly! What if we mix materials? A combination of pliable plastic and some sort of corded material that matches the standard tension requirements? That could work. But we also have to consider costing. Cable ties are cheap but if we're buying them in bulk, perhaps we need to find a supplier that can give us a discount. And then there's marketing. How do we market this? We could target schools and badminton clubs. 'Rackets don't break, they just need a bit of TLC!' That sort of thing. 'No strings attached' - nice tagline, perhaps? Though we might want to avoid 'strings'... Alright, alright. But you're right, "no strings attached" is a bit too on-the-nose. Speaking of that, how would this service work for primary school versus secondary school? The rackets and playing style are quite different. Good point. Primary racket strings are thicker and more durable, so perhaps it would be less of an issue for them. However, we’ve had reports of younger players breaking strings just as often and it's always a bit of a disaster changing them. Hmm, so maybe we can market this as a more simplified, easier for kids to use, for primary schools. For secondary schools, we’d need something more robust. And we have to think about positioning and weight. Placing the ties in the right places could improve the racket's balance and weight distribution. We could also do trials with schools. If we can prove that our method doesn’t negatively affect gameplay, then we've got something.

Ah, lovely to have you all over here. I hope today's tea's to your liking. It's my wife's special blend, she swears by it. Oh, isn't it wonderful now, the aroma, it’s quite enticing. Especially on this kind of day. Speaking of, have you all noticed the new pictures up? I’ve been dabbling with watercolors recently. Oh, I have! They’re fantastic, especially this one here over the fireplace... I think it's a beautiful depiction of the coastline. It captures the essence of Norfolk quite well. Ah yes, that's just by the beach where we would take the children for walks when they were young. I'm glad you like it. My son, John, gave me some of that wonderful watercolor paint he bought from the town's shop. These are really good, similar to the ones we saw in this gallery in London recently. You should consider showing them at a local art fair. They could really appreciate this. Now that's a grand thought, but I'm just doing it for fun. I’ve never had any formal training in art; it's just a hobby to keep my hands and mind busy since I retired. But that doesn’t matter, Arthur! Creativity has no rules. And isn't that exactly what art is for? Personal expression? For the joy of making something beautiful, no matter the "proper" training. I couldn't agree more. Sometimes the best work is untainted by overthinking and just comes from the heart. Well, your kind words are more than enough encouragement for me. I do enjoy it whenever John comes over and we sit for hours chit-chatting about this and that, his ins and outs in his lectures, you know. Oh, yes, John often talks about his lectures in his history of art courses and how today’s students are always curious about the local influence of art on culture and society. Indeed. One could even say that there's almost a ripple effect of art in local communities. Whether it's the grand works we study or personal creations like Arthur’s. It all adds to the sense of place and collective identity. You know, it makes me think of how this house has always been... a kind of meeting spot for us all. We’ve had impromptu DIY art classes when the grandkids were younger using the garden for finger painting.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that one stupid client who today insisted that every report needed to be in triplicate and clearly highlighted in different colors? It’s like, the whole point of going digital is to save resources! Oh, that kind of archaic questions are always kind of annoying. You handled it well though. Yeah, I just played it cool and suggested why it would be better to digitize and use a cloud system for easier access and minimal waste. That’s great! Some people just really love paper. Exactly, and I swear, they looked at me like I just asked to use stone tablets. Well, you did well. And what about your day? Any interesting patients? One patient, she’s been having a lot of trouble with her anxiety and is resisting the medication. It’s a battle. Sometimes it's hard to see progress when it's so slow. Oh, that is tough. I've seen that before. The medication can take a bit to kick in and sometimes people get frustrated while waiting. Exactly. And it adds to her anxiety, you know? It’s like a Catch-22. Yeah, definitely, it’s a tough one. Alright, speaking of tough, help me decide what to do with this kitchen. It doesn’t look much like it belongs in a project coordinators’ house. It definitely doesn’t. Last-minute decision to wing it into spring cleaning? Precisely. But it feels overwhelming. Hmm, maybe we should turn it into a weekend project. I can help you declutter and organize. We could listen to some music while we do it, make a bit more fun. That sounds wonderful! And maybe we can do a little lunch-brewing while we're at it? You know, English tea and biscuits. Sure, and I can tell you all the things I’ve learned about mental health and language during my post-grad studies. Oh, please do! That could actually help me improve my professional communication skills too. And don’t forget, while we clean, I can bitch about my work too! Don’t worry, I’m an expert listener. Alright, let’s decide to tackle the kitchen on Sunday. Sounds like a plan! We can start by throwing out all the trash and seeing what we have left. Oh, and maybe I’ll put on a podcast about the English language. Perfect. I might even have some lingual anecdotes from my job.

I've decided I need to get back into yoga. I've been meaning to do it for ages. It's about time I stop being so sedentary, don't you think, Chris? Yes, you've been telling me that for years! But let's face it, we both lead pretty hectic lives and it's hard to find the time. I know, but we've been right here, in our house, for months. It's not like I have to travel far. Think about it, if we each get just an hour a day, we could manage it. You're right. I used to run a couple of times a week, just like that. Exactly! Well, maybe yoga isn’t your thing, but surely an hour isn't too much to ask. It's not that I disagree with you. But sometimes, after work, especially during the week, the last thing I want is to do another “scheduled” activity. Sometimes I just want to unwind at home or go for a pint. A pint, or a glass of wine? I’ve noticed you often unwind that way too. I'm the same, but lately, I've been thinking about cutting back. I used to enjoy the evenings with a drink, but now... I know what you mean. There's this pull to unwind, but really, it's not much of a vice, is it? What's wrong with a drink? Nothing, I'm not judging it. It just is the elephant in the room for us, and our vices. I mean, we both smoke and drink more than the guidelines suggest. I guess we're just products of our time and our stress. Exactly! And we are quite middle class, aren't we? We've got the luxury of having a choice. It's scary to think of how common these vices are, though. I suppose habits are just that. Funny how we just keep on doing them, because they're comforting. It’s all about balance though, right? Absolutely. Again, it’s about those choices. And yet... Go on. Sometimes I think about whether these things are more habits or really just flaws in our thinking. For example, I just watched something that said most alcohol is consumed by people like us - upper intermediate social grades. And... I thought, is our intelligence or maybe just common sense the flaw here?

Oh, did I ever tell you about's day at the farm today? The children were absolutely fascinated. Oh, really? What did they see? Well, the alpacas were a huge hit! They were so gentle and interested in the kids. The pigs were less cooperative, but the children enjoyed feeding them anyway! And the cows! They were so big! Yes, they were. Emily actually wanted to try and ride one! That's such a typical Emily thing. Absolutely, but to be fair, she's five. Her sense of scale isn't entirely developed yet. What about the children's behaviour? Was it cooperative, I hope? Let's just say, there were a couple of moments. But overall, they were great. They got a little restless by the end, but that's to be expected. They were so excited about everything they saw. They loved the tractor ride the most, didn’t they? Yes, they absolutely did. It was the highlight of the trip, really. Speaking of excitement, have the kids been behaving well at school, especially after this stimulating day? Now that is a different story. We have had some incidents and some behavioural issues. Lucy has been quite restless and getting a bit chatty in class. I talked to her teacher about it this morning and we need to work on that. Right. Seems like the energy was hard to contain after a day like today. Should we monitor their behavior or will it just blow over? From past experience, I think we need to keep an eye on it. You know how after a big event, it can spill over into other areas. I’ve asked the teacher for regular updates, and we might need to set up some after-school activities to use up that energy constructively. That makes sense. What about the other kids? Emily and Matt? Matt has been quite good, actually. Always has been a bit quieter but solid in class. Emily, predictably, has still some growing up to do. Today's company at the farm didn't exactly help that . So the farm trip was fun but the aftermath isn’t without its challenges? Exactly, but that's part of parenting, isn’t it? Figuring out how to balance fun and learning, and then dealing with the fallout. It's exhausting but worth it. I can imagine. We didn't have that many resources for such activities where I grew up but I remember the excitement of even small trips!

I've decided I need a new hobby. I have way too much time on my hands nowadays and knitting seems like such a calming one. You wouldn't happen to have some advice on that, right? That's great! I've actually taken up knitting as well. It's incredibly therapeutic and it's something to focus on. Let’s get into the swing of it, shall we? Yes, absolutely! I've bought some yarn and needles, but I need a plan. Do you have any simple patterns or projects to start with? Well, I started with dishcloths. They're easy and quick to make. Dishcloths, huh? That sounds perfect! Could you maybe show me how to do that properly? Of course, I'd be happy to! Let me just get out the materials we have in the study. So, where were we before we started this... this... magnificent tea and knitting session? I think we were just chatting about all the activities the kids have going on. With the new school year and all the after-school things, it's crazy! Yes, I know, but it's been great for their development. Speaking of developments, how is your PhD study going? Alright, I'm making progress. It’s slow but steady. I've been spending a lot of hours in the library. It’s great the university has so many resources, but finding the motivation to sit down and write can be... a challenge. Oh, I feel that! When I was doing my postdoc research, getting started on my first couple of papers was like pulling teeth. But once you get into it, you can sit for hours. Yeah, I'm finding that. Once I get into a flow, it does make things easier. I'm sure in a few weeks I'll be sitting in my bubble for hours. Sounds familiar! And speaking of bubbles, did you have a chance to watch the latest episode of Queer Eye? As a matter of fact I did! I love that show. It always brings a smile to my face and makes me feel uplifted. Me too. They inspire this really positive vibe... and the celebrities they've worked with! I mean, the reactions when they finally see the room transformed... it’s always like they've won the lottery or something! Yes, it’s great to see, and the way they handle everything with class and heart.

Right, so I've been reading about this incredible museum in London's South Bank. They've got this amazing new exhibit on ancient Egypt. I was thinking we could head there this afternoon. Are you still into museums after all these years, love? You must have seen most exhibits in London by now. Oh, definitely not! There's something about seeing the artifacts up close and learning new things that just keeps drawing me back. And this new exhibit, I've heard it includes some 3D and IMAX stuff. That could be really interesting. 3D and IMAX stuff? I thought those were for kids' movies. Oh, no, no, no. They're actually using it to bring ancient Egypt to life, making it feel much more immersive. They've recreated some of the tombs and even the process of mummification using 3D technology. It's supposed to be quite impressive. That sounds fascinating, love. I've always been interested in history, even though it was never my strong point in school. Maybe it will help me understand things better. That's the beauty of museums and this technology, isn't it? Anyone can come and learn about anything. Plus, the IMAX portion will show some of the world's most incredible structures. They've even included footage of the Great Pyramid and other things we can't normally walk through. And how about transportation? How do you want to get there? A tube ride right into the heart of the South Bank should be convenient. The tube is the easiest, I think. We could get the Jubilee line from here and it's likely to be fairly quiet on a Sunday afternoon. Just need to plan for possible delays due to engineering work or whatever. We can check the Transport for London app or website beforehand to check for any updates. As someone who lived in the area for a while, I can tell you that whenever there's a museum or exhibit, it's usually busier than regular Sundays, but still manageable. Good idea, love. I checked the museum’s website, they’re expecting a bit of a crowd because of the new exhibit. I suppose we should probably get there a bit earlier if we want to beat the rush. And if we're going to a museum on a Sunday afternoon, we’ll need to be prepared for kids.

Right, so I'm going to suggest we have a first round's egg nog ready when everyone arrives. It's a nice way to kick off the evening, don't you think? You're right, that's quite a nice touch. A nod to tradition without being too heavy-handed. We should also have some Prosecco and beer for the more... adventurous among us. Absolutely. I've also thought about suggesting a potluck. I know we're not too fond of complicated menu planning when we're all coming together. Plus, people would get to bring a bit of their own home, you know? True, it's a great idea. It's also more relaxing for the host. Though, let's make it a bit flexible. Say, the main course can be something we can share, like a big roast or a well-done turkey. And individual dishes could add a variety. Yes, and with the potluck, everyone can bring something they're skilled at, so the spread will be good. And it'll save me from being the sole cook on the day! That's wise. So who can bring what? You and me can handle the main dish, right? I was thinking that. I can take care of the turkey and maybe the stuffing. You could do the roast veg, right? You're always the one making the best roast carrots! I'd be glad to. You're right, it's one of my specialties. Who else is coming? We should finalize the guest list soon. Let me get my phone. I was thinking myself, my wife and the kids, your wife and the kids, and maybe Sarah and her partner, and Emily. That's if she’s planning to visit. She usually does try to make it. We won't finalize the list without checking with her though. And maybe a quick text to see if John can make it? It's been ages since we've caught up. Good idea. You can send the text while I check if there's a good movie playing next Friday? I thought it might be nice to cap off the evening with a family movie night, something everyone can enjoy. That sounds like a plan! The kids would love that. And for the movie, how about 'Home Alone'? It's a classic, and it's never fails to get everyone in the mood for Christmas.

Yo, you hear about that one reviewer on Twitter who was complaining about our local bakery today? The one that didn’t even try the bread before leaving a one-star review talked about how it was under-fired. You can’t even get a bad loaf occasionally. It’s just people taking their anger out online these days. Oh, I saw that. It’s crazy how people can be so brutal on social media without even checking the facts. I mean, I've actually worked as a baker before, and it's very easy for things to go wrong if you’re not experienced. That whole 'under-fired' comment just shows they know nothing, doesn’t it? Totally, just like those absurd negative reviews on our café from a few months ago. Someone accused us of purposely making their coffee cold. It was actually the sample from the coffee maker that didn’t even make it to the customer. Hence, we have a new system now, so it doesn’t happen again. It’s just wild how some people can't even spot their own mistakes and instead opt for trolling. But at the end of the day, that’s the internet for you, isn’t it? For every supportive review, you get one bad one from someone who just liked complaining. I think most of us should know better now to take everything online with a grain of salt. But the problem is people genuinely believe it because, you know, it’s on ‘the internet’. And then there's the design aspect, have you guys seen those new commercials for Margate’s rebranding? It’s all about trying to appeal to that younger crowd, which is cool and all, but sometimes feels like they overdo it. Yeah, that's a hell of redesigning the whole image of a place. It’s good that they're trying to appeal to different groups but it can feel a bit forced. Seems like the commerce commission try to make it a bit too vibrant. I actually think it's necessary to keep up with the times. But at the end of the day, you really need to know your core customer base. I read somewhere online that Margate is actually getting a lot of attention from young professionals wanting to escape the city, so maybe it's working? I know a few people who actually moved down there from London, looking for a quieter life.

Oh, did I ever tell you about the time I was trying to get Oisin to eat more vegetables? He was such a hard nut to crack back then. Speaker_2 and Speaker_3, remember? Oh yes, Oisin's vegetable aversion is legendary. What happened? Did you make a "Popeye" healthy food commercial out of it? Close! I set up a reward chart for him. Each time he ate a whole portion of vegetables at dinner, he got to put a sticker on it. It started to work wonders until he figured out the sticking part was more exciting than the eating part. I read that actually, a good way to get kids to eat veggies is to mix them into things they like. Like hiding them in smoothies, or baking them into muffins. That's a great idea! Maybe we can try that with the raspberries in the garden next. That's brilliant, dear! We could make a mixed berry smoothie for dessert. It'll be healthier than ice cream, and most importantly fun! Ooh, and we can even ride bikes to the local farm on the weekend to pick fresh berries ourselves. That sounds like a great plan. It'll be a fun family activity, and maybe get you off your video games for a bit. That sounds like a lovely idea. But it's not just about the fun though, right? The food we eat is important too. I've started doing some small gardening in the back yard. Seems to be helping, seeing those tiny leaves turn into real fruit. That's wonderful! Gardening is a great way to learn about where food comes from. It's also great exercise and relaxing. I always found it soothing to tend to my little patch of herbs and vegetables when I was prepping for exams or stressed out from work. You had exams? As a teacher, did you have to study too? Oh, all the time! But it was worth it. I loved my postgrad studies. There's something about the feeling of being around books and knowledge all day that really fueled me. Totally makes sense. I remember when I was in school, we had to write about where our food comes from for a project. That's when I first thought about the importance of locally grown food. That's so great that they're teaching these kinds of things in school these days.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that eyebrow disaster I had today? I grabbed the tweezers and was about to start when suddenly, I realized I didn't know if I had any plucking skills left—or if I really understood proportion. Still, now, the only reaction from the boss when I walked into the meeting was: "What's with the eyebrows, Sarah?" Oh, dear! That's a right eyebrow story! I hope no one mistook it for a new fashion trend. But even if they did, I bet it didn't look like it belonged in Vogue! True! But seriously, have you seen any good deals at the grocery store this week? We need to do our shopping soon. Oh, actually, while I was at the supermarket yesterday, I noticed Lidl had this amazing special on fresh vegetables and they also had some really good deals on meat. It might be worth checking out. Ah, yes, Lidl usually does have good deals, especially on the meat. But be careful with the meat prices this time of year, they can be a bit off sometimes. That's a good point, Gran. I'll definitely keep an eye on that. Also, how’s everything going with the help around here? I noticed the last time I was here, it seemed like there's a lot of cleaning to do. Anything I can do? Oh, thank you for suggesting that, really. To be honest, we’re managing, but a bit overwhelmed. With me working and trying to help you out, doesn’t leave much time for it. It’s great the lads from the community center have been offering a hand but it’s all so time-consuming. Right. Well, let’s see what we can figure out. Maybe we can set up a schedule for everyone to pitch in whenever they can. And perhaps I can bring over some extra hands next time I visit. Also, and this is a bit off-topic, but changing the subject—does anyone know a good hairdresser nearby? I need a haircut badly. You know, there’s a salon down by the high street run by Helen. She’s been doing family’s hair for years. You know, for what it’s worth, those eyebrows of yours could almost use a few trimmings to match. Ah, Nana, that’s not what Sarah needs right now!

Oh, did I ever tell you about that online sign language class I signed up for? Decided that since little Timmy is starting to make sounds, might as well learn proper signs to help him express more complex thoughts. No, you didn't mention that. Going to teach him and us at the same time eh? Exactly! There's nothing like the pride of being able to communicate with him truly before he can speak. But even if keeps coming backwards, still a useful skill to have. You'll need it if you're around him as much as I plan on enrolling you in! You're not just looking to teach him sign language, you're looking to make sure there’s no language barrier between us either, are you? Something like that!
