They think it’ll make us better readers or something. But, it’s not just about the books. In one of our classes, they asked us about this really difficult topic - hmm, I think it was... about military history or the war, I can’t remember exactly.

Yo, have you seen that new film "17 Again"? We've been planning to watch it; it sounds pretty cool. It's about a guy who goes back to his teenage years, don't you think that would be just insane? Yeah, it does sound really interesting, but I kind of regret watching it because it kind of makes me feel nostalgic for when I was younger. But, I guess that's the point of the film, right? Exactly! It does feel like a very secondary school vibe movie even though it is about high schoolers. You know, it kind of reminds me of some of those English lessons we had. I remember when our English teacher made us read "The Catcher in the Rye". Oh yeah, I was about to say that. That book was pretty big in our English lessons. And the way our teacher discussed it was pretty stellar. I never thought I would enjoy a book about a rebellious teen so much. True. But, English lessons are over now, and our physics teacher is on his game. You know, for the upcoming exam, right? Definitely. I'm a bit nervous about it, to be honest. The new teacher is nice, but some concepts are pretty hard to grasp. I feel you. Like, how he tried explaining the concept of projectile motion the other day was a bit confusing for me. Yeah, but he is really determined to help us understand, you know? And I actually found the practice booklet really helpful. I'm glad you said that 'cause that might help me too. I was thinking of asking him after class if he could go over it with me again. You should totally do that. We can even prep together before the exam or join a study group if you want. That's a great idea. Speaking of our prep, have you checked out the recent school stories by Roald Dahl? Mr. James handed us a copy in class. Oh, sure. I was going to read it over the weekend. I heard it’s quite good for our age group. Absolutely. Stories about school and so much more. It’s fun to see that even though the themes are 50 years old, they still relate to some of the issues we deal with today. Totally. You know, it also makes you think about people at school and how certain situations still ring true across generational lines.

Yo, mate, did you hear about James' latest trip to Transylvania? I mean, what the heck was he even thinking? Oh, talked to him recently. He was like on cloud nine about it, you know? Saying vampires and haunted castles were his kind of drama. Sounds like the kind of story he'd totally spin. But, seriously, how did he even organise that trip? He's not exactly known for his travel planning skills. Yeah, keeps coming up with these spontaneous ideas. Last time was a trip to the countryside, looking for mythical beasts. Says it’s his way of getting out of the urban grind. I guess that's just him. You know, city boy stuck in the countryside, ends up wanting to escape into the wild or the old world. Speaking of city, I had one heck of a week. Ron, the new guy in the bakery, barely speaks English. We're still figuring out how to communicate. Almost ordered him to make a "scone" and he took it as "scone? I’m this close to just making you one!" Oh, poor Ron. I'm sure he’s doing his best. I once tried to explain what "queue" means to my Aussie cousins and we were there, you know, like, at a bus stop or something, and they just looked at me like I’d been speaking Klingon. Yeah, really missed that one time when we’re trying to get a coffee and said "flat white" and the barista asked us if we meant a "flat white person"? Classic. I mean, we've got all these quirky Australian words and the Brits just look at you like you’ve sprouted an extra head. But hey, at least we are known for our warm hospitality. Speaking of which, we are planning a vacation this summer and wanted some advice. Have you guys considered changing the plans to something more... adventurous? Like a road trip maybe? A road trip would be epic! Imagine having a full car of just our laughter and arguments over music playlists. Oh, the arguments would be intense. But, yes, it sounds good. Just need to decide where... Maybe... somewhere rustic and quiet? There's a little place near the coast that has the most amazing views. Could be really chilled. Oh, that sounds lovely. Someone mentioned there's a little café there that serves the best scones ever.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that party we had last weekend? The playlist was epic, and we all danced the night away! I talked to someone who said she really enjoyed the way we mixed classic 80s with new age British pop and hip hop. Did you listen to the new music from The 1975? I love it! I wish I could’ve been there at the party, it sounded like so much fun! Yeah, and speaking of fun, have you guys seen the photos from Thanksgiving? There was one where you were doing a crazy dance with [Speaker_1]’s mother - it was so funny! Oh, that was the best! I almost fell over mid-jig. And speaking of photos, have we made plans for our summer photoshoot? Ooh, yes, please! Can it be Alice in Wonderland-themed? I’ve always wanted to try that ever since I read the book. That sounds fun! I've been saving up for that aerial hoop for ages, maybe we could incorporate that into the shoot. Alright, let’s make it happen, girls! What if we do it at the local park? There's a muddy obstacle course that’d make perfect sense for an Alice-themed shoot. And we could all dress up, of course. An aerial hoop might actually help with the "fall through the rabbit hole" theme doesn’t it? YES! I love it! And can we also include playing all the time when we’re taking photos? We could have different scenes from the book. I’m good with that! I’ve seen some really cool photoshoots with kids and adults playing together while they’re dressed up in scenes. It’s so much fun to look back at. You both are geniuses! Let’s start brainstorming more ideas. What if we each pick a character to play from the book? I can be the Queen of Hearts, Speaker_3 can be the Mad Hatter, and Speaker_2 can be Alice. That sounds perfect! Can I be Alice in Wonderland-style outfit, but with more colorful and fun things, not so much like a fancy Victorian dress? And can we include those silly faces and funny poses? Definitely! I’ve seen this one great mud obstacle course where they had hula hoops and ropes to swing on. We could get all muddy and have a blast. How about we make a day out of it and have a picnic too?

Ah, so many topics we've got to cover. Let's start with the exam results. How'd yours come out, sweetie? Well, I'm glad you asked. My students are doing great and I couldn't be prouder of them! Speaking of students, I just got back from the parents' evening where one of the parents was quite concerned about the pressures on their child. I know, right? All this talk about careers and pressure even at our age is really stressing people out. Speaking of which, did either of you try those new driving lessons I've been tweeting about? Oh, yes. Sent your tweets to highlight the "sparkling city" as you put it, in the middle of nowhere. But yes, I considered driving lessons, but I gave up on that. Oh, looking for a challenging workout, are we? But honestly, I barely go out now. And these driving lessons couldn't compete with the tranquility of simply sitting in the garden and watching the world go by. Now that I'm retired, I've got all the time to just relax and enjoy simple pleasures like this lovely chocolate roulade we have here. Speaking of relaxing, let's also not forget the importance of play fights. Ah, the good old days, right? Though I feel we all still have our silly competitive streaks, even as grown-ups. Oh, definitely! Like when I saw that tweet about Norwich football last week, it got me thinking about the lads I used to play with. We'd always argue about who was the best player. Nowadays, the arguments have less to do with football and more with who has a better hair style. Speaking of skills we still value, or at least think we do, have you heard about the kids' love of Twitch gaming and changing hair colors? It's scary how much time they spend staring at screens. Face it, mum and dad just don't understand, do they? But, it's not all zero sports or outdoors activity. The school's been quite good about organizing sports and even the P.E. teacher agreed to lead a workshop on football just for fun. Yeah! That was brilliant. We even got to learn some cool tricks. But thinking about schools, I wonder what we all thought we'd be when we grew up. I know I wanted to be a vet... Son, I was thinking of being a football player myself until I realized my knees weren't quite as good as my skills at watching it.

I've decided I need to get back into chess. I discovered today that my dad's been playing Chinese chess all this while! I don't know much about it though. Can you teach me some basic rules? Morning, Linda! Sure, I can try. It's quite different from the chess we used to play, but the basics are quite simple. It's called xiangqi in Chinese and it's played on the squares of a 9x10 board. Each player controls 16 pieces divided into two types: “civilian” and “military.” I can help as well. I just had a class on chess variations and Chinese chess in particular. The game is like a war between two kingdoms. Brilliant! Thank you, both of you. And yes, I suppose this could be our little breakfast forum while we talk about it. Before we get into the rules, though, I have a question. What do you think brought about this interest in Chinese chess, Dad? A friend introduced it to me a few years ago. It's been a good way to pass time, especially gardening's not as fun during this cold weather. And while I'm gardening, I like to listen to podcasts and recordings about topics like linguistics or Winston Churchill. Though I must admit, today, technology is so advanced that sometimes I feel old when I see how people are using it. I know exactly what you mean, Al. I couldn't figure out how to transfer clips over through my phone the other day and had to ask my daughter for help! Speaking of which, have you guys heard much about Scotland's push for independence or the effect it might have on the rest of the UK? I worry it might destabilize things, especially for England. It's a complex issue, Linda. It will likely have quite an impact on the whole of the UK, and it's been discussed a lot in my uni. Many of my colleagues are from Scotland, and they have strong feelings about it. Some of them talk about it for hours. Personally, I try not to take sides because it's always difficult to fully understand such large political issues until you're fully immersed. Speaking of studying, I remember when I could have gone to university but... It's funny, job-wise, I ended up in services and if I'm honest, it's got its advantages but the sense of wanting to go further still stays.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that one student I had today? The poor kid was trying to learn articles and was practising using 'a/the' but his pronunciation was all over the place! I had to work with him for ages. Still, he was really determined, though! Oh, isn't that one of the most tricky bits for non-native speakers? Absolutely! It's not just about the rules, you know? It's the intonation and the context too... So how is your new job going? You've been at it for a while now, right? It's going alright. I've just had my first year anniversary at the school. The students are great, just like you said, very dedicated. And the places you get to see through this job! Teaching abroad, that's the life isn't it? Though sometimes you have to deal with politics and bureaucracy at schools too... Oh, politics! We recently had a debate over whether or not to use a new curriculum in English language teaching at our school. Some were for it, others were against it. Interesting! Yeah, it always comes down to what's expected by the government and the school board, while the students need something that actually makes them good English speakers at the end of the day. Exactly! Anyway, it made us think about how students' lives have changed. I mean, I remember when I was at uni, we never had to worry about student loans like they do now. Oh, that's a painful topic. I was lucky enough to have my parents supporting me, but the loan burden these kids have... it's unbelievable. I do wonder what it's done to people's decision to pursue higher education or not. I just wish the government could find a better way to handle it. It's getting ridiculous. Yes, definitely. And then there's the whole pension question. Have you started thinking about yours? Not really. I try not to think about it until I need to. But I guess it's just one of those things you've got to plan for. You know, being semi-retired, sometimes I wish I could go back and collect my pension earlier. Though the real job I dream of is being able to travel whenever I want and not worry about whether my car has its MOT. .

Yo, mate, what are you thinking of studying at Uni? We've got to make some solid plans before GCSEs. Yeah, talked about this recently. Honestly, I'm hooked on human sciences. There's so much you can do with it—psychology, sociology, politics, questions about society and human behaviour. You could argue it covers everything and nothing at the same time, but that's what I like about it. That's pretty cool. I thought about it too, but for me, it's either keeps coming back to maths. There's something about the accuracy and problem-solving that fascinates me. Like how mathematics applies to literally everything, even social sciences. True, mate. Maths is universal, like rugby—it doesn’t change. Everyone gets the same rules, but how you play varies. Also, making calculations on the field is fun. Haha, true! It requires strategy and quick thinking. But speaking of creative thinking, have you ever watched those educational documentaries that pair science and social sciences? They often use maths to analyze human behavior. Yeah! I was watching this one about how they use mathematical models to predict election outcomes or social media influence. It was sick. Right! So, maybe we can combine both in a way. Maths can be used in human sciences; you can't ignore the numbers when studying human behavior. Definitely, perhaps I could look into interdisciplinary studies where Maths is applied to Social Sciences or something like that. Exactly! That could give you a unique edge. Just like how we balance rugby practice with our studies. Exactly! Just last weekend our coach said we've been playing too predictably. Maybe we need the problem-solving skills from maths to spice it up? Precisely! On that note, did you see the drinks menu here? There's a new cocktail called the 'Rugby Kick,' it's supposed to be quite a kick. You aren't seriously considering drinking one of those, are you? No way before 18! But for curiosity’s sake, what’s it made of? I don't know, but it’s a good opportunity to talk about safer alternatives, like mocktails. They often taste surprisingly good and less risky. Good point. Clearly, I need to learn some cocktail-making skills, plus it'd be a fun activity for us. Especially something healthy. Agreed. Maybe we could even book a cooking class that focuses on mocktail recipes?

Right, now I know this topic might seem a bit dry, but it's important you understand the basics of government policies and how they affect us. Especially when it comes to income tax and other financial obligations. Of course, Dad. I'm all ears. I do try to stay informed but sometimes it’s hard to keep up. Well, I'll try and simplify it for you. The basics of income tax in the UK is pretty straightforward, right? We pay taxes on our income, and the more we earn, the higher the percentage of tax we have to pay, up to a maximum of 45%. Yes, I've studied that. But isn't there a lot of controversy about the top rate of tax in 45%? I mean, even some of my students have brought it up in class discussions. That’s right. The controversy usually revolves around whether it's fair to take such a high rate from those who earn more. Some people argue it’s necessary to fund public services, while others say it discourages entrepreneurship and hard work. That makes sense. I remember reading or even discussing it in class that progressive taxation can be seen as a means to reduce income inequality. Exactly. And the government sets this rate and sometimes changes it based on their own economic policy. It’s part of a broader financial strategy to balance the budget and meet the country’s financial commitments. Ah, balancing the budget. I remember that term from my economics studies. How is it different from the political party’s manifesto promises, though? They often say different things and it’s hard to keep track. That’s a very good point. But it's actually quite simple. The government’s budget is the detailed plan for income and expenditure for the next year or so. The manifesto is the party’s general guiding principles and policy promises they make during election campaigns. I see. So, whenever we see a new budget or policy announcement, it's like seeing which parts of the manifesto are being implemented? That’s a fair way to look at it. It might not be a one-to-one correspondence because sometimes there are political pressures or unexpected economic changes that can influence policy. But broadly speaking, yes. And how does the public get information about these policies and budget plans?

So, I hear that your weekend was quite eventful last Saturday. What have you been up to? Oh, it was quite eventful, I talked to my daughter the whole time! You know, Emma's been working so hard and I couldn't be prouder of her. She's really gaining momentum with her new job. That's great to hear! How's she finding it? Any big projects she's working on? Ah, yeah, she's working for this marketing firm in London and they've been on a bit of a roll. They just landed this huge client, and she's been in the thick of it. She's learning so much, but I can tell she's a bit under pressure. It must be quite a bit to take. As usual, she's a bright spot in your life, even from all this way away. It's wonderful that you talk to her so regularly. Absolutely. It keeps me updated and helps me feel like I'm still part of her life in a meaningful way. But it's also given me a bit of a window into what young people are facing these days. So different from when I was working and entering the workforce. Absolutely. The job market has changed a lot over the years. I know it's hard to keep up with all the different types of jobs that exist now, not to mention the grind of trying to stand out in an increasingly competitive field. Honestly, as an Examinations Manager, I see a lot of students trying really hard to keep up with education and the job market all at once. It’s tough. Plus, I don’t think anyone understands the pressure that's on them until they're the one under it. Definitely. I do project coordination and it’s similar in some ways. You have to navigate the expectations of your team, your managers, and the project goals all at once. It can be quite stress-inducing. Different job, but similar pressures. Exactly! That and the continuous push to deliver high standards. It's relentless. I do wish sometimes that people would appreciate more that there’s only so much pressure people can handle before it starts affecting their mental health. But I guess that’s a different conversation altogether. Speaking of which, I had a good chat with Emma about stress and managing it this weekend.

Alright mates, what's on the agenda tonight? We've got the TV, some books, and I've got a bottle of wine open. Anything specific you fancy doing? I'm good with the usual, isn't the wine just lovely though? You've really got a knack for picking some of the best. Yeah, quite a good cellar, John. I’ve always enjoyed your taste in wine. Now, shall we start with something light? Maybe set up a game of Trivial Pursuit or something? Game's always fun, but let's actually. I've been meaning to show you all this new gadget I got. It's an old iPod I picked up from a friend. Loads of old music from the 80s and 90s. An actual iPod? That's kind of retro now, isn't it? It's nice though, gives you a different listening experience. But honestly, I couldn’t believe it when John here showed me his collection of vinyl records too. For me, there's something about the physicality of music, you know? The covers, the sleeves, even the way the needle touches the record. It's all part of the package. Still, this iPod has its own charm. It's surprising how packed it is with songs. Ah, the music, I'd love to hear some of those classics. It'd be a nice change from the usual playlists. It’s all about the ambiance and mood, isn't it? Plus, doesn’t hurt that it's a hell of a lot more portable than schlepping around a record player or a bunch of CDs. Exactly. Though, there's just something about holding those physical records that just won't transfer over to a digital format. Speaking of classic things, has anyone seen the recent job ads around? I've been thinking about applying for something better. With my administrative background and all. Oh, job hunting, that old art. I've been there myself. Just finished up a consulting gig. The industry is always so competitive, isn't it? It's tough, but it's definitely worth it if the right opportunity comes along. However, it's also just as important to care for what you do. Yeah, plus with the recent news about the economy, I'm not sure. Seems like everyone's either looking or holding onto their jobs for dear life. That’s true.

So, I hear you've just come back from the International TEFL Conference. How was it? I've been meaning to attend one myself but couldn't swing it this year. Oh, it was great. It was actually quite enlightening. I learned a lot about the new methodologies in language teaching – you know, all this talk about gamification and project-based learning. But, between you and me, I feel like a lot of it was just fluff. Ah, I know what you mean. Sometimes it feels like these conferences are just an excuse for publishers and tech companies to sell their newest products. Exactly! They're not always as practical as they seem, especially when you're working in a small school with very limited resources. So what about the keynote speaker? Was she any good? Actually, that was probably the highlight of the conference. She's an author of various books on language acquisition and she gave an excellent talk on creative ways to stimulate student interest in learning a new language. That sounds fascinating. I wish I could have seen that. What were her main points? One of the main points she made was about the importance of using authentic materials in the classroom. She said it has to be more than just using the occasional news article. Students respond so much better when the content is interesting and relevant to their lives. That makes sense. But sometimes it's hard to find materials that are both authentic and manageable for students, especially if they're absolute beginners in the target language. For sure. It’s a real challenge. But she gave some practical tips on how to adapt materials and create activities that work for the different levels and the limited resources we might have. That sounds like something I could use. Maybe I’ll try to look up some of her books or try those activities in my own classes, if I can keep up. She said anything about how to ease the workload? Of course! She actually talked about the importance of planning in advance but also being flexible and changing plans if something isn’t working. You know how often we plan an activity only to realize it’s not as effective as we thought in practice. Absolutely. I always overprepare so I can adjust on the fly if needed. It’s just a balancing act between having enough structure and being open to the unexpected.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my online fitness challenge? I signed up for this 30-day squat challenge. I've been finding it so motivating. Really? That sounds interesting. I'm always looking for new ways to get in shape. What kind of workout is it? It’s pretty straight forward. You just need to do a certain number of squats every day of the month. It starts out simple, then gradually increases. I'm up to 100 squats a day now. Crazy when you think about it. That's a great effort! I've heard about those before. Do you feel like you've noticed any changes in your body already? Definitely, I can definitely feel my thighs getting a little stronger. It’s also helped me to maintain some kind of routine during this period of unemployment. It's been quite a challenge, living out of a camper for so long, you know? Definitely. I remember when we started this journey, I thought, "Great, we'll get to see the country!" But sometimes it can be a bit isolating, right? Exactly. I often feel like I'm missing out on the social aspects of life. But the landscape is lovely, at least. I love how different the architecture and the towns are from what I'm used to in England. Yeah, I adore it here. The different dialects in each town, really. Did you notice when we stopped in that café in Tarnów earlier? The barista had a really interesting accent. Oh god, yes! I found it quite hard to understand at first, but it's just so charming. More reason for me to keep doing my part-time TEFL work here. I meet so many wonderful people. TEFL work? How long have you been doing that? This is my second year. I was always really passionate about languages and teaching, and a bit tired of the bureaucracy in school systems in England. This has been such a refreshing change. Plus, it allows me to travel. It does sound incredible! You get to see the country while working and meeting new people. How do you find managing it all? To be honest, it's great when you're young. I have my freedom now to travel and work across Eastern Europe. But I do wish sometimes I could have that stability. I've been thinking about settling for a bit once this season ends.

Ah, so I was reading about these telomeres last night. Fascinating stuff. You know how they talk about how telomere length affects the aging process? Hmm, yes. I've heard about that too. Is it like our cellular clock that just keeps running out, basically? Sort of, but it's way more complex than that. Telomeres are those little caps at the end of chromosomes that get shorter as we age, right? And as they shorten, cells stop dividing properly, and it can lead to aging and disease. That explains why some people age better than others, doesn't it? Even our lifestyles and environments can affect them. Precisely! Lifestyle, diet, and exercise all play a role, as well as stress levels. And while we can't directly lengthen telomeres, adopting healthy habits can slow down their shortening and even increase the activity of enzymes that rebuild them - like telomerase. So how does that relate to anti-ageing research? Is there anything people can take or do to stop or reverse this process? So, there's not really a magic pill yet, but there are studies into telomerase activators and telomere lengthening therapies. Some early results look positive, but it's still largely experimental. It's like the secret to immortality, or at least long life, right? I used to think it was all about the genes, but it seems more holistic than that. Almost. Evolutionarily, it's all about survival of the species. The key is not just prolonging life but living well. Health span over lifespan. Makes sense. There's also this fascinating research into caloric restriction and fasting. Some animals seem to live longer when their food intake is reduced. Maybe the lack of stress on the body allows for better cellular maintenance. On that note, did you see those documentaries about comets and global warming? It's mind-boggling and slightly terrifying to think about the entire universe changing so quickly. It really puts things into perspective. I think about how ancient civilizations like the Egyptians or the people who built the pyramids had no idea about what we take for granted today. Like understanding the tectonic plates and how the earth's crust shifts. Did you know the pyramids are almost perfectly aligned with the stars in the belt of Orion? Amazing, isn't it? The technological advancements and sheer knowledge we've gained. But also makes you thinking about how brief our lifespan is in the grand scheme.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that place we went to today? The new Italian place on the street. They have the best pasta sauce I've ever had! No, you didn't mention it. I was at home, running errands. How was it? It was superb! But I think my mom was a bit disappointed with the coffee. She said it was too sour and not strong enough. Oh, I've got just the thing for that. Remember how I bought that new coffee maker last week? I've been using it a lot. I can show you how it works if you want. I think it would make a huge difference. That would be amazing! I read online that the best coffee taste comes from home-brewed coffee. On that note, did either of you happen to check out the new shopping vouchers we got in the mail yesterday? The big department store is running a sale on baby stuff. Maybe we can pick up a few things for the baby or even a new chair. Oh, actually, I did see that. They’re selling that ergonomic baby chair with the extra support for newborns. I think the kids need one. Yeah, and we were thinking of getting one anyway. Though, it can be quite spendy. I agree, but I think it's worth it. It’s a big one time investment, really. And they also had vouchers, I think? Yes, they were included in the mail. I'll check how that works. Talking of one-time expenses, have you two heard about the EU referendum? I’ve been seeing all these ads everywhere, and my dad says we are supposed to decide whether we stay in or out. It’s all so confusing. Yeah, it's a big deal. But the truth is, it's all very complicated. I’ve been researching it, though, and I think it’s important to stay in. I agree with Speaker_2 on this one. It does affect the economy and millions of jobs. And for us, it’s about more than just economics; it’s about cultural exchange and being part of something bigger. Yeah, I get that. But the ads make everything sound so scary. Ads will do that. But it’s essential to look beyond the propaganda and find reliable sources. SpeakingStarti mind if we change the subject a bit?

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to deal with a patient who insisted on decorating his Christmas tree even though he had deep vein thrombosis? Had the whole ward down on high alert. No, you haven’t! That sounds wild. Why did he want to decorate the tree and how did you manage it? Well, he just loved the festive spirit and decorating his tree was his favourite pastime. He was so determined. So, I had to get creative and have him decorate a small artificial one at the foot end of his bed, with me on hand to make sure he didn’t strain himself. That’s really thoughtful of you. It must have made his day. It did. Made a real difference to his spirits. Now, speaking of Christmas, have you started your own tree yet? Not yet. We’re thinking of having a small, eco-friendly one this year. But I’m considering changing it up and maybe going for something different. Maybe a rustic theme or something exotic next year though. For me, Christmas this year is going to be pretty quiet, to be honest. The ward’s busy and I’m on call a lot over Christmas, but I’ve already sent the kids to the grandparents. They’re over the moon to have them, really. Well, at least you get to spend the day with them at some point? Oh, yes! They’re coming over for Christmas Day, so we’re planning to make a big deal of that and make some yummy food. Mum’s doesn’t come in for Christmas as she usually helps with the day-to-day, but this year we’re doing it all ourselves. Sounds lovely. You know, I just had a thought: have you heard anything from the Smiths next door? I noticed their tree is up already and looking really festive. Oh, they are just really insistent on being first to put theirs up every year. You know how neighbourly gossip is, they’re already boasting about it. But honestly, they’re such lovely people. Our cat loves to sit at the window just watching their garden, it’s so funny. That reminds me! You sent me a picture of Miss Binks sitting by the window. She’s so pretty and calm. Has she been getting into any mischief lately? Not really, thankfully.

Yo, mate, welcome to our new flat in Sussex! I’ve been here for a day already; it’s been super cool so far. The flat’s nice, though it’s a bit of a trek down from Surrey but I love the vibe of this new place. Ah, thanks for inviting me over! I just got here myself and I’m still unpacking and figuring out the place. The flat looks great! Have you connected to the internet yet? I managed to sort it out yesterday. Took a bit of time, but now it's all set up. We’ve got a pretty good provider here, so speeds are good. It’ll be easy for you to connect as well, but I can walk you through if you need. That would be great, thanks. What’s the best way to get the internet sorted here? Is there a setup fee or contract required? No, it turned out to be pretty straightforward. They sent a team out, and we just had to sign a form. No setup fee or anything. You just need to top it up every month, and they have really competitive rates. For me, it’s just a short term thing until I find a new place to stay. I’ve been looking at flats online and should know something soon. That's cool. In the meantime, you can just use our Wi-Fi, no problem. So, what have you done so far? Unpacked a bit? Yeah, started unpacking but it’s a lot! Also, trying to figure out where everything is around here. Do you know the best local food shops? Oh, absolutely! There’s a Tesco just a short walk from here that’s open 24/7, and also some local butchers and bakers in town. The Morrisons less than a mile away has pretty good deals and a wide variety, too. The local market on Thursdays is a must-visit, though. They have all sorts of fresh produce, especially if you’re looking for seasonal stuff. That'll be useful. I’m on a bit of a budget right now, so I’ll try to stick to some of the cheaper options. Have you found any good places to buy other things, like pots and pans? Yeah, there’s an Argos 5 minutes from here and B&Q right next to it. And if you want something specific, just order online and use their next-day delivery.

Oh, wow, it has been ages! I have missed our catch ups. Hope everything is well with you. Thanks, me too! Had the busiest of summers working but I'm glad to finally catch up. I’ve just started my graduate placement, so needless to say, questions are flying left and right. That sounds exciting and daunting at the same time, right? I wish I could have settled into my current job as quickly as I'd thought. Yeah, nothing beats reality does it? I mean, we all thought, okay, you’ve got your degree, you’re all set. But, it's a very different story from then on. Totally. But in the best of ways, I guess - keeps making life interesting, that’s for sure. So, how are your parents? Last time we met, you were handling your mum’s wedding, right? Did it all go smoothly? Oh, yeah, that was a whirlwind! It was a big event, so a lot of planning. But it went incredibly well. My mum is still planning gardening trips with friends. You know she's all about the flowers. I remember seeing the photos. Your mum really outdid herself. I must ask, did you get to travel anywhere over the summer? Yeah, right after the wedding, we decided to take a quick holiday as a family. We went to Cornwall for a few days. The weather was perfect and we hiked a lot. Mum loves the scenery down there. Cornwall is lovely! I've always wanted to visit. Except, unfortunately, I don’t think I’ll be traveling much for a while. Seems like the company's got a whole lot of placements, so I'm expecting to be really busy. That sounds draining but also so rich in experience. Definitely a learning curve. You know, it's interesting to see how everything we learned at university is actually applied – and that there’s so much more to learn. Absolutely. I feel the same about my project coordination job. It's all about adjusting to the team and figuring out the project lifecycle in real-time. Mobility and flexibility is key then, huh? Definitely. Speaking of which, what are your future plans? Any career paths you're considering? Honestly, I enjoy where I am now, but I’m not ruling out anything... I do have interests in event management, you know, the big productions, which is a bit of what I did for mum’s wedding.

Oh, so many topics we've got to cover. Work first? You know how it is, balancing research management and PhD studies don't leave much free time for the fun stuff. Aye, I know the struggle. I kind of do miss the carefree days when I had time to listen to bands non-stop and hit up every gig I could. You're up there now, where are you with your current favourite bands? Oh, I've got a keeps coming back to Arctic Monkeys. Lads from Sheffield, but it's a bit like home to listen to. I've been to quite a few gigs in Newcastle recently, despite the northerners in London not understanding the excitement . Yeah, because the Mancunian accent's so well understood in London! Exactly! Anyway, looking for a gig? I know how you like gigs. Off chance. But this semester's been so hectic with preparations for next year's orals. But yeah, if there's a chance, I'm always game! You should try. It's good for you, mate. You need a break from the thesis. Stampeding over the revision massacre . Revision massacre – that's a nice way of putting it. I love how you say things. It breaks the monotony of the seriousness for a bit. Well, there you go. 'North East lingo’ at work. How about your research? Going alright? Last I spoke to you, you were babbling about medieval chants. Yeah, the medieval chants. Can you imagine, looking at the same manuscripts for months, questioning the significance of a comma. But fun in a weird way. Different kind of music, I suppose. That’s quite a leap, but changing the world takes all sorts. I was reading about a project in Durham that combines advanced AI with research into local dialects for educational purposes. It’s fascinating stuff, really uses of technology that don’t take away from local culture. Sounds interesting! I’d love to read more about that. Again, it’s about those North East dialects and preserving them. Even though we don’t often meet many from around here in Cambridge, you’ve got to keep that connection somehow. True. Cambridge can be a funny place – academically vibrant, but sometimes you wish for a more northern vibe. Even finding decent Gregg’s or a proper chippie can be a challenge . Gregg’s! How gauche of us.

Yo, nan, did you seen any of that politics on the telly? I don't really follow it that closely, but I overheard some stuff about Brexit and talked about it in class. Ah yes, lad, I saw some o' that too. It's a right mess, ain't it? Can't make head nor tail o' it. Exactly! It just seems like they're mucking it all up again, don't it? And it's not just Brexit, lad, there's all sorts o' stuff goin' on, like the MPs and such. I heard about the parliament's all tied up in knots. Yeah, I know, just like the Sports Direct news. They're always arguing and can't decide on anything. [chuckles] Well, you're young and you ain't lived through much, but politics has always been a mess. But sometimes it gets worse than usuall. But doesn't it get confusing? It's like every time I try to ask questions at school or even on the internet, different people say different things. That's because there's always been different views in politics, lad. You just have to sieve through the noise 'n find what you think makes sense. I guess so, but it seems like they can never agree on anything. Shouldn't they just be focusing on making sure everyone's got a job, or good healthcare, or can afford to live? They try, lad, but it's never simple. 'Ere in my day, we didn't have things like that, it was different politics and the country was different. The only thing we could rely on was that things wouldn't change too quickly. But things should change, right? Like, we weren't meant to stop progress, right? I mean, look at how far we've come with technology and stuff. Oh, of course, you're right! But it's changing too quickly and in some ways things are getting worse. Where I live, it's a bit more noticeable because some places ain't changed since I was young. But across country, it's always a bit of a nightmare. It does seem like a mess. So, what was politics like back when you were my age? Was it almost as bad? Oh no, lad, it was different. I was livin' during WWII and post-war times. Politics was all about rebuilding after the war.

Ah, so I heard you've been babysitting Grace and James again. How are they doing? Oh, they're little terrors, but well behaved for the most part. They kept telling me about this 'blood moon' they saw in the news. Do you know what that is? Yeah! A blood moon is when the moon turns reddish. It happens during a lunar eclipse. Exactly! That's right, Tom. It's an interesting astronomical event, isn't it? Yeah, but to a kid, anything unusual in the sky can be quite exciting. And what were you talking about before I arrived? Ah, we were discussing the blood moon, and Tom here was explaining it to us. Hmm, interesting. I must say, these scientific discussions over dinner are a welcome change. When I was teaching, we often had similar conversations in class. Nowadays, I’m more used to just watching the news or reading. I hope I didn’t mess anything up. Not at all, dear. You did fine. It’s good to see young minds exploring new subjects. Well, technology is certainly changing the way we learn and see the world, isn’t it, John? Indeed. But even with all these modern gadgets and all, traditional family dinners like this can't be replaced. There’s something about sitting down, sharing stories... and discussing the world and our lives. And hearing the wisdom of our granny here, who grew up in completely different times! Speaking of which, I remember when lunar eclipses were quite a thing in my day too. Back in Glasgow, my friends and I would often look for them. Wow, really? Yes. Although for us, it wasn't about the scientific aspect as much as it was about the wonder of it. Anyway, about those kids. Grace and James, how are their table manners? Well, they are still learning! But they're pretty good for their age. I’ve been working with them on using their cutlery properly and not playing with their food. Ah, the joys of raising young minds. Remember, John, when you were their age? Oh, come on, how could I forget? Speaking of manners, is there a particular 'Irish way' to eat? Not really, but we do take our family meals quite seriously. You know, enjoying each other’s company, having a good conversation... Like family meals at Fitzgeralds Park. I remember when we’d go there for picnics.

Ah, I hear you've seen some of the latest news regarding the Scottish referendum. What's your take on it all, old chap? Oh, absolutely. It's quite a contentious issue, isn't it? I've been following it closely. As a small business owner, I have to think about how questions like this will affect my company's future and potential trade routes, and all that. Yes, I can see how it would affect you as a business owner. But what about as someone from Hove? Have you got a personal connection to the issue at all? Well, I suppose, as a local in Sussex, it’s a subject that resonates, especially seeing how it impacts our northern neighbors in London. But let’s be honest, even though I was born in Hove, my focus is more on the business implications than the referendum itself. Fair point. It's interesting how it affects different people in different ways. Speaking of livelihoods, I had a peculiar job interview the other day. Really? How'd it go? Was it for a new job at your school? No, no. It was for a part-time position, just a small addition to my pension. Teaching is good, but it doesn't pay as much as it used to. The younger teachers seem to have a lot of energy to spare, but not much experience. It’s a bit of a peculiar dynamic. I see what you mean. I've had to deal with similar things in the workplace. Experience really is invaluable, but it's tough balancing that with the need for fresh ideas and approaches. Exactly! It's a hell of a tightrope to walk. Anyway, the interview itself was bizarre. The whole panel, they were younger than my children! More and more companies are shifting towards younger leadership, isn't it? It’s a little disconcerting at times, but I suppose it's all part of the evolving workplace culture. Indeed. While I was dealing with the younger interview panel, I couldn’t help but think of my daughter. She's struggling to make her way in the job market. The experience of older workers and newer ones, it's a bit of a mixed bag. Ah, family struggles! It's always a challenge, isn't it? I could use some advice there myself. My business is doing all right, but I've had to adapt to so many changes in the past few years, it feels like a constant learning curve.

Hey dad. Hope you didn’t mind me bringing my board games along today? Of course not, mate. You always manage to make the most of the ride. It’s always better with keepsakes right? Makes the trip a bit less routine. Definitely makes the day more fun. Plus, I was just looking at online reviews for a new digital board game app. Seems there’s some good stuff out now. Ah, yeah I’ve seen those. But there’s sometimes nothing like handling the proper pieces, playing the game the old fashioned way. Definitely true. And it’s not like the digital version can account for the actual laughter or banter we have during these games. Speaking of games, I found an interesting article about the world record for the fastest time to create a giant Jenga tower. It’s quite impressive! Can you send that link to me? I’d love to take a look. On it! But here’s a quick anecdote first. They used computer simulations to analyze and optimize the structure. It’s crazy. Of course, that makes sense. I’ve seen kids in gaming areas trying to build towers for the fun of it. But on that scale? Ah, alright. Gosh, I hope the weather remains fine like this for the weekend. Yeah, perfect weather for a game if you ask me. Hopefully no showers for your weekend picnic. Speaking of which, this summer has been great... except for the supermarket prices. Food's getting pretty pricey. Really noticeable at my work. Customers always mention it. Prices going up, but quality sometimes the same. Oh, indeed. I've noticed the same when shopping with mum. Makes preparing lunch a bit more challenging for us lately, isn’t it? To be fair, as someone who uses their lunch break for art, it does impact what I can make at home. I mean, buying fresh supplies becomes more of a decision now. But maybe that’s an art opportunity! Creating meals can be about stretching what you have and making them look as good as possible. Nothing like finding creativity in limitation, right? Good topic for a reflective writing class exercise. Absolutely. It’s all about perspective. We all need to appreciate the small victories and the smart purchases when we can. Speaker_

Alright, so Dad, I was today talking to these lads from work and they were all discussing about driving, and talked about whether it's better to downshift manually or just let the car handle it with automatic. What are your thoughts? Ah, well, lad, when I was workin' at BT, them automatic cars weren't as common as they are now, but I never felt a big difference, to be honest. Always found it easier to just let the car do its job, especially in city traffic. You get used to it, you know? I think there is an argument for both sides. Manual can give you a little more control, especially if you're driving on rural roads or going up hills. However, with most of my work now, I find that automatic is just easier for city driving, handling traffic conditions better. Yeah, I suppose so. I've seen those automatic cars handle the flow much better. But I suppose it's more skill, too, with manual. Indeed, indeed. I remember the '60s and '70s, most people drove manual, but now, not so much. Though, sometimes when you're stuck in a traffic jam, manual can be more of a pain, especially if you're not used to it. True, true. Alright, but let’s change gears. How about farm animals? Ever come across any interesting species in your travels around the country? Ah, farm animals! Late in my working years, I used to love visiting my sister in Wales. There was this one time, we were driving along a rural road and we came across a flock of geese crossing the road. Of course, traffic came to a halt, and it was quite a sight! Dad, that reminds me of when we were out on a family day out and we stopped in these fields. All these sheep were just grazing. We took pictures and stuff. And later, we saw a farm with goats. They were such curious creatures. Ah, goats are almost as fascinating as sheep. In my line of job, we do have to work with farmland occasionally, and there’s something about these animals... the sense of peace and calm they bring to a place. Sure is. I suppose it’s a part of the... natural balance of any community, don’t you think? Even in city life, having a patch of green with animals enriches people’s lives.

Ah, I can't believe how much I'm enjoying these midweek family dinners. Nothing like a good conversation to turn around the week, especially after a long day. Oh, absolutely! I love how we've really found our pace around the dinner table. Just this morning, I was thinking about questions for this week's transcribing project and suddenly realized I knew exactly what I wanted to ask. These dinner conversations really help clarify my thoughts. Indeed! I've never had such stimulating conversations as I have with all of you during these dinners. It's a nice change from my routine, which used to involve endless meetings and spreadsheets. Even though I've been out of the loop for a while, I'm really glad you've all been so understanding and open to my input even now. Definitely, we're lucky to have such a supportive group. Speaking of routines, how's your exercise regimen coming along? I tried joining a yoga class last month and it's been really helpful, physically and mentally. That's great! I've been trying to get into jogging. It's tough, but I've heard it's good for focus too. Did you notice how much more clearly I'm thinking after yoga sessions? Absolutely! Exercise is good for the mind as well as the body. You should give jogging a go if you haven't already. I used to enjoy the long walks on the hills after work. It cleared my mind so well. I'd love that! Possibly, we could even go for a group jog someday? If we all pick a time when we’re available, I'm sure it would be fun and motivating. That sounds like a fantastic idea! We could even use it as a way to work on that punctuality. Speaking of time... did you all make the arrangements for the family event in December? We need to finalize the plan, I think. We talked about it briefly over the last dinner but didn’t quite settle on a plan. Maybe we should set a meeting to discuss it properly? We could use the zoom calls we've been on lately, they've been working quite well for all of us. Yes! Zoom for sure. I have a rough idea about what I’d like so I can share those thoughts over the call.

Alright, kids, so first things first. How was your parents' evening? What did your teachers say about each of you? Oh, my teacher said I’m doing quite well in reading. I read faster than the other kids in class! But in math questions, I kind of got stuck sometimes because sometimes I forget the answers and sometimes the questions make me feel a bit stressed. Yeah, same! Math isn’t very fun for me. But during World Book Day, I dressed as Harry Potter and my teacher said I did a great job, she said I was very good at remembering the character’s name! That’s fantastic! It’s great to hear you both were among the best in read-aloud session but of course, we can work on making maths as fun as reading. What do you think? Maybe you guys want to play some math games at home? That could be fun! Maybe like those flashcard ones we played in class once? And maybe watch a bit or a movie or something that makes me feel a bit better about maths? I can definitely set up some math fun time for you, while the rest of us can have some family dinner. Yay! So, can we talk about what we’re having for dinner? Aha, right, dinner! How about we do a bit of a special meal for World Book Day? Since we’ve been talking a lot about books and characters, maybe we can have a character theme? Like, do we get to be our book characters? Yes! And maybe the food can be like in our characters' favorite books. That sounds fun! So, if you want to be Harry Potter or any character for dinner, what do you think would be the best food to match? Hmmm... I think Harry would love chocolate frogs and pumpkin juice because that’s his favorite! And maybe, if I’m my Harry Potter costume, I can have butterbeer! Oh, great idea! Or perhaps you can enjoy something almost as magical, like a homemade apple crumble or a special themed dessert. I’ll make sure to ask what your preferred food is for the character you want to be. But before dinner, can we watch the circus video that Auntie Sarah sent us? It’s lots of fun! Yeah! It’s about the animals and the acrobats! What a great idea!

Alright so Oisín was running around this morning telling everyone today's the big day for his birthday party celebration and he even asked me to wear his special party hat. Can you imagine me, an IT manager, in a party hat? Oh, that sounds like questions if we haven't seen it yet! The house is gonna be a zoo, I'm sure. And the way he says 'birthday'. Birrthdayoooo! Oh, those early years when they still say things with such charm. It just melts your heart, doesn't it? Absolutely. So, what's the plan for today? We were thinking big but maybe we should scale it down a bit. I think you’re right. We can invite just his closest friends, maybe 8 or 10 kids. And no need for a big party at home. The local park would be lovely. We can set up a few games and maybe a bouncy castle if it’s not too expensive. I’ve been looking at some local prices. The bouncy castle is around €50 for the day. Bounce! Bounce! Honestly, as long as it makes him happy. And then food-wise? We’re thinking sandwiches, some crisps, and some fruit? And a cake of course. Cake! Yes, and I can do the sandwiches. Something simple should be enough, right? Definitely. And for the games, since we’re at the park, maybe we can organize a friendly mini football match or something? That could work. We could even make it a bit more fun with some prize for the winning team… maybe a bag of sweets or something. Sweets! Alright, let’s see how Oisín reacts to all these plans. And if he starts asking for a rapper for the party... I think that’s a bit ambitious for a two-year-old's birthday. Daaadyyy... rapper... I think our little man's already pretty sure of himself. So, who’s in charge of the presents and party bags? I can arrange that. I know Oisín loves puzzles and, well, pretty much any toy that makes noise at the moment. And maybe some picture book or a soft toy. Something that would last longer than the day I’d say. Good idea. And we’ll need to make sure everything is age-appropriate. Right. Also, need to check if any of the kids are allergic to anything. Good point.

Yo, lads! Remember that word game we talked about last time? The one called Bananagrams? Yeah, absolutely! I talked to my cousin the other day and he said they're still into it quite a bit back home. That's great! So, how does it work again? You piece together your tiles like Scrabble, but without a board, right? Exactly! It's more flexible I'd say. You can play it anywhere, anytime. There's an initial "puzzle" set up when you start, and then you can start making words from the tiles in your hand – any direction, even diagonally. I loved that flexibility. It’s a good brain exercise too. How do you decide when to start? Ah, that’s the fun part. Someone just has to say “Go!” and everyone starts building words at the same time. You can also play with the “Dump” rule where you can replace a tile if you don’t like it or if you’re stuck. It adds a bit of strategy and risk-taking! That's really cool! I’m more of a chess and puzzle kind of person, but this sounds like a great combination of both. Exactly! And the best thing is the learning curve’s pretty easy. Perfect for people to pick up and play together. Absolutely! But it can also get quite competitive if you want it to, especially if you start introducing different rules, like the "Peel" rule where you pull more tiles when you use all you have. I like that it doesn’t require much setup, it's straightforward and quick to learn. I might need to get my housemates into it. Definitely consider it. Oh, did I ever tell you about that film we saw last weekend? It was quite possibly the worst I've seen in ages! You're just saying that because you didn’t get to see it with the band you wanted to! I've been meaning to ask you, babe. What do you think of these new ads on TV? Do you think they're influencing our shopping habits more than before? Oh, definitely. Ah, the good old days! I remember when we first moved here in the 60s. It was a real culture shock after being in the countryside. Professor Smith, isn’t it? I’m Alice, one of the Language Research Co-ordinators here. Oh, did I ever tell you about that patient I had last week? The poor lady was complaining about every little thing. "Nurse, my pillow's wrong! Nurse, my food isn't hot enough! Nurse, the TV isn't working!" She was like the goddess of complaints! Oh, sounds like a right nuisance. I've had my share of that at work too, although not of that frequency. I once had someone complain that the coffee wasn't strong enough. I know! It's like, okay, you're not in a luxury hotel, but try to keep it together, you know? You two have got to stop telling each other your most annoying work stories before I get a whole new perspective on how I should behave at work! Aw, sorry if we're boring you! But seriously, that same patient last week, it got so bad, I actually started timing the intervals between complaints. It was a bit like... Ahem, yes? A bit like...? A bit like: "Tic-tic-tic... complaint! Tic-tic-tic... complaint! That sounds about right! You're both hilarious, actually. It’s a good thing you're not working together! But it wasn't all bad, you know. After about the fourth complaint, she kind of gave up, and we got along fine after that. That’s the secret: patience and a thick skin, isn't it? Speaking funny, another funny thing happened at work last week. So, one of my colleagues had his birthday, and we decided to surprise him with a cake. But it turns out he’s seriously allergic to nuts… …and the cake was completely packed with nuts. Oh no, oh no! And what did you do? Oh, well, we had to quickly turn it into a "Five-minute Wonderfully Nuttless Cake". We managed to scrape off all the nuts and came up with a new concept for the frosting. Surprisingly, he still laughed and appreciated the thought. That takes the cake! No... I'll stop any minute now... It was really a panic-driven campaign though. Stuck with a nutty cake and a happy birthday to sing. It’s like, in emergencies, you trust everyone to come up with a functional solution. True, as if no crisis is a real crisis until a swift and creative solution doesn't emerge. I guess that’s something we’re all bringing to the table: adapting to situations when they’re less than ideal.

I've heard of this program on the telly, "Big Brother," you lot are all talking about. Is it really as boring as they say, or is it more scandalous? Oh, it's just a sensational, scandalous kind of fun, really. It's all about the drama and the house drama. Yeah, but sometimes it's useful to remind ourselves how much our lives are different, eh? All that drama for what? For being on TV and... having people watch you 24/7, cooking meals and arguing with strangers in a house. It's a voyeuristic thing, isn't it? But then again, it’s also fascinating to see how people act in a bubble like that. And the money they win... It's a bit like gossip, innit? You watch, and you talk about it, but when it comes down to it, we all have our own lives to live, far removed from that kind of drama. Absolutely. You know, it’s weird when you think about it. These people's lives being projected into everyone's living rooms, while the rest of us are just trying to figure out how to afford the heating bill or to pick up some shopping without having the streets gridlocked or the shelves empty. Exactly, John. There's a stark contrast in priorities, isn’t there? One man's scandal is another man’s... "how can I pay the electricity bill without going broke?" Well, the royalties from that kind of show do seem to keep one or two people in the lap of luxury, though. More's the power of entertainment, I suppose, and the industry surrounding it. Speaking of which, have you noticed how much harder it's become to find what we need in shops lately? You can barely walk around without tripping over someone staring at their phone, or struggling to make room for some new pop-up store selling fancy, overpriced salads. I couldn't agree more. The world of shopping's changed beyond recognition. I remember when a good grocery shop was about finding everything you needed and perhaps a bit of local gossip. Nowadays, it's more about dodging delivery vans and finding a parking space that doesn't cost a small fortune. And all these shops seem to open and close in a flash too! One week it's a boutique, the next, it’s a chippy or a coffee shop.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that film I saw last week? It's quite possibly the most boring film I've ever watched! You're hooked on that one already, aren't you? What was it? It was some period drama. I just couldn’t keep my eyes open for more than 20 minutes. I mean, I love history but the pacing was just so... slow. Sounds like it didn’t quite capture your attention. You know, I’m actually working on my dissertation at the moment and we had to watch a film for one of my modules. Really? What kind of film was it and how was it? It was actually a French art house film called "Amour," directed by Michael Haneke. It was intense and beautiful but also very slow-paced. I can imagine. I guess when it comes to art house films, we're in this together. Absolutely! Now, talking about slower-paced things, have you had a chance to catch up with the family back in Doncaster? Quite a bit actually. My mum’s still over the moon about her new garden. She’s spent endless hours tending to it since they moved to a bigger house. That sounds lovely! My family is always a bit in and out, really. But they did send us a lovely package from London last week. Really? That doesn’t sound ideal but nice of them! Do you have any plans for the holidays? I’m thinking of heading back to Doncaster for a bit. We do have some plans! My parents are hosting a small family gathering on Boxing Day and my sister is flying in from Scotland so it should be fun. What are your plans? That sounds great! I’m changing mine now. My family is planning a big meal on Christmas Day and maybe a day out on Boxing Day. Sounds like you’re all set then. We should take advantage of the fact that we're all together again and maybe catch some of those movies we’ve been wanting to see. Yeah, definitely! There’s one film I’ve been meaning to see and you’ve been dying to watch "The Irishman," right? Oh, absolutely! I’ve been wanting to see that ever since it came out. I’ve heard it’s like three hours long but Scorsese’s style usually keeps me hooked.

Right, so I've been reading about this Scottish Independence referendum and I must say, it's really interesting how polarized opinions are around here. It sure is! I mean, I've seen a lot of arguments about it at school too. A lot of people are talking about it a lot lately. Exactly! You've probably seen it in the news and stuff. As a Brit, I think it's important we all have an opinion of why or why not Scotland should be independent. But as someone from York, I've got a keepsake that might give us a different perspective. Oh, that sounds cool. Tell me! Alright. So, when I used to teach maths in London, we had a journalist come to talk to our class about the 2014 referendum. After the talk, she gave me this [pulls out a small memorabilia item]. It's a replica of the Scottish independence ballot paper from 2014. What does it say? It says "Should Scotland be an independent country?" And you have to vote or Yes or No. Now that was before, this is about the upcoming one, but it gives a good groundwork for what is at stake. I see. So what did you think in 2014? Well, I was in favor of Scots having the right to decide for themselves, but personally, I thought that there were practical benefits to being part of the UK: the strength of the pound, certain shared services, that kind of thing. And there were some concerns about how independence might affect the economy and things like that. I see. I kind of see what you mean, like we've been all through Brexit and stuff so things are a bit less stable already. Exactly, and that's a big point. The world is a different place now than it was in 2014. So you think Scotland should stay in the UK then? You know, after all these years of teaching advanced maths, I believe in thinking clearly about evidence and probabilities. For me, currently, it seems the uncertainty over currency, EU membership, and the potential for economic upheaval outweighs the potential gains of independence for the general Scottish population. Yeah, I see what you mean. But what about the argument that Scotland gets less out of the UK than it puts in? Well, that's a common argument, but it depends on how you measure it.

Oh, did you see that?? Did he just say "D'ya wake up dis mornin'?" Haha, I love how you say that! You almost sounded like he, the presenter, though! But yeah, heard questions like that all the time on Jeremy Kyle. It's kind of embarrassing sometimes, innit? I'm sorry but, as much as I love watching this, sometimes I just can't help cringing at how they talk. You get people from all over and... well, it's just, you know. Fair dos, I used to find it a bit cringy too when I was a bit younger. But as much as we can criticise, it's a part of the culture we're all from. And to be fair, it's partly why I enjoy it so much – its authentic and raw. Exactly! It's like that bit about elision we were talking about the other day, isn't it? He said "We'll 'ave to gang 'em together so we can 'ave a show", see? I mean, I use elision myself, but sometimes I wonder whether 'eavy regional accents like that affect how the wider audience receives the show? Well, I think people from outside the North will probably find it a bit hard to tune in if everyone's speaking in, like, 'God's Own' in there. But really, it's about understanding, innit? I mean, if you're from Liverpool and you hear someone from Manchester say "Hit tha road" instead of "Hit the road", you know exactly what they mean, and it's kind of comforting. But the elision isn't just about ease, right? It’s a part of the rhythm of the language. I noticed in that clip just then, even when they were speaking more or less ‘proper English’, they’d still do it. It’s like it’s a way of showing they’re not posh or something. That's a good point. Plus, I think in these sorts of shows, it's just about being real, isn't it? And for some people, elision or dropping "t"s or "h"s is just how they’ve grown up speaking. And if they're on TV, maybe it’s their moment to shine and show who they really are. Yeah. It's also part of the psychology. Jeremy Kyle makes people feel like they're among their own. But at the same time, I think sometimes it gets too much.

Oh, did you see that last move by Sterling? I swear today's match is more exciting than Jeopardy and Mastermind combined! Right! Sterling's been on fire since he signed the new deal. Though, speaking of deals, how's the knitting going? It's slow, but enjoyable. I've been trying to make a scarf for your niece. Hopefully it'll be ready by Christmas. That's sweet. You'll need it to match the onesie I've been knitting – I'm deciding between Idris and Leopold for the baby. I think Idris is a strong contender. It's unique, but not impossible to pronounce or spell. Agreed. Though, you remember when we were children and parents used to give us these ridiculous football-themed names? My parents almost named my older brother Pele! And you had a potential name like Justin because of Gascoigne. Now that's a story I don’t remember. Sure, I've heard about it but never thought about it in detail. It's true! I actually have the old baby name book at my parents' house. It's hilarious, all these names that were popular or trending back then – like Tarquin or Britney for boys. Oh, Britney? Seriously? I can understand the reasoning for sporty names but Britney for a boy? Shows how times and trends change. Exactly! Well, maybe we can use that for our next pet or something. Except, we've already got Leo and Luna. Right. Seems like the Olympics was where those names came from! Speaking of which, did you watch the Olympics? What were your highlights? Oh absolutely! The opening ceremony was brilliant wasn't it? And the GB team did great! I watched a lot of rowing and tennis. You? I was hooked on the women's volleyball. Specifically, the GB team’s determination despite not winning a medal. It was inspiring. Yeah, indeed! And have you seen the news about 2028? Again, Britain’s expected to host. Hopefully they’ll focus on improving infrastructure and facilities. I hope so too, though I worry about the logistics. 2012 was amazing, but it was a huge task. Definitely. I wrote a piece for my thesis on the economic impact of hosting the Olympics. It's fascinating, but can be a bit of a gamble. Really? Can you share a bit of that with me? I'd love to hear some of the findings.

I keep thinking of that bit in The Bee Movie where Barry says “ask yourselves why isn’t the Whole World doing it?” Well, it sounds so simple but it’s so unrealistic isn't it? Yeah! But it’s funny, because some of his points about the bees and their society make us think about how companies and governments could change! And the way he wanted to pollinate himself? That part is hilarious. But even though it is a kids' movie, it makes me think... if bees could do it, why can't we change our world too? Absolutely. It’s a clever way of sparking those thoughts in even the youngest among us. Speaking of making the world better, does being a queen or king really make a difference? It’s a good question. In the film, the bee hive works pretty well as a monarchy. But in real life, it's a bit more complex. I mean, in some ways, having a figure head can bring a sense of unity and tradition, but in others... I would rather be a prime minister. You get to make more decisions and you can even help people! Well, politics is super important, isn’t it? Like, my Aunty says, all those laws and silly things can only change if we really want to and vote for it. That's a very astute observation. Politics is certainly key in bringing real change. But it's not just about the individuals leading, it's about the collective will of the citizens to choose the path they want for their society. Yeah, I just thought, if England wasn't a monarchy but a real republic, maybe everyone would care more about voting and stuff. That could be true, but we should also consider the changing attitudes and beliefs in society. People are becoming more engaged in politics and wanting to participate more actively, especially the younger generations. But, isn't it funny how we have to pay to see the inside of some palaces? It’s a bit ironic, isn’t it? If the royal family are essentially part of our heritage and national identity, shouldn’t we all just be able to go and see where they live or visit our history? I know! Someone told me about the palace that they visited, and it was cool, but... should we have to pay to see history?

Oh, I'm so glad we stopped here. I needed a break; picking up all those old boxes was exhausting. I know, right? There's something oddly cathartic about clearing out the old, though, isn’t there? Especially when it's things from so long ago. Absolutely. I've been working on clearing out my parent's house out in Thistle Close too. They've lived there for decades, keeps coming across loads of interesting stuff. Oh, that's Thistle Close! Lovely village. Remember when we used to go visit your parents there for pub lunches? Yes! The Queen Vic is still lovely, isn't it? Though I'm not sure if they even serve those same little sandwiches anymore. Really? I've never been! What were those sandwiches like? Oh, they were tiny little triangles. Someone should make a book about regional sandwiches or something. But jokes aside, it really is this odd mix of nostalgia and clearing space for new experiences, isn’t it? Speaking of new experiences, have either of you had the time to watch that new documentary on the NHS? It's apparently quite eye-opening about the technology they’re using now. Hmm, not yet. But isn't it remarkable how technology really is changing things? They say even here, the doctors are using AI to predict health outcomes better. True, and the interior design of those new hospitals! If you'd seen the new wing in Kendal...the attention to detail for patient care. Seems to be making a real difference in care quality. Yawn. Can we talk about something more exciting? Like, did you see the new series on TV? You sure are getting into series lately. I did see that new Doctor Who series, thought it was quite good. A bit predictable, but still entertaining. Though I heard there’s a real rivalry brewing between that and the new Game of Thrones prequel. Game of Thrones? As if I needed more dragons and fireworks! Yeah, but I heard their stag and hen party themes for that book club was the highlight of this year. Imagine drag... Don't give him ideas! though, maybe too soon for that kind of event-management, don’t you think? Speaking of events, did you hear about the auction at the local charity? They're doing a charity run for better healthcare technology. Maybe we could all pitch in a bit?

Yo, mate, did you hear about that new museum that's opening up in the city? It's supposed to have some really unique exhibits and a sweet shuttle bus service. You wouldn’t want to beat yourself down on that, right? Aye, yeah, I saw a bit about that in the news. It kind of caught me eye because they’re doing something with a local artist theme. I’ve been thinking of checking that out. Maybe we could make it a date? Definitely, and it’s not a bad time either, coming up to Christmas, people would most probably be busier with stuff like shopping, Thanksgiving, and what not. Exactly, and I’ve been wanting to check out some of that new shopping area down by the docks. Right, but from what I heard, the parking’s a nightmare, even with the new structure they’re building. It's one of those things I'd rather avoid if I can. True, true. Hmm, maybe we should visit during the week. It's probably quieter then. Been meaning to get on top of that Forth Bridge course this month, too. Forth Bridge? Ah, are you talking about that river crossing? I thought the course was about teaching? Aye, that as well, but also, the interview for the Masters. Need to spend some time prepping for that, but the thought of qualifying for it makes me excited. Good for you, mate! You're doing great things, and the benefits couldn’t come soon enough. You working that hard to move up the ladder doesn’t go unnoticed. Cheers for the support. It's kind of comforting to have someone understand what’s at stake. More than you know. But weren’t we thinking of hitting up a wedding soon? The one in Glasgow? Aye, can't forget about that. We should really get those travel plans sorted. While we’re on changing plans, any news on moving house? No update yet. We did make that real estate agent’s appointment for next week. I hope it goes well because we’re running out of patience with trying to find the right place. It’s like the sweet spots are all taken. True. Maybe we should broaden our search area just a bit. Wonder what’s further out but still relatively close to services and work. A good plan. Also, should we discuss our Christmas plans?

Yo, how was your weekend? Watch any good shows on Netflix? Yeah, watched quite a few. I've been bingeing on that new 'Rick and Morty' season. You should be watching that! It's hilarious. How about you? Ah, I heard rumors about it, but I don’t really have time for anything else right now. I've been swamped with uni work. Any chance of catching up with it later? Now, speaking of bingewatching, have you seen “The Crown” on Netflix? It’s amazing, really captures the royal family dynamics. No, not yet. But I heard about it from my mate. She's a history buff. Seems interesting. Is it any good cosplay-wise too? So, about the weekend, did you go places or just stuck at home? Just chilled at home mostly. Spent most of my time with the family. My mum made this amazing homemade pizza, though. Pizza, you say? That sounds great! I love a good homemade pizza. Yeah, it was really good. Maybe we could have a pizza and movie night sometime? That sounds like a plan! When are you free? Let me check my schedule. Wait a minute, I think Saturday evening is free. What about you? That works for me too! Can we invite some other friends? I know Alex, we could include him as well. Sure, let's invite Alex, and maybe some others. Yeah, we can post on Instagram that evening and see who else is around. Perfect! You're on. Sounds like a plan. Now, let’s get back to the Netflix thing. Have you seen “Euphoria” on HBO? It's pretty wild. Of course! It's so confronting but really well-made. Yeah, that's scary but intriguing. It’s really good for discussing with others because of all the current social issues it touches on. Right. I always take notes so I can later discuss it with my friends or even bring it up in an essay if the topics align. That's smart. Yeah, being engaged with the wider conversation helps. Always. Do you follow any certain influencers on social media? I've been looking into funny content to keep my spirits up during exam season. I often watch Phil Lester on YouTube. His stuff is hilarious and relatable. Phil Lester! Yeah, he's great. I saw that he recently did a video with Emily Hartridge, from '100 things'.

Yo, I was browsing on the internet yesterday and came across an idea online. What if we skyped and played some Pokémon together? Maybe compete in a battle or two. It sounds fun, don't you think? I love that idea, but considering Oisin is napping at the moment, this kind of activity might be best saved for when he's awake. Maybe this weekend? Da?! Oh, Oisin is awake. Looks like our little game night idea might have to wait. Fair enough. So, since we can't skype right now, did you hear that new Gym is open up in London?
