I bet they have some new goodies we can get our hands on soon! Not yet. But speaking of London, maybe you can help me with advice. I've been meaning to start looking for a creative activity to do with Oisin since he's big now. Something fun for both of us. Do you have any ideas? Hmm, he loves playing games? Maybe a trip to a local ice cream shop? Or learning how to play the guitar together? I heard it's good fun and you don't need to know everything. Plus, they make good music tutorials online. Oisin loves music, so the guitar idea might be a nice one. Anything specific you'd suggest for beginners? Sure, I found really good beginner tutorials online. For starters, learning a few simple chords. 'House of the Rising Sun' is a good one for example. But it's not just about the music; I think it would be a good bonding activity too. Plus, who knows, maybe it can become the next career for Oisin! That does sound fun and useful for both of us. I've always loved the idea of learning to play a musical instrument. You know, it's on my bucket list. Definitely. And for Oisin, it can be a great way to develop his motor skills and attention span. Plus, he could be the next Ed Sheeran or something! Or perhaps the next Youtuber reviewing Pokémon cards or making music. Maybe I should look into those tutorials with him. I might even learn something new. Absolutely. And you can always turn it into a family project. Maybe there's even some Pokémon themes you could inspire from. Dada, guitar? Music? Yes, that's right, Oisin. Mommy and I are planning to play some music together.

Oh, look at this! Remember how obsessed we used to be with this? We spent countless hours pretending to grow our own vegetables and fruits! Oh, absolutely! It was just so imaginative and fun back then. And to think that now we hardly have time to water our actual indoor plants... I wonder how many 'vegetables' we 'planted' with that set. You know, those plants never really grew. But the fun was in the act of gardening, not in actually having a harvest! Exactly! And the 'Bako' building set was another favorite of ours. Do you remember? We built those incredible structures—cities, sometimes whole worlds, and we lived in them through our play. And those tiny people we used as 'residents' in our miniature metropolises! We must have spent hours making different buildings and planning out the most fantastical scenarios for our world. I used to think, why weren't we like the others? Why did we spend so much time in our own world instead of joining in with their games of 'follow the leader' or hide and seek? But as I look back, I realize we were probably just much more... introverted dreamers. Or maybe, it was just because we were so close, so comfortable with each other. There was no need to seek out others when we had our own world of imagination. And, thinking of it now, I really do appreciate our childhood. It was carefree, full of endless possibilities. A pause while they both reflect on their shared memories, followed by a knock on the kitchen door. Oh, that must be the post. Can't they see we're having a meaningful and nostalgic conversation here? It's probably just a bill or another advert. You're right. It is just a bill, but funny thinking back, when we were just kids, we had no such worries. And don't forget the weather! It's been such a peculiar spring so far, hasn't it? Indeed. So changeable. One day it's like summer, the next it’s back to winter. It must be confusing for the plants and definitely for us. Well, as someone who used to fret about weather forecasts to plan our playground activities, I find it quite ironic now. But what can you do? It’s just the British weather being its characteristically unpredictable self. It's always been a big topic of conversation for us, hasn't it?

I keep reading that mosquitoes are becoming an increasing problem globally. Did you read that article in The Guardian last week about how warmer temperatures are influencing their distribution? Yeah, I did. I was actually horrified at the time. It’s just another reminder of how our actions are impacting the environment, isn’t it? Going for this walk and seeing all these little critters buzzing about makes me think of that article even more. And to be honest, I had a few bites today before we left for this walk even though I thought I was well-covered. Oh, really? Even with your deet? I always try to stay on top of applying that pesticide. But yes, it’s a real nuisance, especially with children. Exactly! Our little one has such sensitive skin. Just the other morning, she started acting fussy and we realized she had several bites from the night before. We’re looking for alternatives now, creative ways to keep them away without using harsh chemicals. I couldn’t agree more. I recently started using these citronella candles and oregano oil. Worth a try, right? Definitely, I might look into that. I’ve heard mixed results, but it’s worth experimenting. I also saw that some people suggest placing garlic near doors and windows. Did you ever try that? Only in jest! I once had a friend who swore by it but it’s hard to say in practice. But really, the key is to try and minimize standing water around the house. For sure. And since we’re talking about annoyances... I was stuck in such terrible traffic on the way here. London’s never been like this during the day. Oh, same here. I tried to avoid the usual route but I ended up getting stuck just the same. Seems like everyone’s getting back from vacation and going back to work. Exactly. And changing the traffic rules in Birmingham hasn't exactly helped. True. I heard there’s been a lot of debate about that. Anyway, it’s good we’re out here now. This fresh air is always a treat. So true! And look, she’s enjoying the park. She’s always so content outdoors. It’s amazing how different babies are. Mine would be wriggling and fussing nonstop if we didn’t get out for these walks. I know! And don’t even get me started on how different they are at home compared to here.

Yo, mate, had a crazy day today at the golf course. We had these two Aussies come over for a tournament and they were talking about how they don't even use hole-in-ones because they've played so much. It was mental! Oh, that’s interesting! I've always heard questions about why they'd even keep the rule if no one ever got a hole-in-one. Did they explain that to you? Yeah, actually, one of them said it's all about the strategy. They're so focused on making keeps coming that get them close. Crazy perspective, right? Yeah, okay. Like how lazy I’ve been with my phones lately. I’m on it all the time, but barely actually using it for something like exercise or even writing. I feel like I’m just scrolling through social media all day. [laughs] Hence your current situation with the recruitment process, bruh. I feel you on the phones thing though. It’s a mindless habit, isn't it? Like, I’m pretty good with switching it off when I’m on the course, but after that, I’m right back on it. For me, it's usually about checking the theatre schedules. Planning when to watch "Hamlet" is high on my list. How about you, still looking for a job? Stills at it. I’ve been to a few interviews, but nothing’s come through yet. And then there's uni stuff, I need to start preparing for exams again soon. Speaking of which, did you see that new study spot near Manchester? Thought it could be a good place to focus if I ever get there. Yeah, I was thinking of showing it to you. It’s great for studying, lots of quiet spaces. Actually, we should make some plans, maybe combine it with a visit to the new TV show set that just got set up in the city. I’ve heard they’re filming a new series there. Ah, sounds fun! A productive day before getting into the next round of exams would be great. And we should grab a bite somewhere new. Any recommendations? Well, I was thinking of this place called Casa that just opened up. They’ve got this amazing food, and it’s nearby. Plus, they serve so much different stuff, so you can avoid the usual midday slump. Again, sounds good.

Ah, did you hear that, Alan's singing voice is actually getting better. Yeah, his rendition of "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star" was quite impressive for a four-year-old though, wasn't it? Between his singing and your IT jokes, our dinner table sure is a colourful place. Ah well, you never know when your IT skills might come in handy. But seriously, how is school going for you, Thomas? Oh, it's all good. Slightly boring, to be honest. But I got through some really cool math tests recently. Math tests can be tough but good on you for working at it. Ah, watch him, Jack. You're going to be as smart as your uncle one day. Na-na-na-na-na-na-na-na Maybe one day, but for now, I'm just trying to balance school and trying to understand the cloud. Ah, cloud computing. That’s my world. Did I ever tell you the story of the time I migrated a massive data set to the cloud for a multinational company? Almost daily. But isn't it time we actually talked about the plans for your birthday tomorrow? Oh, right! How could I forget that? Uncle Liam, you're having a birthday party? Yes, young man. How did you hear about it? Mum said something about it a few days ago. Yes, we were supposed to make arrangements and finalize everything today. Ah, right. I thought I had sent out the invites last week. I suppose I should probably check. Did we decide on a theme or anything? Umm, no. I think I just assumed it was just a low-key gathering here at home. Well, whether it's low-key or not, we still need to decide on something. I like fireworks! Fireworks already, Jack? Don't worry, we'll see what we can do. But really though, maybe a movie night combined with a small gathering might work. Oooh, that sounds good! What about "Jurassic World"? That's a great idea, but perhaps something more family-friendly for Jack. How about "The Incredibles" or "Finding Nemo"? Those are both great choices. I think "The Incredibles" might be a bit too fast-paced for Jack though. Then "Finding Nemo" it is. Perfect. Now, let's finalize the menu. We could do something simple like a barbecue. That sounds great! Daryl, you take charge of that.

I've got something to share that's almost as hilarious as today's ANON sleeping in his pants incident. What is it then? Are we still on about the pants fiasco or have you thought of something else? Oh no, not the pants story again! Ah, but bear with me this time, actually, I've been thinking about how to deal with ANON's bizarre sleeping habits during our keepsakes here. You know how much he admires construction and architecture stuff, right? Yes, he's always been fascinated by that. Well, I was pondering this idea, as outrageous as it sounds, but maybe we could actually consider extending our old house here, just to accommodate his fantasies. Seriously? You want to add a house extension just because he sleeps in his pants? Yeah, I know it sounds bonkers, but hear me out. For a moment, imagine if it actually happened. We could have a whole new wing dedicated to his "special" sleeping quarters. We'll paint it in the theme of his favorite sports team, decorate with all sorts of construction and building things to make him feel like a mini contractor. I can see that could actually be quite therapeutic for him. He really does love architecture, as I've seen him spend hours sketching buildings in his notebook. But what about us? Would we have to sleep with construction manuals and models next to our beds or something? Maybe we could have a wing for each of the kids, where they could have a mini playschool. Exactly! It's all about making it a fun space for everyone. Of course, this is all just hypothetical and highly unlikely, but it's a fun way to make light of ANON's unique sleep habits. You know, that might not be such a bad idea for his mental well-being. It’s about giving structure to something so abstract. That’s the sweet spot. Besides, it’ll be something for him to be enthusiastic about. And who knows, he might just learn something practical like real job skills. I’ll make sure to remind him of the joys of sleeping in normal clothes if ever we do decide to build this extension. You're right, maybe this whole extension idea is... a bit of a dream. But imagine the fun we could have designing it! That’s what family is about, finding humor in things, despite the odds, and still supporting each other across the youthful rambunctiousness and cheeky remarks.

Ah, Phil, did you manage to sort out the last piece's costing for our research project? It's been giving me a bit of a headache this week. Still fiddling with that, Harold. There's quite a squeeze on the grant now and I think we need to pitch ourselves against a bit more scope this time. Going over the project notes one more time to make sure we cover all our bases. I've been thinking, perhaps we can look at a broader, interdisciplinary approach? Our colleagues in physics might have some valuable input, even if it's just at a theoretical level. You know how it's all related, after all. That’s an interesting idea, Harold. I’ve been following some developments in materials physics that might just bridge the gap between our research. Brilliant! Speaking of bridges, I've been making a bit of a mess of my home decorating over the past month. My wife thought I'd do wonders painting the walls but it's turned into a proper adventure. Home decorating adventures, right? I'm still waiting for my son to help me pick out the perfect Italian tile pattern for this new kitchen. It's been a challenge. I understand the sentiment. I've got this paint that I'm sure is going to need at least another coat; the walls seem to soak it up, you know? And then there's the color scheme, of course. I tore off pages from an Italian design magazine but now I’m not even sure if those really work with the rest of my kitchen. You might benefit from a design consultation. I was thinking of getting one myself but the cost is prohibitive. Perhaps we could use some cross-field expertise, Harold. I know Dr. Patel from the design department. Maybe he’d give us some pointers? At the very least, we could share resources. Ah, that's a solid idea. Of course, while we're figuring out ins and outs, let me know if you want any advice from an academic who's failed at painting. I think I’ll pass on that for now. I have a rough idea but it always helps to bounce ideas off someone else. Speaking of bouncing ideas, did you watch that documentary on the Hadron collider? Fascinating stuff but also a huge amount of funding going into those projects.

Alright, kids! Let's move these bricks around and see what kind of cool builds we can come up with. Remember, we don't just use Lego for building, but for story-telling. We can make a really cool Harry Potter scene now and then swap to a TMNT one – do you have any preferred sets or characters today? OH! Can we do a Hogwarts castle? Or maybe a scene from the Chamber of Secrets? I really loved the part when Harry found the diary! Yeah! Or Malfoy Manor! But I want to make a Lego Slytherin house too! And can we include the magic mirror? That sounds like a great idea, but before we start, let’s sort out all our Lego pieces. You both do well sorting Lego properly, right? It makes building so much easier. I... I try, but sometimes my big brother builds things and then doesn't put it back in the right box. And sometimes I just want to build what I feel like! Yeah, and I find it hard sometimes to remember which pieces go where. But I know if we sort it now while we play, we can build so many good things later! Exactly! Let's create a system. We'll make a few different groups – like all the people, buildings, vehicles, and special pieces. And we can use the big tray to keep everything organized. Can I get the baskets we use for sorting? Okay, this one for people, this one for buildings, and this one for special pieces... Brilliant! Now, while we're sorting, I noticed we have quite a few Harry Potter Lego sets. Why don’t we think about which one we want to build and then you can pick out the pieces we need. You can also add some things from the Simpsons or Ninja Turtles to make it even more interesting. Ooh! Can we do something combined? Maybe Harry Potter meets TMNT? It could be the Hogwarts Ninja Turtles! Haha, that’s a crazy idea! But maybe harder than we think. It could actually be fun! But for now, let's focus on sorting so we can have plenty of pieces to choose from for whatever we decide to build. Okay, I'm sorting the people. You get all the buildings and special pieces? Sounds like a plan. What about sorting out this chocolate we got for Easter?

Oh, did I ever tell you about my flatmate Grace? On the day before we went away, she was frantic about forgetting to book the tickets for her volunteer mission to Zambia! Made me laugh. Did she? That sounds like Grace – always on edge before big trips. How did she cope? She eventually sorted it out, thankfully. But I had to give her a couple of deep breaths and tell her, “Just breathe and it will all work out.” Right, let me guess... she just blurted, “How do you always manage to stay so calm about everything?” Exactly! She says that to me every time. And did you manage to get tickets for the rugby match next week? Yes, actually. We're going with Emily and Ryan. We’re looking forward to it – it’s been ages since we’ve been to a big match together. That sounds fun. I should probably catch up with Emily at some point as well. Definitely. It’s been too long. Speaking of catching up, has Thomas rung you about that study group for the job course? Yeah, I think he’s trying to meet up next Thursday after work. He said it’ll be over coffee at that new café on Brick Lane. Oh, good. I’m still in study mode, really need to keep up with my course. You working over the weekend? I could likely meet up with you if you weren’t... ...being a workaholic. Hey! That's career progression you're looking at there. How about we grab brunch on Sunday? The new place on the high street is supposed to be really good. Sounds like a plan. Maybe we can also catch up with Jade then too? That’d be great. Let’s plan for brunch, then a bit more catch-up later if time allows. Perfect. And by the way, how was your holiday? It was lovely – took the train down to Cornwall, stayed in a cute little B&B in the countryside. We had a great time. Did you know, I even managed to find this amazing little bakery with the most amazing pastries. Oh, I bet! Those Cornish pasties are to die for. They were! I brought back a few for you. That’s so sweet of you – I’ll have to try one now! They are on the table across the room if you want one, or maybe make some tea first?

Alright, Dad, Grace, today we're discussing how to sort out the garden and perhaps the house a bit. It's been a bit of a downer since Mum passed away, you know. Ah, yes, it’s changed things around a bit, hasn’t it? But I suppose that's life. What’s your thoughts, Grace? Erm, well, it’s just that the garden looks a bit... untidy, and it seems like it could do with some weeding, and maybe a bit of renovation in the house as well. Like, the windows need cleaning, and maybe some new curtains. Right, right, I’ve been meaning to do those things. I suppose it’s a project we could all pitch in on, isn’t it? Ooh, yes, it would be good to get the whole family involved. It’s not every day we all get together like this, or even have something to work on together. We could make it a bit of a day out. Yeah, and we could even have a little picnic afterwards. Like we used to do when the kids were little. Ah, that'd be brilliant! We could even have a BBQ if it’s not too cloudy. Alright, but we’ll do it properly. Grace, I think you should take charge of the food and drinks, including sorting out the cleaning and design for the house. Dad, could you look into sourcing some garden tools and seeing what needs to be done outside? Right, I’ve had enough experience with gardening over the years, and it’d be good to get a bit of fresh air. You sure you’re up for it, though? Oh, you know me, Dad. I just need something to structure my days so I don’t sink too deeply into the muck of daily life. And Granny and Grandpa could help with the BBQ and tell us all those old stories we love so much. Oh, I think I could get involved with that. I’ve got plenty of stories and a bit of a knack for making this humble BBQ taste... quite good, really! Ah, I’d wager that sounds like the plan then. When were you thinking of doing it, then? Let’s see... How about next Saturday? That seems like a bit of a clear weekend. Yes, but give us a bit of warning this time around, will you?

So, did you both hear about the real Peter Pan? It's not just a story folks. It's actually based on a real character. Do you remember this picture? What do you mean, Auntie? Did he really fly in London? Well, the real Peter Pan was a boy from Scotland named Peter Llewelyn Davies. J.M. Barrie, the author of Peter Pan, knew Peter and he became inspired by him to write this story. But no, he didn't fly in real life, of course. That's just in the story. But it's about fairies and Indians and pirates, right? How can it be about a real person? Exactly! J.M. Barrie uses real people and places, but he adds a lot of fantasy. He even used his own childhood experiences and people he knew for some characters. A character named Wendy, for example, is based on a close friend of his. So, who is Tinker Bell? Tinker Bell is a fairy in the story. She's quite proud and sometimes a bit jealous of Wendy, remember when Wendy and Peter become friends? Tinker Bell doesn't like that, does she? I don't like her whenever she's mean to Wendy. Me neither. But then she turns nice when she's changing the color of Peter's shadow on the wall. Yes, Tinker Bell is complex, isn't she? Like most characters in real life. So, Auntie, are there other stories or films like this about kids who can fly? There's actually quite a few! You might have seen "Mary Poppins", or "The Wonderful Wizard of Oz". They're not exactly like Peter Pan, but they're all from around the same time period when people were really fond of magical and adventurous stories for children. I wish I could fly too. Well, you can fly in dreams and imagination, and that's just as magical. I've seen the movie "Pan", but the boy who played Peter Pan didn't really look like how I imagined him. You're right. Each portrayal of Peter Pan, whether in films or plays, adds its own interpretation. But what's important is how much fun we have imagining and being inspired by these stories. Can we watch Pan again next week? Sure, sweetheart. Let's plan that after school next week. And next time we talk about Peter Pan, we can also talk about "Finding Neverland", a film about J.M. Barrie and how he came up with the idea for Peter Pan.

Ah, well, seems like we're just passing through Taunton now. You know, I used to live near here, back when I was managing the factory in Chard. It's quite the change from where I am now. I've always loved the views around here, particularly the way the light hits the fields just before sunset. Though, commuting like this to work every day must be quite tiring, isn't it? Indeed, I still find it tiresome at times, especially with this length of journey. But it’s a lifestyle choice, isn’t it? Either the job, or the location. I actually taught for a stint in Exeter a few years ago, and the commute was quite similar. It wasn't easy, but there was so much to enjoy in the city itself that it somewhat balanced it out, you know? Well, there's no denying it's a sacrifice. But I'd say the scenery here in Devon is a hell of a consolation prize. I remembered thinking if I just had a small cottage in some less populated area of Devon, commuting would feel a lot less like... ...a chore, I suppose. That’s so true! We actually considered moving to Taunton ourselves for my job. The commute was appealing, but ultimately, we chose the house for its proximity to schools for the kids. Speaking of which, how's the new school treating you? It’s quite fulfilling, to be honest. I’ve managed to establish a good rapport with my pupils and my fellow teachers are supportive. Taunton does offer a good quality of life, especially outside the school year. But yes, the commute has its drawbacks. I suppose it’s a trade-off we all make in various ways. You know what though? I always thought about moving closer to Wellington. I have a sister who lives just across the Exe, and that’s where my folks are buried. It feels like at some point, we’ll end up there permanently. Wellington sounds lovely. We have a friend who’s from there, she always speaks highly of the community and lifestyle. I’ve met a few people from Wellington during school events. They do have a strong sense of community there. Absolutely, yes. But for now, let’s talk about plans for Christmas, shall we? We should plan something nice for the family, don’t you think?

Oh, I've been so knackered after that vigorous track work. I swear, they say Swedish massage is wonderful for the muscles after a deep activity like that! Ah, Swedish massage. I used to think it was all a bit of a farce back in the days when I was involved with the building society, but now, I've been part of a local hospice and I've seen how beneficial it can be for the elderly. Oh, I've got a keepsake here from a local nursery in Somerset where my son worked. They were introducing Swedish massage to the children there. I have to say, it seemed quite peculiar, but I suppose it's just another sign of how we're continuously trying to make education more holistic. Yes, holistic education - another term that’s becoming all the rage. I always thought it was a bit of a fad, but being at the hospice has taught me to grasp new concepts. After all, if it helps someone find peace or comfort, it couldn’t hurt. I completely agree! So, on that note, have you ever considered this hospice for maybe, yourself or a loved one? It’s different from anything the NHS provides. Actually, my wife passed away there in good care. It was a tremendous help for us, really. The level of attention, especially from some of the female staff members, was quite touching. It made me realise how much of a difference female equality in the workforce can make, even in such contexts. Oh, I see. Female equality is something I’ve always been passionate about, especially in the arts industry where I worked. We were always underrepresented, even though we brought our unique perspectives and talents. Absolutely. I remember attending one of those ME events in the West Midlands where they were discussing the future of female involvement in more male-dominated industries. It was incredibly inspiring, but we had a long way to go, even back then. True, but changing the world takes time. I find that we often focus so much on the destination that we forget about the journey. I suppose that's why I enjoy collecting art and antiques, each piece has its own journey, its own history. That's quite the perspective. I used to be very much about the destination myself, but this retirement has taught me to appreciate the journey.

Mum, I was thinking that we might want to discuss our plans for the upcoming holiday. We still don't have a set destination in mind and I know we've been talking about this for a while now. Ah, yes! Right, isn't it time now, then? You've been postponing deciding on a place for ages. I agree, we should get it sorted out and book something soon. We could miss out on good deals if we leave it too late, especially since you've been eyeing up that deal for that Moroccan villa. That's true. I've been looking at flights and it seems pricey, but the villa itself is quite reasonable. But I have to admit, I'm having a bit of trouble deciding. Tell me, sweetie. What's holding you back from making a decision? Is it the culture maybe? Or are you worried about travel restrictions and COVID? A bit of both, to be honest. With the pandemic, I'm a bit anxious about the situation over there and changing rules could be a hassle. But at the same time, I've always wanted to visit Morocco or even Marrakech specifically. The culture and history are so rich and it's been on my list for ages. I totally understand that. I remember the last time we went abroad, in Greece, the rules changed rapidly and we had to stay really vigilant. But at the end of the day, we had a wonderful time, didn’t we? It was probably the best holiday we've ever had as a family in recent years. Yeah, we did, and it was fantastic. But it's a bit different now. Plus, doesn't your experience in consultancy and training come into play here? I kind of feel like we could use your expertise to plan all this. That's very thoughtful of you to think of me in that light. I could, indeed, help with planning. I used to regularly research destinations and recommend them to companies, but for family, it's different. We want something comfortable and relaxing, but also cultural so we can learn something. Exactly. I was thinking of something that would make the most of our time. Perhaps a city break with some cultural tours but also a bit of relaxation. But I'm also worried about the language barrier. You know, most people speak French and some English in Marrakech and other tourist areas, especially in the hospitality industry.

Yo, mate, did you hear about Leicester City? Yeah, I did. What about them? They just got promoted to the Premier League! I mean, that's huge for them. It definitely is, mate! You a big football fan, ain't ya? Yeah, I'm a massive supporter. Leicester City is a part of my history, you know? Born and raised in Lincoln, grew up watching them. Oh wow, so that's keepsakes right there. You know, when I was in Barbados, it was all cricket, soccer never really caught on there. [laughs] I can only imagine! Cricket is massive here too, by the way. Did you ever play when you were younger in Barbados? Played a bit, but it was more about cricket and track and field. I was actually a pretty fast sprinter at school. That's cool! Fast, eh? I'm more of a bench warmer [laughs], but it's still fun to play. [laughs] I’m more of a spectator now, enjoyed it when I was younger. How’s your student life been lately? It's been alright. Just finished my graduate studies; it's quite a relief to have that part over with. Now I'm trying to find some work experience. It's not easy, but I'm optimistic. That sounds good. Finding a job in this economy... really tough. I remember when I started out, I had to hustle too. For sure. How about your job? Going alright? [sighs] It's good, you know? Been in management for a while now. But the work keeps me going. The company's expanding, so there's a lot on my plate at the moment. Ah, I see. Expanding can be stressful but also rewarding, no? Indeed! But it's changing the business landscape in Barbados. New opportunities, new challenges. Change can be good. Plus, I'm sure you're doing great at it. You always seemed like the take-charge type, even at school. [laughs] Thanks mate, I’ll take that as a compliment. You know, managing people and projects isn’t just about giving orders; it’s about understanding people and processes. Yeah, I suppose so. It's like coordinating a game plan. Always a challenge, but when it works well, it's a great feeling. Totally. Speaking of... I was thinking of visiting the UK next year. Maybe we could catch up properly then? That would be brilliant!

Ah, so I remember when we used to travel via these old school youth hostels. Decent folk mostly, but you know, young and rough 'round the edges. Got some of the best times of my life there! Oh, yes, I remember! We always ended up in some kind of mess at the end of the night! I'm sure you two did! Speaking I had a similar experience when I set up my school project about rebuilding an old underground system. Think about it - the idea of transforming something once used for, well, 'underground' activities into a vibrant hub of learning and culture. It's fascinating really. Fascinating indeed. I never thought about that part of the places when I was younger, but oh, the railways, the organization, the engineering... it's a whole system, innit? Exactly! And creative too! While we were there, we would often visit similar places in Yorkshire - it's like a whole different world up there, innit? The countryside or even just the urban centers have a different charm. Now that's a subject close to my heart. Where did you all go while on 'holidays'? Was it more the seaside or the countryside? Well, after a bit of both, actually. Seaside was fab, nice and relaxing, but I always preferred the country-side. There's something about the fresh air, the quiet, the walking... Although I'm not as mobile these days, that bad leg of mine... but doesn't stop me from enjoying it in my own way, of course. Yes, poor you. Never let the body dictate what your heart wants, though, eh? Absolutely. I've been meaning to look into getting a mobility scooter for me mum, who's in a similar situation. That way she can still get out into the gardens - she's always loved working with her plants. Oh, gardens, that brings back memories! I used to have a small one myself before we moved. Nothing fancy, but so much joy. Makes me miss it now that I'm here mostly. It's good you have you and your household... although this lockdown has been... Indeed, it's been a struggle. Not just for the obvious reasons. Watching too much television, not being able to go out when you want to... but I must admit, I've been enjoying a few programs that... explore the world through our TV sets!

Right, so I've been looking at flights to Paris for our little break. I found a really cheap flight from Stansted that would get us there on Wednesday morning and back on Friday evening. That's great! I've been really excited for this trip. I've never been to Paris and I've heard so many good things. It's going to be totally amazing. I've been there once before and it's absolutely stunning. The food, of course, is amazing and I know we'll have a great time. Are you planning on booking it straight away? You know how quickly prices can change, don't you? Actually, I just need to check with you that the date is fine. Is your schedule still clear? Yeah, totally. But let me double-check my project schedule at work. As a production controller, I have to make sure that I don't have any important deadlines coming up that I might need to be around for. That makes sense. While you're doing that, I can start looking at accommodation options. Someone recommended a hostel near the Latin Quarter or Montmartre. Thoughts? Both places sound lovely! Montmartre would be great if we want to stay in a quieter part of the city. Latin Quarter has lots of action if you're looking for that. Yep, and the food scene in both areas is excellent. We could try a nice little Bistro in Montmartre one evening, maybe? Sounds like a plan! But have you looked into the budget? I'm not really sure what you're thinking in terms of costs. Okay, so the flight from Stansted is under £50 return, and the hostel options I'm seeing are around £20-£25 per night. Add in food, transport and any additional activities and we're looking at around £300-£400 each for the whole trip, depending on what we do. That actually seems pretty reasonable! I think we'll be okay with that. What was the project schedule at your work like? Ah, I'm sure we can manage. I just have a few conference details to confirm over the next week but it's not anything major. It'll be fine to take 3-4 days off. Excellent. Then let's book this. I'll just send you the job numbers and we can finalise. I also need to check my bank balance to make sure everything is covered.

Right, so I was going over my accounts this morning and noticed that groceries have really gone up these past few months. It’s not just the food prices, but the packaging and delivery charges too. I've noticed that Tesco seems to be one of the more affordable options now, but I haven’t seen many price drops on essentials like bread and milk. That’s true. As a language teacher, I often hear foreign students complaining about how expensive things are here. It’s not just food, but service charges too. They can’t understand why even banks keeps changing their fees and interest rates so frequently. Oh, that’s been a real stress for me too. Remember when banks seemed more straightforward? Now I’ve got three different bank accounts scattered with different interest rates and fees to keep track of. Exactly! And don’t even get me started on the railways. The prices keep rising and customer service seems to get worse. Yes, and with all these changes, it feels like we’re constantly playing catch-up. Like last week, I tried to grab a cheap flight to Brighton for a weekend and the prices went up by £50 in under an hour. So I’m now trying to stick with train travel. At least there, I can predict what it's going to cost. I understand your pain. I've had to deal with the rise in council tax as well. It really adds up. And the worst part is, neither technology companies or banks are giving us a break. Honestly, I feel like we’re being squeezed from all sides in terms of costs. Tell me about it. We might have survived the '70s when prices were high but at least things were more predictable then. Now it's inconsistent and that’s what really grates. I don’t understand why mobile phone plans have the same issue. Seems like the price keeps going up but service doesn’t improve, and the contracts keep getting more confusing. If only we had more solid consumer protection laws governing these things. It feels like nobody is accountable anymore for providing good service or fair value for money. Speaking of which, my brother’s daughter got charged £10 for a late return of a book for her online library. Imagine that—paying a fine for something you’re already paying a subscription for.

So, I hear everyone's planning exciting holidays for the first time's break. What are you all thinking of doing? Oh, I've been dreaming about this for ages. I'm planning on heading to Cardiff for a week with a couple of friends. We're going to visit all the popular spots – the Bay, the castle, and maybe even Bute Park if the weather holds up. That sounds like brilliant fun! I've heard of a lovely cozy B&B near the castle. They said it offers a hearty Irish breakfast, which is exactly what I need after a late night out. Haha! Sush, I'm planning to explore more of Wales and I've been wanting to check out Snowdonia. The landscapes up there are just so stunning. Do any of you have any recommendations for good hiking spots? I’m not going on holiday this time around. I’m trying to save money for a more relaxing break later in the year, but I do aspire to visit the Peak District. I love the history and the chance to try all the local pubs for food. So, you like the outdoors, then? We could totally plan a group trip to the Peak District if all of us could make it work with our schedules. How does that sound, while the weather’s still good? I’d love that! Do we also plan to visit places like the Chatsworth House or Bakewell? Ooh, Bakewell tart, yes! There’s one cafe I’ve heard of, really good. And yes, we’re always open to a group outing. Just make sure we also check out all the best local eateries. There’s nothing like trying food from local cafes and pubs, am I right? Definitely. I’ve got this one place in mind near Aberystwyth that does the best fish and chips ever. Fish and chips by the sea – that's the vacation! Speaking of food, does anyone else like baking? I was thinking of trying out a new recipe over the break – maybe that Irish tea cake I saw in a magazine. Baking is my soothing hobby. I’m all for it. Maybe we could do a bake-off? Or even a cooking competition? Like, we could each pick a local dish to make from where we’re from and see who makes the best one. That’s a fantastic idea!

I've been thinking a lot about our life choices. I mean, what happens when we're old? Do you think we'll be living together still, or even thinking the same way? You're already worried about being old? Yeah, I guess so! I mean, I've got a bunch of essays due and all this stuff to think about now, but sometimes I just can't help but wonder... I mean, what if we still hang out with each other even when we're old and grey? Definitely, I think. Like, we're lucky to have each other, right? And if we can stick through university and whatever comes next, that just says something about our relationship. Definitely. But do you think we'll still be making art? I hope so! Maybe not the same kind of art—you know, sometimes I think creative work changes as you get older. But maybe we'll still be making something we love. I was thinking, maybe we could even start something together then. Maybe like a small studio or something. That sounds like a dream! I'm sure we could figure something out, but for now, let's just focus on passing this English literature module. Indeed. A serious topic for later, maybe. Speaking of which, did you get time to work on that essay for Mrs. Henderson? I'm still stuck on my own. To be honest, no. I keep getting distracted by everything else. But last night while gaming, I had this idea for the essay. Maybe I could write about how art and literature evolve with age? How the perspective changes and what that means for the artists and audience? That's brilliant! Of course, you came up with something while gaming. That’s typical! But it actually could make for an interesting essay. You should definitely write on that. Thanks for the vote of confidence. But do you have any tips on how to structure it? Absolutely! Let’s break it down into sections: introduction, the historical perspective, and then how the evolution of perspective affects the art and the audience. Make sure to use real-life examples and tie them back to Mrs. Henderson's coursework. That makes sense. I can start with our discussion earlier, maybe even quote you if you don’t mind being a source on that? We can pretend our flatmate chit-chat is inspirational enough for an academic essay.

I've decided I need to start making healthier choices. I've been meaning to do this for ages. I've joined a diet app and it's been so eye-opening, unreal! Most nights, I'm making something simple like pasta or fish because it's quick and easy, but tonight I thought I'd try something new. Wow, that sounds like a great decision! I've always been a bit guilty of the same thing, especially with my late shifts as a mental health nurse. Sometimes it's hard to find the energy to cook a decent meal after a long day. What's the app called? Maybe it can help me, too. It's called MyFitnessPal. It's great for tracking what you eat and setting realistic goals. I've already noticed a difference. That sounds useful. I need something like that. These past few months have been pretty tough with work. Sometimes I find myself grabbing whatever is closest to hand - usually unhealthy stuff. But let's admit it, comfort food has it's place. Especially when it comes to what you're making tonight though. For me, it's usually a roast or some homemade pasta dish, but tonight I thought I'd make this quinoa and vegetable stir-fry. It's supposed to be really good for you, and quite filling. Quinoa and vegetables, that sounds perfect for us. We've been eating a bit too much takeaway lately. I feel like we always talk about it but can never seem to actually cook for each other properly. We have been. But it's not just about cooking, right? It's also about being mindful of what we're eating and why. For me, food and our habits around it have been all over the place lately. And let's not forget about those side of chips we had together last week. Oh, right! If only we had chips that were good for us. Because science hasn't figured that out yet. We could sit here and complain all day about our diet or we can make small changes. Like tonight - we're not only cooking but it's just the two of us, which is rare. That's true! It's been a while since we've had a good catch-up. And usually we spend it talking about work or our friends, but this could be different.

Right, let's get back to the consent form then, shall we? I've been going over the draft and there are a few things I'd like to discuss. Absolutely, let's do that. Is there anything specific that's caught your eye? Yeah, I think we need to be clearer on what students agree to when they participate in the seminar and the research project. We're gathering data, after all. True, and as the primary researcher, we need to ensure participants are fully informed. But remember, keeps it simple and concise, people won't read too much if it's too wordy, especially if it's online. Agreed, but I also think we need to include what kind of data we'll be collecting, how it'll be used, and whether it can be identified or if it'll be anonymized. Anonymity is a must unless you need individual data, I'd say. We should also address how we'll handle data once the seminar is concluded. Do we store it? And for how long? That's a good point. I think a year or two is reasonable? Maybe we could include a statement about storing it for archive purposes but destroying it if not used within the expected project timeframe. Good idea. And what about the written consent? For research projects like this, sometimes it's not just the form. We may need to include a verbal confirmation or a written statement, or both? I think both are good. But isn't in-person or virtual sign-off more common? Given we’re probably recording parts of the seminar, we’ll need consent for audio/video too. Correct, and we’ll also need the written form for our records, especially for our research ethics committee. I don’t want any issues come audit time. Agreed. How about we include a checkbox on the written form for audio/video consent? We can say something like: "I agree that this seminar can be recorded for academic purposes and that my participation and any questions asked or answered may be included in the research data." That covers it. Plus, I think we should note that participants can withdraw at any time. We need to specify that their data will be destroyed if they request it. Right, and have a contact name and email provided for anyone who wants to withdraw or has concerns.

I keep telling them to choose subjects relevant to the students' interests today. Modern students are so involved in technology and pop culture. I don't know why they insist on the old bookish stuff. It’s just tradition, isn’t it? But I do see your point. I had one student last semester who struggled terribly with Shakespeare and couldn’t understand why he "had" to read it. I had to give him extra tutoring just to help him see the relevance. And how did that turn out? Surprisingly well. By linking his favorite TV shows to Shakespearean themes, he finally started engaging with the material. But it makes me wonder, why do we stick to traditional literature if we can connect to them through more modern means? Exactly. It’s like the "Two Cultures" debate all over again. We’re stuck in a system that doesn’t fully understand its audience anymore. But it’s hard to change, right? You get pushed back by tradition. Someone should study the efficacy of modernizing our syllabus. Oh, absolutely. We should. But it requires time and research. I’ve been considering collaborating with some colleagues on a curriculum study. That sounds like a project for a conference. I’d totally join you on that. Maybe we can present it in Liverpool or Oxford next year? I’d love that. We could really shake things up. But let’s not get too serious about work. How about your side of the fence? Anything new going on with you? Just been prowling real estate sites, it seems like. We talked about that house we’ve been wanting and our budget has increased a bit now. We can actually look at things that really appeal. Oh, that’s exciting! Which part of London were you looking at? Southwark or Lambeth. There are some lovely developments there. We’d really like a garden, but we know it’s challenging in the city. Southwark's got some great parks – I know because I had a conference in that area. But I know what you mean about real estate in London. I mean, house prices! Can we afford a real garden in such an area? It’s about compromise. We could look at shared green spaces or communal gardens. Maybe a co-housing project? Not my first choice but if it means we get something with some greenery.

So, I was browsing through one of those strict vegan or zero-waste cooking channels today. Did you ever consider what an impact cutting down on food waste could make, not just for our wallets but for the environment too? Yeah, it's something Mum talks about a lot, actually. She questions how much food we tend to throw away and often finds ways to repurpose leftovers. It's amazing how much we waste without even realizing it. Absolutely. I found this app that suggests recipes for what you already have at home rather than shopping for new ingredients. It's kind of like an inventory check before you go to the market. Saves money and reduces waste at the same time. That sounds handy. Though, let’s be honest, even with digital tools, ensuring our food doesn't go waste is largely about discipline and organization. And sometimes, well-planned menu planning can make all the difference. Definitely. It also reminded me of how our grandparents used to manage food in the house. Do you remember those summer visits when we would help in the kitchen, and every scrap would end up in a delicious casserole or soup? Oh, definitely. It was all about making use of what you had. I remember the smell of Grandma’s kitchen too—a bit of everything in everything. They taught me the joy of making do with what you have rather than the desire for the next new thing. Absolutely. But while they were very practical, perhaps even more so than we are today, there were also discussions in our family about really old fashioned ideas like dowries. It’s all part of our social and cultural heritage, but it feels like such a foreign concept now. Yeah, it’s weird how much influence such customs could have, especially in arranging marriages. We discussed this in sociology studies the other day. Seems like the value was more in the assets a family could provide. Exactly! It's interesting to see how much of that concept has influenced traditional societies but is slowly fading away. But then there are still areas where concepts like dowries are considered important. It’s all about the context, though, right? No one’s thinking about dowries these days. But I did find out that when it comes to careers, there are still 'closed' industries where certain social influences help a great deal.

I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen Grace's school report? It arrives today and I'm curious about how she's doing. Not yet, I've been a bit tied up at work today. But I can have a look later if you like? Oh, absolutely. It would be really helpful if you could give me an idea of what it says. You seem to have a better knack for understanding those things than I do. Well, that's because I have to read a lot of them in my job. But it's usually just a quick scan for me. I can help you decipher any jargon if there is. Great, thank you. I like how you always translate those education speak terms into plain English for me. You're welcome, that's what I'm here for. Speaking of which, have you thought about what you're going to make for dinner? I can help you if you need a hand. Actually, I was thinking of trying out a new recipe I saw on the internet. It's a bit complicated but sounds delicious. A complicated recipe, eh? Good for you for trying different things. If I'm around to help, I’d be happy to lend a hand. That would be great. It's really nice having us both at home. It feels like ages since we've had a proper evening together without any commitments. It has been silly isn't it? I've really missed our relaxed evenings cooking and talking about our days. Me too. So, what was your day like today? There was quite a bit of work behind the scenes today preparing for the new assessment system. Some people in the team were less than impressed about the changes, but hopefully, it will streamline things. Changing systems can be such a hassle. I know it's necessary but it always feels like it's causing more problems than it solves initially. Exactly. But I think eventually we might find it helps us do our job more efficiently, especially when it comes to analyzing feedback and adjusting our approaches. However, today it just felt like a lot of paperwork and explanations to various people who were resistant to change. That sounds familiar. I was working on a new research project and almost all of my time today was spent going through paperwork.

You two be needin' a voice to listen, eh? No, no, don’t need to tell me what questions are brewin'. I've got years and years of listening under me belt. You always manage to be there for us, John. These days, it’s been a bit tough. Everything's been feeling so out of place. Our line of work was never exactly... rewarding, in the end. Well, that’s one thing we’ve got on our side then. Human connection and friendship. Invaluable and free! But I’ve got a busy week with report cards coming up, but today, I’m all ears. What’s on the mind? Ah, the world's gone all upside down, hasn’t it? Almost seems like we fell through the cracks, all of us. John here was meant for the docks, but they said his 'stature needed a desk'...sounds silly now, but that was the reasoning back then. And me? A career in textiles was the goal, but those factories closed down just when I was hitting my stride. I ended up shuttin’ down my skills for childminding. It was lovable, but it didn’t pay and it got lonely after a while. It’s a common story. I teach a bit more about history now but I teach in a city. I often see those just like us. Folks stuck in old industrial towns where the jobs just vanished overnight. Ah, Costessey back in the day... it was like any job could put food on your table. Now, it's all about what degree you got instead of the sense of wanting to work. But there's still volunteering, right? That’s a job that can't be automated or outsourced...and it's rewarding in its own right. Volunteering’s what keeps John and me still feelin’ like we’re useful, I suppose. We did some work at the local wildlife center at one point. Remember the baby blue tits? Yes! Those little birds, eh? So cute. That’s when I learned I’m not as out of place near nature as I thought I was. That’s beautiful. Folded under the weight of circumstance but still carrying on. You two are remarkable for findin' ways to thrive in retirement. But there's this...ongoing weight, don't you reckon? Even with the community center visits and whatnot...it’s the lack of connection to something that gives you a sense of ‘usefulness’.

So, I've been meaning to try out this new hair mask I've seen advertised. Have you used any of these before? It's supposed to be really good for deep conditioning. Oh, I've tried a couple of different ones. I've used this particular brand, though, and it worked quite well for me. Really? That’s great! What about the colour? You seem to have such nice, vibrant hair... Do you have any tips for maintaining hair colour? Oh, thank you! I get a colour treatment at the salon about every 6 weeks, but in between, I use a colour-preserving shampoo and try not to wash it every day. That’s very sensible. I wash my hair fairly regularly, but maybe I need to change that. Also, have you tried any DIY hair masks? I’ve heard that homemade ones can work just as well. Yeah, sometimes I do. A very simple one is just using olive oil and honey. But honestly, if it's professional products you're after for deeper conditioning, those really work better. For me, it's often about finding the right balance between cost-effective and effective. The different professional products seem quite pricey. Where did you get yours from? Was it at a salon or online? I found it at the local beauty supply store. It wasn't too pricey, considering it's a professional brand. But I agree, it's always about finding balance. There are also some good in-between options, like drugstore brands that have fantastic reviews. That's a good point. I've been buying more things online lately, it's convenient and I can compare reviews easily. Have you found anything good online? I have bought things from different online retailers. Amazon has some good options if you’re a Prime member, they often have discounted prices. I also use Boots. They have a wide range of professional products at decent prices. Really? That's great! I actually have a Boots card so I could use some discounts. I might check them out next time. Yeah, for sure. I've had good luck with their beauty section. They often have deals too, especially for students or with their loyalty scheme. That sounds good. Also, let’s talk nails. I just had a manicure and went for a gel polish. It's lasted really well so far.

Yo, mate, been a while. How's work been treating ya? It's been okay, all things considered. Had a tough case recently, but it's all part of the job, right? You know, one of our neighbors is having a tough time finding a place to park – do you have any suggestions? Parking in Liverpool? You'd think they'd get smart and start building up instead of out, but I'm right there with ya. I had a similar situation with my own flatmate. We even got a bit of a parking plan brewing over in our area. You know, actually, I was at the Walker Art Gallery the other day, just had to check out some of the new exhibitions. Sent my students to write reviews about it, so I had to make sure it was worth a visit. That's clever. I've been thinking of taking my mates to the Walker for the new retrospective of Northern artists. Great idea! Yeah, but I've been so caught up in uni and work, I haven't really had time or energy for much else. Oh, come on, mate. You're gonna finish your postgrad soon enough, and then you can start thinking about all the things you’ve been putting on hold. Like moving house, for instance. Any thoughts yet? Ah, yea, I've been pondering – I'm thinking of moving up to Waterloo, I love the area, but it's tricky finding a place that fits all my needs. I hear ya. And with the Liverpool housing market, it's like finding a needle in a haystack. Exactly. Just last weekend, I helped my sister plan her wedding and it’s amazing how much the venue and parking stress out the whole family. Lol, always the parking. I noticed that at our niece's wedding. Next time, couple should’ve had a valet service or something. That’s a great idea! We could sit here all day talking about parking. Speak for yourself. But for me, I've been thinking about something else, my interview for the MA program at Hope University. I’ve been prepping a bit, but it's making me reconsider how I’ve been managing my finances. That’s huge. Whether I’m teaching or advising students on personal finance, I always emphasize the importance of budgeting. Exactly, so I've started looking seriously at my finances and I realized I need to cut back on this and that.

So, how are you coping with being a stay-at-home mum? It can't be easy. I remember when I was teaching full time and juggling home life, I felt like I was pulling my hair out some nights. Oh, you have no idea how much I admire those who do both. I'm not sure I could swing it. The house gets messy and there's always this perpetual chaos with the little one. It makes me feel guilty sometimes, like I'm not doing enough. Oh, don't even get me started on guilt. That's a whole other conversation for another time. But seriously, you're doing a great job. Raising a toddler is just as much work as running a classroom, if not more. I read that in a book somewhere once. It really stuck with me. What I find hard is the lack of independence though. It's been so long since I had my own space and decided on my own schedule. Do you ever feel like you lost yourself in the process of juggling work and home life? Absolutely. I think any mother or parent will tell you that. It's a balancing act, and sometimes it feels like no matter how hard you try, you can't quite tilt the scale in your favor. But the important thing is, you don't lose yourself; you just adapt and find other things to define you, like being a mother, an individual, or whatever combination works for you. That's a great perspective, I suppose. It makes me think about relationships, though. You know, sometimes when we’re in partnerships and all that, it feels like "us" takes up so much space doesn't it? But it's good to keep the "me" alive too, right? Totally. We've talked about this before, but I believe in maintaining independence within relationships. It’s about being two people, not one entity. You are still a person with your own hobbies, interests, and ambitions—you don’t have to lose all of that. True, but changing the dynamic when children are involved is a whole different story. It's like, all these new vulnerabilities that come with dependence, not just financial but emotional as well. Absolutely. But that’s where communication comes in, isn’t it? And finding that balance together. I have to admit, even with the best of intentions, it's trial and error most of the time.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we were watching that episode of The Office and Ian found the Easter egg where they're all silent and talked in sign language? No, you never did. That must have been wild. It was just so funny! We had no idea until my sister pointed it out. We rewatched the whole episode again and couldn't stop laughing. But actually, that reminds me I saw an awesome Pinterest board about Easter eggs in TV shows. It even had loads of Easter eggs in The Office. You should check it out sometime, really cool to see how much effort they put into these little details. Yeah, I love that kind of thing too. I've been spending way too much time on Pinterest anyway, finding new home decor ideas. My flat's been looking a bit dull lately. Oh, looking for a home decor upgrade, are we? You couldn't say it wasn't needed. I mean, I've been calling my living room 'the cave of productivity' for years now. I can't imagine. You're a PhD student, you should have everything neat and tidy in there. Well, I used to. Now, it's more 'organized chaos'. But seriously, I need to sort it out, especially since we're planning a birthday in there next week. Oh, who's it for? Actually it's for my mate Alex. We're doing a big 'TV and gaming weekend' for him, cause he's just super into things like that. He's always the king of festivities, so I just thought, why not make it all about it? We'll have pizza, burgers, and all the popular TV shows we can find. That sounds great! I could totally help with food. Birmingham's burgers aren't half bad, by the way. You know, that place down the high street in Broad Street? Oh, I know it. I've been there a few times. They serve an awesome burger. And for drinks, unless you could spare some Newcastle Brown Ale... As if I'd let you go without some! But what about decorations? Are you thinking of doing any decorations or just keeping it super casual? I thought maybe a big TV screen or projector outside, with some... I don't know, TV or gaming-inspired decorations? Nothing too over the top, just fun.

Oh, did you find anything interesting on eBay? I just can't believe how many light fittings are out there! I've been finding myself wanting to redecorate all of our rooms but I need to decide on one first to get the ball rolling, you know? Oh, I agree! There's so much out there and it's overwhelming. I spent a good hour just browsing and I think I settled on a couple that I like. I'd love to get your opinion. Which ones did you like so far? Well, I was really fond of this one pendant light, it's a beautiful glass chandelier. But I've been worried about the delivery costs. They say it's 15 quid, but then there's also the postage... Ah, yes - oh we've all been through that. Sometimes you end up spending more than you wanted on delivery, I know that all too well looking for my Ronimoa... Did I tell you about this blackout blind I found? Perfect for those early light mornings, especially now that summer is coming. We could really do with that in the bedrooms, don't you think? That is a brilliant idea! I wasn't even thinking about curtains but blinds are a more practical and modern choice, certainly for the kitchen and probably the bedrooms. I used to have blinds at my old place and they were so easy to clean and maintain. Exactly! And they seem to be more efficient for blocking out light compared to curtains. Although I do have a love for the look of curtains when they're intricately designed… I do too, but finding good deals on blinds on Rightmove can be just as satisfying. Did you start looking into that? More specifically, house hunting? I just tried to get a feel for the market before we decide on a move. Oh absolutely, I've been looking at houses in our area and it's bonkers! Prices are changing so quickly and it's scary to think we might not be able to find anything within a reasonable price that suits what we're looking for. I know what you mean. But we need to be realistic about what we can afford and the area we want to live in. I found a few good places but most of them are almost out of our budget. It's like real estate has become a whole different world.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my day at work? We had the craziest situation. A patient was scheduled for a surgery, and they wouldn’t stop talking about their cat who had recently died. That sounds odd but also kind of heartbreaking. I've had days like that too where a patient finds something to talk about that has nothing to do with their situation at hand. Oh I had a similar situation too! But it was with a patient who keeps coming in with their pet. Crazy how much comfort they get from those animals, isn't it? True! It's such a dynamic shift seeing how much these pets mean to them. Makes me appreciate just how valuable my job is. Do any of you have pets back home? I do! I have two little dogs. They can be a handful, but they’re so much fun. Oh, I love dogs! My little Jack loves my job too, though. He likes people and it makes him happy to see so many people in one day! That's really sweet! I’m more of a cat person myself, but I can see why dogs would love that busy environment. Speaking of which, have either of you heard the latest about the hospital overhaul? It’s supposed to really change the way things are done. Ah, yes. The management is planning to introduce some new, more patient-centered model of care. I’m a bit nervous but also excited about it. Change always brings opportunities, doesn’t it? I don’t think anyone likes change much but, it could be good. I’ve heard they might even need some more staff, including carers. Did you hear about that? More staff? That would be a relief. The wards are always so busy. I hope that comes through. It would definitely be a welcome change if they really do need more staff. Especially with the current shortages we're seeing. It's been tough making ends meet on shifts. Definitely. I've had to turn down some extra shifts because I have a baby at home and it isn't so easy to find childcare on zero hours contracts. That's such a challenge, and it’s one of the reasons I ended up going back to being a general nurse rather than specialized. The hours were more regular. I know it's not ideal for everyone

I've been meaning to ask you, have you ever had one of those nights where you just can't sleep, and you try everything from warm milk to reading but nothing seems to work? Oh, all too often. Especially now that the kids are grown and gone – I miss the chaos but I miss the sleep too! True, my wife used to get up to feed the kids, but now I'm the one getting up to deal with the dog. Are you still on the dog-walk routine at 5 AM? I thought you said you had hired someone for that. Well, the dog thinks I'm the best walker in the world. I can't say no to those puppy eyes. But seriously though, have you seen the latest research on sleep? They have some interesting findings. Apparently, the most important thing is to maintain a regular sleep schedule. That's something my mom used to insist on. "Early to bed, early to rise," she'd say. And I've always found that whenever I'm not firmly in a routine, I don’t sleep as well. Absolutely. And they also suggest avoiding screens at least an hour before bed – that's hard for me in this digital world. Yeah, it’s tough. I've tried using blue light filters on my phone, but sometimes I forget. Me too! Speaking of which, have you considered camping? Haven't done that in ages. Actually, that reminds me... Last year we went with the family to this national park and we got lost because I thought I had loaded the right map on the GPS. How did that turn out? Terrible. Ended up driving for hours before we found civilization again. We were in the middle of nowhere, thankfully it was daytime. Good thing. The GPS failed us completely. We had to rely on a rough map. Next time, I think I’ll use an old-fashioned map if I’m going off the beaten track. You could have saved yourself the trouble if you had just asked the pilot. The what now? I mean, have you noticed how pilots are always meticulous about navigation? Sure, they use technology, but they also know how to read a map and know the lay of the land. That’s not a bad idea. Maybe I should consult a pilot next time I plan a road trip into the wilderness.

Yo, lads! I've decided I'm gonna get a pet hamster. That's brilliant! I've got a ginger one, his name is Bobby. He's a right cheeky little bloke. Aye, I used to have a hamster when I was a kid. They're so quiet isn't they? What kind are you thinking of getting? Ah, I'm not sure yet, but I want one that's easy to look after. All I know for sure is I want a keepsake that can still get me a smile in these tough times. You might want to look at the Syrian hamsters. They're the best for first-time hamster owners. They're friendly, easy to handle, and even have sweet little personalities! Yeah, and they're also the most common type of pet hamster. Hence, you'll get plenty of information on how to care for them online. Ron, you know how it is, there's barely any info on hamsters in Yorkshire. I mean, the pet shop here might not even carry exotic breeds. That's a fair point. I don’t know about you, but I'm a bit wary of different breeds. I've always assumed the traditional kind are easier, but I guess it depends on what they're bred for, yeah? True, you can't just look at looks. Well, actually, you kind of can, but the most important thing is their temperament. Some breeds are friendlier than others. Exactly! For instance, some breeds are more nocturnal and that can be a bit of a surprise if you're not prepared for that. Oh, that reminds me of this video I watched of a Roborovski hamster running in its wheel at 2 a.m. Seems like the owner was pretty amused but also a bit sleep-deprived. Haha, right! If you're going for a small breed, like the Roborovski, you'd need to be up to meet its energy level. You'd also want to consider the cage, bedding, and all the rest for whichever breed you choose. The accommodation is important because hamsters can't just take care of themselves like cats or dogs. Yeah, I got that part cleared already. Bedding, good wheel, and plenty of hiding spots. Where do I find this information? Oh, we can definitely help you with that! I've got a fair few books and resources.

I've decided I need more friends who's as obsessed with winning this game as I am. Well, let me tell you, mate. This is down to luck, right? There's no way to guarantee a win. Especially when some of us tend to roll the dice badly. But, hey, isn't that part of the fun? The risk element makes it interesting. Of course! But, honestly, I still can’t believe I messed up that turn. I needed a certain number to win and I... I just rolled three sixes, which fucked up my plan entirely. Well, mate, I've seen that before, down to even rolling three sixes when you need just one. It’s Risk, darling. You can't win ‘em all. Exactly! But it did get me thinking about maps and geography. Have you guys ever been to some of the places named here? I mean, Kamchatka, Outer Mongolia, Tokyo... Kamchatka sounds like a wonderful place to have a party, doesn’t it? I bet it has the most delightful smells with all those volcanoes. If the smell of sulfur and active volcanoes is your idea of a party, then by all means. But honestly, I think you're worse at pronouncing place names than my A-level geography teacher, who still calls it "Camcatca" sometimes. Oh, come on. It’s "Kam-chat-ka". doesn’t sound that bad. Well, anyway, while we're on the topic, what if one day we could visit the places we conquer in Risk? More realistically: what about a laser level, compass, or a decent set of maps that don’t look like they’ve been through a war? There’s actually been some great updates to digital maps. You can record instructions onto them and even get real-time updates on traffic or condition changes – useful for real-life decision-making, not just for Risk. Ah! That would truly be brilliant. Reminds me, does anyone have a real map of Bedford? We're currently leading in Risk and it’d be useful to know more about the ups and downs of our hometown. As a Learning and Development Assistant, I know that learning about local maps and geography can be very useful. Especially for children. It gives them a sense of place and space. Totally. It's also a good way to teach them practical skills. But honestly, I wish there was a way to suppress the scent wafting from the kitchen.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I was so worried about my uni future that I almost dropped out and applied to be a nanny in Norway? No, that sounds ridiculous! Tell me more. Yeah, it was just one of those times where everything seemed overwhelming and I couldn't see the forest for the trees, you know? I was convinced I wasn't good enough for my course or that I was wasting my time. Right, I've had those moments too. It feels like everyone around you is stressing about grades and careers and suddenly you just need to take a step back and breathe. Exactly. But anyway, I read online about this vacation job in Norway and I thought "oh, how romantic and quaint", you know? Be a nanny, watch kids, live in the mountains—it all sounded appealing because it felt like a nice escape. But my mom was like "Are you going to spend your life watching other people's kids or achieving what you want?” That was a wake-up call. Your mom always says it as it is. Yeah, but it was good. It made me realise that the university was where I needed to be, not escaping on a Norwegian hillside. I’m glad you learned that lesson early on. I’ve had my share of doubts too. I was really stressed about my psychology degree at first. Psychology? That doesn’t come as a surprise! You’re always so into the human mind and stuff. Yeah, the more I learn about it the more I realize it’s both a blessing and a curse. The workload is ridiculous but the content is fascinating. Same here with my course. But what’s really got me changing my mind about uni are the things we aren’t taught in the actual coursework. Like how to deal with failure for example. Our tutors preach resilience and all but it’s real life experiences and friendships like ours that really show you how to bounce back. True. University can feel so much like a bubble sometimes, just focusing on the academics. You forget how vast life and opportunities are outside of here. Exactly! And careers! I’ve been reading up on so many different things lately and I’m not even sure I know what I want yet. You know, do I really want to be in fashion, like the papers say I should, or do I want to stick to the novel idea of maybe working with animals?

Yo, mate, did you finish that history project? Nah, nearly. I just need to write up the conclusion and proofread it once more. You? Thinking about working on it tonight, got a lot of other stuff on too though, like revising for those maths mocks questions. You’re always complaining about something, Tom. Like this year, with the new history teacher, I’ve hardly heard you moan! I’m just stressed, alright? Plus, it’s not even just about the teacher. The content is really dense and complex this year. You know what I mean, though. Remember when we were just worried about comics and video games? [laughs] Yeah, those were simpler times. But now we’ve got exams and life’s getting way more real. Speaking of life, I was thinking about our conversation before. Remember Ron’s story about how some families in our area barely have enough money to feed themselves? Yeah. Sometimes it's hard to believe that while we’re stressing over assignments, some people are facing this sort of poverty and hardship. Exactly. I think most of us kind of assumed we’d never have to deal with stuff like that, but the more you learn, the more it sinks in. It’s like the more you know, the more you realize how worse things can be for some people. It’s disturbing how deep the poverty in Britain still is really. But you never really see it until you get a closer look. I know. And then there’s stuff like it in the news too, how government policies kind of influence it and stuff. Politics can make or break people’s lives, eh? Seems like the government's more concerned with keeping a few rich donors happy than the actual people. If they actually wanted to help, things might be different. But it's hard to argue with the fact that it's a very complex issue. Definitely. It's like, every time you think you understand something, there’s another layer to it. I was reading about consumerism and how it kind of fuels inequality. It’s all linked, see? Yeah, the more I learn, the more I feel like I need to learn. It’s quite overwhelming sometimes. I feel you. Sometimes I wish we could just go back to things being simple again. But you can’t turn back time.

Ah, I've been meaning to talk to you about that recording job I have coming up. It's a bit of a hassle, but it should be good for my portfolio. That's great! You've been really busy with all your projects lately, haven't you? How's that going? It's been tiring but rewarding, I suppose. I've been working a lot with that elderly neighbour of ours, Mr. Thompson, as he wanted to record an audiobook of his life for his grandchildren. He's an interesting chap, and it's been quite the challenge to get everything recorded properly. That sounds like a lovely project. What's been the biggest challenge? Well, Mr. Thompson has been dealing with a bit of arthritis, so we have to take breaks every now and then to let his joints rest. Also, hearing has become a bit of an issue, so sometimes he doesn't catch everything, and I have to repeat things. It's a slow process, but he's been very patient and we've developed a good rhythm now. That's really nice of you to help him, especially considering his condition. So, how about you, what have you been up to lately? Honestly, most of my time has been occupied with the recording job. But I've also started taking physiotherapy sessions for my back. It's not as severe as Mr. Thompson's arthritis, but it's been helpful to stretch and strengthen the muscles. It's taken some getting used to, but it seems to be paying off.
