Physiotherapy is always a good idea. What do you do to help with your back pain? The therapist suggested some exercises and also the use of a different chair at work. It's helped a bit. And, if I may be so bold, I've also been paying more attention to my diet. Tried to cut down on greasy food and I've been losing a bit of weight. Feels good, but it's hard to keep up sometimes. That’s great! Dieting can be tough. I’ve been meaning to try that too. I heard a lot of people lose weight on that keto diet, but I’m not sure about giving up all those carbs... Oh, yes, I've heard of keto! Some friends did it and lost a lot of weight. But be careful, it can be quite restrictive and if not done right, it might not be as healthy as people think.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to organize the intercollegiate debate at Doncaster and everything went haywire? No! What happened? Well, just picture this—we had a room full of future leaders and academics, all ready to present their views on global politics and whatnot. But of course, the sound system decided to ghost us right before the first speaker actually went up. That must've been chaotic! Did you manage to fix it on the spot? Oh, we had to, didn't we? Luckily, one of the audience members just happened to be an amateur tech wizard. He whipped out his laptop, hooked us up to his phone's hotspot, and we managed to stream a makeshift mix from his speakers. That’s quite the quick thinking! I can imagine it turned into a funny story afterwards. Definitely! But in the moment, it was pure chaos. And you know, it taught me a lot about improvisation and the importance of relying on your community, especially in the event planning world. We really bonded as a team after that. I can see how it could be a bonding experience. I had my own job-related chaos recently. My team had this deadline for a product launch and we ended up working on it till the last minute. Honestly? I feel like we all have our versions of that in our respective industries. Exactly! We all have our war stories. True that. Speaking of which, how about this food? Is it to your liking? It’s really good. You should be proud; you’ve stepped up your cooking game, Rach. The pork is beautifully done. Ah, thank you! It’s all about getting the right marinade, really. There’s a trick to it you wouldn’t believe. You know, working with food is another type of event planning—just with less outbursts from sound systems but more likely outbursts of flavor. That’s so true. I’ve always found food to be a way to bring people together. Speaking of which, what’s next with the production schedule for your events? As if I don’t have enough on my plate already. Next week is the annual charity function for the local hospice. It’s a big affair, but I’m excited. We’re going for a retro theme, like the 1920s. We’re planning some jazz, maybe some live music and also a silent auction.

Alright, have you guys seen the new film that just came out? I was thinking of watching it with my flatmates this weekend. What are your thoughts? Are you all into films? Yeah, I've heard it’s supposed to be pretty good. But to be honest, I've been so busy with uni work that I haven't had much time to actually check it out. I'd be up for going if it’s not gonna take too much of our time. Lads, I’ve watched a few films recently. The new Marvel one wasn’t too bad but I wasn’t that into it like the others. What film was you thinking of seeing? Ah, I was thinking maybe the new romantic comedy. It got decent reviews. But honestly, any suggestions are welcome, I’m just finding it a bit tricky deciding on one. Did anyone see “The Old Guard”? I thought it was really good, quite original for a superhero film. Worth a watch if you haven’t seen it. Yeah, that’s the one I was going to suggest! It’s really good. But if we're trying to pick one, maybe we should look for something a bit lighter? A bit lighter, you say? Considering our uni lives can sometimes be a bit hectic, that could be a good idea, couldn’t it? Agreed! I’m for anything that’s more entertaining than emotionally draining. Except, I did enjoy “A Quiet Place Part II.” That was quite engaging and not just about explosions and action. More a focus on the story. Right, so we've got a few suggestions now. The new comedy, “The Old Guard,” and “A Quiet Place Part II.” Anyone else got any ideas? Or maybe we could go for a classic? Something for a classic movie night experience. I’ve got a bunch of old films at my place if we want to have a film marathon. It could be fun to switch things up. A classic movie marathon sounds like an adventure! Like, all the classics from the ‘00s. I recently watched “The Perks of Being a Wallflower” again and really liked it. Oh, that’s actually a good idea! I love the ‘00s movies. “Pirates of the Caribbean,” any of the Harry Potter films, or even “Clueless” for a bit of a laugh. “Clueless” is a must! That film never gets old.

Oh, did I ever have an adventure over the weekend! Ooh, what happened? You seem so chipper about it but I can tell you've got a story. Yeah! So, do you remember how we went to this little café near the Eiffel Tower and tried those croissants? Of course I remember! I hope I'm not missing out on anything. Right, let me start from the beginning. So, we went to this quaint little place – it was supposed to be just delicious, but I wasn’t prepared for the adventure it turned out to be! And what happened? Try laughing at your own story even if it's painfully embarrassing. Sure, I'll do my best! Okay, so, we ordered our croissants and coffee. But the queue was so long and these adorable little dogs were coming in and out. They were so cute! We were practically melting on the spot! I'm sure. Where did you get lost while the dogs were stealing your hearts? It wasn’t quite the dogs. It was when I decided to chase after one of them because it looked like it was going to nibble on someone's pastry. What happened next? So, I climbed over the counter to get the dog and the next thing I knew, I was chasing this fluffy ball of joy all around the café. The people around the café were less amused – the owner was pretty upset, and I just tried to apologize over and over. I was more worried about the dog getting hurt than my dignity! I can just picture it! And what did you end up changing the pastry with? Fortunately, I didn’t drop the pastry in the process. But I did manage to trip on my own feet and end up with a slight limp for the rest of the day! The café staff gave us the cold shoulder, and I’ve never been so embarrassed. Oh my goodness! Did you get any photos of that? That’s got to be a keeper! Only my phone wasn’t with me at the time! I realized later I should have asked someone to take a picture. We had some great photos from elsewhere in the trip though. Well, at least you now have a souvenir t-shirt to remember it by; bruises, across the youth of London and Paris, proudly displayed. Very true!

Yo, mate, how was your weekend? Did you manage to get any chill time or was it all work? To be honest, it was pretty much work and chores, but I did manage to watch a bit of Judge Judy while I was doing the dishes, which was oddly entertaining. You know how it is! Yeah, I know the feeling. Sometimes Judge Judy's judgments are better than real life dramas, right? Definitely! By the way, did you have a chance to look at the new grades for our students? I noticed some interesting trends, particularly with those struggling with referencing. Yeah, I've been meaning to look over them. I was just looking at the students' essay drafts, actually. Some of them need some serious grammar and referencing guidance. I suppose. I've been thinking of setting up a workshop on referencing for the students. You up for helping me out? Of course, I'd love to. We could also use the British National Corpus as a reference. It should make the process more engaging and authentic. For sure! We could also perhaps invite a guest speaker from linguistics if we can swing it. Maybe someone with expertise in Malaysian dialects? I found that while the students seem interested in learning about the UK dialects, they're intrigued by more exotic ones too. That's a great idea! We've had a couple of students from Malaysia this semester, so it could really resonate with them. Yeah, and it would be a nice change of pace from regular classroom sessions. Have you taken any time off recently? Last week I managed to take a few days off to work on my novel. I'm struggling with getting one of my main characters' backstory just right. She's from Chichester, so I tried to get a feel for the place. That sounds fun! I’ve had similar struggles with my own writing. I’ve been meaning to write a short story but I’ve struggled to find inspiration. We could sit together sometime and brainstorm if you want? Absolutely! That’d be great. I often find that just talking about it helps. Speaking of fun, we should celebrate our payday properly sometime. Maybe after this set of exams. Did you have a nice lunch? Actually, I grabbed a coffee with another colleague and we chatted about work and stuff. Our new joiner from the supervisor role.

Yo, Mum, can you help me with this? Yeah, what's up? What's on your mind tonight? I talked to my mates the other day and they said they're all into eating out at this new place in town and I thought we could maybe do that someday. Oh, that sounds fun! But I've got a bunch of vouchers at home that we could use. Do you think you and your mates would be interested in using those before they expire? That could be epic, right? But they might not let us use vouchers at all, you know? Well, many restaurants do accept them, especially if they are for pubs or casual dining places. Might just need to call ahead or check. Right, but anyway, now I'm thinking about making my own dinner. You know how Dad always says homemade is healthier, so I thought I'd do that instead. That's very thoughtful of you. What are you considering making? And do you need any help with it? Well, I thought I'd try to make rice and curry. We have some rice on the side and I've got a left-over curry mix from the weekend. But how do I cook this rice properly? You seem to do it so well. Perfect, let's make it together then. It's pretty easy. First, remember to measure out your rice and water properly. The general rule is two cups of water for every cup of dry rice in most cases, but for some types, it might be different, and the curry mix is going to add a lot of flavor. Okay, 2:1 ratio for plain rice. And the curry mix will add extra flavor because it's salty and has all sorts of stuff in it. But should the measured rice and water go into a pan first, then the curry mix on top? Yes, but before that, you'll want to rinse the rice in cold water to remove some of the starch and any dust. Then, add it to a pan with the cold water and bring it to a boil on high heat. Once boiling, turn it down to a simmer, cover it, and let it cook for about 15 minutes or until all the water has been absorbed. And then stir the curry mix in? No, stir in the curry mix after the rice is done.

Alright mates, thanks for joining me. It's been ages. How've you all been? You know, I've been out of a job for so long, life's been a bit of a rollercoaster. You've not been doing too well, have you, Tom? Between uni and work, I've got my hands full but I've been trying my best to catch up with everyone and make sure everyone's doing okay. Oh, Tom! You're really coming backwards, aren't you? Tom, we've all had our shares of ups and downs. But seriously, have you considered just trying out a bit of volunteer work or taking some courses online? You've got plenty of free time - might even make you feel better about yourself. Yeah, I've thought about it, but you know, applying for jobs, it's just... it seems like nobody wants to give me a chance. I know this is a bit unusual, but I've been looking into some voluntary placement at the student union. There's a project that might help while I'm still at uni. If it sets you up with any contacts, who knows? Well, at least you're not spending all day binge-watching TV like some of us. Alright, alright, I know I've watched "The Office" for the 10th time this week, but at least I'm not doing that full-time. Guys, I'm not joking, though. Job hunting is just so dull and repetitive. Sending CVs, getting rejected, it's a drag. It's okay, Tom. It's tough, really tough. But you've got great skills, and changing the CV and applying for jobs in new sectors might work. Plus, I've heard people say that sometimes, it's just about getting out there, meeting people, attending events. Might be worth a shot? Again, it's the lack of motivation, you know? Where do I even start? Just start with one thing. One day, one CV, one application. Break it down. And seriously, Tom, there's free support here if you need it. In Whitehaven or... anywhere else. There must be something. That's really kind of everyone, thanks. I guess I just get a bit down about it sometimes, but mostly it feels like I'm just... invisible. We're here, we're living it too, in our own ways. We're facing our own struggles, I'm sure.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my day? I organized today's event at work and it was a disaster at first! Well, not a disaster, but chaos. We had a last-minute change of venue and some equipment didn’t arrive. Still, now that the show’s over, I think it went pretty well! You'd think you'd have that sorted by now, eh? I remember when I used to work, I didn't have to deal with all that stuff! Yeah, well, nothing would ever go wrong if I just worked in a quiet, peaceful office all day. Well, at least your job involves a bit of excitement then! How's the work-life balance been treating you lately? It's...different. Since I moved to Cambridge, I find it a bit hard to do anything else outside of work sometimes. But, we did manage to schedule a yoga class last week that was pretty good. You ever thought of trying it out? Yoga? Nah, that’s not really my thing. But I do enjoy walking. That’s enough for me. Fair enough. Walking’s good exercise too. Speaking of which, have you met anyone new since moving here? There’s the people at my local community garden. They’re all good folks. We talk about all sorts of things - gardening, life, the world, and all that. And there’s always something new to learn. That sounds nice! I’ve been meaning to try that too. The only thing I’m part of is my work, and maybe one or two events around the city. More socially speaking, that is. Yeah, getting out and meeting new people can be quite hard sometimes. True, but changing the world from meetings sure keeps things interesting! Indeed it does. Although I’ve not been doing any of that lately. Well, you've got zero reason to stress about it! You’ve earned the right to relax, and enjoy the view from the sidelines. I enjoy reminiscing about those work days sometimes though. Do you ever think about the joys of retirement? Oh, I have plenty of that. But yeah, I do sometimes. I work hard... I do enjoy the challenge, don’t get me wrong. But, there are times when I wish I could just leave that all behind for a bit, too. Maybe sometime I’ll make it a reality.

Alright lads, so first things first, have you two helped clean up after dinner or do I need to tell you again about the importance of helping out at home? Sorry mum, I’ll get it sorted. I’ll grab the trash and start rinsing the dishes. Actually, why don’t you both help each other out? You know, teamwork. That’s something even the game of tennis teaches us, isn't it? Even when you’re playing as individuals, the game requires teamwork. Perfect, uncle Rob is trying to get you both to work together even in cleaning. Wait, but aren't we talking about Ron here? Why talk about tennis? Oh, it's general sportsmanship, for starters. Plus, speaking of sports, have you guys decided if you want to attend the tennis tournament this Saturday? Yeah, I’m in for it. There’s a big competition this weekend. Only if it’s not too far away. I might have to study over the weekend for my exams. Ah, okay, but perhaps you could go for a few hours? It’s a good break and a good way for you both to enjoy yourselves. Actually, that reminds me of when I was in uni… Well, not about the exams but about how we used to play tennis on Sunday afternoons with friends. That sounds fun. Did you guys win often? Sometimes. But more fun was just playing and hanging out. It’s about the spirit of sports, you know? Wait, so why do you mention it? You aren’t going anywhere near a racquet now, are you? No, my racquet days are truly behind me. But speaking of fun, tell me about school. How are things going? Pretty good. I mean, most of it’s the usual stuff. Boys stuff. Boys stuff can be fine. But remember, boys and men, it’s important to express your emotions and talk about your feelings too. True that. In fact, that’s something we all could practice, yeah? Yeah, maybe. But what if someone’s just not emotional, like Ron, huh? Uncle Rob is very emotional when he watches football! But seriously, what Rony means is that everyone expresses emotions differently. We can all be a bit more open and supportive of each other’s ways. Oh, okay. So not all men are aliens then, right? Definitely not. Now, speaking of emotions, have you seen the news about the new film on Hilter?

Alright so, now that the tip’s done and we've gathered all questions for this new furniture store downtown, do you reckon they'd have enough stock for us? I don’t know about stocks, but from what I saw on their website, they do get in new stuff weekly. And like, if not, you could always check if they can order something in from another branch or something. They’re pretty flexible, that’s what I’ve heard. That’s good to know. Flexibility is key with us, especially given our timeline. We’re barely over two weeks to ANON’s friend and his family coming over. We should make the house look decent at least. For sure. We don’t want to be seen as the ones who can’t even put together a decent sitting room. Ah, but have ya thought about what A.N.'s visiting will be like? Them and their kids, they’re really good with John, considering he’s been struggling a bit lately. Absolutely. That doesn’t come up for nothing. Coming back from the park the other day, John seemed a bit brighter, you know? I reckon if it’s just people around the house, less stress about the cleanliness and all that, it just might help. That’s a good point. Speaking of, does anyone know if there's any news about that new building going up near the old Belthorn Library? I heard it'll be something like a community centre eventually, might be a good spot to take John out sometimes. Yes! I saw something about that in the local newsletter. They’re saying it’ll have activities for all ages, which is great because last time we went to that scout show, John was so into the beaver scout bits. Oh, the beaver scout Christmas party was amazing! Yeah, the food, the games... and those silly outfits. And all that energy from the kids! Reminds me of when I used to take my kids... Speaking of that, did you hear about DIY scooter course they're running at the new community centre too? That might be something for the young folk, and John could even watch, keep him engaged. Yeah, I saw that on their Facebook page. They’re also planning some successful talks about what to do with unwanted presents. There’s always so much waste, especially Christmases, and it's good they’re trying to tackle that.

Mum, I've been meaning to catch up with you for ages. How have you been? You know, aside from work. Oh, thanks for asking, dear. I've been alright, just juggling work and that indispensable new project at the school, the examination system overhaul. You know how questions are always coming up and I need to manage everything. But besides that, I've been getting into gymming, it's been keeping me sane. Ah, I see! Gym? That's great for you. I wish I had that kind of discipline, but I've been too busy with this project we're working on. It's been challenging, but I'm hoping it will pay off. Though I heard that our company is conducting some redundancies, just like the other company you were thinking about before. Ah, yes, I heard about those as well. Terrible isn't it? It's such a scary time, especially with your age group being so targeted sometimes. But, we'll manage, we always do, don't we? And you're doing a great job at work. Keep it up, you're really capable and you know, it's not the end of the world if it happens. Yeah, true. But the thought doesn't make it any easier. I'm just trying to stay positive and prepared in case. That's right, always a good plan. Have you seen or heard anything about your granddad recently? He was complaining about his hip problems before, I hope it's not getting any worse. Actually, we did chat a bit about it. He’s been a bit worse, but surprisingly, doesn’t want to do anything about it. Just keep saying how old people should just deal with it. Except, he’s been struggling to get up and down the stairs. That’s concerning. How about we try to talk to him more about it? I can try to visit whenever I can. And perhaps we should look into getting him some professional help to assess the situation properly and maybe some aids to make life a bit easier for him. You sure he’s eating properly? He does eat, but it's mostly comfort foods these days. I've tried encouraging him to eat better, but he just shakes his head at me. Ah, that's the older generation, always resistant to change. Perhaps you could try cooking something he likes, just with healthier options.

Mum, I was thinking that over the summer holidays, instead of binge-watching 'Stick with Mick' all day, we could do some outdoor activities. What do you think? Oh, that's a good idea! As much as I love the idea of you enjoying your favourite programme, spending time outside is also important. But just so you know, sometimes I feel a bit isolated as I have not been working and my social links have been limited while caring for you and [Speaker_3]. Oh, I never even thought about that, Mum. That actually makes me feel kind of guilty for always being on the TV. So you prefer we plan some group activities? Not necessarily group activities, just spending quality time together. It could also be a bit of preparation for the UK trip we're planning in a few weeks. We can't stay cooped up all day. [Looks up from the TV and speaks in a toddler-ish tone] Baa! Mick! [Smiling] Did [Speaker_3] just say Mick? Yeah, or maybe 'Mick is cool'. I’m not entirely sure. [Laughs.] [Letting out a gentle chuckle] It’s great he likes it. But don't worry, we'll make sure he gets to enjoy it, but we can't have the TV on all day, every day. Right, so what activities could we do then? Well, as I said, preparing for your trip is a good start. We should help [Speaker_3] learn a bit more about English things before we go to the UK. We could learn some basic Japanese phrases, or work on vocabulary, but in a fun way. That's actually great. Japanese is really interesting. How about we try to learn the basics of Japanese together? I can find fun apps or videos to help us. That sounds perfect! And if you really want to spend some time on 'Stick with Mick', we can compromise. We could sit together and watch an episode a day, then do some activity after. Plus, I want to encourage you to continue with the guitar lessons you started. How about setting a goal to learn a new song for the trip? Yeah, that sounds great! I was thinking about learning a song from the British pop charts. There's this one song... Yeah. It's 'Shape of You' by Ed Sheeran. It’s catchy and I heard he's from the UK.

I've got to say, it's weird watching films here instead of back home, innit? You're always carrying a Liverpudlian accent with you, even if you're just saying "hello". Sorry, mate! It's a fair cop! But questions are always asked about where I'm from and my accent. Yeah, I remember when we first met, I was like, "Is that a Scouse accent I hear?" It was so... interesting, coming from someone who's used to listening to E-midlands English all day, you know? True, true! It's like, we both are very much northerners in our own way, just with different twists. Yeah, but even though we're making each other's accents sound funnier than they are, our love of films is a common ground. Absolutely, and we both seem to have a spot of trouble at the dentist too. You're from Leicester and I'm from Birkenhead, but we both dislike the dentist. Yeah, and it's funny how both our dentists always tried to talk about football. "So, did you see the Reds play this weekend?" "Did they even ask about the Foxes?" Exactly! It's like they think football is some universal language that transcends everything, even dental anxiety. Can you believe they never asked us about writing, though? I mean, that’s what we do for a living. Probably too busy checking out your teeth to care about your literary endeavors! Right? Anyway, side-tracking, what do you think of these Citibikes? I keep seeing them everywhere in Liverpool since you moved here. Hmm, they're really handy and it's great to see so many people changing the way they move around the city. It’s environmentally friendly too, which is a win-win. Definitely. I’ve actually been meaning to suggest we try one out on one of our weekends here. That sounds like a plan! Plus, could use the exercise after all these popcorn-fueled movie nights here. Ah, true! Although, I still prefer the film-related torture. Especially when we're thinking about films outside the context of their quality. You know, like that film that was so bad it was good? Oh, you mean like the time we watched "The Room"? Yeah! Or the one time we thought trying a 90s rom-com was a good idea… "The Wedding Singer", right? I mean, it's what we get up to living out here, intimacy over film quality!

Oh, so many topics we've got to cover. I'm starving; these freshly baked scones smell amazing and your coffee looks divine! Thanks, love! I spent all morning on it and thought this morning’s catch-up would be the perfect occasion. So, what’s new? Quite a lot actually! First up, I’ve just booked this fantastic beach holiday to Bulgaria for two weeks in July. The kids are buzzing with excitement! That sounds wonderful! We could do with some family time, don't you think? Even lazy beach days with the kids sound Idyllic. Does it involve much planning? It’s been surprisingly hectic, but rewarding. I’ve read that the place we’re staying at has a lot of attractions suitable for all ages. Good, that means it’ll be a real family holiday! Anyway, shall we actually start with another potential claim to fame? I recently landed a new job at the council! So, I'll be firmly settled back in a uniform soon. That’s brilliant! Congrats, Mum. You’re going to love it there. You’ve always been passionate about local politics; this will be perfect for you. Thanks, I’m really looking forward to it. It’s been a while since I’ve been involved in community work. Hopefully, it'll bring back a bit of balance in life. For sure. It’s all about that work-life balance. Speaking of work-life balance, I’ve been meaning to ask you – how’s the new job going? I know it can be tough in primary school. It’s been a whirlwind, to be honest. But the kids are adorable and the team is fantastic. It’s really challenging in its own way, but rewarding. I knew you’d make a brilliant teacher. We should sit down and catch up properly one of these days over a more substantial meal. I’d love to hear all about it. That would be lovely, Mum. I’d also like to pick your brain a bit about professional development. Of course, anytime. And while we’re on the topic of being grown-up and job-focussed, I realised we’ve been pretty lax about family events. The Christening for the new niece... is still on? Yes, it’s coming up soon. Silas is getting his Christening this Sunday. Would you... should we bake any Easter cakes or prepare some homemade goodies for the party?

Ah, I hear you've seen some of the latest teaching trends. What have you discovered? You know how it is, teaching can be a bit of a minefield, but also so rewarding. Oh, you have no idea! I’ve just attended this workshop on interactive learning and artificial intelligence in the classroom. It was fascinating and so practical. The potential for tailored learning and differentiation is huge. It’s like a whole new toolkit for reaching students. That sounds impressive. I’ve been meaning to set up my lessons with more tech, but it can be a bit overwhelming when you’re juggling everything else we do, you know? True, it can be intimidating, but I’ve been using this new platform called Sentio that just launched. It’s like digital flashcards but so much more. You can set exercises, quizzes, even project work, and it monitors the students’ progress and adjusts the difficulty automatically. Wow, that sounds like a lifesaver! How did the workshop react when you presented that? Were they excited about it? Yeah, there was a lot of interest. Some were already using similar tools, so they were keen to compare and share their experiences, but a few were very skeptical about relying on tech too much. You know, that concern about the 'human touch' and so on. I totally get that, but we can't ignore the fact that students today spend so much time online already. Maybe if we can meet them where they are, we can still add that human touch through the content itself, really tailoring it to their interests and needs. Absolutely, that’s a great way to think about it. And it's not about replacing human interaction, but enhancing it. The platform showed me this amazing feature where you can set up virtual one-on-one tutorials or group discussions within the platform itself. More accessibility for those who might struggle to attend, say, a physical session. Ah, I see, that could really make a difference for certain students. I’ve struggled with some who just can’t make it for whatever reason. It’s heartbreaking to see they’re falling behind without wanting to. I know. You could have saved me months of trial and error if I'd known about this earlier!

I've never eaten anything as exotic as an Ortolan before. Is that like a Jewish dish, Alex? Well, it's talked about a lot in Jewish food culture, but it's actually a French delicacy, isn't it? People eat the whole bird, and it's considered quite cruel because they kind of force feed them to fatten them up. Yes, exactly. It's not exactly a common practice, and I'd be surprised if anyone here has tried it. But even if it is controversial, it's still a fascinating example of the diverse foods that we discuss in our Passover Seder. Or-to-lan? Sounds like something out of a Harry Potter book. Everyone laughs Yeah, it does! Anyway, we're on the topic of food. What's everyone's favorite Jewish dish? My mom makes this amazing lamb stew for Passover that is basically out of this world. Right? And her matzo ball soup is top-tier. But for me, I have to say I’m a huge fan of any kind of Sephardic cooking. One of my favorite dishes is pasta sarde - that's pasta with sardines. It’s kind of assumed we only eat matzo balls but there's so much more to Jewish food culture than that! Ah, yes! Sephardic dishes are so diverse and flavorful. A few years ago, I traveled to Italy for a cooking workshop and learned all about Jewish Italian food, which is actually quite different from the Ashkenazi food you might be more familiar with. But it's not just about the food though, right? The food tells stories of migrations and traditions. Did anyone hear about the Jewish-Italian cuisine in New York? I bet that's where those sarde recipes came from, isn't it? That's a great point, Tom. Food can really be a window into culture and history. There’s a similar concept with the entire concept of a Seder dinner — it’s about more than just eating, it’s about remembering and connecting with our past. Absolutely. Like the way each food item on the Seder plate symbolizes something—lettuce or karpas for rebirth or renewal, the charoset for the mortar the Israelites used, etc... As a literary editor, I can see how that works. Each symbol is a word or image that conjures up a whole story. For example, I just read a great book that connects food and immigrant stories.

So, I've been meaning to catch up on some recent TV series. Have you two seen the new season of “The Crown” yet? As someone who loves both books and films, I do struggle though with the concept of e-books versus physical ones. Do you two have a preference or do you think they’re truly interchangeable? Alright, I'm pretty sure no one expects to see two fellows like us, academics, arguing over the latest and greatest gadgets when they're abroad. Exactly! I mean, now that the days of Nokia dominating phones are behind us, there's just so much to choose from and navigate. But, between you and me, I'm kind of nostalgic for the pre-smartphone era. Oh, I hear that! I remember those days. Simple. Reliable. Of course, now, it's a jungle out there – with all these apps, features, and whatnot. Totally, just trying to configure my new phone was a mini project in itself. Was it faster than 4G or 5G? 5G, I believe. But honestly, the difference isn’t always drastically noticeable unless you’re doing something very data-intensive like streaming in 4K. That’s true. But the setup...I swear, these interfaces are designed by tech oracles, not users. Totally, I’ve found myself using different settings to "optimize performance" because they default assumed I'm on a monthly data plan. Did you figure it out, or are you still in the dark? Well, I did a bit of digging . You set it to 'balanced', then you manually adjust things as you need. But man, I still wish they gave a 'dumbphone mode' – just calls, texts, and doesn’t drain battery in 5 minutes. 'Dumbphone mode' – I'd buy that one. Maybe it’s the future? Anyway, side note, I’ve been seeing all these ads for phone cases that matched my new phone. Oh, now that's a very modern problem. Because who knew changing a phone case was more complicated than my entire thesis? Exactly! I remember in my day, you just slipped a defender on. Now, it’s so much more complicated. And the cameras? This one has five! Again, unless you’re a professional photographer, do you really need that? Honestly, no. But companies are treating phone cameras like they're now the primary feature. It’s marketing. Right, I just wanted something that could take a decent picture and that was it. And...we’re already griping about phones when we should be marveling at the world around us . What can I say, technology and nostalgia make for good conversation. Absolutely. So, how's your PhD going? It's intense! There’s so much to read, so much to write, and a deadline that keeps moving, like their own separate life.

Yo, Mum, did you hear about that new documentary on red pandas? It was so cool. They have this one super cool nanny and it was all about her and the red pandas she takes care of. Made me wanna be a red panda nanny too. That’s really sweet, love. I heard they're so playful isn’t it? I remember watching a video about them once and they looked like they just never get tired of play. Mama Malamooche! Oh, I don’t know, mate. Malamooche is just like our little puppy here. But we really need to finalize things soon. That sounds fun and they will love it! I can help you with the arrangements. But it's good you're thinking ahead now. You could help me with the design or something. And have you seen those Japanese films about animals? The animations are amazing and I just love the story of the dog in “Your Name” – whenever it's mentioned, Muffy will sit up and look interested. Dada! Movies, party planning, and a new dog. Speaking of which, how about you two boys play some board games while I put together something simple for dinner? Maybe Scrabble or Monopoly? Sounds fine! Not on the laptop, sweetie, but we can do that later, yes? Here, sit back with me and I’ll read you a story.

Oh, so many Christmases from all over have been brought today. ANON from Manila, how did celebrations differ from the ones you grew up with in England? Oh, it was so drastically different, the Philippines, you know, Christmas season is like a big fiesta. We don’t do a traditional tree, and instead we have this thing called "Pasko" that starts in September and goes up right until the new year. I had to adapt quite a bit when I moved here. That sounds like fun, I always find it fascinating how different places celebrate the holidays. I remember when I was at St Mary's, we had a very traditional English Christmas in London. Cold, just like the weather, but so full of spirit. Carol singing in the streets, big feasts, the works. Ah, you remember when? It seems like just yesterday. Fireworks at midnight? That must've been chaotic. And it must've been freezing. Barrow-In-Furness isn’t quite as snowy, but it was still pretty cold. Yes, but the different foods were the biggest change. You’re so used to mince pies and Christmas pudding. In the Philippines, we have a lot of native delicacies like puto bongbong, bibingka, and leche flan for Christmas. It took me a while to get used to the taste, especially without the familiar spices and herbs in there. Anon, do you miss anything from the traditional Filipino Christmas? I saw on the news they also do that nine-day novena thing. Oh, yes, the Simbang Gabi. It's a nine-day dawn mass done before the 25th. Growing up, my family always attended it. I really miss that warm feeling of getting up early with family, sharing small talk before mass, and then breaking fast after with hot bibingka or puto bongbong. I think that spirit’s the same everywhere. I remember in my hometown of Bognor Regis, we’d always take a walk on Christmas morning, breathe in the sea air, light some fireworks if it wasn’t too windy and wet. To unique traditions around the world! To that. And to connections. It’s lovely to share these different experiences. I suppose it makes you appreciate what you have. We often take our own traditions for granted until someone else shares a different perspective. Absolutely. Speaking of connections, have either of you traveled much since moving across the world?

Oh, did I ever tell you about that culinary disaster I nearly made the other day? Well, no, you didn’t mention anything. What happened? You aren’t normally one to have cooking fiascoes. Oh, this was a real shocker. I was trying out a new recipe for this fancy meal, and I somehow managed to forget the preheating step of the oven before putting in the dish. And how did that turn out? Well, let’s just say the oven was not impressed – it shot flames at me like a dragon and I had to run out the kitchen. Sent my husband to superhero-mode to salvage whatever he could. Oh god, that sounds hilarious. And what was your stellar culinary creation? It was going to be an oven-baked chicken dish, but unfortunately, the oven barely survived the ordeal. Maybe I need a new oven. Well, at least you’re experimenting with new recipes. You and your experiments. True. Where did you all see the new 'Peaky Blinders' episode? It’s at quite a cliffhanger now, isn’t it? Oh, I'm behind on that. Been caught up with work and haven't had much time for TV lately. Alright, don’t worry, no spoilers here! But seriously, you should catch up. It’s quite a thrilling season. I saw it last night, and oh my, it has me on the edge. Seems like the gang's reckoning day is near! I’ll make sure to catch it as soon as I can. It seems quite intense. That’s what everyone’s talking about. You know, after all the dramas of our day jobs – yours being a book for work, mine these new culinary mishaps – it’s nice to take a break with such entertaining content. So true! Speaking of work and entertainment, are you both interested in trying out a new series or book over the weekend? We could all catch up over dinner and discuss if you like. Sounds good to me. I’ve been looking for a new book to read. Are you suggesting one? You know I’m always keen on hearing recommendations. And I do have that new novel from one of my favorite authors that just came out on Kindle. Perfect! I can give you the details if you’d like. It’s actually quite a thought-provoking piece, touches on many themes we’ve discussed before – family, relationships, trust… That sounds intriguing.

You know, I have been thinking. These modern times are all about technology and what not. I just don't get it. Right! I remember telling our grandkids how to send a letter and they looked at me like I was from another world. That's the thing with progress. It can be daunting, especially when you've always done things a certain way. But it can also bring so many benefits. Benefits? I don't see 'em. It's all about staring at those screens all day. What's wrong with a good old-fashioned letter? Well, we can't really go back in time, can we? And think how many new opportunities this technology has opened up for our grandchildren. They're so global now, even at their young age. That's right, and it's good for them. Technology can be a tool, for good or for bad, just like anything else. But it's our choice how we use it. I understand the sentiment, but it just seems too complicated. I tried to show our grandson how to use a computer once and he laughed at me. I ended up feeling like an old relic. Ah, but that's where we need to adapt, right? It's never too old to learn something new. If I were to start again, I'd probably have a better chance than you with these "new-fangled" gadgets. Exactly! There are so many courses out there, even if it’s just basic things like using the internet or sending emails, you'd do wonders for your confidence. And who knows, it might be a little fun too? Fun? You reckon? Of course! It's like mastering a new game. Plus, think of it this way – it might bring some of that gen Y generation closer. Our grandkids might even learn a thing or two from us, old-fashioned ways! It's about balance. Using technology smartly and maintaining those real connections we value. Maybe set a regular time with them to teach you something, or ask them to show you around these apps they use. I hadn't thought of it like that. Sure, they often ask me this and that about old times, and I enjoy sharing my stories... maybe I can get something from them in return. That's the spirit! And these gadgets, despite what they seem, are quite user-friendly once you get the hang of them.

Ah, Sarah, just got back from the brainstorming session with Tom and the team. We're making good progress with that new research project, but I wish we didn't have to deal with all these budget cuts. Sorry to hear that. Budget cuts always complicate things. But on a lighter note, have you guys heard that our department is hosting a Christmas party this year? Yo, so I had this absolute craic of a first day back at school today. Yeah? What happened, then? Was it all the usual first day excitement or something else? Right! I can see that. I suppose it’s a bit too unique... True. But honestly? I’m kinda into it. Like, I really want to see what she has planned for the rest of the year. So you're embracing the youth of it? You never know, this could actually be a really cool change.

Oh, Mum, you haven't changed. We have to talk about the menu every time we try a new restaurant. This place looks nice though, they have a chicken and mushroom pie that I've been dying to try. Ah, thanks so much for coming over today to help clean our house. It's been a bit of a mess lately, especially since the kids' teenage phase is peaking. Yo, how's uni going for you? Thought you'd be banging on about your lectures by now, lol. Honestly, I talked about that less than you'd think. You know I need a distraction from it all sometimes. It’s all about focus and hard work.

I've decided I'm spending my summer's holidays in Paris this year. I've always wanted to see the Eiffel Tower up close and enjoy the city’s bistros. Ah, the City of Lights, right? That’s quite romantic! I’ll have to look at some pictures you bring back. I went to Cornwall last year. The beaches are stunning! Irma, I've always wanted to visit Ireland. Our very own Emerald Isle! There's nothing like the rolling green hills and medieval castles. You'll have fun in Paris, though. It's such a vibrant city! And maybe some tips on the best pubs near the libraries.

Oh, did you see that last move by Sterling? I mean, what a goal that was! Absolutely! He's got unreal speed. You can't teach that. That said, speaking of nailing things, how about we grab a takeaway when the game ends? Oooh, brilliant idea! I still think a solid defensive midfielder would help solidify things, though.

I've been meaning to ask you, Grandma. What do you think of these new Bollywood movies? I've seen quite a few and I think they're really fun, but I've never asked you what your opinion is. Yo, mate, gotta say Rome is something else, huh? We've been here two days and I've already seen more history than I've seen in my whole life. You guys enjoying it? Oh, absolutely. Next time I’m online, I’ll look up storage facilities around here. Because, as you'll probably be aware, I'm making some changes in my life and may need to store some things until I figure out what to keep and what to get rid of. Oh, are you finally putting your writing career first? Because I’ve seen that pile of books and manuscripts under your desk... Haha, yes. Just making space. But real job first, writing later! That’s great to hear!

Yo, mate, did you know that many rivers in London are actually channels that were engineered? It’s crazy how they were originally built for transport and then they've evolved into features of our landscape. Yeah, totally! I remember reading about the Regent's Canal and the Grand Union Canal. We should check out some boat tours when we have time. It could be pretty cool, right? And have you heard about the “canal boats of London” where people live on those boats? Some of them are quite quaint and even stylish, given how they're decorated. Oh, that's actually really interesting! It’s kind of like having an extremely slow, water-based movement to your life. Seems pretty tranquil. Definitely, mate. I read that some of these boats are now even rented out for parties and events, which is wild. Speaking of events, I heard that there are a number of kosher restaurants popping up in London. Do you lot know much about that? As a baker, I’d say I know quite a bit about food rules. But kosher law can be pretty complex. It's not just about pork but all sorts of different dietary laws, right? Exactly. From what I've picked up, kosher rules are strict and they influence everything, right down to the chef’s gloves and even the washing of utensils. Aye, right, it’s serious stuff. Like, in my university course about Jewish culture, we discussed how even the production and handling of food is governed by those rules. Fascinating, it proves that food is more than just sustenance, it’s tied to culture and spirituality. Yeah, totally. Australia’s not the same, we don’t really have that level of strict observance unless you are specifically in areas with high Jewish populations. Different city, different culture. Changing topics, and staying in food but now moving to clubbing. You guys checked out any new clubs in London? I heard one opened up in Shoreditch that’s really popular. Nah, we haven’t. But isn’t there a rule of sorts about not going into clubs with real names? Using pseudonyms or something? Ah, you’re talking about the whole culture around being “in the know”. Like, if I say “The Box,” you know where I mean but if I say the actual name... [Laughs] [Laughs] Spot on! I know that one.

Yo, lads! How've you all been? Yeah, can't complain too much. Been surviving uni chaos and everything. Oh, definitely unreal! I mean, I need a break from all this coursework. Same here – do you ever think this will end? Between studying and trying to balance everything else, it feels like we've all got a lot on our plates. Completely. I had a lecture till 5 today and then I had to race to respond to loads of emails. Crazy stuff. Definitely, and on top of that, there's always the social stuff to keep up with. I've been using Tinder a bit too much lately just trying to find any free time. You're not alone there, mate! I'm making the most of it while I can before we all get tied up with dissertations and project deadlines. True, true. But have you got any luck, though? Any good matches or dates? Mm, yeah, a few decent ones but nothing too serious. It's hard to commit to anything when it feels like we're all just trying to balance so many different things. Definitely know that feeling. I’ve been going on some dates but honestly, it's all a bit exhausting to try and meet people and keep up with uni work at the same time. Right, but it's always good to take a break sometimes. I actually had a date with someone really nice last week, but we’re trying to make it work amongst our schedules and that's proving a bit tricky. That's great to hear! How's it going? Dating someone from uni or outside of it? He’s actually from around the Chester area. Seems lovely and understanding, which is a big plus! I've been on a few dates too, but I still haven't found quite what I’m looking for. Some are just nice but don't really click, and others are a bit too interested in talking about football all day. Haha, football lovers are everywhere! But you know, sometimes I think it’s worth it just for the experience. And plus, you can always learn if you're talking football! Again, agreed. Plus, you never know who you'll meet or what you might learn. Did you all hear about Libby and Jess just got a new housemate? No, what’s the story?

You both remember last year's election, don't you? The outcome really didn't seem to change anything for us, did it? Indeed. It felt like the usual muddle. Still, now and then, you catch a glimpse of something on the news which kind of gives you hope. Like what, a politician not being absolutely hypocritical? Ha, exactly! But seriously though, I've been thinking more and more about how this whole benefits system works. You two have both been on the receiving end for a while. Oh yes. Well, let me tell you, it's not what it used to be. You can't just rely on it like we used to. What with all these cuts and changes, it's a daily worry. Absolutely. I've met so many people who are struggling. It's not just about us, you know? There are families and young people trying to make ends meet and these cuts don't help. Now that I'm retired, I've actually spent quite some time studying this. It seems that most of the benefits are just cut after cut. Makes you wonder what the system is designed for. If it's not for supporting people like us who've worked, why even have it in the first place? I agree. A few years back, it sounded good - you know, in principle: "support for those in need". But the reality, as you both know, is different. It's a constant fight for what doesn't seem much in the end. It's not just the benefit cuts. The procedure itself is just so complex. I've seen people getting caught in bureaucratic nightmares, trying to just apply, never mind the uncertainty of whether it'll be approved or not. The thing that really gets my goat is that all this could be avoided. We've got so many people who are willing to work, willing to contribute, but there just aren't jobs that match their skills, especially in some areas like ours in Norfolk. True, but what about re-training? And isn't it strange how we see all these advertisements for jobs that are minimum wage, yet the training for good jobs is either too expensive or almost out of reach? Exactly. As a childminder, if I were younger, I doubt I could afford to re-train. And even if I could, who's to say there would be jobs available?

Oh, did I tell you about the job interview I had today? It nearly made me consider giving up my current job for the change of scenery! You're shaking your head already! What happened? The salary was a bit lower than I expected, but the kind of work they were involved in seemed fascinating. It’s an environmental project focused on renewable energy and green technology. That does actually sound quite interesting. I'd be surprised if they didn't mention it. But even if it is lower, maybe it’s a better work-life balance or something else to offset that, right? True, true. They did say they offered flexible hours and training programs which could be very beneficial for professional growth. But, you know, as much as we need the extra income, I feel a bit torn. Hence your head shaking! It's hard to let go of a steady income sometimes, even if your heart is in a different place. But considering you've been in your current job for a while, it might be good to stretch those wings and look at new opportunities. That’s what I thought too. But then there's always the worry about stability for the family. You know, the mortgage, the kids' school fees... it's always a juggling act. Absolutely. And the kids' school fees, they keep spiralling out of control. A university education feels like it’s coming up sooner rather than later and that’s really putting the pressure on us. Exactly! But speaking of the kids, how was Sofia's day? I missed seeing her the moment I came home. Well, she mentioned earlier that her art class was cancelled due to a teacher being sick. She seemed a bit disappointed but then got settled with her project of painting a picture for the upcoming charity exhibition at school. Oh, that's right! I completely forgot about the exhibition. I really love seeing her work, she's so talented. You sure she’s okay though? She was a bit grumpy for a while but after some of her favourite food, she seemed to perk up. She said she might need help with the project if it's going to be good enough for the show. Of course, we'll make time to help her. I'm just getting excited thinking about seeing her artwork on display.

Oh, did I sound like I was bemoaning my situation today? I suppose I was, didn’t I? It feels so different being here in Tarnow rather than back home. The weather, for one, is quite odd to me. Still, now, the days are getting a bit longer, which is a welcome change. Yeah, the weather here can be quite dramatic, can't it? I'm used to the unpredictable British weather myself, but there's something very set about it here — even if it is backwards to what we're used to in Britain. Exactly. I have to keep reminding myself that daylight savings is ahead here, despite the northern latitude. Speaking of reminders, I was thinking we should actually start making plans for our holiday together soon. Have you given any thought to where you'd like to go? Actually, I've been going back and forth in my mind. You know, since being here, I've been thinking about where "home" truly feels like. You know, between Britain and… here, I suppose. For me, it's usually about going back to see my family wherever they are. The thought of moving "back home" to specifically Bury feels less daunting once in a while. Do you ever feel like the concept of home is... shifting or evolving? Definitely. Living abroad for as long as I have has certainly changed my perspective on that. For example, last year, when we planned the trip to the Malverns, it really felt like a home trip for me doesn’t it? But it's different from "going home" to Bury. Absolutely. I was planning to visit the UK soon — actually, for my Uncle's funeral. It just feels so... surreal to be attending a funeral from overseas now. Oh, I'm so sorry to hear that. That must be hard. But it's also a chance for a bit of hiatus from everyday things and time to reflect. True. It's forcing some thinking about where I see myself. Funerals make you think about what's truly important, I guess. After being unemployed for so long... It sounds like the TEFL work you do almost acts like a respite for you? Yes! Teaching English here, even part-time, it feels like a lifeline. It gives me structure, connections. But I’ve been thinking I might need to look for more consistent work soon...

Oh, so many options here! Usually I stick to a classic English Breakfast, but they do have some interesting flavours. I've been meaning to try that oriental blend, but I've never had the heart to move away from tradition. Tradition is a wonderful thing! But sometimes it's nice to step out of the comfort zone. Besides, they say the best of everything comes from a little experimentation. I suppose that's true. Besides, it’s not like I’m ordering an exotic fruit mix or anything. It’s still tea, right? True, true. So how was your week? I’m sure you've been swamped with copywriting work. Swamped is an understatement! They're having a rush on campaigns this quarter so I've been working overtime. But it’s stressful, to say the least. Ugh, the glamour of freelance work! But good for you for handling it. You’ve got to love what you do, I suppose. For sure! It’s rewarding, but maybe not as much when it involves overtime. I feel you. Where did you get the tea? You seem so particular. Just a little thing I picked up online. They grind the leaves fresh, or so they claim. Plus, I like supporting local businesses. That’s really thoughtful! I should start doing that more often. It really makes a difference, and you get better quality usually. Well, I’m the opposite when it comes to this. I’m a student and I do all my work here in the pub. More power to you! I couldn’t focus like that. I need a quiet desk and a cup of tea to get anything done. Oh, really? I find the background noise actually helps me focus better. Everyone’s different. But tell me about your course. I don’t often get to hear what it's like from someone actually in it. It’s tough but so rewarding! It's all about the software development and theoretical computer science. Impressive! So, survey programming... how does that fit into your work? I would have thought that came later. Well, actually, it's funny. I’ve been doing it during my breaks. Someone from a local market research firm was looking for help, and it turned out it’s a great fit for my skills. That’s amazing. So, you're really balancing work and study? Yeah, it's a bit hectic but it pays the bills and it’s relevant, so it's worth it.

Oi, isn't it just ridiculous how early the sun peeks through the curtains these days? Got you lot out of bed again before 7! Speaker_2 and  giggles  Oh, Mum! We were wide awake at 5:30! We heard the birds singing too! Yeah, and we were arguing about who gets the most Easter eggs! Eggs, eh? Well, I guess we can't have a morning without some morning madness. So, what are we doing today then? Got any plans already drafted out in your little heads? We were talking last night that maybe we could learn some circus skills! You know, for the school fair next month. I want to learn how to juggle! And balance on a tightrope! Well, balancing on a tightrope might be a bit over the top for a ten year old, but juggling is a good idea! And perhaps we can work out a routine to show off at the fair? But first, let's get some breakfast in us and then we'll see if we can find some video tutorials online. And can we eat pancakes? Or would that be too much sugar this early? Pancakes are always a good idea if you're planning to burn the extra energy. But let's make them whole grain, and I'll also make some eggs to keep you energized. Oh, eggs! Yes! Speaker_3 and Ok, ok, settle down! First things first, we need to eat. And then we can talk about juggling and such later. Hey, you know what? Last night we watched this video about the Neon Moon event. Did you see those cool pictures? They look like they came from another world with all those lights and colors. Oh yes! We looked for hours! They're saying it's this really cool festival with... ...with lots of um, art and music and stuff. Ah, the Neon Moon event, yes. They make it sound quite enchanting, don’t they? It's an art festival with light installations and live music. We might need to get tickets soon if it's something you both are keen on. Maybe as a weekend treat for a couple of Saturdays from now. That would be amazing! Yeah, pleeease! Well, before we make any big plans, let's think about managing our schedules. But we can certainly look into it if we can work out a day that works for all of us.

You both read the news, I assume? Politics has been particularly unpredictable over the past few years. Still, now that the Brexit negotiations seem to have reached an impasse, I find myself wondering what the future holds for us and our children. Right you are, Ellie. I just watched the parliament debates, and to be honest, I have to wonder about the direction this country is going. It's frustrating, especially in our line of work where we're so directly affected by what's happening. What do you mean, specifically? I mean, I studied history in uni, and it seems like there's so much historical significance in those debates. I’m just trying to understand how our politics today relates to our past. Well, that's a fascinating point, Dan. You’re right about the historic aspects. Brexit, in particular, is a case study in the complexities of British politics. It really highlights the divide in the UK – not just between Leave and Remain, but also within the regions, as you'd know well, John. And Wales, of course, has its own intricacies. I've found that it's not just about the national level, but the influence of local concerns and the perceived understanding—or lack thereof—from central governments. But the point you make about regional divides, Ellie, it’s so relevant to what’s happened over the years. For example, look at the miner's strikes in the 80s—see how they are still influencing attitudes today in places like Nantyglo. Yeah, that’s what I’ve read in some of my coursework. The mining industry’s decline, the regional economy, and later the devolution efforts. It does seem like a lot of today's political discourse still echoes those past issues. Exactly. The way regions have been treated historically has a lot to do with current political leanings. It’s a bit depressing, really, when you consider it’s been decades and we're still dealing with similar themes. However, it’s also an important lesson to learn about the depth of history in shaping today's arguments. And it's not just the past, Ellie. The current debate is also about trust. Or the lack of it, in some cases. People feeling left behind, regions feeling ignored, and then there’s the broader rhetoric about representation. It's complex and it affects everyone, not just those directly involved.

Alright, kids! Let's move on from Linton Book Festival. Now, who's up for telling a story of their own creation? I am! I've been thinking about this one all week. Me too! Mine’s about a fairy who lives in a castle made of gingerbread! Oh, that sounds yummy! I love where your imagination takes you. Wait, but before you start, can we even use gingerbread as a setting? Is it not too childish? Oh come on, it's just delicious! And I can have gingerbread soldiers in it too! Absolutely, in the world of story creation, the crazier the better, isn't that right? Anything goes as long as you enjoy it. Okay, okay... So in my story there's a little girl who finds a magical book in the library. It transports her to this magical world where all the animals can talk and... And maybe they all love gingerbread! Where did you get that from? You must have been listening to the adults more often than you let on. Yeah, maybe. Anyway, so in this world, everyone gathers at a grand tree where they share all their stories. But then a giant, book-stealing monster comes and they have to save the book! Wow, that sounds like a real adventure! But it's not just about the giant monster, right? What about the girl's journey? What does she learn? She learns that she doesn't need magic to tell a good story. She realises she has the power to create it herself and that's what's really valuable. Just like us! We're creating stories right now! Exactly! And who's her sidekick? Does she have some animal friends? Oh, there’s this talking fox, very clever and sassy. He always gives zero-filtered advice. And I’ve got those gingerbread soldiers! They're actually just guards protecting the story tree. Ah, I love it. It seems you both share a flair for imagination. So, what about yours now? You're right, I should go first. So... The fairy in the gingerbread castle needs a magic wand to save her castle from the evil mice that are nibbling it away! Yes, the mice! I can see it - cheeky little rodents with big grins. But how does the fairy get the wand? There’s got to be a challenge! Yes! To get it, she has to go on a quest and make friends with the mice, finding out why they’re nibbling the castle.

I've decided I'm going full veggie this week. Got any recommendations for dinner? That sounds like a fun challenge! What got you on this vegetarian kick? You've been really lazy with meat-free options lately, Lizzy. Oh, I agree with Gabby. You've been totally ignoring the whole 'vegetarian option' at our usual dinner preps. Just feel like giving it a proper try. But even if I want to get serious with this, Gabby, do you think it's enough, like, to just not eat meat? Or do I need to think about all the other animal products too? Well, as much as we can in our daily lives, but it's also about making realistic lifestyle changes that you can maintain. It's not just about diet, but also the broader impact of animal agriculture on the environment and animal welfare. You know, like the impact of dairy and eggs. And don’t forget what you're replacing it with is equally important. We don’t want to compensate with overprocessed 'meat substitutes' that could have their own set of problems. Where did you get that from? 'Shmeat'? Have you guys heard about that? Ah, that. Yeah, 'synthetic or cultured meat'—the current buzzword for lab-grown meat, right? There's been a lot in the media about it. But does it count as being truly 'vegetarian' if it’s still essentially meat? But it's promising from an environmental standpoint, isn’t it? Reduced greenhouse gases, land usage... and, of course, zero animal slaughter. More or less. But there’s still the debate over the nutrients and taste. Do we need to produce something that mimics meat when we could just embrace a diet that doesn’t hinge on animal products in the first place? You’re bringing up good points. It’s like, do we need to fix a problem by essentially replicating it, or should we look at the source and make changes from there? And let's not forget, if we're talking about a moral or ethical standpoint of vegetarianism, like reducing animal cruelty, shmeat still doesn’t cover that, right? It's still meat, just made differently. Exactly! It’s like fixing the system by working around it rather than changing our thinking. For me, vegetarianism wasn’t just about diet; it was about understanding and accepting that every choice impacts the world around us.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we had our washing machine acting up just before Christmas? It was a disaster! I was frantic, thinking about all the clothes and bedding that needed washing. That wasn’t very fun, was it? Especially because we kind of have to plan around yours and daddy’s schedules. Like when we get back from work and all that. Well I had to laugh though, didn’t I? Because when I got home and heard what had happened, I joked about how I could finally get some peace and quiet. Dad, you were just being cheeky. He was, but honestly, we did need a good washing machine. We finally managed to send it off for repairs and got a new one. It’s working great now, so problem solved. That’s good to hear. Anyway, shall we actually start on dinner? I’ve got a new recipe for roast chicken I wanted to try. For me! We can’t do too many changes to the dinner ritual though, right? You know him. He’s all about tradition. Like with the TV at New Year’s Eve. Do you really need three different channels at once? It’s all about choice! Besides, there’s always something interesting happening on all three at once. I’m not convinced. I know what you mean though. It's a bit like the internet, isn't it? Sometimes it feels like we need to filter out so much to find what’s actually useful or entertaining. Exactly! But I just like to keep options open. Who knows what little gems you might miss if you only stick to one thing? True. I guess we should talk about language changing too. I mean, I find my own language shifting all the time. Oh for sure. Our grandkids are always adding new words, and it’s fascinating. But sometimes I find myself trying to figure out what they mean! Like when they say “shook.” I used to almost think it was a spelling error. I know, right? “Shook” as in emotional responses. It’s fine, but funny thinking back now. Sure is. I suppose language changing is just a part of life and progress. Speaking of progress, anyone planning a trip or anything big in the new year? What about us watching some old favorite TV shows instead? We haven’t done that in ages.

Alright, boys, who first noticed that Dad uses these peculiar butterfly forks every time we have guests for dinner and no one else ever uses them? Right! They're so funny. Especially now, the way you all react when he pulls them out again! Yeah, it's like... “Wait, is that actually a fork?” Well, keeps things interesting, doesn’t it? Actually, I’ve always wondered where he got them from. He's never really talked about it. Maybe he was given them as a gift in one of his big foreign business trips - oh, speaking of, how was Russia? Oh, Russia... It was a very interesting trip, filled with... very peculiar experiences. Did I ever tell you both about the time we went to the Hermitage and I accidentally or, rather, intuitively walked away from our group to find myself in an isolated part of the museum, surrounded by endless rows of paintings with just a single docent who assumed I was lost? Did she speak English? Well, at first, barely. But somehow we managed to communicate... A bit like us, trying to figure out silly butterfly forks, right? That must have been an interesting conversation! Indeed! Then we shared a 2 minutes of silence, just observing each other and understanding. It was surprisingly powerful. How did you keep quiet for two whole minutes? Well, when you're surrounded by so much beauty and history, words sometimes just don’t seem enough, you know? You know, it's interesting how we do that at your party sometimes, though... sometimes there are those moments of silence when we're all together but just sitting there in our own thoughts, isn't there? Exactly. 2 minutes of silence doesn't always have to be awkward. It can be almost meditative. You know what else I realised? I started to really appreciate my own birthday celebrations now. They don't need to be so loud and chaotic all the time. That's true. It’s not about the size of the party but the connections we make, right? Absolutely. I miss though, the drama of surprise parties and all that. Well, that's the beauty of growing up, adjusting our expectations and sometimes going for the quieter, yet meaningful experiences. I was thinking, what would you like to do for your next birthday? Honestly, just a big family dinner and maybe a small outing to somewhere nearby.

Oh, did I ever tell you about our trip to Cornwall last summer? The sun was shimmering off the sea, the children couldn't get enough of the beach. Tell us, tell us! Did you see any dolphins? And were the sea turtles out and about as well? Ah, yes! We took a guided boat trip and I managed to spot a couple of playful dolphins. But sea turtles, unfortunately, not this time. However, Ellie actually found a beautiful piece of driftwood shaped like a turtle. Yeah, just like the ones in our Adventure Island series! Exactly! She even brought it back home and we are still wondering what to do with it. Maybe we could make a drawing of it and show it to your class? That’s a great idea. It could be a fun project for the class next term. So, where were we thinking of going this summer? Well, if we're keeping the beach theme, how about The Isle of Wight? We could spend a week there in a little cottage and visit the V&A exhibition at the end of the holiday. That sounds fab! But remember, we need to keep an eye on all the little ones for the V&A, they tend to get a bit excited when they’re surrounded by art. Yeah, and what about my food intolerance? Last time we were in Cornwall, they didn’t have anything good that didn’t contain wheat, and I got sick. More reason for us to choose a place with more options. The Isle of Wight should be good — lots of family-friendly spots and catering to all sorts of dietary needs. And we should definitely make sure we'll have time to explore the island and maybe do a little hike. Absolutely! We can do some of the coastal paths. It’s wonderful for the children and so much fun for all of us. And maybe we can take a picnic to enjoy at the top of the hike. Just like in the Adventure Island series! Exactly. It'll be fun to make it feel adventurous. And when we get back, I'll book that V&A exhibit slot. Great! So, we need to solidify the dates, make sure everyone is free, and I’d love to start researching the best spots for us. Maybe a guide book or some recommendations from last year? I can help with research!

Yo, mate, did you finish that history coursework last night? Nah, not quite. I was watching that new Star Wars movie after dinner and talked to my mates till tea time. Made me a bit tired, you know? Same, the new episode was awes – I mean, really good! Absolutely, totally agree. But about that history coursework, it’s due in next week, and right now, I'm stressed out. All this stuff about the American Civil War. It’s so much to remember! [laughing] Dude, you think you have it bad. I have to learn about all the different battles, and I just can't get my head around all of them. So what about the upcoming party at Jack’s house on Friday? You coming? Yeah, definitely! He said it's going to be cool, with the latest DJ and all. That’s nice. How’s the school? Are things good or is there still a lot of drama? Well, you know what sixth form is like. But our new Maths teacher is actually quite cool, she’s trying to make it interesting. [sarcastically] Yeah, right? Because coursework and exams are all about making things interesting... [chuckles] Fair point, mate. Well, at least we're not in the same situation as Alex. A couple of days ago, he got into trouble for texting during a lesson. They gave him a detention. Seriously? That’s pretty strict! But I guess that’s how they learn to respect the rules. For sure. Plus, our school has this new policy now, if you're a prefect you get extra responsibilities. Seems like the school's tryin' to keep us in line. Do you think you'll apply to be a prefect? You seem pretty responsible. Not really sure. I mean, it's a lot of extra work. But it sure looks good on the CV, right? Definitely. Plus, if I'm completely honest, having a few of us in positions of authority might take some weight off teachers' shoulders. True, maybe. [thoughtful] You know, this almost makes me wish I'd taken the opportunity to be a prefect in younger years when I had a chance. [nodding] Yeah. But look on the bright side, it gives us more time to focus on fun stuff like that party next week. [laughs] Exactly! And movies! That Star Wars movie was just the start. My mate bought tickets for a new Marvel one out soon and I’m thinking of asking if anyone else is up for it.

Yo, mate, did you hear about that new bike shop opening up near the university? I think it's quite possibly the coolest shop I've seen so far. Yeah, I've seen that, right? There was quite a bit of hype online and in the local papers. I kind of regret not looking into it sooner. I've been meaning to get a new bike and I heard they've got some real good deals on decent makes. And the prices aren't awful, right? I saw they had a sign saying special early bird discounts if you get in before the end of the month. Yeah, that's correct. They're trying to get more customers initially so they can set up a more permanent customer base. Makes sense, but what about the location? Wasn't it on that one road that always seems to be under construction? Ah, you mean the A183? It's a pain for sure, but the shop's actually in a smaller side street off the main road, so hopefully it won't be too much of an issue getting there. That's a relief, I can't stand it when side roads get clogged up from construction. Trust me, I know what you mean. Suppose we need to check it out soon, make sure its worth the money and the hassle of construction. Absolutely, let's do it next week then? Maybe I can show you this cool road I found on a map, near the coast. It's supposed to be really scenic and great for cycling. That sounds awesome, but realistically, next week is probably just too inconsistent for that. We're both pretty busy this month, but I do want to check out the shop during the week when it's less crowded. Oh, fair point. The fewer crowds, the more fun I reckon. If we can head up on a Wednesday, maybe we can combine it with something else and make a day of it. Wednesday's not bad for me, might work around my schedule. Great! I'll check my schedule too and confirm it later today. And speaking of checking schedules, we should also check the cricket scores today. The England match is on and I’ve been following it. Ah, yes! I've been getting into cricket more and more lately, love how it feels like a proper sport for a change.

"Look at this, Alex! The Szechuan Spicy Prawns sounds amazing! But have you had it before? I'm a bit concerned about the spice level because sometimes, the takeaway places can go overboard on the heat." "It's not so bad, Sarah. I've had it once or twice before and it's very good. The heat is there, keeps it interesting, but it's not overwhelming if you can handle normal spicy foods, you should be fine. They're usually pretty good about communicating the spice levels on their menu." "Yeah, but just in case, we can always ask them to tone it down a bit. They're usually pretty accommodating. But honestly, you guys want to try anything else? I thought we decided on Szechuan, right? Or maybe we could mix it up and get a few different dishes if it's for a group. Someone for the less adventurous at heart or something?" "Alex mentioned the Schezwan, and I've had that, but if anyone wants to try something else, go for it. I'm game for anything that's not too bland. But let’s make sure we get a balance to cater to everyone’s taste. Maybe something sweet and sour or a couple of vegetable dishes?" "Good point, Alex, let’s add some balance then. I could do with something less spicy, considering we’re trying to get all three of us to eat comfortably. Maybe some Kung Pao chicken doesn’t come with that chili oil or something?" "Sounds good! And maybe some stir-fried vegetables to share or something. And let’s consider some wontons or dumplings for those who might want something less meat-heavy. I usually prefer the vegetable options since I'm getting a bit healthier now." "All good suggestions. Also, and this is important, let's make sure we also get something that can accommodate our gluten-free guest. Anyone remember if Sarah is still out of gluten? I think I remember something in the past. Alex, what's the deal with gluten for you?" "Actually, I’ve been off gluten for a couple of weeks to see if it helps with the tummy issues.
